topics_verified.topic: Claude Code headless / non-interactive CLI reference (flags, JSON schemas, stream-json stdin protocol, env vars, setup-token, session storage, failure semantics) as of docs current on 2026-09-27 (docs reference Claude Code v2.1.283)
topics_verified.summary: The official reference for non-interactive use is code.claude.com/docs/en/headless plus cli-reference, and both were current to v2.1.283. `claude -p` exits 0 on success and non-zero on failure (143 on SIGTERM); `--output-format json` returns one object whose success arm carries `result`, `session_id`, `total_cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `num_turns`, `usage`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, `structured_output`, `stop_reason`, and whose error arm (subtypes `error_max_turns`, `error_during_execution`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_max_structured_output_retries`) has no `result` key but has `errors: string[]`. `--input-format stream-json` (with `--output-format stream-json --verbose`) turns the process into a long-lived NDJSON loop: each stdin line is `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":<string|blocks>}}`, each turn emits its own `result`, and the process ends when stdin closes; the CLI-level envelope is not formally documented (Anthropic closed the docs request as not-planned) but the SDK's `SDKUserMessage` type and a Sept-2026 bug report confirm the shape and a `control_request`/`control_response` interrupt channel. Permission modes for `-p` are `default|acceptEdits|plan|auto|dontAsk|bypassPermissions|manual`; `-p` starts in `default` on every plan; `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is refused as root/sudo unless a recognized sandbox is detected; `--permission-prompts none` (v2.1.259+) prevents hangs on prompts. `--bare` (recommended for scripts, future default) never reads OAuth or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so a subscription-backed design must not pass it. `claude setup-token` prints (does not store) a one-year OAuth token for Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, consumed via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; it is not refreshed after a 401, so expiry means regenerate and restart. Transcripts live at `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR|~/.claude>/projects/<cwd with non-alnum→'-'>/<session-id>.jsonl`, `--resume <uuid>` finds them across projects (v2.1.223+), retention is `cleanupPeriodDays` default 30, and Anthropic explicitly does not recommend sharing `~/.claude` across machines or network filesystems. On policy, a support article dated 2026-06-16 says `claude -p`/Agent SDK usage still draws from the subscription's usage limits (the announced separate credits were paused), while the SDK overview forbids third-party developers from offering claude.ai login or rate limits in their products without approval. The native binary needs no Node.js but the documented Linux floor is Ubuntu 20.04/Debian 10, well above CentOS 7.9's glibc 2.17, so the CLI must run inside the container image, not on the host.

findings.claim: `-p`/`--print` runs Claude Code non-interactively; exit code 0 on success, non-zero when the run fails; invalid flags are reported to stderr before the run; in-run failures such as missing authentication are printed as the result on stdout.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails, so your scripts can branch on the exit status. If you pass an invalid flag, Claude Code reports the error to stderr before the run starts. When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout." SIGTERM: "Claude Code exits with code 143 ... leaves the turn that was in progress unfinished and records no result for it. To end the turn instead, send SIGINT". Piped stdin capped at 10MB (exits non-zero above). `-p` rejects `--bg`. The agent-loop page adds: on an error result "The underlying Claude Code process also exits with a nonzero code."

verdict.corrected_claim: `-p`/`--print` runs Claude Code non-interactively. Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails; an invalid flag is reported to stderr before the run starts; a failure inside the run, such as missing authentication, is printed as the result on stdout (and, because it is an error result, the process also exits non-zero, so a caller must check BOTH the exit status and stdout). SIGTERM gives exit code 143 and leaves the in-progress turn unfinished with no result recorded; send SIGINT (or the SDK's `interrupt()`) first to end the turn cleanly. Piped stdin is capped at 10MB and exceeding it exits with a clear error and non-zero status; an unreadable stdin (disconnected pipe) is NOT an error: Claude Code prints a warning to stderr and continues with the command-line prompt (fixed in v2.1.211 on Windows). `-p` rejects `--bg`/`--background` ("--bg and --print conflict"), and also rejects `--cloud` with a task description; `--cloud <session-id>` with `-p` instead queues a message into that cloud session and exits. The "underlying Claude Code process also exits with a nonzero code" sentence lives on the Agent SDK page https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop (the path /docs/en/agent-loop returns 404) and is scoped to "When a query ends on an error result" (subtypes error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution, error_max_structured_output_retries).
verdict.evidence: VERIFIED VERBATIM on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless (fetched 2026-09-27, page title "Run Claude Code programmatically"): "Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails, so your scripts can branch on the exit status. If you pass an invalid flag, Claude Code reports the error to stderr before the run starts. When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout." Also verbatim: "Add the `-p` (or `--print`) flag to any `claude` command to run it non-interactively. Not every CLI option combines with `-p`. Claude Code rejects `--bg`, and rejects `--cloud` with a task description, with an error naming the conflict; `--cloud` with a session ID and `-p` instead queues a message into that cloud session and exits." SIGTERM section verbatim: "If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example with `kill` or from a process supervisor, Claude Code exits with code 143. Claude Code leaves the turn that was in progress unfinished and records no result for it. To end the turn instead, send SIGINT, or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()`, before you stop the process." Also: "On SIGTERM, Claude Code terminates the process tree of any Bash command that is still running. Claude Code then runs SessionEnd hooks and exits." and "set CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1" to continue an interrupted turn on resume. Stdin cap verbatim: "Piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status." Additional nuance the claim omits: "If Claude Code can't read stdin, for example because the process that started it disconnected its end, Claude Code prints a warning to stderr and continues with the prompt from the command line. Before v2.1.211, an unreadable stdin on Windows crashed the session or made it exit silently with no output." Other exit-related facts on the same page: invalid `--json-schema` exits with `Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema`; `--permission-prompts` before v2.1.259 gives "an unknown-option error"; background Bash tasks are killed ~5 s after the final result; background subagent wait ceiling 10 min via CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS; slow stream-json consumers get up to 30 s drain (v2.1.214+). CRITICAL for the Ashley design (critical=true): the persistent-agent design must treat a zero exit + auth-failure text on stdout as impossible per the docs (auth failure is both an error result AND nonzero exit), but must still parse stdout/`--output-format json` `.result`/`.subtype` because the failure text goes to stdout, not stderr; and any Slurm/supervisor teardown that sends SIGTERM (scancel default) yields exit 143 with the in-flight turn unrecorded, so a wrapper should send SIGINT first and give the SessionEnd hooks time. AGENT-LOOP sentence VERIFIED VERBATIM on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop (title "How the agent loop works"): "When a query ends on an error result: A single-shot `query()` call yields the final result message, then raises an error that includes the failure text, such as `Reached maximum number of turns`. The raise is intentional. ... The underlying Claude Code process also exits with a nonzero code. A streaming input session stays alive, and you can keep sending messages, except after a session crash, which emits a final `error_during_execution` result and exits the process." Error subtypes table: success (result field present), error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution, error_max_structured_output_retries (no result field). URL CORRECTION: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-loop returned HTTP 404; the docs index https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt lists the page only as /docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop.md. CORROBORATION from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting: Python SDK raises `ProcessError` "when the Claude Code process exits with a nonzero code" with message `Command failed with exit code 1 (exit code: 1)`; when the CLI reported an error result before exiting the SDK raises `ResultError` / "Claude Code returned an error result: <the CLI's own error report>"; TypeScript gets `Claude Code process exited with code 1. stderr: <tail>` and `Claude Code process terminated by signal <name>` for signal kills. CLI reference https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference: `--print`, `-p` = "Print response without interactive mode"; `--bg`, `--background` row states "Can't be combined with `-p`/`--print`; see the error reference"; `claude auth status` "Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not" (useful pre-flight for the Ashley extension). Error reference https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors index lists the entries `--bg and --print conflict` and `Not logged in · Please run /login` and `Invalid API key`; the detailed body of those entries could not be retrieved through the fetch tool (page truncated), so the exact conflict error string beyond the index label is unverified. No source contradicting any part of the claim was found; the claim is current as of the 2026-09-27 fetch and references Claude Code v2.1.211/2.1.214/2.1.259 behaviors that the local install (2.1.283) postdates.

findings.claim: `--output-format` accepts `text` (default), `json` (single object), `stream-json` (NDJSON events); `--json-schema` adds a `structured_output` field; `stream-json` requires `--verbose`, and `--include-partial-messages` adds `stream_event` lines.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "`text` (default): plain text output; `json`: structured JSON with result, session ID, and metadata; `stream-json`: newline-delimited JSON for real-time streaming". Example: `claude -p "Summarize this project" --output-format json | jq -r '.result'`. Streaming: `claude -p "Explain recursion" --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages`; "The last line of the stream is a `result` message". CLI ref: `--include-partial-messages` "Requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json`". Invalid schema: `Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema` and exit code 1 (v2.1.205+). Slow consumers: exit wait "capped at 30 seconds" (v2.1.214+). Extra flags: `--include-hook-events`, `--forward-subagent-text`, `--replay-user-messages`.

verdict.corrected_claim: `--output-format` (print mode only) accepts `text` (default), `json` (a single result object) and `stream-json` (newline-delimited JSON events). `--json-schema` makes the `result` object/message carry a `structured_output` field (use with `--output-format json`, or read the final `result` line of `stream-json`). With `--print`, `--output-format stream-json` is refused unless `--verbose` is also passed (exit 1, stderr `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`); `--include-partial-messages` (requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json`) adds `stream_event` lines, and the last line of the stream is a `result` message. An invalid `--json-schema` exits 1 with `Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema: <validator diagnostic>` (v2.1.205+; earlier versions silently returned unstructured text). For slow consumers the exit drain is capped at 30 seconds (v2.1.214+; ~2 s before). Related flags: `--include-hook-events` (requires `--output-format stream-json`), `--forward-subagent-text` (requires `--print` and `stream-json`; v2.1.211+), `--replay-user-messages` (only with `--input-format=stream-json` and `--output-format=stream-json`; present in the binary and changelog but not on the CLI reference page).
verdict.evidence:
CLAIM HOLDS. critical=true (the persistent grid-side Claude Code process will run `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`, and omitting `--verbose` kills it at startup).

1. Official headless page, fetched 2026-09-27 (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless), verbatim: "`text` (default): plain text output"; "`json`: structured JSON with result, session ID, and metadata"; "`stream-json`: newline-delimited JSON for real-time streaming". "To get output conforming to a specific schema, use `--output-format json` with `--json-schema` ... with the structured output in the `structured_output` field." "If the value isn't a valid JSON Schema, `claude` exits with `Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema` followed by the validator's diagnostic. ... Before v2.1.205, Claude Code silently ignored an invalid schema and returned unstructured text, and treated any schema containing `format` as invalid." "Use `--output-format stream-json` with `--verbose` and `--include-partial-messages` to receive tokens as they're generated." "The last line of the stream is a `result` message with the final response text, cost, and session metadata." "If your consumer reads the stream slowly, Claude Code waits for the queued output to drain before exiting, scaling the wait with how much is still queued, capped at 30 seconds. Before v2.1.214 the exit wait was capped at about two seconds". jq examples present exactly as claimed: `claude -p "Summarize this project" --output-format json | jq -r '.result'` and the streaming filter `select(.type == "stream_event" and .event.delta.type? == "text_delta")`. `--forward-subagent-text` / `CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT` "requires Claude Code v2.1.211 or later".

2. Official CLI reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference): `--output-format` "(options: `text`, `json`, `stream-json`)"; `--include-partial-messages` "Requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json`"; `--include-hook-events` "Requires `--output-format stream-json`" and "`SessionStart` and `Setup` hook events are always included"; `--forward-subagent-text` "Requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json` ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.211 or later"; `--verbose` row: "Emit all events in the output stream ... Requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json`". NOTE: neither docs page states the reverse rule that stream-json REQUIRES --verbose; the headless page only says "use with". `--replay-user-messages` does NOT appear on the CLI reference page at all.

3. Upstream changelog (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md, latest heading 2.1.283), grepped locally with version headings resolved: 2.1.205 "Fixed `--json-schema` silently producing unstructured output when the schema was invalid, and schemas using the `format` keyword being rejected"; 2.1.214 "Fixed stream-json output truncation at exit for slow-reading SDK/pipeline consumers; the exit drain now scales with queued bytes instead of a flat 2s cap"; 2.1.211 "Added `--forward-subagent-text` flag and `CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT` environment variable"; 1.0.109 "SDK: Added partial message streaming support via `--include-partial-messages` CLI flag"; 1.0.86 "SDK: Added `--replay-user-messages` to replay user messages back to stdout". Version numbers in the claim (2.1.205, 2.1.214) match exactly.

4. Direct test of the installed binary, 2.1.283 (Claude Code), at c:\Users\grego\.vscode\extensions\anthropic.claude-code-2.1.283-win32-x64\resources\native-binary\claude.exe, run with `--bare` and a bogus ANTHROPIC_API_KEY so no subscription credential was read and nothing billed:
 - `claude --bare -p "say hi" --output-format stream-json` (no --verbose) -> exit 1, empty stdout, stderr exactly: `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`. So the --verbose requirement is enforced at argument validation, before any network call.
 - `--output-format json --json-schema '{"type":"not-a-real-type"}'` -> exit 1, stderr exactly: `Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema: data/type must be equal to one of the allowed values, data/type must be array, data/type must match a schema in anyOf`.
 - `--help` verbatim: `--output-format <format>  Output format (only works with --print): "text" (default), "json" (single result), or "stream-json" (realtime streaming) (choices: "text", "json", "stream-json")`; `--include-hook-events ... (only works with --output-format=stream-json)`; `--include-partial-messages  Include partial message chunks as they arrive (only works with --print and --output-format=stream-json)`; `--forward-subagent-text  Forward subagent text and thinking blocks as assistant/user messages with parent_tool_use_id set (only works with --print and --output-format=stream-json)`; `--replay-user-messages  Re-emit user messages from stdin back on stdout for acknowledgment (only works with --input-format=stream-json and --output-format=stream-json)`; `--input-format <format> ... (choices: "text", "stream-json")`; `--verbose  Override verbose mode setting from config`.
 - `--output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages` with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES=0 -> 4 NDJSON lines: `system/init` (carries `session_id`, `tools`, `mcp_servers`, `model`, `permissionMode`, `slash_commands`), `system/status`, `assistant`, then last line `"type":"result"` with `session_id`, `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, `is_error`, `num_turns`, `subtype`, `result`, `api_error_status`. `--output-format json` -> exactly one JSON object on stdout with the same shape. No `stream_event` lines were observed only because the 401 aborted before any token streamed; the `stream_event` type name is confirmed by the official jq example. Without the retry override, the bogus key produced `system/api_retry` events (`attempt`, `max_retries`:10, `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status`:401, `error`:"authentication_failed") exactly as the headless page documents.
 - Side finding for the synthesizer: on the 401 failure the result object had `"subtype":"success"` together with `"is_error":true` and exit code 1; gate on `is_error`/exit status, not on `subtype`.
 - `--json-schema` combined with the default `text` output format passed argument validation (the run proceeded to the API), so it is not rejected, but there is no JSON object in which `structured_output` could appear; use `--output-format json` as the docs say.

5. Dated third-party confirmation of the --verbose error string: https://github.com/monzta1/project-handsoff/issues/129 (2026-09-18) quotes "When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose" as the exit-1 message from current Claude Code.

Not verifiable here: exact wording of the docs before 2.1.205/2.1.214; token-level `stream_event` lines could not be produced without a valid credential. Nothing in the claim was found to be outdated or wrong for 2.1.283.

findings.claim: The JSON result object schema (TypeScript `SDKResultMessage`) has a success arm with `result: string` and an error arm with `errors: string[]` and NO `result` field; both carry `session_id`, `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `num_turns`, `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `is_error`, `stop_reason`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, `uuid`.
findings.detail: Verbatim success arm: `{ type: "result"; subtype: "success"; uuid: UUID; session_id: string; duration_ms: number; duration_api_ms: number; is_error: boolean; api_error_status?: number | null; num_turns: number; result: string; stop_reason: string | null; ttft_ms?: number; ttft_stream_ms?: number; user_message_uuid?: string; user_message_uuids?: string[]; ... total_cost_usd: number; usage: NonNullableUsage; modelUsage: { [modelName: string]: ModelUsage }; permission_denials: SDKPermissionDenial[]; queued_turn_count?: number; structured_output?: unknown; deferred_tool_use?: {...}; terminal_reason?: TerminalReason; fast_mode_state?; fast_mode_disabled_reason?; origin? }`. Error arm: `subtype: "error_max_turns" | "error_during_execution" | "error_max_budget_usd" | "error_max_structured_output_retries"; uuid; session_id; duration_ms; duration_api_ms; is_error; num_turns; stop_reason; total_cost_usd; usage; modelUsage; permission_denials; queued_turn_count?; errors: string[]; startup_failure_reason?: SDKStartupFailureReason; ...`. `Usage` = `{ input_tokens; output_tokens; cache_creation_input_tokens; cache_read_input_tokens; cache_creation: {ephemeral_5m_input_tokens; ephemeral_1h_input_tokens}; server_tool_use; service_tier: "standard"|"priority"|"batch"|null; speed; inference_geo; iterations; output_tokens_details }`. `ModelUsage` = `{ inputTokens; outputTokens; thinkingTokens?; cacheReadInputTokens; cacheCreationInputTokens; webSearchRequests; costUSD; contextWindow; maxOutputTokens; canonicalModel?; provider?; costBasis?: 'list'|'managed'|'unknown' }`. `SDKPermissionDenial` = `{ tool_name; tool_use_id; tool_input }`. `SDKStartupFailureReason` includes `org_pin_api_key_conflict`, `org_verify_failed`, `managed_settings_invalid`, `gateway_signin_required`, `proxy_invalid`, `temp_dir_unusable`, `cwd_unavailable`, `shell_tool_missing`, `session_held_by_background`, `worktree_resume_refused`, `worktree_unverified`.

VERDICT ON EACH PART OF THE CLAIM: (a) success arm `result: string` — CONFIRMED in docs and .d.ts. CRITICAL DESIGN FACTS FOUND ALONGSIDE (critical=true for a laptop->grid prompt relay that parses the result JSON): (1) `startup_failure_reason` requires Agent SDK v0.3.274 or later and appears only on a zeroed `error_during_execution` result; by default Claude Code writes that result ONLY for `worktree_unverified`, `worktree_resume_refused`, and `session_held_by_background` (on `continue`). For every other known startup failure it "ends with stderr output, a non-zero exit, and no result message" unless the env var `CLAUDE_CODE_STARTUP_FAILURE_RESULTS` is set to `1`. A relay that blocks waiting for a result JSON must set that variable or also watch the exit code/stderr. (2) headless docs: "Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails"; "When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout"; SIGTERM -> exit code 143 with no result recorded for the in-progress turn; use SIGINT or `interrupt()` to end the turn first. (3) `subtype: "success"` does not imply `is_error: false`: the success arm carries `is_error: boolean` and `api_error_status?: number | null`, and the docs condition `first_content_frame_ms` on "the success arm only, when `is_error` is false". Check both `subtype` and `is_error`. (4) `usage` is "main agent loop only" and per-turn in streaming-input sessions; `modelUsage` and `total_cost_usd` are cumulative across turns and across `--resume`/`--continue` ("read the latest result rather than summing across results"); both are client-side estimates, not billing. (5) With `claude -p --output-format json` the result object is this same message; documented jq paths are `.result`, `.session_id`, `.structured_output`; `--output-format stream-json --verbose` emits it as the last line with `type: "result"`. (6) Version gates on optional fields: `first_content_frame_ms`/`first_stream_post_*` need Agent SDK v0.3.260+; `output_tokens_details` needs v0.3.228 (bundles Claude Code v2.1.228); `thinkingTokens` v0.3.257+; `canonicalModel`/`provider` Claude Code v2.1.218+; `costBasis` v2.1.246+; `fast_mode_disabled_reason` v2.1.219+. (7) `TerminalReason` full union: `blocking_limit | rapid_refill_breaker | prompt_too_long | image_error | model_error | api_error | malformed_tool_use_exhausted | aborted_streaming | aborted_tools | stop_hook_prevented | hook_stopped | tool_deferred | max_turns | background_requested | completed | budget_exhausted | structured_output_retry_exhausted | tool_deferred_unavailable | turn_setup_failed`. (8) `origin` is absent on results emitted before any user turn (startup errors) and equals `{ kind: "task-notification" }` for SDK-injected follow-up turns; filter on `origin.kind` before treating a result as the answer to a relayed prompt. (9) The .d.ts documents `result_index?` ("a gap in a stream-json sequence means a result was lost") and `queued_turn_count?` ("Absent on fatal startup results").

"All result subtypes carry `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `num_turns`, and `session_id`". "A streaming input session stays alive, and you can keep sending messages, except after a session crash, which emits a final `error_during_execution` result and exits the process." `total_cost_usd` is a "client-side estimate" from a bundled price table.

verdict.corrected_claim: Result subtype semantics (Claude Agent SDK, verified 2026-09-27): `result` text is present only on `subtype: "success"`; `is_error` is always true on the four `error_*` arms; `stop_reason` (`string | null` TS, `str | None` Python) common values are `end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `refusal`; after a Claude Code process crash the final event is an `error_during_execution` result whose `usage`, `total_cost_usd` and `modelUsage` may be zeroed and whose `stop_reason` is `null`, after which the process exits (single-shot and streaming input alike). `total_cost_usd` is a client-side estimate computed locally from a price table bundled at build time (unless a `modelPricing` settings table is in effect). [ADDENDA, not corrections — the literal claim held but is incomplete in two ways the design depends on: (1) `is_error` is NOT the complement of `subtype === "success"`: on `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, and then `result` holds the API error string (possibly empty) rather than Claude's answer, with `api_error_status` carrying the HTTP status — so a wrapper must check `subtype === "success" && is_error === false` before treating `result` as the answer. (2) Not every failure yields a result message: the SDK docs' own code comments say "connection or process failures yield no result message", and known startup failures write an `error_during_execution` result (with `startup_failure_reason`, zeroed totals, Agent SDK v0.3.274+) only for a subset unless `CLAUDE_CODE_STARTUP_FAILURE_RESULTS=1` is set; the rest "end with stderr output, a non-zero exit, and no result message". Also `stop_reason` can be `"tool_deferred"` when a `PreToolUse` hook returns `permissionDecision: "defer"`.]

VERDICT: not refuted. Every sentence of the claim and the DETAIL block was found verbatim on the official page today. Two omissions were found on the reference pages that a synthesizer should carry forward; they are listed as addenda, not as refutations.

1. Table — CONFIRMED verbatim at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop (section "Handle the result"): `success` "Claude finished the task normally" / Yes; `error_max_turns` "Hit the `maxTurns` limit before finishing" / No; `error_max_budget_usd` "Hit the `maxBudgetUsd` limit before finishing" / No; `error_during_execution` "An error interrupted the loop (for example, a cancelled request)" / No; `error_max_structured_output_retries` "No valid structured output was produced within the configured retry limit: every attempt failed validation, or a model fallback retracted the completed output with no successful retry" / No. Followed by: "The `result` field holds the final text output and is only present on the `success` variant, so always check the subtype before reading it."

2. Common fields — CONFIRMED verbatim: "All result subtypes carry `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `num_turns`, and `session_id` so you can track cost and resume even after errors." Followed by the bullet: "After a session crash, the final result is an `error_during_execution` whose cost fields may be zeroed and whose `stop_reason` is `null`, and the process exits after emitting it."

3. Streaming-session sentence — CONFIRMED verbatim in the Note: "A streaming input session stays alive, and you can keep sending messages, except after a session crash, which emits a final `error_during_execution` result and exits the process." Same Note: "A single-shot `query()` call yields the final result message, then raises an error that includes the failure text, such as `Reached maximum number of turns`. The raise is intentional. ... The underlying Claude Code process also exits with a nonzero code."

4. stop_reason — CONFIRMED verbatim: "The result also includes a `stop_reason` field (`string | null` in TypeScript, `str | None` in Python) indicating why the model stopped generating on its final turn. Common values are `end_turn` (model finished normally), `max_tokens` (hit the output token limit), and `refusal` (the model declined the request). On error results that the loop produced, `stop_reason` carries the value from the last assistant response before the loop ended; the result Claude Code synthesizes after a session crash carries `null`." Note: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/stop-reasons now returns HTTP 307 to https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop#handle-the-result — the standalone stop-reasons page is gone; cite agent-loop.

5. Client-side estimate — CONFIRMED verbatim at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking (Warning box): "The `total_cost_usd` and `costUSD` fields are client-side estimates, not authoritative billing data. The SDK computes them locally from a price table bundled at build time, unless a [`modelPricing`] table is in effect. They can drift from what you are actually billed when: pricing changes; the installed SDK version does not recognize a model; billing rules apply that the client cannot model." Same page, "Recover totals after a session crash": "When the Claude Code process crashes, it emits a final `error_during_execution` result and exits, in single-shot and streaming input mode alike. That result may carry zeroed `usage`, `total_cost_usd`, and `modelUsage`, so recover the call's totals from what arrived before it." Also: "`error_during_execution` after a session crash: every cost field may be zeroed." And "Before v2.1.277, a session that you resumed through the SDK or `claude -p` started its totals at zero".

6. is_error on error arms — CONFIRMED but INCOMPLETE. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python.md (ResultMessage): "`is_error`: `True` when the conversation ended in an error state. Always `True` on the `error_*` subtypes. On `subtype=\"success\"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error." and "`result`: text of the final assistant message on `subtype=\"success\"`, or `None` on the `error_*` subtypes. When `subtype=\"success\"` and `is_error=True`, this holds the API error string if one is available but can be empty, so check `api_error_status` and the preceding `AssistantMessage` content for detail." and "`api_error_status`: the HTTP status code of the terminating API error. `None` when the turn ended without one. Populated only on `subtype=\"success\"`." The TypeScript union at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript.md (SDKResultMessage) agrees: the `success` arm has `is_error: boolean; api_error_status?: number | null; result: string; stop_reason: string | null;` and the error arm has `subtype: "error_max_turns" | "error_during_execution" | "error_max_budget_usd" | "error_max_structured_output_retries"; is_error: boolean; stop_reason: string | null; errors: string[]; startup_failure_reason?: SDKStartupFailureReason;` with no `result` field. Per-field note: "`first_content_frame_ms` ... Present on the success arm only, when `is_error` is false." Design consequence: gate on `subtype === "success" && !is_error` before showing `result` to a student.

7. Crash always emits a result? — PARTIALLY QUALIFIED. All three pages' code comments say: "connection or process failures yield no result message." TypeScript reference, `startup_failure_reason`: "Claude Code sets it on the `error_during_execution` result it writes before exiting on a known startup failure. That result carries zeroed totals, and its `errors` array carries the same text as stderr. ... Requires Agent SDK v0.3.274 or later. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_STARTUP_FAILURE_RESULTS` to `1` in `env` to receive this result for every `SDKStartupFailureReason` value. Without that variable, Claude Code writes the result only for these failures, and the rest end with stderr output, a non-zero exit, and no result message". `SDKStartupFailureReason` values include `org_pin_api_key_conflict`, `org_verify_failed`, `org_pin_mismatch`, `managed_settings_invalid`, `remote_settings_required_unavailable`, `gateway_signin_required`, `gateway_access_denied`, `proxy_invalid`, `temp_dir_unusable`, `worktree_unverified`, `worktree_resume_refused`, `session_held_by_background`. Also `queued_turn_count`: "Absent: the final result that Claude Code emits after a crash or fatal startup error omits the field, and may carry zeroed totals." Design consequence: the relay on the Slurm node must also watch process exit code / stderr, not only the result stream; a SIGKILL (e.g. Slurm wall-time or OOM kill) cannot emit any result.

8. Extra stop_reason value — TypeScript reference: "When a `PreToolUse` hook returns `permissionDecision: \"defer\"`, the result has `stop_reason: \"tool_deferred\"` and `deferred_tool_use` carries the pending tool's `id`, `name`, and `input`." Python reference also lists `terminal_reason` (`"completed"`, `"max_turns"`, `"api_error"`, `"aborted_streaming"`, `"aborted_tools"`, ...) as a separate loop-exit field, `None` "on synthesized error results emitted when the session fails fatally".

9. Sandbox failure path (relevant to a Singularity container): TypeScript reference: "When `enabled` is `true` and the sandbox can't start, `query()` reports a `result` message with `subtype: \"error_during_execution\"` and the reason in `errors`."

findings.claim: `--input-format stream-json` makes `claude -p` a long-lived bidirectional process: stdin takes newline-delimited JSON user messages, each becomes a new turn with its own `result` event, and closing stdin ends the process. Each message must be one newline-terminated JSON line (256M-character line budget).
findings.detail: CLI ref: `--input-format` "Specify input format for print mode (options: `text`, `stream-json`)" example `claude -p --output-format json --input-format stream-json`. Errors page (v2.1.257+): `Error: stream-json input carried over 256M characters with no newline. Each stream-json message must be a single newline-terminated JSON line: either the producer is not newline-terminating its messages, or one message exceeded this budget.` (exit code 1). Cost-tracking page: "In streaming input mode, one `query()` call carries multiple user turns and each turn emits its own result message"; `usage` covers only that turn, `total_cost_usd`/`modelUsage` are running totals; `/clear`, `/reset`, `/new` reset totals and give a new `session_id`. CLI ref on `--max-turns`: "With `--input-format stream-json`, a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit". Headless: background Bash tasks are killed "about five seconds after Claude has returned its final result and stdin has closed".

verdict.corrected_claim: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose` runs Claude Code as a long-lived process: stdin takes newline-delimited JSON user messages (one `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}}` object per line), each message becomes a new turn that emits its own `result` event (all turns share one `session_id` until the app sends `/clear`, `/reset` or `/new`, which reset the running `total_cost_usd`/`modelUsage` totals and issue a new `session_id`), the process stays alive while stdin is open and exits when stdin reaches EOF (exit 0 after no/successful turns; exit 1 when the last result carried `is_error: true`). The flag pairing is mandatory, and the CLI reference's example `claude -p --output-format json --input-format stream-json` does NOT run on 2.1.283: `--input-format stream-json` with `--output-format json` or `text` exits 1 at startup with `Error: --input-format=stream-json requires output-format=stream-json.`, and `--output-format stream-json` in print mode without `--verbose` exits 1 with `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`. Each message must be one newline-terminated JSON line: a non-JSON line exits 1 with `Error parsing streaming input line (type=unknown, N chars): SyntaxError`, and more than 268,435,456 characters with no newline exits 1 with `Error: stream-json input carried over 256M characters with no newline. Each stream-json message must be a single newline-terminated JSON line: either the producer is not newline-terminating its messages, or one message exceeded this budget.` on stderr (budget enforced since v2.1.257; earlier versions buffered without limit until the process crashed). `--max-turns` applies per turn: a queued message starts a new turn with its own limit. Background Bash tasks started during the run are killed about five seconds after the final result has been returned and stdin has closed.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core mechanism CONFIRMED (long-lived process, NDJSON stdin, one result per message, EOF ends process, 256M budget/v2.1.257). REFUTED on one design-critical point: the CLI-reference example the claim cites (`claude -p --output-format json --input-format stream-json`) is rejected by Claude Code 2.1.283; stream-json input REQUIRES `--output-format stream-json`, which in print mode REQUIRES `--verbose`. Marked critical=true where noted.

verdict.corrected_claim: Session flags (Claude Code CLI, current docs as of 2026-09-27, latest release 2.1.283): `--continue`/`-c` loads the most recent conversation in the current directory; interactively it skips sessions created with `claude -p` or the Agent SDK and sessions whose first prompt was `/loop`, but `claude -p --continue` includes `-p`, SDK and `/loop` sessions. `--resume`/`-r` accepts a session ID, a session name, or the absolute path to a session's `.jsonl` transcript file; with no argument it opens an interactive picker. Resuming by NAME resumes directly only on an exact single match — an ambiguous name opens the session picker with the name pre-filled as a search term (`claude --resume <name>`) or reports an error (`/resume <name>`); the docs do NOT say "the most recent session with that name is resumed". `--session-id <UUID>` sets the session ID and must be a valid UUID; it cannot be combined with `--resume`/`--continue` unless `--fork-session` is also passed. `--fork-session` creates a new session ID when resuming (use with `--resume` or `--continue`). `--no-session-persistence` is print-mode only (`CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1` does the same in any mode). `--replay-user-messages` re-emits stdin user messages on stdout and REQUIRES `--input-format stream-json` and `--output-format stream-json` (SDK flag, added 1.0.86). `claude -p --resume <id>` works from any directory on the same machine (searches the current project and its worktrees, then every other project) from v2.1.223; the cross-project lookup resolves only when exactly one other project holds a transcript with that ID, otherwise `No conversation found with session ID: <session-id>` and exit code 1. Resumed `-p` runs report the whole conversation's `total_cost_usd` from v2.1.277. `-p --resume`/`-p --continue` start in the permission mode a fresh `-p` run would, except a session that ended in plan mode resumes in plan mode (v2.1.246+) only if `--permission-prompt-tool` is passed without `--permission-prompts none`, no `--permission-mode`/`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, no `--fork-session`, and not via channels. `--mcp-config`, `--settings`, `--plugin-dir`, `--fallback-model`, `--add-dir` and mid-session `/add-dir` directories are NOT restored and must be passed again. `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1` makes a resume continue an interrupted turn (set `0` to disable, honoured from v2.1.221; bounded by `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS`, v2.1.211+; continuation text from `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT`).

findings.claim: Transcripts are stored at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`, where `<project>` is the working-directory path with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by `-` (truncated to 200 chars + hash when longer); `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates the whole tree; `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` (v2.1.234+) pins the project directory name; retention is `cleanupPeriodDays` (default 30, minimum 1).
findings.detail: Verbatim: "By default, Claude Code stores transcripts as JSONL at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`, where `<project>` is your working directory path with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-`. For a working directory whose converted name exceeds 200 characters, Claude Code truncates the name to 200 characters and appends a hash of the full path". "The entry format is internal to Claude Code and changes between versions, so scripts that parse these files directly can break on any release." Example: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/srv/tenant-a CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME=work claude` writes `/srv/tenant-a/projects/work/` (name 1-64 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-], must be set in the shell env, not settings `env`). Settings-reference: `cleanupPeriodDays` Default `30`, "Setting `0` fails validation, so pick a large value such as `3650`". `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1` suppresses transcript writes in all modes. Auto memory at `projects/<project>/memory/` is never swept. Subagent transcripts: `projects/<project>/<session>/subagents/`; large tool outputs: `projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/`.

verdict.corrected_claim: Transcripts are stored at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl` (on Windows `~/.claude` = `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`), where `<project>` is the working-directory path with every character other than letters and digits replaced by `-` (e.g. `-Users-you-my-project`); when the converted name exceeds 200 characters it is truncated to 200 and a hash of the full path appended (cross-project collision on such paths was a bug fixed in 2.1.224). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates settings, session history, plugins AND `.credentials.json` (Linux; keyed Keychain entry on macOS); it may be set in the shell, user settings or managed settings but is ignored in project/local settings. `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` (v2.1.234+) pins the `projects/<name>/` directory for both transcripts and auto memory, but only when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is also set, only when the value is 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-] (not a Windows device name), and only from the shell environment that starts `claude` (a settings-file `env` block cannot set it). Retention is `cleanupPeriodDays` (whole number, default 30, minimum 1; `0` fails validation since 2.1.89 — before that it silently disabled persistence; docs suggest `3650` for long retention); the sweep covers `<session>.jsonl`, `.orphaned-*`/`.superseded-*` variants, `<session>/subagents/` and `<session>/tool-results/`, and is skipped under `claude -p --bare` or paused when the retention period cannot be safely determined. Auto memory at `projects/<project>/memory/` is exempt from the sweep on v2.1.228+ (the directory is removed only if empty for the whole retention period; before 2.1.228 the sweep could delete files inside it); note the memory `<project>` is keyed to the git repository root (worktrees/subdirectories share one), whereas the transcript `<project>` is the exact working directory, so the two can differ unless pinned with `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME`. `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1` skips writing prompt history and transcripts in all modes (such sessions do not appear in `--resume`, `--continue` or up-arrow history); `--no-session-persistence` does the same for a single `claude -p` run. The JSONL entry format is internal and changes between versions; use `/export`, hook `transcript_path`, or `claude -p --resume <id> --output-format json` instead of parsing.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim HELD on every stated fact; additions below are precision caveats, not contradictions. Checked 2026-09-27 against live official pages (fetched HTML via WebFetch and raw .md via curl) plus the anthropics/claude-code CHANGELOG (latest heading 2.1.283, matching the installed extension version).

[critical=true] PATH + NAMING — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions#where-transcripts-are-stored, verbatim: "By default, Claude Code stores transcripts as JSONL at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`, where `<project>` is your working directory path with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-`. For a working directory whose converted name exceeds 200 characters, Claude Code truncates the name to 200 characters and appends a hash of the full path, so the directory name stays within filesystem limits." Corroborated at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory: "`<project>` is your working directory path with every character other than letters and digits replaced by `-`, such as `-Users-you-my-project`." Changelog ## 2.1.224: "Fixed long (>200 char) project paths resolving to another project's session directory under a shared sanitized prefix; session list, rename, fork, delete and `/resume` no longer cross projects" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md). Format-instability sentence confirmed verbatim: "The entry format is internal to Claude Code and changes between versions, so scripts that parse these files directly can break on any release."

[critical=true] CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars row: "Override the configuration directory (default: `~/.claude`). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path. ... Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings." Credentials also follow it — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication: "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." and "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead". (Design note: a persistent grid Claude Code in Singularity must bind a stable CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR on Panasas/CephFS, not /tmp, or the Pro/Max login and transcripts vanish with the sweep.) Also: `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1` on v2.1.251+ "removes Claude Code's own configuration-store pointer variables (such as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`)" from Bash/hook/MCP children. Windows: settings page says "On Windows, `~/.claude` means `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings).

[critical=true] CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME — sessions page "Name the project directory yourself": "Requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later." Example verbatim: "`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/srv/tenant-a CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME=work claude`" -> "writes the session's transcripts to `/srv/tenant-a/projects/work/` and its auto memory to `/srv/tenant-a/projects/work/memory/`, whatever the working directory is." Three rules verbatim: "Claude Code ignores `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset."; "Use 1-64 letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores: don't use a Windows device name such as `con`. Claude Code ignores any other value and uses the derived name."; "Set it in the shell environment that starts `claude`: Claude Code reads it once at startup from that environment, so an `env` block in a settings file can't set it." env-vars row repeats: "reads it only from the environment you start `claude` from, never from a settings file `env` block ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later". Changelog ## 2.1.234: "Added the optional `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` environment variable: hosts that give each session its own config directory can choose a short name for the per-project transcript directory". Memory page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) confirms it also pins auto memory, v2.1.234+.

[critical=true] RETENTION — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#cleanupperioddays verbatim: "* **Type**: number of days, a whole number, minimum `1`" / "* **Default**: `30`" / "Setting `0` fails validation, so pick a large value such as `3650` for long retention. To stop Claude Code from writing transcripts at all, see Plaintext storage." claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically: "The default is 30 days and the minimum is 1; setting `0` fails with a validation error." Changelog ## 2.1.89: "Changed `cleanupPeriodDays: 0` in settings.json to be rejected with a validation error — it previously silently disabled transcript persistence"; ## 0.2.117: "Introduced settings.cleanupPeriodDays"; ## 2.1.83: "Fixed tool result files never being cleaned up, ignoring the `cleanupPeriodDays` setting". Sweep-skip cases verbatim (claude-directory): "**Bare mode**: when you run `claude -p` with `--bare`, Claude Code doesn't run the sweep in that session." and "**Paused sweep**: if Claude Code can't safely determine the retention period, it pauses the retention cleanup sweep". Precedence: `cleanupPeriodDays` "Takes the value from the highest source that sets it" (managed > CLI --settings > project local > project > user).

[critical=false] SUBAGENTS / TOOL-RESULTS — claude-directory table verbatim: "`projects/<project>/<session>/subagents/` | Subagent conversation transcripts, removed with the parent session transcript when it ages out" and "`projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/` | Large tool outputs spilled to separate files, and full-size copies of images that MCP tools return". Also swept: "`projects/<project>/<session>.orphaned-<timestamp>-<suffix>.jsonl`, `projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl.superseded-<timestamp>`". Note the sub-agents page itself (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) does NOT document these paths; claude-directory is the source.

[critical=false] AUTO MEMORY "never swept" — holds with two caveats. claude-directory verbatim: "**Auto memory**: the sweep doesn't delete the memory files in a project's auto memory directory, `projects/<project>/memory/`. Claude Code removes that directory only if it has been empty for the whole retention period. Before v2.1.228, the sweep treated folders inside the memory directory as session data and could delete old files beneath it." Changelog ## 2.1.228: "Fixed session cleanup deleting contents inside a project's memory folder". Memory page: "Claude Code deletes old session transcripts after the `cleanupPeriodDays` retention period, but excludes the memory files in the memory directory from that retention sweep." SUBTLETY the claim omits (memory page verbatim): "Each project gets its own memory directory at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. The `<project>` path is derived from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories within the same repo share one auto memory directory. Outside a git repo, the project root is used instead." — i.e. memory `<project>` = git root, transcript `<project>` = cwd; they differ when launching from a repo subdirectory.

[critical=true] SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY — sessions table row: "Suppress transcript writes in all modes | `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` | Environment variable". env-vars row verbatim: "Set to `1` to skip writing prompt history and session transcripts to disk. Sessions started with this variable set do not appear in `--resume`, `--continue`, or up-arrow history. Useful for ephemeral scripted sessions". Single-run variant: "Suppress writes for one non-interactive run | `--no-session-persistence` | CLI flag with `claude -p`".

[critical=false] Script-safe alternatives (sessions#access-conversations-from-scripts): hooks/statusline receive `transcript_path`; `claude -p --resume <session-id> --output-format json "..." | jq -r '.result'`; `claude --resume <transcript-path>` accepts an absolute .jsonl path; `claude --resume <session-id>` searches every project on the machine since v2.1.223. Deletion: `claude project purge`; `claude rm <id>` on a background session leaves the transcript on disk.

Version context: installed VS Code extension 2.1.283 = latest changelog heading, so all "requires vX" thresholds above (2.1.83, 2.1.89, 2.1.224, 2.1.228, 2.1.234, 2.1.248, 2.1.251) are satisfied. findings.claim: Anthropic explicitly does not recommend sharing `~/.claude` across machines or network filesystems; `.credentials.json` lives there (mode 0600 on Linux) and `~/.claude.json` holds `oauthAccount`, `hasCompletedOnboarding`, `projects[].hasTrustDialogAccepted`.
findings.detail: claude-directory page: "`~/.claude` is not recommended for sharing across machines or network filesystems. Session transcripts, OAuth tokens, and application state are machine-specific." Kept indefinitely: `history.jsonl`, `stats-cache.json`, `.credentials.json` (deleted on logout), `downloads/`. `claude project purge [path] [--dry-run]` removes a project's directory under `projects/`. Authentication page: "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`"; with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set the file lives under that directory. Trust for `-p` in an untrusted folder: set `projects["<path>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted` to `true` in `~/.claude.json`.

verdict.corrected_claim: Anthropic's Claude Code docs do NOT contain any statement recommending against sharing `~/.claude` across machines or network filesystems; the sentence "`~/.claude` is not recommended for sharing across machines or network filesystems. Session transcripts, OAuth tokens, and application state are machine-specific." does not appear on the claude-directory page or any other official page checked on 2026-09-27. What the docs do say: on Linux credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`; with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set, `.credentials.json` moves under that directory (default `~/.claude`; documented use is "running multiple accounts side by side"); `.credentials.json` is managed through `/login` and `/logout` and is listed under "Keep these state files" (not in the "Kept until you delete them" table, which lists `history.jsonl`, `stats-cache.json`, `remote-settings.json`, `cache/changelog.md`, `policy-limits.json`; the two files deleted on logout in that table are `remote-settings.json` and `policy-limits.json`); no `downloads/` directory is documented. `claude project purge [path]` deletes a project's transcripts and auto memory under `projects/`, per-session `tasks/`/`debug/`/`file-history/` entries, matching `history.jsonl` lines AND the project's entry in `~/.claude.json` (which holds its trust decision); flags are `--dry-run`, `-y`/`--yes`, `-i`/`--interactive`, `--all`. `~/.claude.json` is documented as holding "theme, OAuth session, per-project trust decisions, your personal MCP servers, and UI toggles"; the only documented per-project trust key is `projects["<path>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted` (set to `true`, where `<path>` is the git repository root, or the folder itself outside a repository) — needed for `-p`/SDK runs to apply a project's `permissions.allow`/`additionalDirectories`, since `-p` never shows the trust dialog. The field names `oauthAccount` and `hasCompletedOnboarding` are not documented anywhere in the official docs and must be treated as undocumented internal state (they exist in practice but Anthropic gives no contract for them). The closest documented machine-locality statements are: "Auto memory is machine-local ... Files are not shared across machines or cloud environments" (memory page) and "Parallel sessions on one machine share a saved login and coordinate its renewal so that only one process refreshes the token at a time" (troubleshoot-install page).

findings.claim: `--permission-mode` accepts `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, and `manual` (alias of default, v2.1.200+); a `-p` run starts in `default` (Manual) on every plan unless a flag or `permissions.defaultMode` says otherwise.
findings.detail: CLI ref: "Accepts `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, or `manual` as an alias for `default` ... Overrides `defaultMode` from settings files ... For `-p`, that's `default` when nothing is configured". Headless: "For `-p`, the built-in starting permission mode is Manual on every plan". `dontAsk`: "Claude Code denies every call that would otherwise prompt"; reads in working dirs and the read-only command set still run; `AskUserQuestion` denied even if allowed. `acceptEdits`: writes files and auto-approves `mkdir`, `touch`, `mv`, `cp`; other shell commands still need `--allowedTools` or `permissions.allow`. `auto`: classifier reviews actions; in `-p` without `--permission-prompt-tool`, repeated blocks do not stop the run. Settings key `permissions.defaultMode`: `auto` and `bypassPermissions` "don't take effect from project or local settings, so set them in `~/.claude/settings.json`" (v2.1.257+). SDK `PermissionMode` union: `"default" | "acceptEdits" | "bypassPermissions" | "plan" | "dontAsk" | "auto"`.

The `manual` alias selects the permission mode the UI labels Manual and requires Claude Code v2.1.200 or later; `claude --help` lists it in place of `default`, and both values work. Overrides `defaultMode` from settings files. Without this flag or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, a new session starts in the permission mode described in [which permission mode a session starts in]. findings.claim: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (== `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) is refused when running as root or under sudo on Linux/macOS with a fixed error string; the check is skipped inside a recognized sandbox; `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` makes Claude Code reject the flag; in `-p` no acceptance dialog is shown.
findings.detail: Verbatim error: `--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons`. "The check is skipped automatically inside a recognized sandbox. To run autonomously in a container, use the dev container configuration, which runs Claude Code as a non-root user." "In non-interactive mode no dialog is shown, and a background session started with `--bg` is refused until you've accepted the dialog in an interactive session." Refused with `--restricted` (v2.1.248+). Common-setups table: "Run fully unattended inside a container | `claude -p "<prompt>" --dangerously-skip-permissions` | Required: a container, VM, or the sandbox runtime; on Linux and macOS, run it as a non-root user". Env var `IS_SANDBOX`: "Set to `1` if running in a sandbox environment". `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` adds the mode to the cycle without starting in it. Deny rules still apply in bypassPermissions.

verdict.corrected_claim: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is equivalent to `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. On Linux and macOS, Claude Code (verified in the shipped v2.1.283 binary) exits with code 1 and prints exactly `--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons` when `process.getuid() === 0` AND neither `IS_SANDBOX` is set to the exact string `"1"` nor `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP` is set; the same check also fires for `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` (the predicate tests `permissionMode==="bypassPermissions" || allowBypass===true`). "Recognized sandbox" in the docs means exactly those two env vars; presence of `/.dockerenv` does NOT skip the check, so a root Docker container is still refused. `IS_SANDBOX` is NOT documented anywhere in the official Claude Code docs (zero hits in the current 10.2 MB llms-full.txt corpus and in archived env-vars/settings pages from 2025-09-02, 2026-03-14, 2026-04-27); the quoted description "Set to `1` if running in a sandbox environment" does not appear on the cited page and should be treated as an undocumented escape hatch known only from the binary and GitHub issue #58150. `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` (scope: any settings file, typically managed) makes Claude Code print `Bypass permissions mode was disabled by settings` to stderr and CONTINUE with the flag stripped (permissionMode reset to the normal starting mode, allowBypass cleared) rather than exiting; docs phrase this as "rejects the flag". In `-p` no acceptance dialog is shown; a `--bg` session is refused with `--bg with bypassPermissions requires accepting the disclaimer first. Run \`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions\` once interactively.` unless the dialog was accepted (or `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true` is set in user/local/managed settings, which is the key Claude Code writes on acceptance); `--bg` cannot be combined with `-p` (`--bg and --print conflict`). `--restricted` (v2.1.248+) refuses bypassPermissions. Deny rules block in every mode including bypassPermissions; allow rules have no effect there. Common-setups row is verbatim correct and adds: "In this `-p` run, the few calls that would still prompt are denied instead." For a Singularity/Apptainer container on the grid the root check is moot because the container runs as the invoking user (uid preserved) unless `--fakeroot` is used, in which case uid appears as 0 and the check fires.

Claude Code then rejects the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag, and ignores an agent definition's `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` ... Scope: Any file. Typically set in managed settings ... Type: the string `"disable"` ... Per-session overrides: this key takes precedence over `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which Claude Code rejects while the key is set ... Before v2.1.223, Claude Code applied the frontmatter permission mode even with bypass disabled." "### `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt` Skip the confirmation dialog Claude Code shows before a session enters `bypassPermissions` mode, whether from `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or from `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"`. Claude Code writes `true` here in your user settings when you accept that dialog once. Scope: User, local, or managed. An untrusted repository can't skip the dialog for you." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings: "`permissions.defaultMode` values `auto` and `bypassPermissions` don't take effect from project or local settings; set them in user or managed settings instead ... DESIGN RELEVANCE (Ashley / grid, critical=true): Apptainer user docs https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/security.html: "To provide security in these environments a container needs to run as the user who starts it on the system." and "In non-suid mode all operations run as the user who starts the apptainer program." So inside `singularity exec`/`apptainer exec` on the grid `process.getuid()` is the student's uid, not 0, and the root check never fires; no `IS_SANDBOX=1` is needed. Do NOT launch with `--fakeroot`: uid then maps to 0 and the check fires (workaround would be `IS_SANDBOX=1`, undocumented). Recommended persistent-agent launch: `claude -p ... --dangerously-skip-permissions` (no dialog; unresolvable prompts are denied) or, if running interactive `claude` under tmux inside the Slurm job, pre-seed `~/.claude/settings.json` with `"skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true` (or run once interactively) so the disclaimer cannot block an unattended start; do not use `--bg` from a script (refused until acceptance; also conflicts with `-p`). If WSU later deploys managed settings with `disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"`, the flag is silently stripped (stderr message only) and a `-p` job will run in `default` mode where permission-needing calls are denied — the extension should detect the string `Bypass permissions mode was disabled by settings` on stderr.

findings.claim: `--allowedTools`/`--allowed-tools` and `--disallowedTools`/`--disallowed-tools` take permission-rule syntax: `Bash(git diff *)` (trailing space+`*` = prefix match; `:*` suffix equivalent), bare tool names, `Read(//abs/path)`, `Read(~/x)`, `Edit(/rel-to-settings-source)`, `WebFetch(domain:host)`, `mcp__server__tool`; a bare deny name removes the tool from context, `"*"` removes every tool, `"mcp__*"` every MCP tool; `--tools` restricts which tools exist at all.
findings.detail: Headless: `--allowedTools "Bash(git diff *),Bash(git log *),Bash(git status *),Bash(git commit *)"`; "The space before `*` is important: without it, `Bash(git diff*)` would also match `git diff-index`." Permissions page: `Bash(*)` == `Bash`; `Bash(ls *)` matches `ls` and `ls -la` but not `lsof`; `Bash(ls:*)` same as `Bash(ls *)`; compound commands split on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `|&`, `&`, newlines and each subcommand must match; wrappers `timeout`, `time`, `nice`, `nohup`, `stdbuf`, `command`, `builtin`, `noglob`, bare `xargs` are stripped; `/usr/bin/curl` and `sh -c 'curl ...'` do NOT match `Bash(curl *)`. Path rules: `//path` absolute, `~/path` home, `/path` relative to settings source, `path` relative to cwd; only `Read(...)`/`Edit(...)` are consulted (rules on Write/Glob are ignored with a startup warning, v2.1.210+). `mcp__` rules with parentheses are skipped when loaded from settings files (use `--disallowedTools`). Allow-rule globs only after literal `mcp__<server>__` prefix. CLI ref `--disallowedTools`: "`"Edit"` removes Edit, `"*"` removes every tool, and `"mcp__*"` removes every MCP tool. A scoped rule such as `Bash(rm *)` leaves the tool available and denies only calls that match". `--tools`: "Explicitly allow only these tools (deny all others)".

verdict.corrected_claim: `--allowedTools`/`--allowed-tools` and `--disallowedTools`/`--disallowed-tools` take permission-rule syntax: `Bash(git diff *)` (trailing space+`*` = prefix match that also matches the bare command; `:*` suffix is equivalent but only recognised at the END of a pattern), bare tool names (`Bash(*)` == `Bash`), `Read(//abs/path)`, `Read(~/x)`, `Edit(/rel-to-settings-source)`, `Read(path)`/`Read(./path)` relative to cwd, `WebFetch(domain:host)`, `mcp__server`, `mcp__server__tool`, `mcp__server__*`. A bare deny name removes the tool from Claude's context; `"*"` removes every tool and `"mcp__*"` every MCP tool (deny/ask only; `EndConversation` cannot be removed while any other tool remains). `--tools` restricts which BUILT-IN tools exist: `""` disables all built-ins, `"default"` = the default set (which on macOS/Linux/WSL leaves out `Glob` and `Grep`), or a list like `"Bash,Edit,Read"`; it does NOT affect MCP tools — to remove those use `--disallowedTools "mcp__*"`. The phrase "Explicitly allow only these tools (deny all others)" is no longer the documented wording. Nuances: only `Read(...)`/`Edit(...)` path rules are consulted; a path rule on `Write`, `NotebookEdit`, `Glob` or `MultiEdit` is accepted but never consulted and warns at startup (v2.1.210+), EXCEPT a `Glob` rule passed via `--allowedTools` (no warning), and a bare tool-name deny such as `Write` still works at the tool level. `mcp__` rules WITH parentheses are skipped when loaded from settings files (listed in the invalid-settings dialog and `claude doctor`); pass them with `--disallowedTools` instead. Allow-rule tool-name globs work only after a literal `mcp__<server>__` prefix; unanchored allow globs (`"*"`, `"B*"`, `"mcp__*"`) are skipped with a warning. Compound commands split on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `|&`, `&`, newlines and every subcommand must match an allow rule; a dangling `&&`/`||` (e.g. `npm test &&`) makes the command unparseable so no allow rule approves it. Wrappers stripped before matching: `timeout`, `time`, `nice`, `nohup`, `stdbuf`, `command`, `builtin`, `noglob`, and bare `xargs` (not `xargs -n1 ...`, not `command -v`, not `nocorrect`). `/usr/bin/curl ...` and `sh -c 'curl ...'` do NOT match `Bash(curl *)`; `watch`/`setsid`/`ionice`/`flock` and `find -exec`/`-delete` cannot be prefix-approved. A managed-settings deny cannot be overridden by `--allowedTools`.

As a deny rule, both forms remove the tool from Claude's context."; table row "`Bash(ls *)` | `ls -la`, `ls` | `lsof`" and "`Bash(ls*)` | `ls -la`, `lsof`"; "The `:*` suffix is an equivalent way to write a trailing wildcard, so `Bash(ls:*)` matches the same commands as `Bash(ls *)`." and "The `:*` form is only recognized at the end of a pattern. In a pattern like `Bash(git:* push)`, the colon is treated as a literal character"; "The recognized command separators are `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `|&`, `&`, and newlines. A rule must match each subcommand independently."; "When `&&` or `||` has nothing after it, such as in `npm test &&`, Claude Code treats the command as unparseable"; "The stripped wrappers are `timeout`, `time`, `nice`, `nohup`, and `stdbuf`, plus the shell builtins `command` and `builtin`, and zsh's `noglob`... Two related forms aren't stripped: the query form `command -v`... and zsh's `nocorrect`."; "Bare `xargs` is also stripped... an invocation like `xargs -n1 grep pattern` is matched as an `xargs` command"; "Exec wrappers such as `watch`, `setsid`, `ionice`, and `flock` can't be auto-approved by a prefix rule... The same applies to `find` with `-exec` or `-delete`"; table row "`Bash(curl *)` | `curl https://example.com` | `/usr/bin/curl https://example.com`, `sh -c 'curl https://example.com'`" (Doesn't match column); path table "`//path` Absolute path from filesystem root", "`~/path` Path from home directory", "`/path` Path relative to the settings source", "`path` or `./path` Path relative to current directory"; "Claude Code checks file permissions against `Edit(path)` and `Read(path)` rules only. If you write a path rule for `Write`, `NotebookEdit`, `Glob`, or the legacy `MultiEdit` tool instead, Claude Code accepts the rule but never consults it, and warns at startup, except for a `Glob` rule passed in `--allowedTools`... Claude Code doesn't warn about a tool-name rule with no path, such as a deny rule for `Write`; it matches that rule at the tool level everywhere. Requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later."; "`WebFetch(domain:example.com)` Matches fetch requests to example.com"; "To match a parameter on an MCP tool, pass a deny rule with `--disallowedTools`. When Claude Code loads a settings file, it skips any `mcp__` rule that has parentheses. A scoped rule like `Bash(rm *)` leaves the tool available and blocks matching calls"; "a managed settings deny can't be overridden by `--allowedTools`, and `--disallowedTools` can add restrictions beyond what managed settings define." (2) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless — verified verbatim: `--allowedTools "Bash(git diff *),Bash(git log *),Bash(git status *),Bash(git commit *)"` and "The trailing ` *` enables prefix matching, so `Bash(git diff *)` allows any command starting with `git diff`. The space before `*` is important: without it, `Bash(git diff*)` would also match `git diff-index`." (3) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (and its .md rendering, 126,033 bytes, fetched via curl because WebFetch truncated before the row) — `--disallowedTools`, `--disallowed-tools` row verbatim: "Deny rules.
