findings.claim: `--permission-prompts none` (v2.1.259+) stops a `-p` run from waiting on any permission host; anything that would prompt is denied, `AskUserQuestion` is removed, and denials are reported as `permission_denied` system events and in `permission_denials`; `--permission-prompt-tool <mcp_tool>` delegates prompts to an MCP tool (exit 1 if that tool is missing at first approval).
findings.detail: Headless: "Pass `--permission-prompts none` when nobody is available to answer permission prompts ... With the flag, your run doesn't consult the host or wait on it. Anything that would prompt is denied unless a `PermissionRequest` hook allows it, Claude is told that nobody can approve the request and not to retry it". "The `--permission-prompts` flag requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later. Earlier versions reject it with an unknown-option error." Example: `claude -p "Update the dependency pins and run the tests" --permission-mode auto --permission-prompts none`. Errors page: missing `--permission-prompt-tool` tool → "the non-interactive run exits with this error, and exit code 1, on the first tool call that needs approval".

verdict.corrected_claim: `--permission-prompts none` (v2.1.259+) stops a `-p` run from waiting on any permission host; anything that would prompt is denied, `AskUserQuestion` is removed, and denials are reported as `permission_denied` system events and in `permission_denials`; `--permission-prompt-tool <mcp_tool>` delegates prompts to an MCP tool (exit 1 if that tool is missing at first approval).
verdict.evidence:
CLAIM HOLDS. Every element verified against official code.claude.com pages fetched 2026-09-27, plus the installed binary. critical=true for the Ashley design (persistent unattended `claude -p` in a Slurm job with no human at the prompt).

(1) Headless page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless, section "Turn off permission prompts in unattended runs"), verbatim: "Pass `--permission-prompts none` when nobody is available to answer permission prompts, for example in a scheduled job. The flag matters most when your run has a permission host: an Agent SDK app with a `canUseTool` callback, or an MCP tool you pass with `--permission-prompt-tool`. Without the flag, your run waits for that host to answer each permission request." ... "With the flag, your run doesn't consult the host or wait on it. Anything that would prompt is denied unless a `PermissionRequest` hook allows it, Claude is told that nobody can approve the request and not to retry it, and the run continues. In a `-p` run with no host, these requests are denied either way, and the flag also tells Claude not to retry them. Permission rules, `PermissionRequest` hooks, and the permission mode you set still decide every call first; Claude Code denies only the requests that nothing else resolves." ... "With `--permission-prompts none`, Claude Code removes the tools that need an answer from a person, such as `AskUserQuestion`, so Claude can't call them. Any MCP elicitation request that no `Elicitation` hook answers is cancelled." ... "With `--output-format stream-json`, denials appear as `permission_denied` system messages, and the final result message lists them in `permission_denials`." ... Note: "The `--permission-prompts` flag requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later. Earlier versions reject it with an unknown-option error." Example command confirmed verbatim: `claude -p "Update the dependency pins and run the tests" --permission-mode auto --permission-prompts none`.

(2) CLI reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference): `--permission-prompts` — "Set who answers permission prompts in print mode. With the default `host`, Claude Code sends them to the Agent SDK host or the `--permission-prompt-tool` tool. Pass `none` when nobody can answer, and Claude Code denies them instead. ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later", example `claude -p --permission-prompts none "query"`. `--permission-prompt-tool` — "Specify an MCP tool to handle permission prompts in non-interactive mode. Claude Code waits for that tool's MCP server to connect before running the first turn, up to the `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup timeout, 30 seconds by default. The prompt tool can't approve an MCP tool marked as requiring user interaction: Claude Code converts an `allow` result for one to a deny. This restriction requires Claude Code v2.1.199 or later", example `claude -p --permission-prompt-tool mcp_auth_tool "query"`. `--permission-mode` accepts `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `manual` (alias for `default`, v2.1.200+).

(3) Errors page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#mcp-permission-prompt-tool-not-found; raw markdown downloaded from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md, 528 KB, section at line 2917), verbatim: "The tool you passed to `--permission-prompt-tool` wasn't among the connected MCP tools when the run first needed a permission decision, either because its server never connected or because no connected server exposes a tool by that name. Claude Code still sends your prompt: the non-interactive run exits with this error, and exit code 1, on the first tool call that needs approval, so it produces no answer even though the request was made. Before the first prompt, Claude Code waits up to the per-server connection timeout of 30 seconds set by `MCP_TIMEOUT` for that server to connect. Before v2.1.206, startup didn't wait for the server to finish connecting, so a slow-starting but healthy server produced this error too." Exact error string: `Error: MCP tool mcp__permissions__approve (passed via --permission-prompt-tool) not found. Available MCP tools: none`. Fix: `claude mcp list`; tool name must match `mcp__<server>__<tool>`; raise `MCP_TIMEOUT` if slow. Same page, "auto mode classifier" section: "Elsewhere in a `-p` run without a `--permission-prompt-tool`, there is no prompt to fall back to, so the action doesn't run and the run continues."

(4) Independent check against the installed binary (outside the docs): C:\Users\grego\.vscode\extensions\anthropic.claude-code-2.1.283-win32-x64\resources\native-binary\claude.exe reports `2.1.283 (Claude Code)`; its `--help` lists `--permission-prompts <target>  Who answers permission prompts with --print: "host" (the SDK host or --permission-prompt-tool) or "none" (nobody: anything that would prompt is denied automatically; the permission mode still decides everything else) (choices: "host", "none", default: ...)`. Probe `claude.exe --bare -p "say hi" --permission-prompts bogus` was rejected before any API call with `error: option '--permission-prompts <target>' argument 'bogus' is invalid. Allowed choices are host, none.` and exit code 1. So the local 2.1.283 install (the one the VS Code extension ships) satisfies the v2.1.259 floor. No standalone `claude` is on the Windows or WSL PATH on this machine; only the extension-bundled binary exists.

Precision notes (not refutations): (a) the `permission_denied` system messages exist only in `--output-format stream-json`; the `permission_denials` list is on the final result message. (b) Denial is "unless a `PermissionRequest` hook allows it" — hooks, permission rules and mode decide first. (c) The default value of `--permission-prompts` is `host`. (d) `dontAsk` mode denies everything that would prompt regardless of the flag, and also denies `AskUserQuestion` and `requiresUserInteraction` MCP tools even when an allow rule matches. (e) For the Ashley design: a persistent unattended run needs `--permission-mode auto` (or `dontAsk`/`acceptEdits` plus `--allowedTools`) together with `--permission-prompts none`; `--bare` skips OAuth/keychain and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so a subscription-authenticated run must NOT use `--bare`.

findings.claim: `--max-turns <n>` and `--max-budget-usd <usd>` are print-mode only, have no default limit, and end the run with `error_max_turns` / `error_max_budget_usd`; subagent spend counts toward the budget; restored totals from `--resume` do not.
findings.detail: CLI ref: `--max-turns` "Limit the number of agentic turns (print mode only). Exits with an error when the limit is reached. No limit by default." `--max-budget-usd` "Maximum dollar amount to spend on API calls before stopping (print mode only). Spend from subagents counts toward the cap. When you return to a conversation with `--continue` or `--resume`, totals restored from earlier runs don't count toward it. Once spend reaches the cap, spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached`, and Claude Code stops background subagents that are still running; the cap-enforcement behaviors require Claude Code v2.1.217 or later". Example `claude -p --max-budget-usd 5.00 "query"`. Agent-loop: max turns "counts tool-use turns only".

findings.claim: System-prompt flags: `--system-prompt` and `--system-prompt-file` replace the default prompt and work only with `-p`; `--append-system-prompt` and `--append-system-prompt-file` append and work in any mode; `--append-subagent-system-prompt(-file)` for subagents (with `-p`).
findings.detail: Table verbatim: `--system-prompt` "Replace the default system prompt (print mode only)" example `claude -p --system-prompt "You are a Python expert" "query"`; `--system-prompt-file ./system-prompt.txt`; `--append-system-prompt "Always use TypeScript"`; `--append-system-prompt-file ./extra-rules.txt`. "When `--system-prompt` or `--system-prompt-file` is set, the `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` flag is ignored." Resumed conversations: see cli-reference#system-prompt-flags-in-resumed-conversations.

findings.claim: `--model` takes an alias (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`) or a full model name and overrides the `model` setting and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`; `--fallback-model` takes a comma-separated chain tried in order; `--effort` takes `low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultracode`.
findings.detail: Rows: `--model` example `claude --model claude-sonnet-5`; `--fallback-model` "Enable automatic fallback to the specified model(s) when the primary model is overloaded or not available, for example a retired model. Accepts a comma-separated list tried in order" example `claude --fallback-model sonnet,haiku`; persisted via `fallbackModel` setting. `--effort` example `claude --effort high`; env `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` overrides `--effort` and `/effort`. Resumed sessions continue on their prior model unless `--model`/`ANTHROPIC_MODEL` is given. In `-p`, `/model sonnet` and `/effort <level>` are accepted as prompt text (v2.1.205+).

findings.claim: `--mcp-config <files-or-json...>` loads MCP servers; with `-p` Claude Code waits for pending servers up to `MCP_TIMEOUT` (default 30000 ms) before the first turn (v2.1.221+); `--strict-mcp-config` fails at startup on invalid MCP config (v2.1.220+); invalid entries otherwise appear in `system/init`.`mcp_server_errors` and the run continues.
findings.detail: CLI ref rows verbatim: `--mcp-config` "Load MCP servers from JSON files or strings (space-separated). When you pass this flag with `-p`, Claude Code waits for still-pending servers to connect before running the first turn, up to the `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup timeout, 30 seconds by default"; `--strict-mcp-config` "Fail at startup if MCP server configuration is invalid rather than deferring the error until first use. Useful in CI/CD workflows. Requires Claude Code v2.1.220 or later". (Python SDK describes `strict_mcp_config` as "Use only servers in `mcp_servers`, ignore project config".) Headless: `mcp_server_errors` entries have `name`, `type` (`unknown_type`, `url_missing_type`, `invalid_config`, `reserved_name`), `message` (v2.1.219+); stderr warning `Warning: 1 MCP server skipped due to invalid config:` only when run in a terminal. `-p` shows no per-server approval prompt and connects a project's `.mcp.json` servers even in untrusted folders unless `--bare`.

findings.claim: `--settings <file-or-json>` applies for one session above user/project/local files and below managed settings (file >2 MiB → exit 1); `--add-dir <dirs...>` grants file access (paths must exist; UNC network paths refused) but does not load `.claude/` config except skills; `--verbose`, `--debug[='mcp,startup']`, `--debug-file <path>`.
findings.detail: Precedence (settings page): 1 Managed (`managed-settings.json`, MDM, claude.ai console) > 2 Command line (`claude --settings`) > 3 Project local `.claude/settings.local.json` > 4 Shared project `.claude/settings.json` > 5 User `~/.claude/settings.json`. "Environment variables aren't a level in this stack". `--settings` example `claude --settings '{"model": "claude-opus-5-5"}'`; with `-p` it also waits for pending MCP servers up to `MCP_TIMEOUT`. `--add-dir` "Validates that each path exists as a directory. You can't add most network paths, such as `\\server\share`"; persist via `permissions.additionalDirectories`. `--debug` "The filter binds only in the `=` form; a space-separated filter enables debug mode without filtering"; debug log at `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt`. `--verbose` "Print verbose output, including file operations, tool calls, and API requests".

findings.claim: `--bare` (recommended for scripts, to become the default for `-p`) skips hooks, skills, commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md, and NEVER reads OAuth credentials, the keychain, or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; it needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper`, so it cannot be used with a Pro/Max subscription.
findings.detail: Headless verbatim: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain. For the Anthropic API, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` ... or supply an `apiKeyHelper` in the `--settings` JSON." Note: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." Authentication page: "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." `--bare` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1` (env-vars: "OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read"). Bare mode still loads skills from `--add-dir` `.claude/skills/`. Without `--bare`, a `-p` run executes hooks from the project's `.claude/settings.json` and connects `.mcp.json` servers with no trust dialog.

verdict.corrected_claim: `--bare` (recommended for scripted and SDK calls; the docs say it "will become the default for `-p` in a future release") skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md, and sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1` (equivalent). In bare mode Claude Code "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", "does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`", and does not read Anthropic profiles or federation variables; Anthropic authentication must come from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` supplied via `--settings` (Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry provider credentials are still read). The headless page states outright that "bare mode doesn't use your subscription login", so a Pro/Max subscription cannot drive a `--bare` run. Bare mode still loads skills from an `--add-dir` directory's `.claude/skills/` (but not its `.claude/commands/` or `.claude/agents/`), and the project's `env` block and helpers such as `awsAuthRefresh` still apply. Without `--bare`, a `-p` run "runs the hooks in a project's `.claude/settings.json` and connects the servers in its `.mcp.json`, even in a folder you've never trusted", with no workspace trust dialog and no per-server approval prompt. Design consequence (critical=true): the persistent grid Claude Code for Ashley must NOT pass `--bare` (nor set `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`) if it is to run on the student's Pro/Max subscription; use `claude setup-token` -> `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (precedence rank 5, above `/login` OAuth at rank 7, below `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` at rank 3) with plain `-p` or interactive mode instead, and control what the untrusted project can run with `--setting-sources user`, `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'`, `--strict-mcp-config`, or `disabledMcpjsonServers`.
verdict.evidence:
All quotes fetched 2026-09-27 from code.claude.com (official). critical=true for the design: the subscription-vs-bare conflict is confirmed, not refuted.

1. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless ("Start faster with bare mode"), verbatim: "Add `--bare` to reduce startup time by skipping auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md." / "A directory you name with `--add-dir` is a partial exception: bare mode loads skills from its `.claude/skills/` folder, but still skips its `.claude/commands/` and `.claude/agents/` folders." / "Without `--bare`, a `-p` session runs the hooks in a project's `.claude/settings.json` and connects the servers in its `.mcp.json`, even in a folder you've never trusted. A `-p` session shows no workspace trust dialog and no per-server approval prompt." / "Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before running it, because bare mode doesn't use your subscription login" / "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain. For the Anthropic API, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment ... or supply an `apiKeyHelper` in the `--settings` JSON. Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry continue to read their own provider credentials as usual." / Note: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release."

2. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication ("Generate a long-lived token"), verbatim: "[Bare mode] does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." Also: "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." Also: "Claude Code doesn't read profiles or federation variables in bare mode, in Claude Desktop, or in cloud sessions." Authentication precedence list: 1 cloud provider vars, 2 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, 3 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` ("In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present"), 4 `apiKeyHelper`, 5 `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, 6 Anthropic profile/federation, 7 "Subscription OAuth credentials from `/login`. This is the default for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users." Linux credential store: `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode `0600` (or under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`).

3. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (fetched as .md, 507 KB), verbatim `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` row: "Set to `1` to run with a minimal system prompt and only the Bash, file read, and file edit tools. MCP tools from `--mcp-config` are still available. Disables auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md. Skills in a directory you pass with `--add-dir` still load. OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read, so Anthropic authentication must come from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` in `--settings`. Equivalent to passing `--bare`". `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` row: "OAuth access token for claude.ai authentication. Alternative to `/login` for SDK and automated environments. Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials. Generate one with `claude setup-token` ... To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY`: "Set to `0` to force auto memory on even when `--bare` mode ... would otherwise disable it".

4. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (fetched as .md), verbatim `--bare` row: "Minimal mode: skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster. Skills in a directory you pass with `--add-dir` still load. Claude has access to Bash, file read, and file edit tools. Sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`." Also `--settings`: "Path to a settings JSON file or an inline JSON string ... no larger than 2 MiB"; `--setting-sources`: "Comma-separated list of setting sources to load (`user`, `project`, `local`)"; `--strict-mcp-config`: "Only use MCP servers from `--mcp-config`, ignoring all other MCP configurations."

5. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions ("What runs before you trust a folder"), verbatim: table row for `.mcp.json` servers under "`claude -p` or the SDK, folder never trusted": "Connected without asking, approved or not."; hooks/env/apiKeyHelper row: "Used." Mitigations listed: "Pass `--setting-sources user` ... so Claude Code reads neither the project's settings files nor its `.mcp.json`"; "Start with `--bare` so Claude Code reads no hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, or `.mcp.json` servers from the project. The project's `env` block and helpers such as `awsAuthRefresh` in its settings files still apply, and Claude Code reads `apiKeyHelper` only from `--settings`"; "Pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'`"; "Add a `disabledMcpjsonServers` entry".

6. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills ("Skills from additional directories"): confirms `--add-dir` loads `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/agents/` normally, and "bare mode ... restrict[s] them further"; "Claude Code watches skill directories for file changes, except in bare mode."

7. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference (`apiKeyHelper` section): runs via `/bin/sh` on Linux, output sent as both `X-Api-Key` and `Authorization: Bearer`; cache TTL 5 min via `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS`; no bare-mode exemption stated there.

Minor precision notes (not refutations): the claim's "needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper`" omits that Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry provider credentials are still read in bare mode, and that the project's `env` block still applies. Not stated anywhere in the docs: whether `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (bearer, rank 2) is honoured in bare mode; the headless page names only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `apiKeyHelper`, so treat `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`-in-bare as unverified. No release date or version is given for when `--bare` becomes the `-p` default; the docs say only "a future release", so a plain `-p` design should pin the Claude Code version or check `system/init` output rather than assume today's default persists.

findings.claim: `-p` keeps running after the final turn while background subagents/workflows finish, up to `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default 600000 ms = 10 min, `0` = wait forever); plain background Bash tasks are killed ~5 s after the result once stdin closes; Monitor watches time out at 5 min by default.
findings.detail: Env-vars row: "Ceiling in milliseconds on idle waiting for background subagents and workflows after the final turn in non-interactive mode with the `-p` flag ... Default: `600000`, or 10 minutes ... Set to `0` to wait indefinitely. This cap is separate from the five-second grace period that applies to plain background Bash tasks". Headless: "When a turn starts while the [working] directory is missing, Claude Code emits a warning message in `stream-json` output, and shell commands fail until the directory exists again" (session keeps running if cwd is deleted). Deleted cwd at startup → exit 1.

findings.claim: Authentication precedence in `-p`: provider vars (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`/`_VERTEX`/`_FOUNDRY`) > `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (Bearer) > `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (X-Api-Key; always used when present in `-p`, overriding a subscription login) > `apiKeyHelper` > `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` > Anthropic profile/WIF credentials > `/login` subscription OAuth credentials.
findings.detail: Numbered list verbatim (1-7). On `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present." On `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`: "A long-lived OAuth token generated by `claude setup-token`. Use this for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login isn't available. If you run `/login` while the variable is set, Claude Code switches the current session to the new login, but reads the variable again in every new session". Settings `env` block can set a variable to `""` to cancel a shell export ("Claude Code treats an empty value as unset for provider selection"). `apiKeyHelper` output is sent "as both the `X-Api-Key` and `Authorization: Bearer` headers"; re-run after `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` (default 300000) or on 401/403. `forceLoginOrgUUID` blocks `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`/`apiKeyHelper` sessions at startup.

verdict.corrected_claim: Authentication precedence (interactive and `-p`, per the live official page on 2026-09-27): 1. cloud provider credentials when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` is set > 2. `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (sent as `Authorization: Bearer`) > 3. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (sent as `X-Api-Key`; "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present", overriding a subscription login) > 4. `apiKeyHelper` output > 5. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (one-year token from `claude setup-token`) > 6. Anthropic profile / Workload Identity Federation credentials > 7. `/login` subscription OAuth credentials. QUALIFIERS the original claim omitted: (a) item 6 is conditional: a profile that `ant auth login` wrote (`user_oauth`) ranks above `/login` only when named in `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`; an unnamed active `user_oauth` profile ranks BELOW a working `/login` credential; only `oidc_federation` profiles and the `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`+`ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID` pair always rank above `/login`. (b) A signed-in Claude apps gateway session sits outside the list and outranks item 1. (c) CRITICAL for a headless subscription job: `--bare` "does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`", "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", and doesn't read profiles or federation variables, so under `claude -p --bare` only items 1-4 exist; `--bare` "will become the default for `-p` in a future release". (d) `/login` is a terminal-only command and is not available in `-p`, so in `-p` the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is used for the whole session and can only be replaced by generating a new token and restarting. (e) `forceLoginOrgUUID` blocks `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`/`apiKeyHelper` sessions at startup only when set from a MANAGED source; in user/project/local settings a single UUID merely pre-selects the organization at login. (f) The `""`-in-`env` rule is documented for provider-selection variables ("treats the empty value as unset for provider selection"; "Subprocesses still inherit the empty value"); it is not documented for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, for which the documented remedy is `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. (g) `apiKeyHelper` is re-run after the TTL (five minutes by default, `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS`), on `401`/`403`, and (v2.1.246+) when the cached output is an expired JWT; the 401/403 and JWT cases apply "only when the helper's output is the credential Claude Code sends and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` isn't set".
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core claim HOLDS against the live official page fetched 2026-09-27 (page cites v2.1.265; sibling headless page cites v2.1.283 = the installed extension version, so the docs are current). refuted=false because the 7-item order and every quoted sentence appear verbatim; the corrected claim adds scope qualifiers and one design-critical omission, none of which reverse the order.

[1] NUMBERED LIST — VERBATIM MATCH (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#authentication-precedence). "When multiple credentials are present, Claude Code chooses one in this order: 1. Cloud provider credentials, when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` is set. ... 2. `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. Sent as the `Authorization: Bearer` header. ... 3. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable. Sent as the `X-Api-Key` header. ... In interactive mode, you are prompted once to approve or decline the key, and your choice is remembered. ... In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present. 4. `apiKeyHelper` script output. ... 5. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. A long-lived OAuth token generated by `claude setup-token`. Use this for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login isn't available. If you run `/login` while the variable is set, Claude Code switches the current session to the new login, but reads the variable again in every new session until you remove it from your shell profile or the `env` block of a settings file. 6. Anthropic profile and federation credentials, the credentials that the `ant` CLI and Workload Identity Federation use. A profile that `ant auth login` wrote ranks here only when you name it in `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`; otherwise it ranks below `/login`. 7. Subscription OAuth credentials from `/login`. This is the default for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users." Also: "If you have an active Claude subscription but also have `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set in your environment, Claude Code uses the API key once you approve it. ... Run `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to fall back to your subscription, and check `/status` to confirm which method is active." critical=true (design must guarantee the Slurm job environment does NOT carry ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or the student's subscription is silently bypassed in -p).

[2] ITEM 6 QUALIFIER (same page, "Anthropic profiles and federation credentials" table): Named profile via `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE` -> "Above, whichever auth mode the profile has"; Federation variables `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` and `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, both set -> "Above"; Active profile (`active_config` file or profile named `default`) -> "Above when its auth mode is `oidc_federation`; below a working `/login` credential when its auth mode is `user_oauth`". Config dir default `~/.config/anthropic` (macOS/Linux) or `%APPDATA%\Anthropic` (Windows). The claim's flat "profile/WIF > /login" is therefore conditional. critical=false.

[3] GATEWAY OUTSIDE THE LIST (same page): "A signed-in Claude apps gateway session sits outside this list: it is a provider selection like Amazon Bedrock ... and it outranks them." critical=false.

[4] BARE MODE DROPS ITEMS 5-7 — OMITTED BY CLAIM. authentication page: "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." and "Claude Code doesn't read profiles or federation variables in bare mode, in Claude Desktop, or in cloud sessions." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless#start-faster-with-bare-mode: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain. For the Anthropic API, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment ... or supply an `apiKeyHelper` in the `--settings` JSON." and Note: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." critical=true (the persistent grid Claude Code must run `-p` WITHOUT `--bare` to use a Pro/Max subscription; when `--bare` becomes the `-p` default the subscription path breaks unless the extension pins behaviour or the docs add an opt-out).

[5] /login UNAVAILABLE IN -p (headless page, Note under "Create a commit"): "Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available." So the claim's "/login while the variable is set" sentence applies only to interactive sessions. env-vars row (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars): "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | OAuth access token for claude.ai authentication. Alternative to `/login` for SDK and automated environments. Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials. Generate one with `claude setup-token`. Unless you run `/login`, Claude Code uses the token you set for the whole session. To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". critical=true (token rotation for a 30-day-wall Slurm job requires a restart of the `claude -p` process).

[6] setup-token facts (authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token): "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`"; "It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable"; "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." cli-reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference): "`claude setup-token` — Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription." Also `claude auth status` — "Show authentication status as JSON. Use `--text` for human-readable output. Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not". critical=true.

[7] EMPTY-STRING RULE — HOLDS, SCOPED (env-vars, "Precedence"): "In a settings file you can set a variable but you can't remove one. To override a variable you can't unset, such as a stale `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` exported by a shell profile you don't control, set it to an empty string in the `env` block: `"CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX": ""`. Claude Code treats the empty value as unset for provider selection. Subprocesses still inherit the empty value." Claim wrote "an empty value"; doc says "the empty value ... for provider selection". Not documented for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. critical=false.

[8] apiKeyHelper — HOLDS WITH ADDITIONS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#apikeyhelper): "Claude Code runs the command through the system shell, `/bin/sh` on macOS and Linux and `cmd` on Windows, and sends its output as both the `X-Api-Key` and `Authorization: Bearer` headers." Re-run cases: "After the cache lifetime, five minutes by default or the interval you set with `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS`." / "When a request to the Anthropic API, directly or through an LLM gateway, fails with `401` or `403`." / "Before sending a request ... when the cached output is a JWT that expired after the helper produced it. Requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later." / "The last two cases apply only when the helper's output is the credential Claude Code sends and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` isn't set." The env-vars row for `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` says only "Interval in milliseconds at which credentials should be refreshed"; the number 300000 is not printed in the apiKeyHelper entry (five minutes = 300000 ms; the literal `300000` on that page belongs to a different key's `refreshIntervalMs` example). Also authentication page: helper failure -> "`Your apiKeyHelper script is failing` within three attempts. Before v2.1.208, helper failures surfaced as a generic 401 after about ten silent retries." critical=false.

[9] forceLoginOrgUUID — HOLDS ONLY FROM A MANAGED SOURCE. authentication#restrict-login-to-your-organization: "`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper`: blocked at startup, since organization membership can't be verified for an environment credential"; "Cloud provider sessions such as Amazon Bedrock: not blocked"; "Anthropic profile or federation credentials: not blocked". settings-reference#forceloginorguuid: "Scope: Any file. Only a managed source enforces the restriction; a single UUID in any other settings file pre-selects the organization during login without restricting it." Also `claude setup-token` and `/install-github-app` "enforce only `forceLoginMethod`, so they can mint a token in a different organization". critical=false (WSU is not deploying managed settings; irrelevant unless a student's machine carries an employer's managed-settings.json).

NOT VERIFIED: whether the web-login callback works from a compute node (docs note a paste-code fallback "common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers"), and the exact release in which `--bare` becomes the `-p` default (docs say only "a future release").

findings.claim: `claude setup-token` runs the same browser OAuth flow as `/login`, prints a one-year OAuth token to the terminal without saving it, requires a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan, and is consumed only via the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable; the token can make model requests only (no Remote Control, no claude.ai connectors); it enforces `forceLoginMethod` but not `forceLoginOrgUUID`.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token` ... The command opens the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, and the token prints to the terminal after you approve access in the browser. It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable ... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." CLI ref: `claude setup-token` "Generate long-lived OAuth token for CI". Env-vars row: "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | OAuth access token for claude.ai authentication. Alternative to `/login` for SDK and automated environments. Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials ... To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". Community sources report the token prefix `sk-ant-oat01-` (issue #18340; not in official docs). `/login` fallback in SSH/containers: `Paste code here if prompted` when the browser cannot reach the local callback server.

verdict.corrected_claim: `claude setup-token` opens the same browser authorization flow as `/login` and, after approval, prints a one-year OAuth token to the terminal without saving it anywhere; it requires a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise subscription. The only documented consumer is the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable (set in the shell or in a settings-file `env` block; GitHub Actions exposes it as the `claude_code_oauth_token` input), BUT: (1) bare mode (`--bare` or `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`) does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` at all and requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead; (2) the variable ranks 5th in authentication precedence, below cloud-provider selection (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`/`VERTEX`/`FOUNDRY`), `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `apiKeyHelper`, so any of those present in the environment silently override it; it takes precedence only over keychain/`.credentials.json` logins and profiles. The token can only make model requests: it cannot establish Remote Control sessions (error `Remote Control requires a full-scope login token`) or fetch claude.ai connectors; locally configured MCP servers still work. On Claude Code v2.1.212 or later, `claude setup-token` enforces `forceLoginMethod` but not `forceLoginOrgUUID`, so it can mint a token in a different organization; before v2.1.212 it enforced neither key. When the token expires or is revoked, requests fail with `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` or `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`; Claude Code keeps sending the expired env value rather than falling back to a stored login (v2.1.225+), `/status` shows an `Auth token` row reading `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and the fix is to generate a new token and restart. Sessions using this variable never receive the 3-day `Your login expires in 3 days` warning or the `Login expired · Please run /login` message. The `sk-ant-oat01-` prefix appears only in community reports (issue #18340), not in official docs.

VERDICT: core claim confirmed verbatim; refuted on two design-relevant points (bare mode ignores the variable; precedence is not "only"/absolute) and one version qualifier (forceLoginMethod enforcement is v2.1.212+). Details as data:

[CONFIRMED, critical=true] Same flow, one-year, not saved, plan requirement, model-requests-only. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token verbatim: "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token` ... The command opens the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, and the token prints to the terminal after you approve access in the browser. It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable wherever you want to authenticate ... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." Shell forms shown: `export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=your-token` (macOS/Linux/WSL), `$env:CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN = "your-token"` (PowerShell), `set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=your-token` (CMD).

[REFUTED: "consumed only via env var" is incomplete, critical=true] Same page, immediately after: "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain" and "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars row `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`: "Set to `1` to run with a minimal system prompt ... OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read, so Anthropic authentication must come from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` in `--settings`. Equivalent to passing `--bare`". DESIGN IMPACT: the persistent grid runner must NOT use `--bare`/`CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1` if it is to run on the student's subscription token; and if `-p` later defaults to bare, subscription auth in the runner breaks.

[REFUTED: precedence is not absolute, critical=true] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#authentication-precedence lists, in order: 1. cloud provider credentials when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`/`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`/`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` set; 2. `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (sent as `Authorization: Bearer`); 3. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (sent as `X-Api-Key`; "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present"); 4. `apiKeyHelper`; 5. "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. A long-lived OAuth token generated by `claude setup-token`. Use this for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login isn't available. If you run `/login` while the variable is set, Claude Code switches the current session to the new login, but reads the variable again in every new session until you remove it from your shell profile or the `env` block of a settings file."; 6. Anthropic profile/federation credentials; 7. subscription OAuth from `/login`. So the variable is overridden by any stray `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the container/Slurm environment. Also: the variable can be supplied via a settings-file `env` block, not only the shell.

[CONFIRMED verbatim, env-vars row] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (raw .md line 327): "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | OAuth access token for claude.ai authentication. Alternative to `/login` for SDK and automated environments. Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials. Generate one with `claude setup-token`. Unless you run `/login`, Claude Code uses the token you set for the whole session. To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". Matches the claim's DETAIL exactly.

findings.claim: When a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` expires or is revoked, Claude Code keeps sending it after a 401 (no fallback to stored login, v2.1.225+); the fix is a new `claude setup-token` and a restart. Expired `/login` credentials in `-p` fail with `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` and structured error code `authentication_failed`.
findings.detail: Errors page: `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` and `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`; "If you authenticate with the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable, Claude Code keeps sending the value you set after a request fails with a 401 ... Generate a fresh token with `claude setup-token` and restart with it, or unset the variable and run `/login`." `/status` shows the credential as an `Auth token` row reading `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Login expired: "In non-interactive mode (`-p`) and the Agent SDK, the message reads ... `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`". Interactive warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (v2.1.217+ three days; not shown when `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` supplies the credential). "A background session ... that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again."

verdict.corrected_claim: When a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` expires or is revoked, the session sees the API-rejection messages `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` / `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`, and on Claude Code v2.1.225 or later Claude Code keeps sending the env-var value after the 401 rather than switching to a stored login's token (before v2.1.225 a transient 401 could replace the variable's value mid-session with a stored login's short-lived access token, which then expired and broke headless sessions until restart). The fix is a fresh `claude setup-token` and a restart with the new value, or unset the variable and run `/login`. `/status` shows the credential as an `Auth token` row reading `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. A different state, an expired `/login` credential whose refresh token the OAuth service rejected (Claude Code clears the saved login and stops each request locally, v2.1.206+), reads `Login expired · Please run /login` interactively and, in `-p` and the Agent SDK, `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` with structured error code `authentication_failed`; sessions authenticated with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or an API key never see that message. The startup warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (v2.1.203+, five days before v2.1.217, three days from v2.1.217) appears only when a claude.ai or Claude Console `/login` is the active credential; the docs' explicit exclusion list names cloud providers, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `apiKeyHelper`, and no advance-expiry warning of any kind is documented for the one-year setup-token. The 3-day-warning and "background session ... outlives the login stops making progress ... can't recover until you sign in again" passages are on the Authentication page (#renew-an-expiring-login), not the Errors page.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim HOLDS in every substantive element; two supporting passages in DETAIL are mis-attributed (they are on the Authentication page, not the Errors page) and one sub-clause ("not shown when CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN supplies the credential") is a reasonable inference the docs do not state verbatim. Nothing contradicted.

METHOD: WebFetch of code.claude.com/docs/en/errors truncated before the auth sections, so the raw markdown (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md, 528,276 bytes, fetched 2026-09-27 via curl in WSL) was downloaded and grepped; same for the CHANGELOG (821,156 bytes, top header `## 2.1.283`). WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) so no third-party sources; all findings below are from official Anthropic pages actually fetched.

--- FINDING 1 [critical=true] Errors page, section `### OAuth token revoked or expired` (errors.md lines 1130-1150; anchor #oauth-token-revoked-or-expired). Verbatim:
"Your saved login is no longer valid. A revoked token means you signed out everywhere or an admin removed access; an expired token means the automatic refresh failed mid-session."
"Both messages report a rejection the API returned for a request Claude Code sent. When the saved login has already been cleared after a failed refresh, you see [Login expired](#login-expired) instead. If you authenticate with a long-lived token in [`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`](/docs/en/env-vars), you see the same messages when that token expires or is revoked."
Code block: `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` / `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`
Bullet: "If you authenticate with the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable, Claude Code keeps sending the value you set after a request fails with a 401, rather than switching to a stored login's token. [`/status`](/docs/en/commands) shows this credential as an `Auth token` row reading `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Generate a fresh token with [`claude setup-token`](/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token) and restart with it, or unset the variable and run `/login`. Before v2.1.225, Claude Code could replace the variable's value mid-session with the short-lived access token from a stored login, and the session failed with 401 errors again once that token expired."
Also: "If the error returns within the same session after re-authenticating, run `/logout` first to fully clear the stored token, then `/login`".
=> Confirms: keeps sending after 401; no switch to stored login; v2.1.225 boundary; setup-token + restart fix; /status `Auth token` row.

--- FINDING 2 [critical=true] CHANGELOG `## 2.1.225` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md line 2260): "Fixed a transient 401 replacing a long-lived `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` with a stored login's short-lived token, breaking headless sessions until restart". Note the trigger was a TRANSIENT 401 (any 401, not only expiry) — so on <2.1.225 a persistent headless session could lose its one-year token on a network blip; our Singularity image must ship Claude Code >= 2.1.225 (current: 2.1.283). Related changelog lines with version headers: `## 2.1.117` "Fixed Plain-CLI OAuth sessions dying with \"Please run /login\" when the access token expires mid-session — the token is now refreshed reactively on 401" and "Fixed `/login` having no effect when launched with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var and that token expires"; `## 2.1.118` "Fixed `/login` having no effect in a session launched with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` — the env token is now cleared so disk credentials take effect"; `## 2.1.229` "Updated `/login` to repeat the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` override warning after a successful login"; `## 2.1.234` "`claude setup-token` now rejects unexpected extra arguments instead of silently ignoring them" and "after `/login` while `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set, the stale-token reminder no longer leaks into Claude's automatically resumed turn"; `## 2.1.216` "Fixed auto mode denying commands with \"HTTP 401\" classifier errors after the OAuth token expired or rotated mid-session"; `## 2.1.274` "Fixed self-hosted runner sessions failing every turn with a 401 after a few failed token refreshes ... fetches a new token after a 401". No changelog line mentions `authentication_failed`, `could not be refreshed`, or `login expires`.

--- FINDING 3 [critical=true] Errors page `### Login expired` (errors.md lines 1164-1195; anchor #login-expired). Verbatim: "Claude Code tried to renew your saved claude.ai or Claude Console login and the OAuth service rejected the stored refresh token, so Claude Code cleared the saved credentials. After that, each model request stops locally with this message before it reaches the API, because only `/login` can create new credentials." "Before v2.1.206, Claude Code sent the model request anyway with whatever credential remained in the environment, and every model then failed with [There's an issue with the selected model] or a 401 instead of a prompt to sign in." Code block: `Login expired · Please run /login`. "In [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) (`-p`) and the [Agent SDK](/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview), the message reads as follows, and the structured error code is `authentication_failed`:" code block: `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`. "This is not the same state as [OAuth token revoked or expired]. Those messages report a rejection the API returned. Claude Code itself produces `Login expired` for a login it already failed to renew, so it sends no request." "Sessions authenticated with an API key, [`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`](/docs/en/env-vars), or a third-party provider don't use the saved login and never see this message." "/status shows a `Login` row reading `Expired — log in again` ... Before v2.1.210, `/status` gave no indication in this state". What to do: "In non-interactive mode, run `claude` in the same environment, complete `/login`, then rerun your command. For automation that can't sign in interactively, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or [generate a long-lived token with `claude setup-token`]". Sibling: "Could not refresh your login because another Claude Code process is refreshing it" -> -p code `server_error`, message `Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh...`. "Your account is on hold" -> -p code `account_on_hold` (before v2.1.235 reported as Login expired).

--- FINDING 4 [critical=true] Headless page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md), `system/api_retry` event table, field `error`: "error category: `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `account_on_hold`, `billing_error`, `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `cloud_credential_error`, or `unknown`". Also: "When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout." and "Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails". `-p` mode: "Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available." Bare mode: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain ... Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before running it, because bare mode doesn't use your subscription login" and Note: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." DESIGN RISK: our persistent -p runner must NOT pass `--bare` (Authentication page: "[Bare mode] does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead."), and a future release making `--bare` the `-p` default would break subscription-token headless use unless the flag is explicitly negated.

--- FINDING 5 (attribution correction) The "3 days" warning and the "background session" sentence are on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#renew-an-expiring-login, NOT the Errors page (grep of errors.md for "expires in 3 days" and "outlives the login" returned nothing). Verbatim: "When the login you created with `/login` is within three days of expiring, Claude Code shows a warning at startup: `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. Before v2.1.217, the warning appeared five days out." "The warning is informational and never blocks a request". "The warning appears only when a claude.ai or Claude Console login is the active credential, and not when a cloud provider, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` supplies the credential." (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is not in that explicit list; the claim's "not shown when CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN supplies the credential" follows from "only when a claude.ai or Claude Console login is the active credential" plus precedence rank 5 > 7, but is inferred, not quoted. No expiry warning for the setup-token itself is documented anywhere fetched.) "Renewing early matters most for sessions that run unattended. A [background session in agent view](/docs/en/agent-view) or a [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." CHANGELOG `## 2.1.217` confirms: "Changed the login-expiry warning to appear 3 days before expiry instead of 5".

--- FINDING 6 [critical=true] Authentication page, `### Generate a long-lived token`: "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`"; "The command opens the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, and the token prints to the terminal after you approve access in the browser. It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable"; "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish [Remote Control] sessions or fetch [claude.ai connectors]. MCP servers you configure locally still work." CLI reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference): `claude setup-token` = "Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it." "Requires a Claude subscription." Precedence list item 5: "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. A long-lived OAuth token generated by `claude setup-token`. Use this for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login isn't available. If you run `/login` while the variable is set, Claude Code switches the current session to the new login, but reads the variable again in every new session until you remove it from your shell profile or the `env` block of a settings file." Item 7: "Subscription OAuth credentials from `/login`. This is the default for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users." Credential storage on Linux: `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode `0600`; honours `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.

IMPLICATIONS FOR ASHLEY DESIGN (Slurm 30-day max wall, persistent -p Claude Code in Singularity): (a) setup-token path: one-year fixed token, no refresh, no advance warning; on expiry/revocation the job's requests fail with the 401 messages and only a new token + process restart recovers — build the restart into the runner; (b) /login path: credentials auto-refresh reactively on 401 (2.1.117+) but a refresh-token rejection clears the login and every -p turn returns `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` / `authentication_failed` until an INTERACTIVE `/login` (unavailable inside -p) is done in the same environment/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; (c) never pass `--bare`; (d) pin Claude Code >= 2.1.225 in the container (2.1.283 current); (e) parse `system/api_retry` `error` == `authentication_failed` in stream-json to detect the state.

verdict.corrected_claim: As of 2026-06-16 (support article "Last Updated June 16, 2026", banner "Update June 15"), and still with no newer official statement as of 2026-09-27, `claude -p`, the Claude Agent SDK and third-party-app usage draw from a Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise subscription's ordinary usage limits; the separately announced monthly "Agent SDK credit" (Pro $20, Max 5x $100, Max 20x $200, Team Standard $20, Team Premium $100, plus Enterprise tiers) was paused and "isn't available"; API-key (Claude Console) users get no credit and stay pay-as-you-go. QUALIFIERS the original claim omits (all from official docs, all design-relevant): (1) subscription-funded headless use requires the CLI to read OAuth credentials, i.e. a `/login` credential or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token`; `--bare` "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", "does not read CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN", "doesn't use your subscription login", and Anthropic says `--bare` "will become the default for `-p` in a future release"; (2) if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present", silently moving billing to pay-as-you-go; (3) "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK", so a student-facing extension must launch the official `claude` CLI and let the student log in themselves rather than wrapping the SDK behind its own claude.ai login.

verdict.corrected_claim: The Agent SDK note is quoted accurately, but it is not the controlling text and the claim misplaces the line. The controlling statements are the Claude Code "Legal and compliance" page (code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) and the support article "Log in to your Claude account" (support.claude.com, dated May 19, 2026). Together they say: (1) a platform MAY preinstall/run Claude Code "in hosted sandboxes or other agent infrastructure" and an end user MAY sign in to "the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code" — provided the binary is unmodified, no built-in auth method is removed/disabled/restricted, each end user authenticates with their own credentials, and the platform does not pay for, resell or intermediate usage; this requires agreeing to the Commercial Terms. (2) What is PROHIBITED is for the developer to "offer Claude.ai login into their own applications", to "route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users", and — the rule the claim omits — to "collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." Therefore the Ashley design's step "collect credentials (... Claude subscription)" is the part that crosses the line, not the students' use of their own subscriptions: Ashley must never take, store or forward a student's Claude OAuth token or setup-token; the student must run `claude` / `claude auth login` / `claude setup-token` themselves on the grid node (Anthropic's own flow; SSH/container logins use the "Paste code here if prompted" code path) and place any `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in their own environment. Ashley should remain a launcher/transport for the unmodified `claude` CLI rather than an agent product built on the Agent SDK with its own system prompt, because SDK-built products "should use API key authentication". Additional constraints: `--bare` does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or any OAuth credential; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment always overrides the subscription in `-p` mode; the setup-token is one-year, "requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan", and "can only make model requests" (no Remote Control); `/login` credentials expire and an unattended session "stops making progress once the credential expires", so a 30-day persistent Slurm job must plan for renewal. Branding: "Claude Code"/"Claude Code Agent" not permitted; "Claude Agent" and "{YourAgentName} Powered by Claude" allowed; you may say in plain text that the product runs Claude Code but not use the name/logo in your product or feature name. Subscription access via third-party tools is at Anthropic's discretion and may be drawn from "usage credits rather than subscription limits"; enforcement may occur "without prior notice". The press-reported enforcement/reinstatement timeline (2026-01-09, winbuzzer 2026-02-19, VentureBeat) could not be verified in this session.

verdict.corrected_claim:
The four headline rows hold verbatim against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (fetched 2026-09-27): `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — "Override the configuration directory (default: `~/.claude`). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path. ... Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings"; `.credentials.json` also moves ("If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead" — authentication page). `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` — "Set to `1` to disable automatic background updates. Manual `claude update` still works. Use `DISABLE_UPDATES` to block both"; `DISABLE_UPDATES` — "Set to `1` to block all updates including manual `claude update` and `claude install`". `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` — "Set to any non-empty value, such as `1`, to disable nonessential network traffic: auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, the `/feedback` command, Claude-drafted feedback, release notes, the PR and MR status badge checks, and availability checks such as the fast mode check"; it ALSO disables feature-flag fetching (Remote Control, claude.ai skill/plugin sync, `claude import`, artifact comments become unavailable) and stops background plugin `command`-source runs; it does NOT cover the WebFetch domain safety check (`skipWebFetchPreflight`) or official-marketplace auto-install (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL`). `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` — "Set to any non-empty value, such as `1`, to opt out of telemetry. **Setting it to `0` or `false` still opts out** ... Also disables feature-flag fetching". `claude doctor` confirms with an `Auto-updates` line reading `disabled (set by env: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER)` "On a native or npm installation". `env` in settings.json: "Values here are plain text in the settings file and reach every subprocess Claude Code starts", and a settings-file `env` value overrides the same variable exported in the shell.

CORRECTIONS to the DETAIL: (1) `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` does NOT override `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`; it "enable[s] OpenTelemetry data collection for metrics and logging. Required before configuring OTel exporters" (your own OTel collector), is "Ignored in project and local settings", and no page states any override of the Anthropic-telemetry opt-out. Only unsetting `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` turns Anthropic telemetry back on (the survey has a separate `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY_FOR_OTEL=1` opt-back-in). (2) The "any non-empty value" rule applies to exactly six variables — `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING`, `CLAUDE_CODE_TMUX_TRUECOLOR`, `FALLBACK_FOR_ALL_PRIMARY_MODELS`, `IS_DEMO`. `DISABLE_COST_WARNINGS` ("Set to `1`"), `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING` ("Set to `1`") and `DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND` ("Set to `1`") are ordinary on/off variables: "set `1` or `true` to turn it on and `0` or `false` to turn it off, in any casing". `DO_NOT_TRACK` is likewise boolean ("`0` leaves telemetry on"). (3) `DISABLE_BUG_COMMAND` is only "the older name" still accepted for `DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND` (which disables `/feedback`, `/bug`, `/share` and Claude-drafted feedback). (4) `DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS` does not appear anywhere in the current env-vars, settings-reference, monitoring-usage or claude-directory pages; do not rely on it. (5) Version gates: ignoring `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`HOME`/`XDG_*` in project+local settings dates from v2.1.251; ignoring the OTel export group there requires v2.1.282+ (local extension is 2.1.283, so both apply). Not verified either way: whether `~/.claude.json` ("App state, OAuth, UI toggles, personal MCP servers") relocates under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — the claude-directory page says only "every `~/.claude` path on this page lives under that directory instead", and `~/.claude.json` sits beside, not inside, `~/.claude`; test on the grid before assuming.

findings.detail: Rows verbatim: `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` "Set the maximum number of output tokens for most requests. Defaults and caps vary by model ... Claude Code defaults to 32000 for model IDs it doesn't recognize ... and lowers values above a model's cap to the cap. Increasing this value reduces the effective context window available before auto-compaction triggers". `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` "Fixed token budget for extended thinking. Claude Code caps it at one token below the request's max output tokens and never below 1,024 ... When unset and thinking is enabled, models with adaptive reasoning choose their own thinking depth ... Set to `0` to disable thinking on the Anthropic API, except on Opus 5.5 and the Fable m[odels]". `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` "(default: 120000, or 2 minutes)"; `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` "(default: 600000 ...) Useful for ephemeral scripted sessions". `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` "Set to `1` to run with a minimal system prompt and only the Bash, file read, and file edit tools ...
