findings.claim: The Claude Code binary is a native executable that does not use Node.js at runtime; documented Linux support floor is Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 10+/Alpine 3.19+ (glibc and musl builds), so CentOS 7.9 (glibc 2.17) is unsupported on the host and the CLI must run inside the container image; the native installer places a symlink at `~/.local/bin/claude` into `~/.local/share/claude/versions/` and auto-updates unless `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`.
findings.detail: System requirements verbatim: "Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, Alpine Linux 3.19+ ... 4 GB+ RAM, x64 or ARM64". Install: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash` (`| bash -s stable`, `| bash -s 2.1.89` to pin); "`claude --version` ... prints a version number such as `2.1.211 (Claude Code)`". npm: "the npm package requires Node.js 22 or later ... the package downloads a native binary that doesn't use your Node.js at runtime ... The installed `claude` binary does not itself invoke Node." Platforms: `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-x64-musl`, `linux-arm64-musl`, ... Manifest at `https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/{VERSION}/manifest.json` (GPG fingerprint `31DD DE24 DDFA B679 F42D 7BD2 BAA9 29FF 1A7E CACE`, signed from 2.1.89). apt/dnf/apk repos exist (`https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code/rpm/stable`). Troubleshooting: "When installing Claude Code in a Docker container, installing as root into `/` can cause hangs"; `Error loading shared library` indicates musl/glibc binary mismatch; the VS Code extension "bundles a private copy of the CLI inside the extension directory ... and does not add it to PATH". No numeric glibc minimum is published; the Ubuntu 20.04 floor implies glibc >= 2.31 (inference).

verdict.corrected_claim: The Claude Code CLI is a native single executable (embedded Bun runtime; v2.1.283's linux-x64 binary embeds "Bun v1.4.3") that does not invoke Node.js at runtime; the documented Linux floor is "Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, Alpine Linux 3.19+ ... 4 GB+ RAM, x64 or ARM64 processor". Anthropic publishes no numeric glibc minimum, but the actual current linux-x64 binary (2.1.283, latest as of 2026-09-27; stable = 2.1.274) requires GLIBC_2.26 (symbol reallocarray@@GLIBC_2.26 in .gnu.version_r), so on CentOS 7.9 (glibc 2.17) the dynamic loader refuses it outright; the measured floor is glibc >= 2.26, not the claim's inferred >= 2.31. The CLI therefore must run inside a container image with glibc >= 2.26 (any Ubuntu 18.04+/Debian 10+/RHEL 8+ base; Ubuntu 20.04+ to stay inside the documented floor). The container fixes glibc only: Singularity shares the host kernel (grid kernel 5.15 is fine; the ELF is tagged "for GNU/Linux 3.2.0", Bun recommends >= 5.6) and the host CPU, and the recorded CentOS-7 failures on GitHub (#69980, #64889, #50819) were Bun SIGILL/kernel-epoll faults, not glibc-symbol faults, all closed "not planned", so pin and smoke-test the version inside the image. The native installer (`curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`, which 302-redirects to https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/bootstrap.sh) downloads the binary to `$HOME/.claude/downloads`, verifies its SHA256 against `{VERSION}/manifest.json`, then runs `"$binary_path" install [stable|latest|VERSION]`; the binary places a symlink at `~/.local/bin/claude` into `~/.local/share/claude/versions/` and needs write access to `~/.local/bin/` and `~/.claude/`. Native installs auto-update in the background; `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` stops only the background check (`claude update` and `claude install` still work), `DISABLE_UPDATES=1` blocks all update paths, and since v2.1.207 a custom launcher at `~/.local/bin/claude` is left in place by updates. The VS Code extension (requires VS Code 1.94.0+) bundles a private CLI copy and does not add `claude` to PATH; its `claudeCode.claudeProcessWrapper` setting names an executable to launch the Claude process instead (bundled binary path passed as an argument). Separately and critically: VS Code Remote-SSH's server itself requires "kernel >= 4.18, glibc >=2.28, libstdc++ >= 3.4.25" and lists CentOS/RHEL 8+ only, so Remote-SSH to a CentOS 7.9 compute node is unsupported by VS Code independent of Claude Code.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core claim held; three particulars corrected (glibc floor, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER scope, page attribution) plus one adjacent design blocker found. Set refuted=true only for those particulars; do not discard the confirmed parts below.

CONFIRMED (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup, fetched 2026-09-27): System requirements verbatim: "macOS 13.0+ / Windows 10 1809+ or Windows Server 2019+ / Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 10+ / Alpine Linux 3.19+"; "Hardware: 4 GB+ RAM, x64 or ARM64 processor". Install: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`, `| bash -s stable`, `| bash -s 2.1.89`; "A working installation prints a version number such as `2.1.211 (Claude Code)`". npm: "As of v2.1.198, the npm package requires Node.js 22 or later ... the package downloads a native binary that doesn't use your Node.js at runtime" and "The installed `claude` binary does not itself invoke Node." (claim omitted the "As of v2.1.198" qualifier). Platforms: `darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64-musl, linux-arm64-musl, win32-x64, win32-arm64`. Symlink: "On macOS and Linux, the native installer manages the launcher at `~/.local/bin/claude` as a symlink into `~/.local/share/claude/versions/`. If you replace that launcher with your own script or symlink, auto-update and `claude update` leave it in place ... Before v2.1.207, the auto-updater replaced a custom launcher at that path". Auto-update: "Native installations automatically update in the background"; `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` "only stops the background check; `claude update` and `claude install` still work. To block all update paths, including manual updates, set `DISABLE_UPDATES` instead"; `claude doctor` shows `disabled (set by env: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER)`; settings `autoUpdatesChannel` ("latest" default | "stable"), `minimumVersion`. Manifest: `https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/{VERSION}/manifest.json` + `.sig`; fingerprint `31DD DE24 DDFA B679 F42D 7BD2 BAA9 29FF 1A7E CACE`; "Manifest signatures are available for releases from `2.1.89` onward"; "Linux: binaries are not individually code-signed". dnf: `baseurl=https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code/rpm/stable` (and `/latest`); apt `https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code/apt/stable stable main`; apk `https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code/apk/stable`. Alpine/musl runtime needs `libgcc`, `libstdc++`, `ripgrep` + `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0`. Uninstall: `rm -f ~/.local/bin/claude; rm -rf ~/.local/share/claude`.

CONFIRMED but on a different page than the claim states (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install, not /troubleshooting): "### Install hangs in Docker — When installing Claude Code in a Docker container, installing as root into `/` can cause hangs."; "### Linux musl or glibc binary mismatch — `Error loading shared library libstdc++.so.6: No such file or directory` ... can happen on glibc-based systems that have musl cross-compilation packages installed, causing the installer to misdetect the system as musl"; "The VS Code extension does not place `claude` at this location. It bundles a private copy of the CLI inside the extension directory for its own chat panel and does not add it to PATH."; "A native install shows a symlink into `~/.local/share/claude/versions/`"; "The installer needs write access to `~/.local/bin/` and `~/.claude/`"; WSL1 `Exec format error` workaround `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 "$(readlink -f "$HOME/.local/bin/claude")" "$@"` (issue #38788); "On FreeBSD, the installer reports the platform as unsupported. Before v2.1.205, it treated FreeBSD as Linux".

CONFIRMED (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code): "VS Code 1.94.0 or later"; "The extension bundles its own copy of the CLI ... To run `claude` in VS Code's integrated terminal, you also need the standalone CLI install"; "the extension does not add `claude` to your PATH"; setting `claudeProcessWrapper`: "Executable used to launch the Claude process. The bundled binary path is passed as an argument when present. Set this to a separately installed `claude` binary if the extension build doesn't include one for your platform ... In a wrapped setup, conversations start in Manual mode unless you set `initialPermissionMode`"; "An 'Unsupported platform' error at activation means no binary is bundled for your platform". critical=true: this is the hook for launching the extension's CLI inside Singularity under Remote-SSH.

CONFIRMED (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars): `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` "Set to `1` to disable the auto-updater that checks for new Claude Code versions"; `DISABLE_UPDATES` "Set to `1` to disable update checks entirely"; `CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE`; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` "(default: `~/.claude` on macOS/Linux ...)".

INSTALLER MECHANICS (https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/bootstrap.sh, the 302 target of https://claude.ai/install.sh): `DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL="https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases"`; version from `$DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL/latest` (or `/stable`); downloads to `"$HOME/.claude/downloads"`; musl detection `if [ -f /lib/libc.musl-x86_64.so.1 ] || [ -f /lib/libc.musl-aarch64.so.1 ] || ldd /bin/ls 2>&1 | grep -q musl; then platform="linux-${arch}-musl"`; NO glibc-version check, NO kernel check, NO CPU-flag check; `"$binary_path" install ${TARGET:+"$TARGET"}`; "Checksum verification failed" on mismatch. The script itself never touches ~/.local; the binary's `install` subcommand does.

MANIFEST (https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.89/manifest.json): keys `version` ("2.1.89"), `buildDate` ("2026-03-31T23:01:10Z"), `platforms` (8 entries, each `binary`, `checksum`, `size`). 2.1.283 manifest (fetched via curl) adds keys `manifestSignatureEnforcement`, `commit`, `modsCommit`, `sdkCompat`; linux-x64 `binary=claude size=241556664` (242 MB, plan image size accordingly). `https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest` returned `2.1.283`, `/stable` returned `2.1.274` on 2026-09-27.

MEASURED, critical=true (direct inspection of https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.283/linux-x64/claude, SHA256 1859583ce32920595c61ef868bee52e1b1594f7486db209935e01f1e5e804ae2 = manifest checksum): `file`: "ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, dynamically linked, interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, for GNU/Linux 3.2.0, not stripped"; NEEDED: librt.so.1, libc.so.6, ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, libpthread.so.0, libdl.so.2, libm.so.6 (no libstdc++/libgcc NEEDED in the glibc build); `readelf -V` .gnu.version_r max = GLIBC_2.26 (symbol `reallocarray@@GLIBC_2.26`; also GLIBC_2.17 clock_gettime/clock_nanosleep/secure_getenv); embedded string "Bun v1.4.3". CentOS 7.9 ships glibc 2.17 -> loader error of the form `version 'GLIBC_2.26' not found (required by claude)`. This REFUTES the claim's inference "implies glibc >= 2.31": the measured floor is 2.26 (RHEL 8 / Ubuntu 18.04 / Debian 10 satisfy it). Bun's own docs (https://bun.sh/docs/installation) say "Bun's glibc binaries require glibc 2.17 or newer" and "Bun runs on kernels as old as 3.10 (RHEL 7)", "We recommend kernel version 5.6 or higher" — that 2.17 statement does NOT hold for the Claude Code build.

GITHUB, critical=true for the container plan (all closed "not planned", no maintainer statement of minimum glibc/kernel/CPU): #69980 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/69980, Aug 3 2026) CentOS 7.9.2009, kernel 3.10.0-1160, glibc 2.17, Xeon E5-2697A v4 with avx2: 2.1.170 worked, 2.1.176 "Illegal instruction ... exit: 132" after auto-update swapped the symlink; workaround `ln -sfn ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<last-known-good> ~/.local/bin/claude`. #64889 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/64889) Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, glibc 2.39, Emerald Rapids: SIGILL in bundled "Bun v1.3.14 ... Linux x64 baseline" for 2.1.113–2.1.161; "2.1.112 (last Node-based release)"; env vars BUN_JSC_useJIT=0 etc. ineffective. #50819 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/50819) "Debian 12 container on CentOS 7 host", kernel 3.10: TUI input dead from 2.1.113, `--print` works — i.e. a container did NOT rescue a kernel-level fault. Implication for the grid: kernel 5.15 clears the kernel class; glibc 2.17 is cleared only inside the container; CPU/JIT SIGILLs are host-CPU-bound and are cleared by neither, so pin a version (`bash -s <VERSION>` or `minimumVersion`/`DISABLE_UPDATES=1`) and run `claude --version` as a smoke test inside the image on each node type. Note #64889/#69980 state the Node->Bun single-executable switch occurred at 2.1.113 (reporter text, not official docs).

ADJACENT BLOCKER, critical=true, outside this claim's original scope (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/linux): VS Code Server prerequisites "kernel >= 4.18, glibc >=2.28, libstdc++ >= 3.4.25"; supported "CentOS/RHEL 64-bit x86 (8+)", "Ubuntu ... (20.04+)", "Debian ... (Buster/10+)"; CentOS 7 / RHEL 7 not supported. VS Code 1.139 Remote-SSH to a CentOS 7.9 compute node will fail on the same glibc 2.17 before Claude Code is even involved; the design needs either the VS Code Server also inside the container (or a sysroot workaround, not on the official page fetched) or a different connection model (e.g. terminal/tunnel from inside the Singularity job).

NOT FOUND: no Anthropic page publishes a numeric glibc minimum; no maintainer statement on CentOS/RHEL 7. WebSearch budget was exhausted this session; all evidence above is from fetched official pages, the fetched installer script, the fetched manifests, the downloaded binary, and three GitHub issues.

findings.claim: `-p` mode runs skills/commands from the prompt string (`/skill-name`), accepts `/model`, `/effort`, `/config key=value`, `/mcp`, `/compact`, `/clear` as prompt text (v2.1.205+), but not terminal-only commands such as `/login`.
findings.detail: Headless note verbatim: "User-invoked skills and custom commands work. Include `/skill-name` in the prompt string and Claude Code expands it before running. Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available. `/model`, `/effort`, `/fast`, `/color`, and `/rename` accept the value as an argument ... `/mcp` with no argument prints a text summary ... To change a setting, pass `key=value` to `/config`, for example `/config thinking=false`." Cost-tracking: `/clear`, `/reset`, `/new` in streaming input start a new `session_id` and reset running totals.

findings.claim: CLI subcommands relevant to the design: `claude auth login [--console|--sso|--email]`, `claude auth status [--text]`, `claude auth logout`, `claude setup-token`, `claude doctor`, `claude update`, `claude install [stable|latest|<version>]`, `claude mcp ...`, `claude project purge [path] [--dry-run]`, `claude agents --json`, `claude daemon status`, `claude remote-control`.
findings.detail: From the CLI commands table: `claude auth login` "Sign in to Anthropic account" (`claude auth login --console`), `claude auth status` "Show authentication status" (`--text` human-readable), `claude setup-token` "Generate long-lived OAuth token for CI", `claude doctor` "Print installation and settings diagnostics" (read-only, no session), `claude install [version]`, `claude update`, `claude project purge [path]` "Delete local Claude Code state for project", `claude agents --json [--all] [--cwd <path>]`, `claude attach <id>`, `claude logs <id>`, `claude stop|rm|respawn <id>`, `claude daemon status`, `claude daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]`. `claude update` prints `Successfully updated from <old version> to version <new version>` or `Claude Code is up to date (<version>)`.

findings.claim: Interrupting a running `-p` turn: SIGINT ends the turn (a result is recorded); SIGTERM exits 143 with no result and runs only `SessionEnd` hooks; on resume the interrupted turn is left as-is unless `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1`.
findings.detail: Headless verbatim: "On SIGTERM, Claude Code terminates the process tree of any Bash command that is still running. Claude Code then runs `SessionEnd` hooks and exits ... Running a command: Claude Code records the command as killed in the session. Waiting for an answer to a permission prompt: ... Claude Code leaves the prompt unanswered." "When you resume the session, Claude Code leaves the interrupted turn as it is, and your next prompt drives the conversation. To have Claude Code continue the interrupted turn on resume instead, set `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1`." Sessions page: a tool still running at crash time "doesn't finish or run again when you resume" (v2.1.281+ marks it cut off).

verdict.corrected_claim: Interrupting a running `claude -p` turn (Claude Code v2.1.236 or later; local install is v2.1.283): SIGTERM exits with code 143, leaves the in-progress turn unfinished and records no result for it, terminates the process tree of any running Bash command (recorded in the session as killed), leaves any pending permission prompt unanswered, starts no new tool call or model request, and runs no hook other than `SessionEnd` (default budget 1.5 s; raise with per-hook `timeout` up to 60 s or `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS`). To end the turn instead, send SIGINT or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()` before stopping the process; the docs state this by contrast with SIGTERM's "records no result" and, for `interrupt()`, that the receipt "arrives before the interrupted turn's SDKResultMessage", but they do not state SIGINT's exit code or spell out "a result is recorded" for SIGINT, and `Stop` hooks do not run on a user interrupt. On resume (`claude -p --resume <session-id>` or `--continue`), the interrupted turn is left as-is and the next prompt drives the conversation; a tool still running at process end is marked cut off and Claude is told to check whether it took effect (v2.1.281+; earlier versions dropped the call or showed it as user-interrupted). Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1` makes Claude Code continue the interrupted turn automatically (sending `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT`, default "Continue from where you left off."), bounded by `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS` (v2.1.211+; a turn that ended in an API error auto-resumes only within six hours); `=0` disables it only on v2.1.221+.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds; not refuted. Two soft spots and several version qualifiers added. critical=true for the Ashley design (persistent -p Claude Code in a Slurm job that will be SIGTERM'd at wall-time or requeue, then resumed).

SOURCE 1 (fetched 2026-09-27, raw markdown https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md, section "### Stop a run with SIGTERM"), verbatim: "If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example with `kill` or from a process supervisor, Claude Code exits with code 143. Claude Code leaves the turn that was in progress unfinished and records no result for it. To end the turn instead, send SIGINT, or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()`, before you stop the process." / "On SIGTERM, Claude Code terminates the process tree of any Bash command that is still running. Claude Code then runs [`SessionEnd` hooks] and exits. While exiting, Claude Code starts no new tool call, sends no new model request, and runs no hook other than `SessionEnd`." / "* **Running a command**: Claude Code records the command as killed in the session. * **Waiting for an answer to a permission prompt**: if you send SIGTERM to the process, Claude Code leaves the prompt unanswered. If your program closes the session through the Agent SDK, the SDK ends Claude Code's input before sending any signal, and Claude Code cancels the prompt as soon as the input ends." / "When you [resume the session], Claude Code leaves the interrupted turn as it is, and your next prompt drives the conversation. To have Claude Code continue the interrupted turn on resume instead, set [`CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1`]." -> Every SIGTERM/resume element of the claim is confirmed verbatim.

SOFT SPOT A (SIGINT "a result is recorded"): the word "SIGINT" appears exactly once across headless.md, sessions.md, hooks.md, env-vars.md and agent-sdk/typescript.md (grep of the raw files), in the sentence above. The docs do not state SIGINT's exit code in -p mode nor literally that a result is emitted; "ends the turn" is asserted only by contrast with SIGTERM's "records no result". Supporting: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript.md, SDKControlInterruptResponse: "on a clean interrupt it arrives before the interrupted turn's [`SDKResultMessage`]" (so interrupt() yields a result message); "`interrupt()` ... Only available in streaming input mode"; `SDKResultMessage` subtypes are only "success" | "error_max_turns" | "error_during_execution" | "error_max_budget_usd" | "error_max_structured_output_retries" (no interrupted subtype). Changelog (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md): "Fixed Ctrl+C not working in `-p` (print) mode"; "Fixed SDK/print mode not preserving the partial assistant response in conversation history when interrupted mid-stream"; "Fixed external SIGINT (e.g. IDE stop button, `kill -INT`) not running graceful shutdown". Treat "result recorded on SIGINT" as plausible-by-inference, not quoted.

SOFT SPOT B (hooks on SIGINT): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md "### Stop": "Runs when the main Claude Code agent has finished responding. Does not run if the stoppage occurred due to a user interrupt. API errors fire [StopFailure] instead." So SIGINT ends the turn but does not fire Stop.

VERSION QUALIFIERS from CHANGELOG.md (line->header mapped with awk): v2.1.212: "Fixed SIGTERM during a running Bash tool orphaning the command's process tree in print/SDK mode; the CLI now aborts the turn, kills the tree, and exits 143". v2.1.236: "SIGTERM in print/SDK mode no longer records an interrupted turn or synthetic tool denials before exiting; running commands are still terminated and the process still exits with code 143" (so "no result recorded" is v2.1.236+; before that an interrupted-turn record was written). v2.1.221: "Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=0` not disabling interrupted-turn auto-resume; falsy values are now honored". v2.1.269: "Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN` re-running a turn that had failed with an API error over 6 hours earlier, or longer ago than `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS` when set". v2.1.274: "Fixed a local `claude -p --resume` started with `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN` not reporting background tasks the previous process left unfinished". v2.1.281: "Fixed resuming a session that ended during a tool call: Claude now sees the call and is told its outcome is unknown, and a manual resume no longer adds a hidden \"Continue\" message".

SESSIONS PAGE (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md, "What a resumed session restores"), verbatim: "A tool that was still running when the previous process ended, for example in a crash, doesn't finish or run again when you resume. Claude sees the call marked as cut off before its result was recorded and is told to check whether it took effect before running it again, unless [`CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN`] is set. Before v2.1.281, Claude Code dropped the cut-off call from the conversation or showed it to Claude as one you interrupted." Also: "Claude Code leaves sessions created with [`claude -p`] or the [Agent SDK] out of the session picker and out of `claude --continue`. You can still resume one by passing its session ID to `claude --resume <session-id>`. ... When you run [`claude -p --continue`], Claude Code includes `-p`, SDK, and `/loop` sessions." Resume by session ID works from any directory on v2.1.223+.

ENV VARS (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.md, table rows), verbatim: "`CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN` | Set to `1` to automatically resume if the previous session ended mid-turn. Used in SDK mode so the model continues without requiring the SDK to re-send the prompt. To turn this off, unset the variable or set it to `0`. Before v2.1.221, Claude Code ignored `0` and other falsy values..." / "`CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS` | Maximum age in milliseconds of the last transcript message for a session that ended mid-turn to continue automatically on resume. ... Unset or `0` means no bound, except that a turn whose last request failed with an API error resumes only while that error is less than six hours old. ... a negative or non-numeric value applies a one-hour bound. Spawn scripts for long-running agents can set this so a restart against an old transcript doesn't re-run a stale prompt. ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.211 or later" / "`CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT` | Override the continuation message Claude Code sends to Claude when `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN` continues an interrupted turn instead of resending its prompt ... Defaults to `Continue from where you left off.`"

SESSIONEND DETAILS RELEVANT TO SLURM SIGTERM->KillWait->SIGKILL (hooks.md "### SessionEnd"): `reason` values are only `clear`, `resume`, `logout`, `prompt_input_exit`, `other` (`bypass_permissions_disabled` removed in v2.1.234); there is no signal-specific reason, and the docs do not say which reason a SIGTERM exit reports. "SessionEnd hooks have a default timeout of 1.5 seconds." Extend via per-hook `timeout` ("The overall budget rises automatically to match the highest per-hook `timeout` in your settings files, up to 60 seconds") or "`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS` ... The value you set also becomes the timeout for each hook without its own `timeout`" (v2.1.268+; before that it raised only the overall budget). "SessionEnd hooks have no decision control. They can't block session termination".

RELATED -p EXIT BEHAVIOUR (headless.md "Background tasks at exit"): a background Bash task "is terminated about five seconds after Claude has returned its final result and stdin has closed"; background subagents/workflows hold the process open up to `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default `600000`, v2.1.182+, `0` = no cap).

NOT FOUND ANYWHERE: SIGINT exit code in -p mode; an explicit statement that SIGINT writes a `result` line; which SessionEnd `reason` SIGTERM produces. WebSearch budget was exhausted for this session (200/200), so verification used WebFetch plus raw-markdown curl of the same official pages and the official CHANGELOG; no third-party sources were needed or used.

topics_verified.recommendation: Run one persistent process per student inside the Singularity container (never on the CentOS 7.9 host: the binary's documented floor is Ubuntu 20.04/Debian 10) as the student's own non-root UID, launched as: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-prompts none --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Bash(sbatch *)" ... [--add-dir ...] [--max-budget-usd N]` and optionally `--session-id <uuidv4>` you generate so the laptop knows the id before the first `result`. Do NOT pass `--bare` (it refuses OAuth and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`), do NOT set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the job environment (it silently overrides the subscription in `-p`), and avoid `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (refused as root, and the docs reserve it for isolated containers; if used, run as a normal user and understand `IS_SANDBOX`). Feed prompts as one NDJSON line each: `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}}` (content may be a block array with base64 images); treat every `{"type":"result",...}` line as end-of-turn keyed by `session_id`, read `subtype` before `result` (the key is absent on error/interrupted turns), and keep the process alive by keeping stdin open; close stdin to exit cleanly, send SIGINT to end a turn, and expect exit 143 on SIGTERM. Use `{"type":"control_request","request":{"subtype":"interrupt","request_id":"..."}}` for cancel only as best-effort (feature-detect via `system/init`.`capabilities`), since the CLI-level control protocol is undocumented. Authenticate with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token` run on the student's laptop (one-year token, Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise only, not refreshed after 401, so the extension must detect `authentication_failed`/`OAuth token revoked` and prompt re-mint); keep the token in the job's environment, not in a settings file on shared storage. Put `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` on the student's CephFS path (e.g. `/rs/rs_grp_oschome/<id>/.claude`) with `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR` off the swept `/tmp`, set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_CONNECT_IDE=0`, pin the binary version in the image, and note Anthropic's statement that `~/.claude` is not recommended on network filesystems: one writer per config dir at a time, and resume after a job restart with `claude -p --resume <session-id>` (which searches all projects under that config dir) rather than sharing a live transcript. Set `cleanupPeriodDays` high (e.g. 3650) if transcripts must outlive 30 days. Before shipping, get written clarification from Anthropic on whether a university-distributed extension that wraps each student's own subscription falls under "third party developers ... offer claude.ai login or rate limits", because that note is the single largest policy risk; the 2026-06-16 support article confirms `claude -p` draws on the subscription's own usage limits.
open_questions: The CLI-level stdin protocol for `--input-format stream-json` (user envelope, control_request/control_response for interrupt, set_permission_mode, initialize) is not in Anthropic's docs (issue #24594 closed not-planned); the shapes above come from the SDK's TypeScript types and a Sept-2026 bug report and should be verified against the pinned binary version before relying on interrupt.
No numeric glibc minimum is published for the native binary; the container image's glibc must be tested (Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 10+ documented; CentOS 7.9's 2.17 is presumed unsupported).

Whether a single `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` on CephFS/Panasas (network FS) is safe for one long-lived writer plus occasional `claude -p --resume` readers is unverified; Anthropic says sharing `~/.claude` over network filesystems is not recommended but gives no failure mode.

Whether a university-distributed VS Code extension that drives `claude -p` with each student's own Pro/Max token counts as a 'third party developer offering claude.ai login or rate limits' under the Agent SDK overview note needs written confirmation from Anthropic; press reports describe active enforcement against third-party harnesses in 2026.
Behavior of a 30-day-wall process when the subscription's 5-hour/weekly usage window is exhausted (rate_limit error category vs. process exit) is not documented for stream-json input mode.

Whether `claude setup-token` can complete over an SSH session without a browser on the same machine (the `/login` flow has a 'Paste code here if prompted' fallback; setup-token is said to use the same flow but the fallback is not stated for it) — plan to mint the token on the laptop and ship it to the job environment.

`--session-id` is documented in the raw CLI reference as 'must be a valid UUID'; whether a v4 UUID generated by the extension is accepted for a brand-new session in `-p --input-format stream-json` (vs. only for resume) should be tested.

The docs say `--bare` 'will become the default for `-p` in a future release'; if that lands, subscription-backed `-p` would break unless an opt-out flag exists — pin the binary version and watch the changelog.

topics_verified.topic: Claude Pro/Max subscription rate limits, Claude Code -p limit behaviour, extra usage, concurrency, and the Consumer Terms / Usage Policy / Claude Code legal page as they bear on running a student's Claude Code persistently on an HPC node (and on a lab pooling subscriptions)
topics_verified.summary: Pro and Max quotas are per-account rolling allowances: a five-hour session window plus a weekly window that resets at a fixed time assigned to the account, shared across claude.ai, Desktop, Cowork and Claude Code, with additional model-family (Opus/Sonnet) windows; usage credits ("extra usage", formerly pay-as-you-go) can be enabled by the subscriber at claude.ai Settings > Usage and are billed at standard API rates with a monthly spend limit, and they apply to Claude Code. When a window is exhausted the CLI prints one of four documented strings ("You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm", "... weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am", "... Opus limit ...", "... Sonnet limit ...") and blocks requests until the reset; the stream-json protocol emits a `rate_limit_event` with `status: "rejected"`, `resetsAt`, `utilization` and, when included usage is gone and credits are off, `errorCode: "credits_required"`; the final `result` message carries `is_error` and `api_error_status` (HTTP status), and a failed `-p` run exits non-zero with the failure text placed in the `result` field on stdout. The documented `-p` JSON body for a subscription limit is not spelled out verbatim anywhere I could fetch, so that exact payload must be captured empirically. `--fallback-model` does not help: the model-config page says rate-limit, billing and authentication errors "never trigger a switch". The interactive auto-continue-at-reset feature (`autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, v2.1.234+) is documented for interactive claude.ai-signed-in sessions only, so an unattended worker must implement its own wait using `resetsAt`. Nothing in the docs or terms forbids one person running several Claude Code sessions or machines on one subscription; they share the same quota, and GitHub issue #96872 shows an infrastructure 429 ("Rate limited", `rateLimits: null`) appearing at 6+ concurrent sessions at only 27% quota. Headless use of a subscription is explicitly sanctioned: `claude setup-token` mints a one-year OAuth token for "CI pipelines, scripts, or other environments where interactive browser login isn't available", set as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, requiring Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, and not read in `--bare` mode. The legal side is unambiguous against pooling: the Consumer Terms say "You may not share your Account login information, Anthropic API key, or Account credentials with anyone else. You also may not make your Account available to anyone else"; the Claude Code legal page says OAuth is "intended exclusively for purchasers" of subscription plans "to support ordinary use", that "Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage", that customers "may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf", and that developers "may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." The Consumer Terms contain no explicit multiple-accounts or "rate limit" clause; the operative anti-circumvention text is "bypassing any of our systems or protective measures" (Consumer Terms) and the AUP's ban-evasion and multi-account-coordination clauses. Legitimate shared routes are Team seats (2-150 seats; Standard $20-25 at 1.25x Pro, Premium $100-125 at 6.25x Pro, per-member limits, admin spend limits on usage credits), Enterprise (seat + usage at API rates), Console API keys with workspace spend/rate limits and a per-user-capped "Claude Code" workspace, and the institution-level Claude for Education plan (contact sales; no individual student price is published).

findings.claim: Pro and Max usage limits are shared across Claude (web/desktop) and Claude Code; all activity counts against the same per-account allowance.
findings.detail: Support article 'Using Claude Code with your Pro or Max plan' (updated August 19, 2026): "Both Pro and Max plans offer usage limits that are shared across Claude and Claude Code, meaning all activity in both tools counts against the same usage limits." The 'How do usage and length limits work?' article: "Your usage of all different Claude product surfaces (claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Desktop) counts towards the same usage limit."

verdict.corrected_claim: Pro and Max usage limits are shared across claude.ai (web/desktop/mobile), Claude Code (terminal, IDE extensions) and other Claude surfaces; there is no separate Claude Code quota. The shared allowance is not a single number but a set of concurrently metered windows: a rolling five-hour session limit and a weekly limit (both shared across all models), plus per-model-family sub-limits (Opus, Sonnet) that block only that family. Anthropic tunes Claude Code's share of these windows independently of chat (May 6, 2026: "Doubling Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans"), so "shared" means one pool, not identical accounting per surface.
verdict.evidence:
CLAIM HOLDS (critical=true for the Ashley design: a persistent Claude Code job on the grid draws down the student's own claude.ai allowance).

Official confirmations fetched 2026-09-27:
1. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11145838-using-claude-code-with-your-pro-or-max-plan (page now titled "Use Claude Code with your Pro or Max plan"; slug still resolves; shows only "Updated over a week ago" — the "August 19, 2026" date in the claim DETAIL could NOT be verified). Verbatim: "Both Pro and Max plans offer usage limits that are shared across Claude and Claude Code, meaning all activity in both tools counts against the same usage limits." Covers Pro, Max 5x, Max 20x; IDE (VS Code/Cursor/JetBrains) usage counts toward the same limits; Team/Enterprise deferred to article 11845131.
2. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work — verbatim: "Note that your usage of all different Claude product surfaces (claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Desktop) counts towards the same usage limit."
3. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs — for Team/Enterprise seats: "each member's Claude Code usage draws from a per-seat allowance that resets on a rolling five-hour window and a weekly window. The allowance is shared with Claude chat and Cowork". Also: "/usage ... figures are approximate and computed from local session history on this machine, so usage from other devices or claude.ai is not included" (the attribution breakdown is per-machine; the plan usage BARS are account-wide). Cache TTL "is an hour on a subscription and drops to five minutes once you're drawing on usage credits".
4. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11049741-what-is-the-max-plan — "Your session-based usage limit will reset every five hours. Max plans also have a weekly usage limit that applies across all models." "Max 5x includes five times the Pro plan's per-session usage allowance"; "Max 20x includes 20 times".
5. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices — Settings > Usage shows "five-hour session and weekly usage limits" for "Pro, Max, Team, or seat-based Enterprise plan"; weekly bar "for all models, and for Fable (if included in your plan)".

Precision qualifiers (why corrected_claim is tightened, not refuted):
A. Multiple concurrent windows, not one allowance. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md (curl, 527 KB, section "You've hit your session limit"): error strings verbatim "You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm", "You've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am", "You've hit your Opus limit · resets 3:45pm", "You've hit your Sonnet limit · resets 3:45pm". "The session and weekly limits are shared across all models, so switching models doesn't restore access. The Opus and Sonnet limits each apply only to requests to that model family, so switching to a model outside the family with /model keeps you working." "Usage counts against the session and weekly allowances at the same time. A single burst of heavy activity, such as a large workflow fanout, can exhaust the weekly allowance before the session window resets." Warning string: "You've used 85% of your session limit · resets 3:45pm". Wait line: "Usage limit reached · continuing automatically at 3:45pm · esc to cancel" (Claude Code >= v2.1.234; managed setting `autoContinueAtUsageLimit`; `/rate-limit-options`; status line `rate_limits` fields) — directly relevant to a persistent grid daemon that should survive a limit.
B. Claude Code's share is tuned separately from chat. https://www.anthropic.com/news/higher-limits-spacex (May 6, 2026): "Doubling Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans." and "Removing the peak hours limit reduction on Claude Code for Pro and Max accounts." The post does not state whether claude.ai chat limits changed; how a Claude-Code-specific doubling is implemented inside a shared pool is NOT documented anywhere official I found — unknown.
C. Pool has widened over 2026: Claude Design folded into the same pool ~May 27-28, 2026 per user reports (https://piunikaweb.com/2026/05/28/claude-design-usage-limits-with-claude-ai-and-claude-code/ — not official; no Anthropic changelog found). Cowork is named as sharing on the official costs page.
D. Extra usage: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-extra-usage-for-paid-claude-plans — usage credits "billed at standard API rates" for "Pro, Max 5x, or Max 20x", apply to claude.ai and "Claude Code terminal usage"; "Your plan's included usage limit will reset every five hours once you reach it." Managed in Claude Code via `/usage-credits` (requires `/login` with claude.ai subscription, not API key).

Design consequences: a long-lived Claude Code session sends full context per turn ("a one-line question in a session that has been open all day still draws usage for the whole conversation"); scheduled tasks, cross-session messages and subagents all bill the same shared pool. Students on Pro will exhaust the weekly window fastest.

findings.claim: Max plans have a five-hour session limit and a separate weekly limit across all models; the weekly limit resets at a fixed per-account time; Max 5x/20x are 5x/20x the Pro per-session allowance; Anthropic reserves the right to add other caps.

findings.claim: Claude Code prints four documented usage-limit strings and blocks further requests until the reset time in the message; session and weekly limits span all models, Opus/Sonnet limits are per model family; a warning appears at 85%.
findings.detail: Error reference, section 'You've hit your session limit': exact strings `You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am`, `You've hit your Opus limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your Sonnet limit · resets 3:45pm`. "Claude Code blocks further requests until the reset time shown in the message. The session and weekly limits are shared across all models, so switching models doesn't restore access." Warning form: `You've used 85% of your session limit · resets 3:45pm`. "Usage counts against the session and weekly allowances at the same time. A single burst of heavy activity, such as a large workflow fanout, can exhaust the weekly allowance before the session window resets."

verdict.corrected_claim: Claude Code's error reference documents four usage-limit messages verbatim: `You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am`, `You've hit your Opus limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your Sonnet limit · resets 3:45pm`; the actually printed string appends the IANA timezone in parentheses, e.g. `You've hit your session limit · resets 1:10am (Europe/Moscow)`, so match on the prefix, not the whole line. The docs state "Claude Code blocks further requests until the reset time shown in the message"; the session and weekly limits are shared across all models, while the Opus and Sonnet limits "each apply only to requests to that model family" and switching outside the family with `/model` keeps you working. Since v2.1.234, in an INTERACTIVE session signed in with a claude.ai subscription, Claude Code by default waits in the open session (`Usage limit reached · continuing automatically at 3:45pm · esc to cancel`) and auto-continues after the reset (setting `autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, `/config` row "Continue automatically at usage limit"); it does NOT offer this wait for `-p` runs or background sessions, does not start it on its own in Remote Control or agent-team teammate sessions or when the reset is more than 24 h away (weekly limit), and re-arms at most twice in a row. The 85% figure is NOT a documented threshold: the docs say Claude Code "can warn you" with "a message such as `You've used 85% of your session limit · resets 3:45pm`"; the documented way to watch remaining allowance continuously is the statusline JSON `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage` / `rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage` (0-100) plus `resets_at` (Unix epoch seconds), present only for claude.ai Pro/Max subscribers after the first API response. Usage counts against the session and weekly allowances at the same time; "A single burst of heavy activity, such as a large workflow fanout, can exhaust the weekly allowance before the session window resets."

findings.claim: In stream-json / Agent SDK output, hitting a subscription limit is signalled by a `rate_limit_event` message with `status: "rejected"`, a `resetsAt` epoch and `utilization`; when included usage is exhausted and credits are unavailable it carries `errorCode: "credits_required"`.
findings.detail: TypeScript SDK reference, `SDKRateLimitEvent`: `type: "rate_limit_event"; rate_limit_info: { status: "allowed" | "allowed_warning" | "rejected"; resetsAt?: number; utilization?: number; errorCode?: "credits_required"; canUserPurchaseCredits?: boolean; hasChargeableSavedPaymentMethod?: boolean }`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later." Python SDK page documents `RateLimitInfo` with `rateLimitType: Literal["five_hour", "seven_day", "overage"]`, `overageStatus`, `isUsingOverage`. verdict.corrected_claim: In Agent SDK output (TypeScript `SDKMessage` union / Python `Message` union), a subscription rate-limit state change is signalled by a `type: "rate_limit_event"` message whose `rate_limit_info.status` is `"allowed" | "allowed_warning" | "rejected"`, with optional `resetsAt` (Unix epoch) and `utilization` (0.0-1.0); when a claude.ai subscription's included usage is exhausted the rejection carries `errorCode: "credits_required"` plus `canUserPurchaseCredits` and `hasChargeableSavedPaymentMethod` (TypeScript type; requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later, documented only on the TS SDK page, not in the CHANGELOG 2.1.181 entry). CORRECTIONS TO THE DETAIL: the Python `RateLimitInfo` dataclass uses snake_case fields `status`, `resets_at`, `rate_limit_type`, `utilization`, `overage_status`, `overage_resets_at`, `overage_disabled_reason`, `raw`; `RateLimitType = Literal["five_hour", "seven_day", "seven_day_opus", "seven_day_sonnet", "overage"]` (five values, not three); there is NO `isUsingOverage`/`is_using_overage` field; and the Python dataclass does NOT model `errorCode`/`credits_required`, `canUserPurchaseCredits` or `hasChargeableSavedPaymentMethod` (only reachable via `raw`, "Full raw dict from the CLI, including fields not modeled above"). The event is an observability event emitted on status CHANGE (e.g. allowed -> allowed_warning), not only on rejection; the quota 429 also surfaces as `SDKAssistantMessage.error: 'rate_limit'` and `system/api_retry` `error: "rate_limit"`. Status-line JSON exposes `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage` (0-100), `rate_limits.five_hour.resets_at` (Unix epoch seconds), `rate_limits.seven_day.*` and (v2.1.251+) `rate_limits.spend_limit.*`, present only for claude.ai Pro/Max subscribers (or behind a Claude apps gateway spend limit) and only after the first API response; a window is dropped once its `resets_at` passes. The CLI headless page (`claude -p --output-format stream-json`) does not list `rate_limit_event` among documented stream events; it is documented only on the SDK reference pages.

findings.claim: The final `result` message in `--output-format json` carries `is_error: boolean` and `api_error_status` (HTTP status of the API error that ended the turn); error runs use subtypes `error_max_turns`, `error_during_execution`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_max_structured_output_retries` with an `errors: string[]` array and no `result` field; the process exits non-zero on failure and puts in-run failure text in `result` on stdout.
findings.detail: TypeScript SDK `SDKResultMessage`: success arm has `subtype: "success"`, `is_error: boolean`, `api_error_status?: number | null`, `result: string`, `terminal_reason` (includes `"api_error"`, `"blocking_limit"`, `"budget_exhausted"`); error arm has `errors: string[]` and no `result`. Headless page: "Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails ... When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout." SDK agent-loop page: "The underlying Claude Code process also exits with a nonzero code." Agent SDK troubleshooting: Python raises `ProcessError` (`Command failed with exit code 1`) or `ResultError` (`Claude Code returned an error result: <the CLI's own error report>`). No page states the exact JSON body or exit code for a subscription usage-limit rejection; GitHub issue #87983 (v2.1.235, Aug 2026, subscription auth from a systemd unit) reports `claude -p "/usage" --output-format json` sometimes exiting 5 or returning `is_error: false` with no `result` key.

verdict.corrected_claim: In `claude -p --output-format json` (and as the last line of `stream-json`), the final `result` object has two arms. (1) `subtype: "success"`: carries `is_error: boolean`, `api_error_status?: number | null`, `result: string`, `stop_reason`, `num_turns`, `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, optional `structured_output`, optional `terminal_reason`. `api_error_status` is populated ONLY on this arm: "the HTTP status code of the API error that terminated the conversation. Absent or null when the turn ended without an API error." (2) `subtype` in {`error_max_turns`, `error_during_execution`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_max_structured_output_retries`}: carries `errors: string[]`, `is_error` (always true), optional `terminal_reason`, optional `startup_failure_reason`, and NO `result` field. CRITICAL correction: an API failure that ends the run — missing/expired auth, subscription usage limit, 429, model-not-found 404 — is NOT reported with an `error_*` subtype. Claude Code reports `subtype: "success"` with `is_error: true`, `api_error_status` set (e.g. 404, 429), `terminal_reason` e.g. `"api_error"`, and the error text in `result` (which "can be empty"; e.g. `"API Error: Rate limit reached"`, `"There's an issue with the selected model (...)"`, `"You've hit your session limit · resets ..."`). The `error_*` subtypes are reserved for limits you set (`--max-turns`, `--max-budget-usd`, structured-output retries) and for `error_during_execution` (cancellation, crash, known startup failure). A consumer must therefore test `is_error` (or `terminal_reason`), never `subtype !== "success"` alone. Exit code: docs state "Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails" and "When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout"; a 404 API failure is reported with exit code 1 at v2.1.173 (SDK issue #1031). However, an open issue (#79500, v2.1.49, has-repro) shows a rate-limit API error returning `subtype:"success"`, `is_error:true`, exit code 0; and #87983 (v2.1.235) shows `claude -p "/usage" --output-format json` intermittently exiting 5 or exiting 0 with `is_error:false` and no `result` key. The exact exit code and `terminal_reason` value for a subscription usage-limit rejection are not documented anywhere official. Both SDKs raise on `is_error: true` regardless of subtype: Python `ResultError` (subclass of `ProcessError`, since claude-agent-sdk 0.2.140; before that a plain `Exception`) with attributes `subtype`, `errors`, `result`, `api_error_status`, `terminal_reason`, `session_id`, `data`; a bare `ProcessError` message is `Command failed with exit code 1 (exit code: 1)` / `Error output: Check stderr output for details` (fixed text). TypeScript rejects the `for await` loop with a plain `Error`: `Claude Code returned an error result: <text>` or `Claude Code process exited with code 1. stderr: <tail>`. SIGTERM exits 143 with no result recorded.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: the field names and error subtypes in the claim are correct, but the claim's taxonomy is subtly wrong in the way that matters for our design: it says "error runs use subtypes error_*" and separately "puts in-run failure text in result" without stating that API failures (auth, usage limit, 429, 404) travel on the SUCCESS arm with is_error=true. Exit-code guarantee is documented but contradicted by an open issue at v2.1.49 and intermittent at v2.1.235.

findings.claim: The raw API rejection for a subscription usage limit is HTTP 429 `rate_limit_error` with message "This request would exceed your account's rate limit. Please try again later."; Claude Code's internal string form is `Claude AI usage limit reached|<unix epoch reset>` and the user-facing form was "Claude usage limit reached. Your limit will reset at 2pm (America/New_York)".
findings.detail: GitHub issues titled `Claude AI usage limit reached|1749924000` (#2087, v1.0.24, 2025-06-14), `...|1762952400` (#11429, v1.0.83, 2025-11-11) log `Error: 429 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"This request would exceed your account's rate limit. Please try again later."}}`; #5977 quotes "Claude usage limit reached. Your limit will reset at 2pm (America/New_York)". These are older CLI versions; the current CLI wording is the 'You've hit your ... limit' family. The stream-json `system/api_retry` event's `error` category list includes `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `billing_error`, `account_on_hold`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`.

findings.claim: `--fallback-model` does not help with subscription usage limits: rate-limit, billing and authentication errors never trigger a fallback switch.
findings.detail: Model configuration, 'Fallback model chains': "When the primary model is overloaded, unavailable, or returns another non-retryable server error, Claude Code can switch to a fallback model instead of failing the request. Authentication, billing, rate-limit, request-size, and transport errors ... never trigger a switch; those follow their normal retry and error handling." Flag: `claude --fallback-model sonnet,haiku` (comma list, capped at three); persistent form is the `fallbackModel` settings array. CLI reference describes the flag as fallback "when the primary model is overloaded or not available, for example a retired model".

verdict.corrected_claim: `--fallback-model` does not help with subscription usage limits: rate-limit, billing and authentication errors never trigger a fallback switch.
verdict.evidence:
CLAIM HOLDS (critical=true for the Ashley design: a persistent Claude Code job on a student's Pro/Max subscription cannot use --fallback-model to survive "You've hit your session limit" / "You've hit your weekly limit"; it will block until the reset time).

PRIMARY SOURCE, fetched 2026-09-27, raw markdown https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md, section "### Fallback model chains", verbatim: "When the primary model is overloaded, unavailable, or returns another non-retryable server error, Claude Code can switch to a fallback model instead of failing the request. Authentication, billing, rate-limit, request-size, and transport errors, and a denial by your organization's policy check, never trigger a switch; those follow their normal retry and error handling." Also: "The switch lasts for the current turn only, so your next message tries the primary model first again." / "Claude Code caps chains at three models after duplicate removal and ignores extra entries." / flag: `claude --fallback-model sonnet,haiku` ("accepts a comma-separated list") / settings: `{"fallbackModel": ["claude-sonnet-5", "claude-haiku-4-5"]}` (array) / "The `--fallback-model` flag takes precedence over the `fallbackModel` setting." / "`\"default\"` expands to the default model" / "Claude Code doesn't confirm the chain at startup and `/status` doesn't display it." / entries outside `availableModels` are dropped; compaction won't fall back to a model with a smaller context window. Note the docs list MORE never-switch classes than the claim names: request-size, transport, and org inference-hook policy denial (the last since v2.1.239) in addition to auth/billing/rate-limit.

CLI REFERENCE https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (fetched), `--fallback-model` row verbatim: "Enable automatic fallback to the specified model(s) when the primary model is overloaded or not available, for example a retired model. Accepts a comma-separated list tried in order." Example `claude --fallback-model sonnet,haiku`.

SETTINGS REFERENCE https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md `### fallbackModel` verbatim: "Name backup models for Claude Code to try, in order, when your primary model is overloaded or unavailable... Without a chain, Claude Code retries the same model and then surfaces the server's error" / "Type: array of model aliases or IDs" / "Default: unset" / "this key doesn't merge across settings files: the highest-precedence file that defines it supplies the whole chain" / "keeps at most three distinct allowed models".

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS ON A SUBSCRIPTION LIMIT, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md, "Usage limits" section verbatim: exact strings `You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am`, `You've hit your Opus limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your Sonnet limit · resets 3:45pm`. "Claude Code blocks further requests until the reset time shown in the message. The session and weekly limits are shared across all models, so switching models doesn't restore access. The Opus and Sonnet limits each apply only to requests to that model family, so switching to a model outside the family with `/model` keeps you working." (That is a MANUAL `/model` switch, not the fallback chain.) Warning string: `You've used 85% of your session limit · resets 3:45pm`; remaining allowance is exposed via `rate_limits` fields in a custom status line. Same page, "Automatic retries": "Claude Code retries transient failures up to 10 times with exponential backoff" including "Temporary 429 throttles, but not a gateway's spend-limit `429`"; "When you're signed in with a claude.ai subscription, this includes 429 throttles that don't carry your plan's quota headers. Before v2.1.199, Claude Code retried those throttles only for API key and Enterprise sign-ins." `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1` retries `429`/`529` capacity errors indefinitely for unattended sessions, BUT "Claude Code fails at once when a standard-speed request gets a `429` that reports a spend limit or exhausted usage credits" (since v2.1.239). `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES` default 10, capped at 15 as of v2.1.186. Same page line ~4991: Claude Code "can switch to a fallback model in three specific cases": "A configured `--fallback-model` takes over after an availability error, for that turn only, with a notice in the transcript"; the other two are content-classifier "Automatic model fallback" (Fable/Opus safety flags, v2.1.219+) and availableModels step-down; none is a usage-limit case.

CHANGELOG https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog.md (raw, fetched): v2.1.166 (2026-06-06): "Added `fallbackModel` setting to configure up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary model is overloaded or unavailable; `--fallback-model` now also applies to interactive sessions" and "Claude Code now retries a turn once on the fallback model when the API rejects an unexpected non-retryable error; auth, rate-limit, request-size, and transport errors still surface immediately". VERSION NUANCE: before v2.1.166 `--fallback-model` applied only to non-interactive (-p) sessions; v2.1.152 made a not-found primary switch for the rest of the session; v2.1.178 made compaction honour the chain; v2.1.247 made subagents use the chain. Local extension is 2.1.283, so all apply.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE SOUGHT AND REJECTED: GitHub anthropics/claude-code#65782 (2026-06-06, closed) only asked for the v2.1.166 semantics to be documented and restates "auth, rate-limit, request-size, and transport errors surface immediately". openclaw/openclaw#158144 (2026-09-25) reports a weekly-limited profile "falls to model fallback every turn", but the "model fallback" there is openclaw's own mechanism switching to `openai/gpt-6-sol`, not the Claude CLI's `--fallback-model`; the CLI itself "fails immediately" with `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Sep 27, 6pm (UTC)`. No source found in which a plan usage limit triggered a `--fallback-model` switch.

DESIGN IMPLICATION FOR ASHLEY: a fallback chain only covers 529/overloaded, retired/404 model, and unexpected non-retryable server errors. Subscription session/weekly limits hard-block until reset; only the per-family Opus/Sonnet limits can be worked around, and only by an explicit `/model` change. For an unattended Slurm job, set `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1` for capacity 429/529, and expect an immediate failure (not a retry, not a fallback) on plan-quota 429s; surface `rate_limits` from the status line to the student instead.

findings.claim: Claude Code retries temporary 429 throttles (up to 10 attempts with exponential backoff, v2.1.199+ for subscription sign-ins) but distinguishes them from plan-quota limits by the presence of 'unified quota headers'; a real plan limit is not retried and blocks until reset.
findings.detail: Error reference 'Automatic retries': "Claude Code retries transient failures up to 10 times with exponential backoff ... Temporary 429 throttles, but not a gateway's spend-limit `429` ... When you're signed in with a claude.ai subscription, this includes 429 throttles that don't carry your plan's quota headers. Before v2.1.199, Claude Code retried those throttles only for API key and Enterprise sign-ins." 'Server is temporarily limiting requests': message `API Error: Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit)`; "Claude Code tells these apart from your plan limit by the absence of the unified quota headers a real limit response carries." `API Error: Request rejected (429) · this may be a temporary capacity issue. If it persists, check https://status.claude.com.` is documented as the API-key/Bedrock/Vertex tier limit and advises "Reduce concurrency: lower `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY`, avoid running many parallel subagents".

verdict.corrected_claim: Claude Code retries temporary 429 throttles with exponential backoff, up to 10 attempts by default (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES, default 10, capped at 15 since v2.1.186). For claude.ai-subscription sign-ins this has applied since v2.1.199; before that only API-key and Enterprise sign-ins retried them. It tells a throttle from a plan limit by the ABSENCE of the unified quota headers that a real limit response carries, and shows the throttle as `API Error: Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit)`. A real plan limit (`You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm` / weekly / Opus / Sonnet) is NOT retried within that budget and "blocks further requests until the reset time shown in the message" -- BUT with two documented qualifications: (1) with `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1` (the documented setting for "unattended sessions such as eval harnesses, CI jobs, or remote workers", v2.1.186+) Claude Code retries 429/529 indefinitely and "backs off up to 5 minutes between attempts, or until the limit resets when the response carries a rate-limit reset time, so a session that hits a usage limit waits out the remaining window"; only a 429 reporting a spend limit or exhausted usage credits fails at once (v2.1.239+); (2) since v2.1.234, an interactive session signed in with a claude.ai subscription waits in the open session and auto-continues the interrupted task after the reset by default (`autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, default true, user-or-managed scope; re-arms at most twice in a row), but this wait is not offered in background sessions or `-p` runs and is not auto-started in Remote Control or agent-team teammate sessions. `API Error: Request rejected (429) · this may be a temporary capacity issue. If it persists, check https://status.claude.com.` is the API-key / Amazon Bedrock / Google Cloud project rate limit, and the doc advises "Reduce concurrency: lower `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY`, avoid running many parallel subagents, or switch to a smaller model with `/model` for high-volume scripted runs" (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY default 10).
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core of the claim holds verbatim as of 2026-09-27; only the final clause ("a real plan limit is not retried and blocks until reset") is over-absolute, and the omission is critical=true for a persistent unattended Claude Code on the grid.

CONFIRMED VERBATIM from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors (fetched raw as https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md, 527 KB, 2026-09-27):
- "## Automatic retries" (line 341): "Claude Code retries transient failures up to 10 times with exponential backoff before showing you an error."
- line 350-351: "* Temporary 429 throttles, but not a gateway's spend-limit `429`, which isn't a throttle; see [Spend limit reached]. * When you're signed in with a claude.ai subscription, this includes 429 throttles that don't carry your plan's quota headers. Before v2.1.199, Claude Code retried those throttles only for API key and Enterprise sign-ins."
- "### Server is temporarily limiting requests" (line 719-727): "The API applied a short-lived throttle that is unrelated to your plan quota." message `API Error: Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit)`. "Claude Code tells these apart from your plan limit by the absence of the unified quota headers a real limit response carries. As of v2.1.199 this is retried automatically with backoff before being shown, whichever way you authenticate. On earlier versions, a session signed in with a claude.ai subscription failed the turn on the first occurrence; only API key and Enterprise sign-ins retried it." (Claim says "presence"; doc phrases it as absence-on-throttle / presence-on-real-limit -- equivalent.)
- "### Request rejected (429)" (line 734-751): "You have hit the rate limit configured for your API key, Amazon Bedrock project, or Google Cloud project." message `API Error: Request rejected (429) · this may be a temporary capacity issue. If it persists, check https://status.claude.com.` Advice: "Run `/status` and confirm the active credential is the one you expect. A stray `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in your environment can route requests through a low-tier key instead of your subscription." and "Reduce concurrency: lower `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY`, avoid running many parallel subagents, or switch to a smaller model with `/model` for high-volume scripted runs". Also: "When a proxy, load balancer, or gateway ... answers with its own HTML 429 page, the text after the `·` is that page's title ... Before v2.1.281, the whole page's markup was printed after the `·`."
- "You've hit your session limit" (Usage limits section, ~line 650-660): messages `You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am`, `You've hit your Opus limit · resets 3:45pm`, `You've hit your Sonnet limit · resets 3:45pm`. "Claude Code blocks further requests until the reset time shown in the message. The session and weekly limits are shared across all models, so switching models doesn't restore access." -- this supports the claim's "blocks until reset".
- "### Tune retry behavior" table (line 389-394): `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES` default 10, "Capped at 15 as of v2.1.186; as of v2.1.199 `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` raises the default and removes the cap." `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` default unset: "Set to `1` in unattended sessions such as CI jobs to retry `429` and `529` capacity errors indefinitely instead of failing after `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES` attempts. Claude Code fails at once when a standard-speed request gets a `429` that reports a spend limit or exhausted usage credits, even one from a gateway spend cap that resets on a schedule. Before v2.1.239, the watchdog retried these indefinitely. ... On v2.1.199 or later it also raises the default retry count for other transient errors ... to 300, roughly three hours of backoff". `API_TIMEOUT_MS` default 600000.
- "Spend limit reached" (line 787): gateway "marks each blocked `429` response `x-should-retry: false`, so Claude Code shows this message without retrying."

WHY THE FINAL CLAUSE IS OVER-ABSOLUTE:
(1) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (fetched raw as env-vars.md, line 356) on `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG`: "Set to `1` for unattended sessions such as eval harnesses, CI jobs, or remote workers. ... The watchdog backs off up to 5 minutes between attempts, or until the limit resets when the response carries a rate-limit reset time, so a session that hits a usage limit waits out the remaining window. ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.186 or later". So with the watchdog a real plan usage limit IS waited out / retried; only spend-limit or exhausted-usage-credits 429s fail at once. verdict.corrected_claim: Automatic wait-and-continue after a claude.ai usage-limit reset exists from Claude Code v2.1.234 (CHANGELOG 2.1.234: "Claude Code now continues your session automatically when a claude.ai usage limit resets"; errors page: "Before v2.1.234, Claude Code didn't offer this wait"). It is on by default only in interactive sessions signed in with a claude.ai subscription. After a continued turn hits the limit again it re-arms at most twice in a row, then shows `Automatic continue stopped after repeated usage-limit hits · /rate-limit-options to try again`. It is NOT started automatically in three cases: Remote Control and agent-team teammate sessions (a person at that terminal can still start it with `/rate-limit-options`), a reset more than 24 hours away (weekly limit), and an Opus/Sonnet-family limit while running a model outside that family. It is NOT OFFERED AT ALL (not merely undocumented) for background sessions and `-p` runs ("the menu row isn't available"), for API keys / cloud providers / usage-based billing, and for an LLM gateway without a saved claude.ai login. The wait ends without continuing if you exit Claude Code ("the wait doesn't restart when you resume the session"), if the session is handed to Claude Desktop, a background session or the cloud, or if a `UserPromptSubmit` hook blocks the continuation prompt; after a >~30 min machine sleep it degrades to `Your usage limit has reset · press enter to continue` (manual). Setting `autoContinueAtUsageLimit` (Boolean, default `true`) is read from user settings, `--settings` and managed settings only; a project/local settings file that sets it turns the feature OFF rather than being ignored; `/config autoContinueAtUsageLimit=false` works in `-p` but the `key=value` form cannot turn it back on. Open GitHub issue #91535 (2026-09-02, v2.1.236, no maintainer reply as of 2026-09-27) reports it does not fire in a detached tmux session with no client attached, so a persistent interactive Claude Code inside a Slurm job cannot be assumed to auto-continue. No changelog entry from 2.1.235 through 2.1.283 (newest, 2026-09-25) changes this behaviour; 2.1.271 added a separate pause/continue for dynamic workflows only.

IMPLICATION FOR THE ASHLEY DESIGN: a persistent Claude Code on the grid driven by `claude -p` / Agent SDK gets NO auto-continue (explicitly "not offered"), and an interactive session left detached in tmux/screen inside the Slurm job is reported not to auto-continue either; the >24 h weekly limit never auto-continues in any mode. [1] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication (section "Generate a long-lived token") — CONFIRMED verbatim: "For CI pipelines, scripts, or other environments where interactive browser login isn't available, generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`" / "The command opens the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, and the token prints to the terminal after you approve access in the browser. It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable wherever you want to authenticate" / "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." / "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." critical=true.

[2] Same page, "Authentication precedence" — CONFIRMED: rank 1 cloud provider (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`/`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`/`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`), 2 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (Bearer), 3 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (X-Api-Key; "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present."), 4 `apiKeyHelper`, 5 `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` ("A long-lived OAuth token generated by `claude setup-token`. Use this for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login isn't available."), 6 Anthropic profile/federation, 7 subscription OAuth from `/login`. Design consequence: any stray `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the student's grid shell profile silently overrides the subscription token and bills the API. critical=true.

[3] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference — CONFIRMED verbatim table row: "`claude setup-token` | Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription." `--bare` row: "Minimal mode: skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster ... Sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`". Note: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is NOT listed on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (only documented on the authentication page); the claim did not assert otherwise.

[4] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless ("Start faster with bare mode") — STRONGER than the claim and critical=true for our persistent-daemon design: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain." (so neither `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` nor a `/login` credential works under `--bare`), and the Note: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." DESIGN RISK: a grid daemon built on `claude -p` with a subscription token must NOT pass `--bare`, and will break when `--bare` becomes the `-p` default unless an opt-out flag ships; pin the Claude Code version in the Singularity image and re-verify on upgrade.

[5] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview — critical=true qualifier the claim omits: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead." Consequence: "Ashley" may launch the unmodified `claude` CLI with the student's own `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (the docs-endorsed path), but must not itself be an Agent SDK app that consumes students' subscriptions.

[6] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions — the canonical unattended-subscription use, confirming intent: "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`: an OAuth token that authenticates with your Claude subscription, available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. Generate one by running `claude setup-token` locally." and "an OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran `claude setup-token`" (per-student tokens; never a shared lab token). "If you authenticate with an OAuth token, runs use your Claude subscription instead of API billing."

[7] https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/97350 (opened 2026-09-26, Claude Code 2.1.281, open, no maintainer reply) — the obvious `--bare` workaround does not work: a `sk-ant-oat01-` setup-token value returned by `apiKeyHelper` is sent as `X-Api-Key` and rejected with `401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"API key is invalid."}}`; the same token succeeds via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and, per the reporter, via `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (Bearer). The `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` route is unofficial and undocumented; do not design on it.

[8] Minting the token on the grid: authentication page says the flow opens a browser; the login-code fallback ("paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt ... common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers") means it can be run over SSH, but the cleanest design mints on the student's laptop (browser present) and ships the token to the compute node via SSH environment / a 0600 file. Token lifetime is one year (no renewal warning is documented for it; the 3-day `/login` expiry warning applies only to `/login` credentials). Token format observed in the wild: `sk-ant-oat01-...` (issue #97350).

[9] https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11145838-using-claude-code-with-your-pro-or-max-plan — Pro/Max covers Claude Code in terminal and "supported IDEs, including VS Code"; usage limits shared across Claude and Claude Code; page does not address CI/automation or token sharing, and does not contradict the docs.
