verdict.evidence:
VERIFIED (all three quotes match character-for-character on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions, fetched 2026-09-27):
(1) Manual setup > "Add an authentication secret": "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`: an OAuth token that authenticates with your Claude subscription, available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. Generate one by running `claude setup-token` locally. See Generate a long-lived token". Workflow input is `claude_code_oauth_token` (vs `anthropic_api_key`).
(2) Best practices > "Manage costs" (claim said "Costs section"; heading is actually "Manage costs" — trivial): "If you authenticate with an OAuth token, runs use your Claude subscription instead of API billing."
(3) "Set up for an organization": "For a secret shared across repositories, authenticate with an API key from the Claude Console rather than an OAuth token, since an OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran `claude setup-token`." Same section also offers workload identity federation (inputs `anthropic_federation_rule_id` fdrl_..., `anthropic_organization_id`, `anthropic_service_account_id` svac_..., `anthropic_workspace_id` wrkspc_...; needs `id-token: write`) as the no-long-lived-secret alternative.
Note: the action repo's own docs/setup.md (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/docs/setup.md) still says "Pro and Max users can generate this by running `claude setup-token` locally" — narrower/stale vs the docs page's "Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise". Docs page is authoritative.

ADDITIONAL OFFICIAL FACTS THE DESIGN DEPENDS ON (critical=true), from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication (fetched 2026-09-27):
- Lifetime: "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`". "It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable".
- Scope: "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." => a grid-resident Claude Code authenticated via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN cannot use Remote Control; prompt delivery must be SSH/shared-FS as designed.
- "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead."
- Precedence list: 1 cloud provider vars, 2 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, 3 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, 4 apiKeyHelper, 5 CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN ("Use this for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login isn't available"), 6 Anthropic profile/federation, 7 subscription OAuth from /login. A stray ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the Slurm job env silently overrides the student's subscription token.
- CLI reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference): "`claude setup-token` Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription."
- `claude setup-token` and `/install-github-app` "enforce only `forceLoginMethod`, so they can mint a token in a different organization".
- Login-code fallback: "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers." Relevant to running setup-token/login on the grid.

USAGE-POLICY BOUND ON THE CLAIM (critical=true), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance (fetched 2026-09-27), section "Authentication and credential use": "OAuth authentication is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications." "Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users. Moreover, developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." Permitted carve-out: "Nor does it prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code". Hosting conditions ("Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?"): "The Claude Code binary must not be modified" and "Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf. Each end user must authenticate with their own Anthropic API key, Claude subscription plan credentials, or 3P inference provider credential". "Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice." Agent SDK overview (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview): "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK." => Ashley must run the unmodified @anthropic-ai/claude-code CLI in the container, have each student perform `claude setup-token`/`/login` through Anthropic's own flow, and must NOT itself "collect, store, or intermediate" the Claude OAuth token (the task text's "collect credentials (... Claude subscription)" needs rewording: the extension may open the login flow or tell the student where to export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on the grid, but should not hold the token in its own store). If Ashley drives Claude through the Agent SDK instead of the CLI, subscription auth is not permitted. Secondary 2026-02-19/20 press coverage of this policy (theregister.com, gigazine.net) found via search but not relied on; the official page above is the authority.

No evidence found contradicting any of the three quoted sentences.

findings.claim: Interactive `/login` works over SSH and inside containers via a paste-in code; Linux credentials land in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (mode 0600) or under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; a `/login` credential expires and is refreshed, with a 3-day warning, and unattended sessions stall when it expires, whereas `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` sessions never see 'Login expired'.
findings.detail: Authentication page: "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers." "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead". Startup warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (v2.1.203+); "Renewing early matters most for sessions that run unattended ... a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires." Error reference 'Login expired': -p form is `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`, code `authentication_failed`; "Sessions authenticated with an API key, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or a third-party provider don't use the saved login and never see this message." The login lifetime itself is not stated.

verdict.corrected_claim: Interactive `/login` works over SSH, in WSL2 and inside containers: when the browser cannot reach Claude Code's local callback server it shows a login code, which is pasted at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt; if pasting into the interactive prompt does nothing, `claude auth login` reads the code from standard input. On Linux the credential is written to `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with mode `0600`, or to `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.credentials.json` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set. The `/login` credential is refreshed automatically (parallel sessions on one machine share the saved login and a refresh lock, v2.1.211+); its lifetime is not stated anywhere in the docs. A startup warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` exists, but the warning was introduced in v2.1.203 at FIVE days and changed to three days only in v2.1.217. Once the stored refresh token is rejected the credentials are cleared and every model request fails locally with `Login expired · Please run /login` (in `-p`/SDK: `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`, error code `authentication_failed`, v2.1.206+); a background or Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress and cannot recover until someone signs in again. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` sessions never see `Login expired` or the refresh-lock message because they do not use the saved login, BUT the token is a one-year token that is never refreshed in place: when it expires or is revoked the session fails with `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` / `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`, and the only fix is a new `claude setup-token` and a restart. Such tokens can only make model requests (no Remote Control, no claude.ai connectors), outrank the `/login` credential in precedence, and are not read in `--bare` mode.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: mostly held; two defects. (1) Version attached to the 3-day warning is wrong. (2) "never see 'Login expired'" is literally true but the design inference (token sessions do not stall on expiry) is false; they fail with a different 401 message and cannot self-heal.

CONFIRMED VERBATIM — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication (fetched 2026-09-27):
- "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers." [critical=true]
- "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." [critical=true]
- "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead, including the file the macOS fallback writes, and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory too, so a session with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` reads a different entry." [critical=true]
- "Claude Code manages `.credentials.json` through `/login` and `/logout`."
- Section "Renew an expiring login": "When the login you created with `/login` is within three days of expiring, Claude Code shows a warning at startup: `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. Before v2.1.217, the warning appeared five days out." ... "The login lifetime itself is unchanged; the advance warning is what v2.1.203 adds." ... "Once the stored login expires and can't be refreshed, each model request fails with `Login expired · Please run /login` until you sign in again. Before v2.1.206, Claude Code reported an expired login on model requests as a model error instead." ... "`/status` shows a `Login` row reading `Expired — log in again` ... requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later." ... "The warning appears only when a claude.ai or Claude Console login is the active credential, and not when a cloud provider, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` supplies the credential." ... "Renewing early matters most for sessions that run unattended. A background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." [critical=true]
- LOGIN LIFETIME: not stated on this page, nor on errors, troubleshoot-install, env-vars or cli-reference (grep for lifetime|one-year|valid for|expires after in errors.md returned nothing). Confirms the claim's "not stated".
- Section "Generate a long-lived token": "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`" ... "It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable" ... "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." ... "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." [critical=true]
- Authentication precedence: item 5 `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` ranks above item 7 "Subscription OAuth credentials from `/login`". "If you run `/login` while the variable is set, Claude Code switches the current session to the new login, but reads the variable again in every new session until you remove it from your shell profile or the `env` block of a settings file."

CONFIRMED VERBATIM — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#login-expired (fetched as https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md, lines 1130-1215):
- "### Login expired — Claude Code tried to renew your saved claude.ai or Claude Console login and the OAuth service rejected the stored refresh token, so Claude Code cleared the saved credentials. After that, each model request stops locally with this message before it reaches the API, because only `/login` can create new credentials." Message: `Login expired · Please run /login`. "In non-interactive mode (`-p`) and the Agent SDK, the message reads as follows, and the structured error code is `authentication_failed`: `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`". "Sessions authenticated with an API key, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or a third-party provider don't use the saved login and never see this message." Fix: "In non-interactive mode, run `claude` in the same environment, complete `/login`, then rerun your command. For automation that can't sign in interactively, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or generate a long-lived token with `claude setup-token`." [critical=true]
- REFUTING CONTEXT — "### OAuth token revoked or expired": "If you authenticate with a long-lived token in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, you see the same messages when that token expires or is revoked." Messages: `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` and `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`. "If you authenticate with the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable, Claude Code keeps sending the value you set after a request fails with a 401, rather than switching to a stored login's token. `/status` shows this credential as an `Auth token` row reading `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Generate a fresh token with `claude setup-token` and restart with it, or unset the variable and run `/login`. Before v2.1.225, Claude Code could replace the variable's value mid-session with the short-lived access token from a stored login, and the session failed with 401 errors again once that token expired." [critical=true — a persistent grid session on a one-year token WILL eventually fail; it just fails with a 401 rather than 'Login expired', and requires a new token + process restart]
- "Could not refresh your login because another Claude Code process is refreshing it": -p message `Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh...`, code `server_error`; same "never see this message" sentence for `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

CONFIRMED VERBATIM — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install (section "OAuth login fails in WSL2, SSH, or containers"): "When Claude Code runs in WSL2, on a remote machine over SSH, or inside a container, the browser usually opens on a different host and its redirect can't reach Claude Code's local callback server. After you sign in, the browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back automatically. Paste that code into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt to complete login." ... "If pasting the code into the interactive prompt does nothing ... use `claude auth login` instead, which reads the pasted code from standard input". Also (section "Not logged in or token expired"): "Parallel sessions on one machine share a saved login and coordinate its renewal so that only one process refreshes the token at a time. Before v2.1.211, waking the machine from sleep could cause two sessions to renew with the same token, which revoked the saved login and prompted every open session to log in again at once." [critical=true — the refresh lock is documented for ONE machine; behaviour when login node and compute node both read the same Panasas/CephFS `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is NOT documented; unknown]. `OAuth error: Invalid code. Please make sure the full code was copied` = "the login code expired or was truncated during copy-paste".

CONFIRMED — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md (top version 2.1.283):
- 2.1.203: "Added a warning when your login is about to expire, so you can re-authenticate before background sessions are interrupted" (no day count).
- 2.1.206: "Fixed an expired login failing every model with a misleading 'There's an issue with the selected model' error instead of prompting to run `/login`".
- 2.1.217: "Changed the login-expiry warning to appear 3 days before expiry instead of 5" [this is the defect in the claim's "(v2.1.203+)" attribution].
- 2.1.225: "Fixed a transient 401 replacing a long-lived `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` with a stored login's short-lived token, breaking headless sessions until restart".
- 2.1.117: "Fixed `/login` having no effect when launched with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var and that token expires" (confirms tokens expire).
- 2.1.238 area: "Fixed Remote Control disconnecting with 'login expired' when a brief network hiccup delays renewing your sign-in".

CONFIRMED — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.md: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` = "OAuth access token for claude.ai authentication. Alternative to `/login` for SDK and automated environments. Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials. ... Unless you run `/login`, Claude Code uses the token you set for the whole session. To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` = "Override the configuration directory (default: `~/.claude`). ... Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings."
CONFIRMED — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference.md: `claude auth login` (flags `--email`, `--sso`, `--console`), `claude auth status` ("Show authentication status as JSON. Use `--text` ... Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not"), `claude setup-token`.
CONFIRMED — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control: "You're authenticated with a long-lived token from `claude setup-token` or the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. These tokens can only make model requests, so they can't establish Remote Control sessions. Run `claude auth login` to authenticate with a full-scope session token instead." Also "API keys are not supported" for Remote Control.
CONFIRMED — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain." and "Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available" in `-p` mode.

DESIGN IMPLICATIONS FOR ASHLEY (critical): (a) `/login` paste-code flow is viable on a compute node inside Singularity; `claude auth login` via stdin is the robust fallback. (b) For a 30-day persistent Slurm job, a `/login` credential of unstated lifetime is refreshed automatically but if refresh fails the job stalls with `authentication_failed`; poll `claude auth status` (exit 1 = not logged in) or watch for the 3-day warning to trigger re-login from the laptop. (c) A `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` avoids refresh-lock and 'Login expired' but dies at one year with a 401 and cannot be rotated without restarting the process; it also forbids Remote Control and `--bare`. (d) Sharing one `~/.claude/.credentials.json` across login node and compute nodes over Panasas is undocumented; consider a per-node `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. (e) Grid install should be >= v2.1.217 (3-day warning), >= v2.1.225 (token not clobbered by transient 401), >= v2.1.211 (refresh lock); current is 2.1.283.

findings.claim: No official document limits the number of concurrent Claude Code sessions or machines per subscription; concurrency merely draws on the same per-account quota, but users report an infrastructure-level 429 ('Rate limited', rateLimits: null) at 6+ simultaneous sessions well under quota.
findings.detail: Support 'Log in to your Claude account' (updated May 19, 2026): "To use your Claude account across multiple devices, enter the same email address you use to log in on your usual device." — no concurrency clause. Claude Code costs page notes per-developer costs vary with "running multiple instances or automation" and that `/usage` "usage from other devices or claude.ai is not included" in local attribution. GitHub issue #96872 (opened 2026-09-24, Desktop 2.1.280, Max plan, single account/machine): `status: 429`, `error.type: rate_limit_error`, message `"Rate limited"`, `rateLimits: null`, retried up to 10 times; 14.3% of minutes with 6+ concurrent sessions hit it vs 0.3% with one, while 5-hour usage read 27% and weekly 26%; began ~2026-09-16; no maintainer answer yet. Issue #95349 (v2.1.276, macOS) reports the 5-hour session bucket not refreshing after switching to a second paid account on one machine (`/logout` + `/login`).

verdict.corrected_claim: No official Anthropic document states a numeric cap on concurrent Claude Code sessions or on devices per Pro/Max subscription; concurrency draws on the same per-account 5-hour and weekly quota. Doc explicitly warns: "Renewing early matters most for sessions that run unattended. A background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." — relevant to a 30-day QoS-primary job.

(y/n)"); interactive `claude --remote-control` / `--rc`; in-session `/remote-control` / `/rc`; VS Code extension supports `/remote-control`. "Your local Claude Code session makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports on your machine." "To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside `tmux` or `screen`." "While Remote Control is connected, the session transcript ... is stored on Anthropic servers." Resume after server stop: `claude remote-control --continue` / `--session-id <id>` (v2.1.200+), works "for about four hours after the server stopped". `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`/`DO_NOT_TRACK` with Remote Control requires v2.1.283 or later (our installed extension version). Their anti-circumvention language is (i) §3: "You also must not abuse, harm, interfere with, or disrupt our Services, including, for example, introducing viruses or malware, spamming or DDoSing Services, or bypassing any of our systems or protective measures." and (ii) the §3 bullet "Except when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it, to access the Services through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise." Two qualifications the original claim omitted: (a) §1 states the Terms "include our Acceptable Use Policy" (linked to anthropic.com/aup, now titled "Usage Policy", effective September 15, 2025), whose "Do Not Abuse our Platform" section does address accounts: "Coordinate malicious activity across multiple accounts to avoid detection or circumvent product guardrails", "Utilize automation in account creation or to engage in spammy behavior", "Circumvent a ban through the use of a different account, such as the creation of a new account, use of an existing account, or providing access to a person or entity that was previously banned", and "Intentionally bypass capabilities, restrictions, or guardrails established within our products ... without prior authorization from Anthropic"; §2 of the Terms also forbids sharing: "You may not share your Account login information, Anthropic API key, or Account credentials with anyone else. You also may not make your Account available to anyone else." Merely holding several accounts is still not prohibited anywhere found. (b) The "explicit permission" for scripted subscription use is not really the `claude setup-token` docs alone; the operative statement is code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance, which permits OAuth subscription credentials only for "ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications", assumes "ordinary, individual usage" for advertised Pro/Max usage limits, allows "an end user ... signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code", and forbids third-party developers to "collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." The setup-token docs then describe the sanctioned mechanism: a one-year `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` "For CI pipelines, scripts, or other environments where interactive browser login isn't available", Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise only, model requests only, not read in `--bare` mode.

verdict.corrected_claim: The Claude Code "Legal and compliance" page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance; the docs.anthropic.com URL 301-redirects there; fetched 2026-09-27; carries no date or version marker and has been revised at least once since 2026-02-18) is Anthropic's published policy statement, not itself the governing legal text: it says Claude Code use "is subject to" the Consumer Terms of Service (Free, Pro, Max), the Commercial Terms of Service (Team, Enterprise, API) and the Anthropic Usage Policy, and it defers to them. All five sentences quoted in the original claim appear verbatim on the current page. The claim's license mapping is incomplete in a way that changes the design: the page's section "Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?" states that "preinstalling or running Claude Code in your products or services (e.g. in hosted sandboxes or other agent infrastructure) requires agreeing to our Commercial Terms of Service" and complying with two conditions: "The Claude Code binary must not be modified" (customers "may not remove, disable, or restrict any authentication method built into it") and "Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf" ("Each end user must authenticate with their own Anthropic API key, Claude subscription plan credentials, or 3P inference provider credential"). So students are under the Consumer Terms, but whoever operates the Slurm/Singularity-hosted Claude Code is asked to agree to the Commercial Terms. The sentence "Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK" does not exclude non-interactive use: Anthropic's support article "Use the Claude Agent SDK with your Claude plan" (updated 2026-06-16) states "Claude Agent SDK, claude -p, and third-party app usage still draw from your subscription's usage limits" (a planned separate monthly Agent SDK credit was paused 2026-06-15). The page's carve-out permits the design's core: "Nor does it prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code". What it forbids is the extension doing the sign-in: "developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." Therefore Ashley must not collect the Claude subscription credential; the student runs the unmodified binary's own /login (or `claude setup-token`, which prints a one-year token for `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) on the compute node, and the resulting `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (mode 0600 on Linux) belongs to the student, never to the extension or a shared account. Enforcement: "Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice" (verbatim); server-side enforcement in early 2026 returned "This credential is only authorized for use with Claude Code and cannot be used for other API requests." (secondary sources).
verdict.evidence:
VERIFICATION METHOD: fetched the live page twice (HTML at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance and raw Markdown at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance.md) on 2026-09-27; both identical. https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/legal-and-compliance returns 301 Moved Permanently to the code.claude.com URL. Page has no "last updated" marker.

FINDING 1 (critical=true) — QUOTES HOLD. Every sentence in the claim's DETAIL appears verbatim on the live page: "Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK." / "OAuth authentication is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications." / "Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users. Moreover, developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." / "Nor does it prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code as described under Can customers offer Claude Code in their products? above." / "Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice." / License bullets: "Commercial Terms of Service - for Team, Enterprise, and Claude API users"; "Consumer Terms of Service - for Free, Pro, and Max users". Section headings on the page: Legal agreements (License; Commercial agreements; Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?), Compliance (Healthcare compliance (BAA)), Usage policy (Acceptable use; Authentication and credential use), Security and trust (Trust and safety; Security vulnerability reporting).

FINDING 2 (critical=true) — WHAT THE CLAIM OMITS, AND WHY IT IS SUBTLY WRONG. (a) The page is not "the governing text"; it says "Your use of Claude Code is subject to" the Consumer/Commercial Terms and "Claude Code usage is subject to the Anthropic Usage Policy" and "Claude Code remains governed by Anthropic's standard terms ... regardless of the platform through which it is accessed." (b) The omitted section "Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?" reads verbatim: "Unless we've mutually agreed otherwise, preinstalling or running Claude Code in your products or services (e.g. in hosted sandboxes or other agent infrastructure) requires agreeing to our Commercial Terms of Service and complying with the conditions below: * The Claude Code binary must not be modified. Claude Code must be installed and run as published by Anthropic, and customers may not remove, disable, or restrict any authentication method built into it (including methods that permit signing in with a Claude account or the user's own API key). * Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf. Each end user must authenticate with their own Anthropic API key, Claude subscription plan credentials, or 3P inference provider credential (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry). That usage is billed directly to the end user under their own agreement with Anthropic or, for third-party inference providers, with the applicable provider." A Claude Code inside a Singularity container in a Slurm job, launched by a university-distributed extension, is "agent infrastructure"; the operator is asked to agree to the Commercial Terms even though each student is on Consumer Terms. Name/logo rule on the same page: "You can accurately say, in plain text, that your product has Claude Code preinstalled or that it runs Claude Code. But you can't use the Claude Code or Anthropic names or logos as part of your own product, feature, or company name". Also the page's provisioning carve-out: "This does not restrict how customers provision and manage their own API keys or third-party inference provider credentials — for example, configuring an API key in a development environment, secrets manager, or machine image for use by the customer's own authorized users — provided the resulting usage is billed to the key owner ... and is not resold or intermediated".

FINDING 3 (critical=true) — THE DESIGN'S "COLLECT CREDENTIALS (... Claude subscription)" STEP IS THE PROHIBITED ACT. Verbatim: "developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." The permitted path is the student signing in to the unmodified binary themselves. Mechanics from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication (fetched 2026-09-27): "On Linux, credentials are stored in ~/.claude/.credentials.json with file mode 0600."; "If you've set the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable, Claude Code keeps the .credentials.json file under that directory instead"; headless login: "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the Paste code here if prompted prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers."; "press c to copy the login URL"; long-lived token: "generate a one-year OAuth token with claude setup-token ... It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN environment variable ... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions"; "Bare mode does not read CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. If your script passes --bare, authenticate with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper instead."; expiry warning: "Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew" (v2.1.203+), failure string "Login expired · Please run /login"; "Renewing early matters most for sessions that run unattended." Precedence: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN ranks 5th, "Subscription OAuth credentials from /login" 7th; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (3rd) overrides a subscription once approved.

FINDING 4 (critical=true) — NON-INTERACTIVE USE ON A SUBSCRIPTION IS CURRENTLY PERMITTED AND DRAWS FROM PLAN LIMITS. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15036540-use-the-claude-agent-sdk-with-your-claude-plan (last updated 2026-06-16): status note dated 2026-06-15 says the announced separate Agent SDK credits (Pro $20/mo, Max 5x $100/mo, Max 20x $200/mo, Team Standard $20/mo, Team Premium $100/mo, Enterprise Premium $200/mo, per-user, non-rolling) are paused and "Claude Agent SDK, claude -p, and third-party app usage still draw from your subscription's usage limits." Corroborated by https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless: `claude -p` is documented as the CLI form of the Agent SDK; "--bare ... doesn't use your subscription login"; "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain." Note the Agent SDK overview (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) still carries: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead." and "Use of the Claude Agent SDK is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service". Reading: the student's own `claude -p` on their own login is in scope; an extension-operated SDK harness on the student's login is not.

FINDING 5 (critical=true) — SUPPORT ARTICLE THE LEGAL PAGE LINKS ADDS QUALIFIERS. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13189465-logging-in-to-your-claude-account (updated 2026-05-19), heading "Authenticating to subscription plans": "Subscription plans can only be used by subscribers, and the usage included in these plans is designed to support ordinary use of native Anthropic applications" (lists "the Claude web, desktop, and mobile applications and Claude Code"); "Anthropic may at its discretion allow paid subscribers who have enabled usage credits to use certain third-party tools to access Anthropic services"; "Use of third-party tools that misrepresent their identity to Anthropic's servers, attempt to route third-party traffic against subscription limits, or otherwise violate applicable terms or policies is prohibited". Ashley must not present itself to api.anthropic.com as Claude Code; it should only launch the real binary.

FINDING 6 (critical=true) — CONSUMER TERMS FORBID A SHARED OR EXTENSION-HELD ACCOUNT. https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms ("Effective October 8, 2025"): "You may not share your Account login information, Anthropic API key, or Account credentials with anyone else. You also may not make your Account available to anyone else."; use restriction: "Except when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it, to access the Services through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise."; scope: "Our Commercial Terms of Service govern your use of any Anthropic API key, the Anthropic Console, or any other Anthropic offerings that reference the Commercial Terms of Service. For clarity, this does not include Claude.ai or Claude Pro use for individuals or entities." Claude Code's documented `-p` and `setup-token` "for CI pipelines and scripts" constitute the "explicitly permit" carve-out for the student's own automation. https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup ("Effective September 15, 2025") contains no clause on credential sharing, third-party subscription use, or rate-limit circumvention; only ban-circumvention via other accounts.

FINDING 7 (critical=false) — PAGE HISTORY. The 2026-02-18 version (quoted in https://github.com/AndyMik90/Aperant/issues/1871, opened 2026-02-18, and https://aihackers.net/posts/anthropic-claude-code-oauth-policy-feb-2026/, dated 2026-02-19) read: "OAuth authentication (used with Free, Pro, and Max plans) is intended exclusively for Claude Code and Claude.ai." and "Using OAuth tokens obtained through Claude Free, Pro, or Max accounts in any other product, tool, or service — including the Agent SDK — is not permitted and constitutes a violation of the Consumer Terms of Service." Neither sentence is on the current page; the current page replaced them with the "purchasers ... ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications" wording and added the "Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?" section and the two-paragraph carve-out. Secondary sources report server-side enforcement against third-party harnesses (OpenCode, Roo Code named) with the error "This credential is only authorized for use with Claude Code and cannot be used for other API requests." (aihackers.net; not independently verified against an Anthropic source). https://yage.ai/share/claude-code-subscription-not-a-developer-credential-en-20260321.html (2026-03-21) reports the compliance-page PR merged 2026-03-19. Wayback Machine and gigazine.net were unreachable from this session, so the exact revision date is unverified.

FINDING 8 (critical=true) — ANTHROPIC'S FIRST-PARTY ALTERNATIVE TO A BESPOKE PROMPT RELAY. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control (fetched 2026-09-27): "Subscription: available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported."; "run claude and use /login to sign in through claude.ai ... Without an eligible login, claude remote-control exits with an error"; error strings: "Remote Control requires a claude.ai subscription.", "You must be logged in to use Remote Control. Remote Control is only available with claude.ai subscriptions.", "Remote Control requires a full-scope login token" ("You're authenticated with a long-lived token from claude setup-token or the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN environment variable. These tokens can only make model requests, so they can't establish Remote Control sessions."); "To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside tmux or screen."; "Your local Claude Code session makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports"; requires direct api.anthropic.com (a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry disables it); "While Remote Control is connected, the session transcript ... is stored on Anthropic servers"; server mode flags `--continue`, `--session-id`, `--spawn same-dir|worktree|session`, `--permission-mode`; resume works "for about four hours after the server stopped". This is the sanctioned way to send prompts from a laptop/phone/browser to a persistent Claude Code on a compute node without the extension touching credentials.

FINDING 9 (critical=false) — PLAN COVERAGE. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11145838-use-claude-code-with-your-pro-or-max-plan (updated 2026-08-19): plan covers Claude Code in the terminal and "VS Code, Cursor and other VS Code forks, and JetBrains IDEs like IntelliJ and PyCharm"; usage shared with claude.ai. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs: "/usage-credits after signing in with your claude.ai subscription through /login; the command isn't available with API key authentication"; prompt-cache lifetime "is an hour on a subscription and drops to five minutes once you're drawing on usage credits".

NOT VERIFIED: exact date of the page revision (Wayback unreachable); any Anthropic staff statement; whether Anthropic has ever granted the "mutually agreed otherwise" exception to a university.

verdict.evidence:
CONFIRMED against the live official page (fetched 2026-09-27; page shows no last-updated date). Verbatim from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance, section "Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?": "Unless we've mutually agreed otherwise, preinstalling or running Claude Code in your products or services (e.g. in hosted sandboxes or other agent infrastructure) requires agreeing to our Commercial Terms of Service and complying with the conditions below: * The Claude Code binary must not be modified. Claude Code must be installed and run as published by Anthropic, and customers may not remove, disable, or restrict any authentication method built into it (including methods that permit signing in with a Claude account or the user's own API key). * Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf. Each end user must authenticate with their own Anthropic API key, Claude subscription plan credentials, or 3P inference provider credential (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry). That usage is billed directly to the end user under their own agreement with Anthropic or, for third-party inference providers, with the applicable provider." The API-key provisioning carve-out is also verbatim: "This does not restrict how customers provision and manage their own API keys or third-party inference provider credentials — for example, configuring an API key in a development environment, secrets manager, or machine image for use by the customer's own authorized users — provided the resulting usage is billed to the key owner under their agreement with Anthropic (or the applicable provider) and is not resold or intermediated as described above."

ADDITIONS the claim omits, all from the same page (critical=true for the Ashley design):
(1) Explicit permission for exactly our scenario: "Nor does it prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code as described under Can customers offer Claude Code in their products? above." So a lab-hosted, unmodified `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` CLI in a Singularity job, with each student signing in with their own Pro/Max account, is permitted.
(2) Constraint on the extension's credential handling (critical=true): "Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users. Moreover, developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." The task's "collect credentials (... Claude subscription)" must therefore NOT mean the extension harvesting the student's Claude.ai OAuth token/session (e.g., copying ~/.claude/.credentials.json from the laptop to the grid); the student must complete `claude` login through Anthropic's own OAuth flow inside the hosted binary. Anthropic "reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice."
(3) OAuth scope: "OAuth authentication is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications." Developers building products, "including those using the Agent SDK, should use API key authentication".
(4) Rate-limit caveat: "Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK." A 30-day persistent worker fed prompts is still individual use if one student drives it, but automated fan-out would not be.
(5) License split: Commercial Terms apply "for Team, Enterprise, and Claude API users"; Consumer Terms "for Free, Pro, and Max users". The HOST (lab) agrees to Commercial Terms; each STUDENT remains under Consumer Terms for their Pro/Max sign-in.

Consumer Terms (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms, effective October 8, 2025): "You may not share your Account login information, Anthropic API key, or Account credentials with anyone else." and "You also may not make your Account available to anyone else." verdict.corrected_claim: Pooling several students' individual Pro/Max subscriptions into one shared Claude Code worker is not permitted by the governing text. (1) Consumer Terms of Service, effective October 8, 2025, s.2 "Account creation and access": "You may not share your Account login information, Anthropic API key, or Account credentials with anyone else. You also may not make your Account available to anyone else." (2) Claude Code "Legal and compliance" page, "Authentication and credential use": OAuth authentication "is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans"; "developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow"; and under "Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?": "Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf. Each end user must authenticate with their own ... Claude subscription plan credentials". (3) GitHub Actions doc: "an OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran `claude setup-token`", so a secret shared across users should be a Console API key. One refinement: the phrase "ordinary, individual usage" is not a prohibition; the exact sentence is "Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK" — it describes what the rate limits are sized for, so pooling would also break the limit assumption, but the prohibitions rest on (1)-(3). No lab/classroom exception exists for pooling; Anthropic's documented route for a group is Claude for Teams ("For teams of 2 to 150", Claude Code included, each member still logs in with their own claude.ai account) or the institution-wide Claude for Education plan (contact sales). The sanctioned pattern for Ashley is one worker per student, running the unmodified `claude` binary, authenticated by that student completing Anthropic's own login flow themselves (either `claude` /login with the "Paste code here if prompted" fallback that the docs say is common "in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers", or the student running `claude setup-token` and exporting `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in their own environment). Second refinement, critical for the design brief: the extension itself must NOT "collect" or store the student's Claude OAuth token or session token in its own credential store or relay it — that is the literal conduct the legal page forbids for developers. The brief's item "collect credentials (... Claude subscription)" should be reworded to "launch Anthropic's own sign-in flow inside the student's container".

verdict.corrected_claim: Console API keys are the pay-per-token route ("On the Console and on cloud providers, usage is billed per token to your organization"). Hard caps, verified 2026-09-27: (1) Usage-tier monthly spend caps: Start $500 USD, Build $1,000 USD, Scale $200,000 USD; Custom tier has no cap. New orgs may start in an "Evaluation tier" with lower limits. At the tier cap, requests return HTTP 429 with error.type `rate_limit_error`, `error.details.error_code` = `enforced_spend_limit_reached`, and NO `retry-after` header; usage pauses until 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the next month. (2) Self-set org spend limit (Settings > Billing > Spend limits > "Adjust limit"/"Set limit"; cannot exceed the tier cap) and per-workspace spend limits: when hit, requests return HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error` with a message beginning `You have reached your specified API usage limits` or `You have reached your specified workspace API usage limits`. (3) Per-workspace rate limits (RPM/ITPM/OTPM per model tier, "Rate limits" tab) and per-workspace spend limits ("Spend limits" tab) can be set lower than, never higher than, org limits; not settable on the Default Workspace; org-wide limits always apply; per-workspace rate-limit configuration is not available on Claude Platform on AWS. (4) A "Claude Code" workspace is auto-created when the first org member signs in to Claude Code with a Console account; "Claude Code mints a per-user API key in this workspace at sign-in. You cannot create keys in it manually from the Console"; "Claude Code usage is rate-limited separately, and admins can cap its share of the organization's limits under Settings > Workspaces"; "It is the only workspace that supports per-user monthly spend limits". Its limits are checked separately: "Claude Code requests over that workspace's limit can instead receive a 429 that carries a `retry-after` header." Archiving it disables Console-billed Claude Code sign-in for the whole org. CORRECTIONS: (a) The Console role is named "Claude Code User" (Admin API enum `claude_code_user`), described as "Can use playground and Claude Code" / "Can access Claude Code workspace in your org"; only the Claude Code authentication page calls it the "Claude Code role: users can only create Claude Code API keys". Since Claude Code v2.1.242 a Console account can also sign in WITHOUT creating any API key ("Sign in with your Console account (recommended)" stores an OAuth profile; "Create an API key (legacy)"), so "mints a per-user API key at sign-in" describes the legacy path; whether keyless sign-ins are metered against the Claude Code workspace's limits is not stated in the docs fetched. (b) `--max-budget-usd` is documented on the CLI reference page, not the costs page (which only cross-references it): "Maximum dollar amount to spend on API calls before stopping (print mode only)"; subagent spend counts; at the cap "spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached`, and Claude Code stops background subagents that are still running"; cap enforcement requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later. It is a client-side cap for `claude -p`, not a Console control. (c) None of these Console caps apply to a student authenticating with a personal Pro/Max subscription; there the ceilings are the plan's 5-hour and weekly windows plus an optional usage-credits monthly spend limit at claude.ai Settings > Usage.
