Verdict: the substantive claim is CONFIRMED verbatim against official docs fetched 2026-09-27; refuted=true only for two subtly wrong details (role name/description; where --max-budget-usd is documented) and one version-specific staleness (per-user key minting vs keyless Console sign-in). Design impact: LOW/non-critical — the Ashley design authenticates students with their own Pro/Max subscription, so Console tier caps, workspace limits and the Claude Code workspace do not apply to them; this material matters only if a Console-billed org route is offered as a fallback.

SOURCES FETCHED AND WHAT EACH SHOWED:

1. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits (fetched OK). Spend limits table verbatim: "| Start | $500 USD |", "| Build | $1,000 USD |", "| Scale | $200,000 USD |"; "Organizations on the Custom tier have no monthly spend cap". "Reaching your spend cap": "API usage pauses until 00:00 UTC on the first day of the next month"; JSON example with "type": "rate_limit_error", "details": { "error_code": "enforced_spend_limit_reached" }; "The error type is `rate_limit_error`, the same as for a rate limit, but the response has no `retry-after` header. Retrying, including the SDKs' automatic retries, fails until access resumes." "Setting your own spend limit": Settings > Billing, "Adjust limit (or Set limit...)", "Your spend limit cannot exceed your current tier's cap." "When usage reaches a spend limit you set, requests return HTTP 400 with error type `invalid_request_error`. The message begins `You have reached your specified API usage limits`, or `You have reached your specified workspace API usage limits` for a workspace limit". Verbatim: "Limits on the Claude Code workspace are checked separately: Claude Code requests over that workspace's limit can instead receive a 429 that carries a `retry-after` header." "Setting lower limits for Workspaces": "You can't set limits on the default Workspace." "If not set, Workspace limits match the Organization's limit." "Organization-wide limits always apply, even if Workspace limits add up to more." Response headers table: `retry-after` "Not sent with the spend-cap 429". Also: "New organizations ... may start in the Evaluation tier, with limits below the standard limits". Note: "Per-workspace rate limit configuration and fast mode are not available on Claude Platform on AWS."

2. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/workspaces (fetched OK; served as https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces). "Claude Code workspace" section verbatim: "When a member of your organization first signs in to Claude Code with their Claude Console account, Anthropic automatically creates a **Claude Code** workspace in the organization and adds that member to it." Bullets: "Claude Code mints a per-user API key in this workspace at sign-in. You cannot create keys in it manually from the Console." "A Claude Code key stops working if its owner is removed from the workspace or organization, unlike a workspace key." "Claude Code usage is rate-limited separately, and admins can cap its share of the organization's limits under Settings > Workspaces." "It is the only workspace that supports per-user monthly spend limits." Warning: "Archiving the Claude Code workspace disables Claude Code sign-in through Console billing for the whole organization." "Set workspace limits": "Rate limits: On the Rate limits tab, set limits per model tier for requests per minute, input tokens, or output tokens"; "Spend limits: On the Spend limits tab, cap monthly spending and configure alerts". "You can set workspace limits lower than (but not higher than) your organization's limits". Note: "You cannot set limits on the Default Workspace". Workspace ids use `wrkspc_` prefix; response header `anthropic-workspace-id` identifies the workspace a request counted against.

3. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs (fetched OK). Confirms billing model: "On Teams and Enterprise plans, usage draws from each member's seat allowance. On the Console and on cloud providers, usage is billed per token to your organization." Console row of the table: See spend = Console usage page; Cap spend = "Workspace spend limits"; per-user reporting = Console dashboard platform.claude.com/claude-code and Claude Code Analytics API. Note: "When you first authenticate Claude Code with your Claude Console account, a workspace called "Claude Code" is automatically created for you... You cannot create API keys for this workspace; it is exclusively for Claude Code authentication and usage." It mentions --max-budget-usd only in passing ("the multiplied figure also counts toward `--max-budget-usd`", linking to /docs/en/cli-reference#cli-flags) — so the claim's "costs page documents --max-budget-usd" is a location error. Rate-limit recommendations table (TPM/RPM per user by team size) present. For Pro/Max: "/usage-credits" opens claude.ai Settings > Usage to set a monthly spend limit; plan ceilings are the 5-hour and weekly windows.

4. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (fetched OK). Verbatim: "`--max-budget-usd` — Maximum dollar amount to spend on API calls before stopping (print mode only). Spend from subagents counts toward the cap. When you return to a conversation with `--continue` or `--resume`, totals restored from earlier runs don't count toward it. Once spend reaches the cap, spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached`, and Claude Code stops background subagents that are still running; the cap-enforcement behaviors require Claude Code v2.1.217 or later". Example: `claude -p --max-budget-usd 5.00 "query"`.

5. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication (fetched OK). "Claude Console authentication" > "Assign roles" verbatim: "**Claude Code** role: users can only create Claude Code API keys"; "**Developer** role: users can create any kind of API key". This is the source of the claim's wording. Same page, "Sign in without an API key": "You can sign in to your Console account without creating an API key ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later." Two routes: "Sign in with your Console account, labeled `(recommended)` ... It creates no API key" vs "Create an API key, labeled `(legacy)`: Claude Code creates a Console API key for you". Also: "Unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before you sign in without a key." Authentication precedence list: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (2) > ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (3) > apiKeyHelper (4) > CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (5) > profiles (6) > subscription OAuth from /login (7). "If you have an active Claude subscription but also have `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set in your environment, Claude Code uses the API key once you approve it" — relevant trap for Ashley: never export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the student's container if the subscription is intended.

6. https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10186004-claude-console-roles-and-permissions (fetched OK; "Last Updated: August 18, 2026"). Six roles: User; "Claude Code User" — "Can use the playground and Claude Code", "Can access Claude Code workspace in your org"; Limited Developer; Developer; Billing — "Cannot access Claude Code workspace in your org"; Admin. No role literally named "Claude Code" and no "can only create Claude Code API keys" wording.

7. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api (fetched OK). "Organization roles and permissions" table: `user` "Can use playground"; `claude_code_user` "Can use playground and Claude Code"; `developer` "Can use playground and manage API keys"; `billing`; `admin`. (Says "five organization-level roles" while the support article lists six incl. Limited Developer — internal inconsistency between Anthropic pages, noted, not resolved.)

8. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication (fetched OK). Key types table: Personal key, Service account key, Workspace key (legacy). No org-role table on this page.

NOT RETRIEVED: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/console-access-control returned HTTP 404 (guessed URL). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors fetched but the "Request rejected (429)" / "spend limit reached" section bodies were truncated by the fetch tool; only the index rows were visible. Not needed: the rate-limits page is the authoritative statement of the 429/400 behaviour.

UNKNOWN (stated plainly): whether a Console sign-in that uses the keyless (OAuth profile) path since v2.1.242 is metered against the Claude Code workspace's per-user spend limits the same way the legacy minted key is — the workspaces page describes only the minted-key path.

findings.claim: Claude for Education is an institution-wide plan obtained through Anthropic's Education sales team; it includes Claude Code, API access and Learning mode; no individual student price or .edu discount is published; the Claude Campus Program gives selected student ambassadors a USD 3,600 stipend and API credits, not subscriptions.
findings.detail: claude.com/solutions/education: "A comprehensive university-wide plan for institutions, including its students, faculty, and staff"; lists "Claude Code: Write and debug research code directly in your terminal or IDE", "Claude Developer Platform" API access, "Learning mode"; CTA "Contact our Education team"; no pricing or per-student route. Pricing page lists an Education plan with "Student and faculty access" and "Academic research and learning mode". claude.com/programs/campus: three tracks (Builder Club, Campus Conversations, Science Workshops), each "Receive a USD3,600 cash stipend"; "Students anywhere in the world can apply"; 18+ with work authorization; no mention of Claude Code or Pro seats.

findings.claim: Setting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the worker's environment silently switches billing from the subscription to the API key, and in `-p` mode the key is always used without a prompt.
findings.detail: Env vars page: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — "When set, this key is used instead of your Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription even if you are logged in. In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present." Support article: "If you have an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable set on your system, Claude Code will use this API key for authentication instead of your Claude subscription (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plans), resulting in API usage charges rather than using your subscription's included usage." Also `--bare` mode "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain" and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `apiKeyHelper`.

verdict.corrected_claim: PARTIALLY REFUTED (the "silently" generalization is wrong; the -p and --bare clauses hold). Corrected: An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the worker's environment outranks the student's subscription login and bills the Console account, but it is silent ONLY in non-interactive mode. Official authentication precedence (code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, "Authentication precedence"): 1 cloud-provider vars (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`/`_VERTEX`/`_FOUNDRY`) > 2 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` > 3 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` > 4 `apiKeyHelper` > 5 `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` > 6 Anthropic profile/federation > 7 subscription OAuth from `/login`. So `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and an `apiKeyHelper` also override the subscription, and an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` even beats a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` passed into the container. Behaviour by mode: (a) `-p` / non-interactive: "the key is always used when present" — no prompt, so a `claude -p` worker switches billing with no warning. (b) Interactive `claude` (e.g. in tmux): "you are prompted once to approve or decline the key, and your choice is remembered"; the "Use custom API key" toggle in `/config` "only appears while `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set", and `/status` "marks the credential that isn't in use" — an interactive worker would BLOCK on that approval prompt rather than switch silently. (c) `--bare`: "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", also "does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`"; needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` in `--settings` JSON; and "will become the default for `-p` in a future release" (a `-p` worker relying on the subscription is therefore at risk on upgrade). (d) Exception: Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions "always use your subscription credentials" — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` there does not override; this exception does not apply to a self-run grid worker. Fallback to the subscription: `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, confirm with `/status`. Subscription OAuth on Linux lives in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (mode 0600; relocated by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`); a one-year subscription token comes from `claude setup-token` → `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise only; model requests only, no Remote Control or claude.ai connectors).
verdict.evidence: Fetched 2026-09-27. (1) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars — the claim's own source, verbatim entry [critical=true]: "`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | API key sent as `X-Api-Key` header. When set, this key is used instead of your Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription even if you are logged in. In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present. In interactive mode, you are prompted to approve the key once before it overrides your subscription. To use your subscription instead, run `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`". The claim quoted this entry but omitted the interactive-prompt sentence, which is what makes "silently" wrong for interactive sessions. (Note: this page's table was truncated in my fetch after `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, so I did not see the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`/`CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` rows there; those facts come from the authentication and headless pages below.) (2) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication — "Authentication precedence" [critical=true], verbatim numbered list: "1. Cloud provider credentials, when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` is set. ... 2. `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. Sent as the `Authorization: Bearer` header. ... 3. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable. Sent as the `X-Api-Key` header. ... In interactive mode, you are prompted once to approve or decline the key, and your choice is remembered. To change it later, use the "Use custom API key" toggle in `/config`. The toggle only appears while `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in your environment. In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present. 4. `apiKeyHelper` script output. ... 5. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. A long-lived OAuth token generated by `claude setup-token`. ... 6. Anthropic profile and federation credentials ... 7. Subscription OAuth credentials from `/login`. This is the default for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users." Also: "If you have an active Claude subscription but also have `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set in your environment, Claude Code uses the API key once you approve it." "Run `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to fall back to your subscription, and check `/status` to confirm which method is active. When a login and an API key are both configured, `/status` marks the credential that isn't in use." Exception: "Cloud sessions always use your subscription credentials. If you set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in the cloud environment, it doesn't override your subscription credentials." First launch: "If you've set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable, Claude Code skips the login prompt and asks you to approve the key instead." Credential storage: "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead". setup-token: "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token` ... set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable ... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors." "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." Also: "`apiKeyHelper`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` apply to the CLI and the surfaces that wrap it, including the VS Code extension, the Agent SDK, and GitHub Actions." (3) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless — "Start faster with bare mode" [critical=true]: "Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before running it, because bare mode doesn't use your subscription login". "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain. For the Anthropic API, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment, with a key created in the Claude Console, or supply an `apiKeyHelper` in the `--settings` JSON. Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry continue to read their own provider credentials as usual." Note box: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." Also: "When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout." (4) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference — `--bare` row: "Minimal mode: skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster. ... Sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`"; `claude setup-token`: "Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription."; `claude auth login --console` "to sign in with Anthropic Console for API usage billing instead of a Claude subscription"; `claude auth status` "Show authentication status as JSON ... Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not". (5) https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11145838-using-claude-code-with-your-pro-or-max-plan (page date August 19, 2026) — the claim's quote is verbatim: "If you have an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable set on your system, Claude Code will use this API key for authentication instead of your Claude subscription (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plans), resulting in API usage charges rather than using your subscription's included usage." This article does not mention the interactive approval prompt. (6) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs — "The Session block in `/usage` shows API token usage and is intended for API users. Claude Max and Pro subscribers have usage included in their subscription"; "`/usage-credits` ... the command isn't available with API key authentication" (a quick tell for which billing is active). (7) Adjacent, design-relevant, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead." Ashley's worker must therefore run the Claude Code CLI itself under the student's own login, not an SDK app rebranded as a product. Not verified: whether a flag exists to keep `-p` non-bare once `--bare` becomes the default — the docs I fetched do not name one.

findings.claim: Limit resets: Anthropic occasionally grants free 'limit resets' that restore a five-hour or weekly window to full; used from Settings > Usage ('Reset for free') or from the limit-reached card; single use, expire on a stated date.
findings.detail: 'What is a limit reset?' (updated this week): "Limit resets are given occasionally to eligible plans, and set your usage limits back to full when you choose to use one." "Depending on the limit reset shown, either your five-hour session limit or your weekly usage limit go back to full right away." "Once you use it, you can't undo it"; unused resets expire.

findings.claim: Usage-credits consent for Fable-family models can stall an unattended session: a consent prompt that nobody answers closes after `dialogExpiry` (5 min default) and the turn ends with a documented message; Remote Control clients cannot display it.
findings.detail: Error reference: `Fable limit reached · continuing on Fable 5.1 uses usage credits, and the prompt to confirm went unanswered — nothing was sent · answer it where this session is running, or /model to change` and `Fable 5.1 now uses usage credits · the prompt to confirm went unanswered — nothing was sent ...`. "This happens in Remote Control sessions, background sessions, and agent team teammate sessions." Fix: `/model` to a model that doesn't bill usage credits, or set `dialogExpiry` to a longer value or `"never"`.

topics_verified.recommendation: 1) Architecture: one persistent worker per student, authenticated only with that student's own credential; never a shared or lab-owned pool of student subscriptions. The sanctioned pattern in Anthropic's own text is "an end user ... signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code". 2) Credential handling in the Ashley extension: do not have the extension collect, store or relay the Claude.ai OAuth token or session cookies ("developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow"). Instead, have the extension open a terminal on the compute node (or locally) and let the student run `claude setup-token` (one-year token) or `claude` + `/login` (paste-code flow works over SSH/containers); the student writes the token into their own grid home (e.g. `~/.claude/env` or `~/.bashrc`, mode 0600) and the Slurm job exports `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from there. Prefer setup-token over `/login` for a 30-day job because `/login` credentials expire and refresh, and an unattended session "stops making progress once the credential expires". Ensure `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset in the job (it silently takes over billing in -p mode) and do not pass `--bare` (it ignores `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`). 3) Limit handling in the worker: run with `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, watch for `rate_limit_event` (`status: "rejected"`, `resetsAt`, `errorCode: "credits_required"`) and the result's `is_error`/`api_error_status`; on a rejection, park the queue until `resetsAt` and surface "You've hit your session/weekly limit · resets …" to the student in VS Code; do not rely on `--fallback-model` (documented as never triggering on rate-limit/billing errors) or on the interactive auto-continue (documented for interactive sessions only). Poll `/usage`-style data sparingly (the usage endpoint itself rate-limits). Keep concurrency per student low (one worker, few subagents): issue #96872 shows infra 429s at 6+ concurrent sessions even at 27% quota. 4) Capacity: tell students Pro/Max windows are 5-hour + weekly and are shared with their claude.ai chat; offer the documented overflow: enable usage credits at claude.ai Settings > Usage with a monthly spend limit (Pro/Max only), which the CLI exposes via `/usage-credits`. 5) For the lab/program itself, use the legitimate shared routes: a Claude Team plan (2+ seats, Premium seats 6.25x Pro, per-member limits, admin spend limits, `forceLoginOrgUUID` to pin logins), or Console API keys in a workspace with spend and rate limits (the auto-created "Claude Code" workspace supports per-user monthly caps and Claude-Code-only roles), or ask WSU to negotiate Claude for Education, which includes Claude Code institution-wide. Under any org plan the same rule holds: one seat/key identity per student, billed to the org, not one student's subscription serving others. 6) Before shipping, capture empirically the exact `claude -p --output-format json` payload and exit code at a real subscription limit (not documented verbatim), and note issue #87983's `is_error:false`-with-no-`result` envelope so the worker treats a missing `result` as failure.
open_questions: Exact `claude -p --output-format json` body (result text, is_error, subtype, api_error_status) and process exit code when a Pro/Max subscription 5-hour or weekly limit is hit on Claude Code 2.1.283 — no official page states it verbatim; must be captured by running a -p call at the limit.
Whether the interactive auto-continue-at-reset (`autoContinueAtUsageLimit`) has any effect on `-p`/stream-json runs; docs describe it only for interactive claude.ai-signed-in sessions.

The lifetime of a `/login` OAuth credential (docs give a 3-day expiry warning and refresh semantics but no absolute lifetime) versus the stated one-year `setup-token` lifetime; and whether a setup-token can be revoked from claude.ai if a student's grid home is compromised (revocation path not documented on the pages fetched).

Whether an extension that merely launches `claude setup-token` in a terminal and lets the student paste the token into their own dotfile counts as 'collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials' — the legal page's wording targets third-party developers routing requests for their users; a written answer from Anthropic sales/legal (contact-sales link on the legal page) would settle it for a university deployment.

The undocumented concurrent-session/infrastructure 429 ('Rate limited', rateLimits: null) reported from ~2026-09-16 at 6+ simultaneous sessions (issue #96872) — no maintainer statement yet on per-plan concurrency caps.

Whether WSU already holds a Claude for Education or Team/Enterprise agreement (which would change both the terms — Commercial vs Consumer — and the login-restriction settings the extension should ship).
Whether the Consumer Terms were revised after October 8, 2025 in a way not captured by the fetched page (the page shows 'Effective October 8, 2025' with a 'Previous Version' link only).

topics_verified.topic: Running Claude Code inside Singularity/Apptainer on a Slurm compute node whose host is CentOS 7.9 (glibc 2.17, kernel 5.15)
topics_verified.summary: Claude Code is now a single Bun-based native ELF binary on Linux; since v2.1.113 the npm package ships the same binary with no JavaScript fallback, so "npm vs native installer" is not a glibc escape hatch. Official requirements list Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 10+/Alpine 3.19+ (no RHEL/CentOS 7); the native installer performs no glibc check; a user diff shows 2.1.243 raised the maximum required symbol from GLIBC_2.17 to GLIBC_2.26, and 2.1.176 already SIGILLed on a CentOS 7.9/glibc 2.17 host. Running on the host is therefore not viable; running inside a node:22-bookworm (glibc 2.36) container is, because Apptainer/Singularity containers share only the host kernel (5.15 satisfies Bun's 5.6 recommendation) and use the image's glibc. Claude Code writes to ~/.claude (transcripts, credentials 0600, shell snapshots, plugins), ~/.claude.json (OAuth session, trust), and /tmp/claude-<uid>; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR moves all of the first two, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR moves the third, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 stops writes to ~/.local/share/claude. Apptainer pulls docker:// images to SIF unprivileged (no root/fakeroot), binds $HOME, CWD, /tmp, /var/tmp, /proc, /sys, /dev by default, uses the host network namespace unless --net, and honours APPTAINERENV_/SINGULARITYENV_ prefixes plus --env/--env-file in both 3.8 and 1.2; critically, non-setuid Singularity 3.8 must extract every SIF to a sandbox directory per run and cannot use --writable-tmpfs, whereas Apptainer 1.1+ mounts SIF with bundled squashfuse and, on kernel >=5.11, uses unprivileged kernel overlayfs, so the apptainer/1.2.2 module is the right runtime. --dangerously-skip-permissions is refused for uid 0 (so never --fakeroot), and Anthropic's own devcontainer docs endorse it for a non-root user inside a container. Subscription auth works headlessly via the paste-code login flow or a one-year `claude setup-token` in CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; that token cannot start Remote Control, which needs a full /login and Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, uses outbound HTTPS polling only, and must live in tmux/screen. No published report of Claude Code inside Apptainer was found; the closest are HPC-center pages (JHPCE, CU Neurology, Anthropic's own SLURM+tmux write-up) and issue #42952 (Bash tool shell-snapshot failure under HPC cgroups). Slurm facts verified verbatim: pam_slurm_adopt denial strings and its PrologFlags=contain requirement, srun --x11 (no --x11 on sbatch), --signal=B:USR1@N semantics (up to 60 s early, batch-shell only, needs background+wait+trap), --requeue vs PreemptMode=REQUEUE, --dependency=singleton, and srun --jobid --overlap --pty as an ssh alternative. VS Code adds a second glibc wall: VS Code Server 1.99+ needs glibc >=2.28, so Remote-SSH must land inside the container via `RemoteCommand` + `remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand`, and the Claude Code VS Code extension bundles its own native binary that would also fail on the host.

findings.claim: Claude Code's official Linux system requirements list Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+ and Alpine 3.19+; RHEL/CentOS 7 is not listed, and the package-manager section covers apt (Debian/Ubuntu), dnf (Fedora/RHEL) and apk (Alpine) only.
findings.detail: Setup page: 'Operating system: macOS 13.0+, Windows 10 1809+ or Windows Server 2019+, Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, Alpine Linux 3.19+'. Official docs, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install#native-binary-not-found-after-npm-install : "The `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` npm package downloads the native binary as a per-platform optional dependency, such as `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64`. npm then runs the package's postinstall script, which copies that binary into place as the `claude` command; until it runs, `claude` is a placeholder script." ... "The native binary is delivered only as an optional dependency, so there is no JavaScript fallback if it is skipped, and running `install.cjs` again can't place a binary that was never downloaded." ... "If postinstall can't run in your environment at all, `node node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli-wrapper.cjs` finds the downloaded package and launches it, at the cost of an extra Node process on each start. If the wrapper prints `Could not find native binary package` instead, the platform package was never downloaded" ... "Prebuilt binaries are published for `darwin-arm64`, `darwin-x64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-x64-musl`, `linux-arm64-musl`, `win32-x64`, and `win32-arm64`. Claude Code does not ship a binary for other platforms" ... "Corporate npm mirror ... Ensure your registry mirrors all eight `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-*` platform packages in addition to the meta package." Also: on Windows "bin/claude.exe is that same shell-script placeholder rather than a real executable".

5. cli-wrapper.cjs is a launcher, not a JS implementation. https://unpkg.com/@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.283/cli-wrapper.cjs : detects platform/arch, maps to `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-<platform>`, `require.resolve`s it and `spawnSync`s the binary; error string `[${WRAPPER_NAME}] Could not find native binary package "${info.pkg}".`; musl detection via `report.header?.glibcVersionRuntime === undefined`. https://unpkg.com/@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.113/install.cjs : hardlink (fallback copy) of the platform binary into bin/claude.exe; on failure prints `[... postinstall] Native package "${info.pkg}" not found.` and `Fallback: node <dir>/cli-wrapper.cjs`. Neither file contains Claude Code itself.

6. WHY refuted=true (one wrong detail): the claim says "ships only the native glibc binary". False for Linux: https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64/2.1.283 has os ["linux"], cpu ["x64"], libc ["glibc"], description "Native binary for Claude Code on linux-x64", unpackedSize 241,557,250 B; https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64-musl/2.1.283 has libc musl, "Native binary for Claude Code on linux-x64-musl", 235,311,792 B. npm selects between them by the `libc` field. Issue #50270 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/50270, title "v2.1.113+ broken on Termux/Android: native binary requires glibc, no JS fallback", opened 2026-04-18, still open, no maintainer reply) is an Android/bionic problem -- neither glibc nor musl -- not evidence of glibc-only. Second additional error quoted there: `error: "bin/claude.exe" has unexpected e_type: 2`.

7. Nuance for the design (NO node.js on the grid host): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#install-with-npm : "As of v2.1.198, the npm package requires Node.js 22 or later. On an older Node.js version, npm prints an `EBADENGINE` warning during install rather than failing; the install completes and `claude` still runs, since the package downloads a native binary that doesn't use your Node.js at runtime." and "The npm package installs the same native binary as the standalone installer ... The installed `claude` binary does not itself invoke Node." So npm is pointless on a node-less host; use the native installer `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash` (installs to ~/.local/bin/claude -> ~/.local/share/claude/versions/), or pin with `bash -s <version>`, or download the platform binary and verify against `https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/{VERSION}/manifest.json` (GPG-signed from 2.1.89). Env vars: `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` stops background checks; `DISABLE_UPDATES` blocks all update paths; `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0` if bundled rg fails. Alpine/musl runtime needs `libgcc`, `libstdc++`, `ripgrep`.

8. NOT VERIFIED (web search budget exhausted): the minimum glibc version the linux-x64 native binary requires. The platform package READMEs state no floor; the setup page lists Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 10+ (glibc 2.31 / 2.28) as supported OSes, which is suggestive but not a stated glibc requirement. This matters if anyone runs the binary directly on the CentOS 7.9 host (glibc 2.17); inside a Singularity/Apptainer container the image's glibc governs, not the host's, so the design should test `claude --version` inside the chosen image rather than assume. critical=true for: (a) no JS fallback -> a node-less host cannot substitute; (b) npm path requires Node at install time only; (c) native installer needs no Node; (d) glibc floor unknown.

findings.claim: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates the whole ~/.claude tree (settings, session history, plugins) AND the credentials file; when set, ~/.claude.json is also written inside that directory, which is the documented way to persist a login in a container.
findings.detail: env-vars: 'CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR — Override the configuration directory (default: ~/.claude). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path. ... Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings'. authentication: 'If you've set the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable, Claude Code keeps the .credentials.json file under that directory instead'. devcontainer: 'It stores your OAuth account, personal MCP servers, and per-project trust in ~/.claude.json, a separate file outside that directory, so mounting a volume at ~/.claude alone doesn't keep you signed in. Mount a named volume at ~/.claude and set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to the same path so Claude Code writes .claude.json inside the volume.' Example: "containerEnv": {"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR": "/home/node/.claude"}. Note GitHub issue #30538 reports the VS Code extension ignoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (not verified here).

verdict.corrected_claim: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.claude) relocates the whole ~/.claude tree — settings, session history/transcripts, plugins, cache, IDE lock files — AND the Linux/Windows credentials file .credentials.json (on macOS it also keys the Keychain entry to that directory), AND, when set, Claude Code writes .claude.json (OAuth account/sign-in session, personal MCP servers, per-project trust) inside that directory instead of at ~/.claude.json. Mounting a persistent volume at the directory and setting CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to the same path is the documented way to keep a login across container rebuilds; the documented alternative for CI/containers is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from `claude setup-token` (model requests only; not read in --bare mode). CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is honoured from the shell, user settings or managed settings and is dropped from project/local settings `env` (since v2.1.251). The claim's env-vars quote is stale wording: the current env-vars row reads "Directory where Claude Code stores its configuration, cache, and data files (default: `~/.claude`). Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings"; the "settings, session history, and plugins" sentence is on the /settings page. GitHub issue #30538 (VS Code extension ignores CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) is still OPEN as of 2026-09-22, but the CHANGELOG records extension-side fixes in 2.1.268, 2.1.269, 2.1.271, 2.1.274 and 2.1.275 for CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR "set in a settings file or the `environmentVariables` setting", so on extension 2.1.283 the extension reads it from `claudeCode.environmentVariables`; the last "still reproduces" report on the issue is ext 2.1.181 (2026-06-19).
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds in substance on every point; two precision corrections (stale quote attribution; #30538 status). All URLs below were fetched 2026-09-27.

[1] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer — section "Persist authentication and settings across rebuilds", verbatim: "Claude Code stores its authentication token, user settings, and session history under the ~/.claude directory. It stores your OAuth account, personal MCP servers, and per-project trust in ~/.claude.json, a separate file outside that directory, so mounting a volume at ~/.claude alone doesn't keep you signed in. Mount a named volume at ~/.claude and set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to the same path so Claude Code writes .claude.json inside the volume." Example verbatim: "mounts": ["source=claude-code-config,target=/home/node/.claude,type=volume"], "containerEnv": {"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR": "/home/node/.claude"}. Same page: "To carry authentication across codespaces, store ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from claude setup-token as a Codespaces secret." Same page, login-in-container: "copy the code shown in the browser and paste it at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt". Same page warns dev containers with --dangerously-skip-permissions can exfiltrate "the Claude Code credentials stored in ~/.claude". critical=true (design depends on CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR + persistent dir to keep the Slurm-job CLI signed in).

[2] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json — live reference config, line 43 "remoteUser": "node"; line 46 "source=claude-code-config-${devcontainerId},target=/home/node/.claude,type=volume"; line 50 "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR": "/home/node/.claude". [3] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication — "Credential management", verbatim: "On Linux, credentials are stored in ~/.claude/.credentials.json with file mode 0600." ... "If you've set the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable, Claude Code keeps the .credentials.json file under that directory instead, including the file the macOS fallback writes, and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory too, so a session with a different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR reads a different entry." Also: "claude setup-token" prints a one-year OAuth token; "It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN environment variable"; "It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors"; "Bare mode does not read CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN." Auth precedence: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (5) outranks subscription OAuth from /login (7). critical=true (credentials-file relocation is the half of login persistence that .claude.json does not cover; setup-token is the fallback path for a headless Slurm job).

[4] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars — CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR row, verbatim: "Directory where Claude Code stores its configuration, cache, and data files (default: `~/.claude`). Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings". The claim's wording "Override the configuration directory ... All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path" does NOT appear on this page today. The page contains no mention of .claude.json or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. critical=false (wording only).

[5] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings — Info box, verbatim: "To keep the home-directory files somewhere else, set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; Claude Code then stores your settings, session history, and plugins there instead." Next paragraph: "Claude Code also keeps a fifth file, ~/.claude.json, that it writes for itself ... It holds your sign-in session, MCP server configurations, per-project state such as trust decisions, and the global config keys that /config writes for you." Corrupt-file behaviour: backups go to ~/.claude/backups/.claude.json.backup.<timestamp> (five kept). critical=false.

[6] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory (also fetched as .md, 109,985 bytes) — verbatim: "If you set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, every ~/.claude path on this page lives under that directory instead." Page lists ~/.claude.json ("App state, OAuth, UI toggles, personal MCP servers"), .credentials.json ("your login credentials"), plugins/, projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl (transcripts), history.jsonl, sessions/, debug/, backups/. Also: "Don't delete ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json, or ~/.claude/plugins/: those hold your auth, preferences, and installed plugins." critical=false.

Claude Code drops each one ... and logs a warning you can see with claude --debug. They include: Variables that choose where Claude Code stores or writes its own files: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, and the operating-system directory variables such as HOME, TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP, and the XDG_* family." "Global config settings": "Save these keys in ~/.claude.json, not in a settings file. Claude Code ignores them anywhere else." critical=false.

findings.claim: Claude Code writes these paths under ~/.claude (or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR): projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl transcripts, sessions/, debug/, shell-snapshots/, file-history/, plans/, history.jsonl, plugins/, backups/, .credentials.json, settings.json; the age sweep defaults to cleanupPeriodDays=30.

Removed on clean exit'; 'debug/ — Per-session debug logs'; 'history.jsonl — Every prompt you've typed'; 'backups/ — Earlier versions of ~/.claude.json'; 'cleanupPeriodDays ... default is 30 days and the minimum is 1'. sessions doc: transcripts at '~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, where <project> is your working directory path with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by -' (names >200 chars are truncated + hashed). verdict.corrected_claim: Claude Code writes these paths under ~/.claude (or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR): projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl transcripts, sessions/, debug/, shell-snapshots/, file-history/, plans/, history.jsonl, plugins/, backups/, .credentials.json, settings.json; the age sweep defaults to cleanupPeriodDays=30 (minimum 1; 0 fails validation). verdict.corrected_claim: Claude Code's own temp tree is <tmp>/claude-<uid>/ on Unix (<tmp>/claude/ on Windows, no uid), where <tmp> is /tmp on macOS and Node os.tmpdir() on Linux and Windows — i.e. on Linux $TMPDIR, then $TMP, then $TEMP, else /tmp. CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR replaces <tmp> (added v2.1.5, 2026-01-12). The tree holds the per-session scratchpad (<tmp>/claude-<uid>/<project>/<session-id>/scratchpad/) and, since v2.1.275 (2026-09-17), pasted/attached images in a per-session images/ directory. Spilled large tool outputs are NOT in the temp tree: they go to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/ (under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), together with full-size copies of images MCP tools return. On a cluster whose /tmp is swept, set CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR to a short path on persistent storage in the shell environment, user settings or managed settings — it is dropped with a warning from project and local .claude/settings.json (since v2.1.251) — and keep ~/.claude on persistent storage too. At startup (macOS/Linux) Claude Code exits 1 rather than start if <tmp>/claude-<uid> cannot be created (ENOSPC) or fails the symlink / ownership / 0700 checks ("Refusing to use it"). Because the Linux default follows $TMPDIR, a Slurm prolog or Singularity environment that exports TMPDIR silently relocates the tree unless CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR is set explicitly.

verdict.corrected_claim: Native installs auto-update in the background: Claude Code checks on startup and periodically while running, downloads new versions under ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ and, on macOS/Linux, manages ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink into that directory (re-pointed on update ONLY when the installer created it; since v2.1.207 a custom script/symlink at that path is left in place, new versions still land in versions/, and every version is kept on disk). Updates take effect on the next start. DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 stops only the background check (`claude update` and `claude install` still work; `claude doctor` then shows "disabled (set by env: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER)" on the Auto-updates line). DISABLE_UPDATES=1 is stricter and blocks all update paths including manual `claude update` and `claude install`. If an npm global install cannot auto-update because the npm global directory is not writable, Claude Code shows a one-time notice at startup and `claude doctor` lists the fixes. `autoUpdatesChannel` is "latest" (default) or "stable" (~1 week old); `minimumVersion` is a floor that auto-update and `claude update` will not go below; managed `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` make Claude refuse to start outside a range and updates respect the ceiling. Devcontainer doc: to pin, install with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@X.Y.Z` in the Dockerfile and set "DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER": "1" in containerEnv. The npm package (Node.js 22+ required as of v2.1.198, older Node only prints EBADENGINE) installs the same native binary via a per-platform optional dependency; the installed `claude` does not invoke Node at runtime.

Whether the linux-x64 native binary runs on CentOS 7.9 glibc 2.17 was NOT verified here (out of this claim's scope). (c) DISABLE_UPDATES was verified only in the env-vars table and setup prose; no independent `claude doctor` output string for DISABLE_UPDATES was found (only the DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER string is documented). WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) so no third-party corroboration was sought; all evidence is first-party official docs.

verdict.corrected_claim: Subscription (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise) authentication works without a browser on the compute node. Interactive path: `claude` (or `claude auth login`) on the node prints a login URL (press `c` to copy it); the student opens it in the laptop browser; because the browser cannot reach the CLI's local callback server (documented as common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers) the BROWSER shows a login code after sign-in, which the student pastes into the node terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt; the terminal then shows `Login successful`. The CLI does not print the code. Headless path: `claude setup-token` runs the same browser authorization flow, prints a one-year OAuth token to the terminal, saves nothing; set it as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. That token requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan, "can only make model requests", cannot establish Remote Control sessions (exact error: `Remote Control requires a full-scope login token`) or fetch claude.ai connectors, and is NOT read in `--bare` mode (`--bare` = `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`: "OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read", authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` in `--settings`). Precedence (v2.1.283 docs): (1) cloud provider when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`/`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`/`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` set; (2) `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (Bearer); (3) `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (X-Api-Key; approved once interactively, "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present"); (4) `apiKeyHelper`; (5) `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; (6) Anthropic profile / federation credentials (a `user_oauth` active profile ranks BELOW `/login` unless named in `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`); (7) `/login` subscription OAuth. A signed-in Claude apps gateway session sits outside the list and outranks all of it. Expiry: for the credential created by `/login`, a startup warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (added v2.1.203 at five days out; three days only from v2.1.217; informational, never blocks); once it expires and cannot be refreshed, each model request fails with `Login expired · Please run /login` (also seen as `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`; before v2.1.206 it surfaced as a model error). The warning is documented only for `/login` credentials, not for `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; for that token the docs say only "To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". The `/login` credential's own lifetime is NOT stated anywhere in the docs ("The login lifetime itself is unchanged"). `/login` is not available under `-p`. On Linux credentials live in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (mode 0600), or under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if set.
