VERDICT: claim holds; refinements below. All URLs fetched 2026-09-27; docs state latest CLI 2.1.283 (2026-09-25).

[critical=true] PASTE-CODE FLOW — verbatim, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication: "If the browser doesn't open automatically, press `c` to copy the login URL to your clipboard, then paste it into your browser. If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers. When login completes, the terminal shows `Login successful`". Corroborated, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install section "OAuth login fails in WSL2, SSH, or containers": "the browser usually opens on a different host and its redirect can't reach Claude Code's local callback server. After you sign in, the browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back automatically. Paste that code into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt to complete login." and "Alternatively, press `c` at the interactive login prompt to copy the OAuth URL, or copy the URL that `claude auth login` prints, and open it in a browser on your local machine." Failure string: "`OAuth error: Invalid code. Please make sure the full code was copied`, the login code expired or was truncated during copy-paste." REFINEMENT: the claim's headline says "the login flow prints a code" — the CLI prints a URL; the browser shows the code. Direction matters for the extension UI (student must relay URL node→laptop and code laptop→node). No `--device-code`/`--no-browser` flag exists in https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference; `claude auth login` supports only `--email`, `--sso`, `--console`; `claude auth status` "Show authentication status as JSON. Use `--text` ... Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not" (useful for the extension's health check).

[critical=true] SETUP-TOKEN — verbatim, authentication page: "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token` ... The command opens the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, and the token prints to the terminal after you approve access in the browser. It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable ... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." cli-reference: "Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars row `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`: "OAuth access token for claude.ai authentication. Alternative to `/login` for SDK and automated environments. Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials ... Unless you run `/login`, Claude Code uses the token you set for the whole session. To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions: "an OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran `claude setup-token`". NOTE: docs do not explicitly say the paste-code fallback applies inside `setup-token`; it says "the same browser authorization flow as `/login`" — inferred, not stated. Also setup-token "enforce[s] only `forceLoginMethod`" not `forceLoginOrgUUID`.

[critical=true] BARE MODE — verbatim, authentication page: "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain. For the Anthropic API, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` ... or supply an `apiKeyHelper` in the `--settings` JSON." and "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." env-vars row `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`: "OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read, so Anthropic authentication must come from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` in `--settings`. Equivalent to passing `--bare`". Also bare mode doesn't read Anthropic profiles. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: the persistent grid Claude Code must NOT use `--bare` if it is to run on the student's subscription; and if `-p` ever becomes bare-by-default, subscription auth under `-p` breaks — pin the version or pass an explicit non-bare mode.

[critical=true] REMOTE CONTROL — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control: "Subscription: available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported." Error "Remote Control requires a full-scope login token": "You're authenticated with a long-lived token from `claude setup-token` or the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. These tokens can only make model requests, so they can't establish Remote Control sessions. Run `claude auth login` to authenticate with a full-scope session token instead." Also "Remote Control requires claude.ai subscription auth." + "`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, so this session is using API-key auth". Also fails when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is not api.anthropic.com or any `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` is set. So if Ashley's laptop→node prompt transport were Remote Control, only a `/login` credential (paste-code flow) works on the node, never setup-token.

[critical=true] PRECEDENCE — authentication page "Authentication precedence" numbered 1–7 exactly as in claim; extra: "A signed-in Claude apps gateway session sits outside this list ... and it outranks them"; profile nuance: active `user_oauth` profile ranks "below a working `/login` credential". env-vars row `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: "When set, this key is used instead of your Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription even if you are logged in. In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present. In interactive mode, you are prompted to approve the key once before it overrides your subscription. To use your subscription instead, run `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`". Also: "If you run `/login` while the variable [CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN] is set, Claude Code switches the current session to the new login, but reads the variable again in every new session". Upstream CHANGELOG (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md) records a fixed bug "a transient 401 replacing a long-lived `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` with a stored login's short-lived token, breaking headless sessions until restart" — do not mix a stored `/login` and the env token in the same config dir; use `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to separate.

[critical=true] EXPIRY — authentication page "Renew an expiring login": "When the login you created with `/login` is within three days of expiring, Claude Code shows a warning at startup: `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. Before v2.1.217, the warning appeared five days out. ... The login lifetime itself is unchanged; the advance warning is what v2.1.203 adds. Once the stored login expires and can't be refreshed, each model request fails with `Login expired · Please run /login` ... Before v2.1.206, Claude Code reported an expired login on model requests as a model error instead." `/status` shows `Login` row `Expired — log in again` (v2.1.210+). "The warning appears only when a claude.ai or Claude Console login is the active credential, and not when a cloud provider, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` supplies the credential." "A background session ... or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." CHANGELOG confirms independently: 2.1.203 "Added a warning when your login is about to expire, so you can re-authenticate before background sessions are interrupted"; 2.1.217 "Changed the login-expiry warning to appear 3 days before expiry instead of 5"; 2.1.206 "Fixed an expired login failing every model with a misleading 'There's an issue with the selected model' error instead of prompting to run `/login`". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors also lists `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`, `OAuth token refresh failed — run /login to re-authenticate`, `OAuth token revoked` / `OAuth token has expired`. UNKNOWN (say plainly): the docs never state how long a `/login` credential lasts or how long its refresh keeps working unattended; for a 30-day `primary` QoS job this is unmeasured — the only documented one-year figure is for `setup-token`, which in turn has no documented advance warning and no Remote Control.

[critical=false] STORAGE — authentication page: "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`" and "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead". On the grid `~` is Panasas and shared across warrior and compute nodes, so a `/login` done once on any node is visible to all (filesystem fact, not a doc claim). `/login` is unavailable under `-p`: headless page "Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available."

Sources fetched: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.md ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md

findings.claim: Non-interactive mode supports a long-lived multi-turn worker: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`, fixed `--session-id <uuid>`, `--resume <id|/path/to.jsonl>` from any directory (v2.1.223+), `--continue`, `--fork-session`, `--permission-prompts none` (v2.1.259+); SIGTERM exits 143 and leaves the turn unfinished unless CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1.
findings.detail: cli-reference: '--input-format — Specify input format for print mode (options: text, stream-json)'; '--session-id — Use a specific session ID for the conversation (must be a valid UUID)'; '--fork-session — When resuming, create a new session ID'; '--permission-prompts — Set who answers permission prompts in print mode ... Pass none when nobody can answer ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later'; '--max-turns ... With --input-format stream-json, a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn'. headless: 'If you stop a claude -p run with SIGTERM ... Claude Code exits with code 143 ... To end the turn instead, send SIGINT'; 'set CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1' to continue the turn on resume; 'Piped stdin is capped at 10MB'; 'Claude Code finds the session by its ID in any project on this machine. Before v2.1.223, Claude Code looked for the ID only in the current project directory'. Bare mode: '--bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls' but 'bare mode never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain' (API key only).

verdict.corrected_claim: Non-interactive mode supports a long-lived multi-turn worker, but the command line must include --verbose: `claude -p --verbose --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json` (without --verbose, Claude Code 2.1.283 exits 1 with `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`). It supports a fixed `--session-id <uuid>` (rejects non-UUIDs with `Error: Invalid session ID. Must be a valid UUID.`), `--resume <session-id|name|/abs/path/to.jsonl>` from any directory (cross-project ID lookup since v2.1.223, resolved only when exactly one other project holds a transcript for it), `--continue` (most recent conversation in the CURRENT directory; `claude -p --continue` includes -p/SDK sessions), `--fork-session` (optionally with `--session-id` to choose the fork's ID, since v2.0.73), and `--permission-prompts none` (added v2.1.259; choices "host"|"none", default "host"). SIGTERM exits 143 and leaves the in-progress turn unfinished with no result; that is unchanged by any env var. `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1` only changes the NEXT resume, making Claude Code continue the interrupted turn automatically (bounded by `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS`; a turn that failed with an API error auto-resumes only within 6 hours). `--bare` (= `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`) never reads OAuth credentials, the keychain, or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so a worker on a student's Claude Pro/Max subscription must NOT use --bare; subscription auth in an unattended job comes from `claude setup-token` -> `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (one-year token) or a stored /login (Linux: `~/.claude/.credentials.json`), and any `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment is always used instead in -p mode. Anthropic's SDK docs state that, unless previously approved, third-party developers may not offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim is substantively right but the quoted command line is wrong as written, and two details are compressed misleadingly. Findings (critical=true where the Ashley design depends on it):

[1] critical=true — --verbose is REQUIRED with -p + stream-json output. Tested on the binary bundled with the VS Code extension (C:\Users\grego\.vscode\extensions\anthropic.claude-code-2.1.283-win32-x64\resources\native-binary\claude.exe, `claude --version` -> `2.1.283 (Claude Code)`), with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointed at a dead local port so no API traffic occurred. Both `claude --bare -p --max-turns 1 --output-format stream-json "x"` and `claude --bare -p --max-turns 1 --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json` exit 1 with the exact string `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`. The headless page's own streaming example is `claude -p "Explain recursion" --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages` and every cli-reference example pairs `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, but neither page states the requirement as a rule; the claim's command omits it. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless ("Stream responses"); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference; local binary test.

[2] critical=true — Long-lived multi-turn worker is supported. cli-reference: `--input-format` "Specify input format for print mode (options: `text`, `stream-json`)"; 2.1.283 --help: `--input-format <format> Input format (only works with --print): "text" (default), or "stream-json" (realtime streaming input)`; `--replay-user-messages` "Re-emit user messages from stdin back on stdout for acknowledgment. Requires `--input-format stream-json` and `--output-format stream-json`"; `--max-turns` "With `--input-format stream-json`, a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit". Agent SDK doc: "Streaming Input Mode: a persistent, interactive session ... allows the agent to operate as a long lived process that takes in user input, handles interruptions, surfaces permission requests, and handles session management"; queued messages "process sequentially, with ability to interrupt"; stdin user-message shape `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."},"parent_tool_use_id":null}`. Changelog: 2.1.265 "Fixed non-interactive sessions (`-p` with stream-json input, Agent SDK, cloud sessions) resetting the shell working directory at each new user message; a `cd` now persists across turns"; 2.1.257 "Fixed unbounded memory growth when non-JSONL data is piped into `claude -p --input-format stream-json`; it now fails fast with a clear error"; 2.1.281 "Fixed `--input-format stream-json` sessions (Agent SDK, VS Code extension) ... failing every turn with an error when an earlier assistant message had plain-string content"; 2.1.274 "Improved startup in `--input-format stream-json` sessions: the first turn no longer waits up to 2s for still-connecting MCP servers". Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md (top entry 2.1.283).

[3] critical=true — --session-id: cli-reference row `--session-id` "Use a specific session ID for the conversation (must be a valid UUID)". Local 2.1.283 with `--session-id not-a-uuid` exits with exact string `Error: Invalid session ID. Must be a valid UUID.` (validated before any network call). Changelog 2.0.73: "Added support for custom session IDs when forking sessions with `--session-id` combined with `--resume` or `--continue` and `--fork-session`".

[4] critical=true — --resume from any directory / .jsonl path: cli-reference `--resume`, `-r` row: "Resume a specific session by ID or name, or show an interactive picker ... In place of an ID, you can pass the absolute path to a session's `.jsonl` transcript file ... When you pass a session ID, Claude Code searches the current project directory and its git worktrees, then every other project on this machine. Before v2.1.223, the ID search covered only the current project directory and its git worktrees." Sessions page adds a constraint the claim omits: "The cross-project search resolves the ID only when exactly one other project holds a transcript with messages for it, so a hand-copied duplicate makes Claude Code report not-found"; error string `No conversation found with session ID: <session-id>`. Transcripts live at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl` (`<project>` = cwd path with non-alphanumerics -> `-`), relocatable with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` (v2.1.234+); "The entry format is internal to Claude Code and changes between versions". `-p` sessions are excluded from the picker and from plain `claude --continue` but "You can still resume one by passing its session ID to `claude --resume <session-id>`". Note: the 2.1.223 changelog section itself does not mention the cross-project lookup; the version number rests on three doc pages (headless, cli-reference, sessions) that all say "Before v2.1.223". Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference.

[5] --continue: cli-reference: "Load the most recent conversation in the current directory ... Skips sessions created with `claude -p` or the Agent SDK ... `claude -p --continue` includes `-p`, SDK, and `/loop` sessions"; headless: on v2.1.257+ `--continue` opens a finished background session but not a running one. `--fork-session`: "When resuming, create a new session ID instead of reusing the original (use with `--resume` or `--continue`)". Non-interactive resume does NOT restore the stored permission mode: "`claude -p --resume` or `claude -p --continue`. Claude Code starts the run in the permission mode a new `claude -p` run would start in" (plan mode excepted, v2.1.246+). Changelog 2.1.137-era line: "Fixed fork-session lineage being lost after compaction in headless and SDK sessions".

[6] critical=true — --permission-prompts none: cli-reference "Set who answers permission prompts in print mode. With the default `host`, Claude Code sends them to the Agent SDK host or the `--permission-prompt-tool` tool. Pass `none` when nobody can answer, and Claude Code denies them instead ... Requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later"; headless: "The `--permission-prompts` flag requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later. Earlier versions reject it with an unknown-option error"; "With `--permission-prompts none`, Claude Code removes the tools that need an answer from a person, such as `AskUserQuestion`"; denials appear as `permission_denied` system messages and in the result's `permission_denials`. Changelog 2.1.259: "Added `--permission-prompts none` for unattended headless hosts". 2.1.283 --help: `(choices: "host", "none", default: "host")`. For -p "the built-in starting permission mode is Manual on every plan", so pass `--permission-mode` (auto|acceptEdits|dontAsk) or `--allowedTools` explicitly.

[7] critical=true — SIGTERM / 143 / interrupted turn: headless: "If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM ... Claude Code exits with code 143. Claude Code leaves the turn that was in progress unfinished and records no result for it. To end the turn instead, send SIGINT, or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()`, before you stop the process." "On SIGTERM, Claude Code terminates the process tree of any Bash command that is still running. Claude Code then runs `SessionEnd` hooks and exits." "When you resume the session, Claude Code leaves the interrupted turn as it is ... To have Claude Code continue the interrupted turn on resume instead, set `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1`." CORRECTION to the claim's phrasing: the env var does not alter exit/turn behaviour at SIGTERM time; it governs the next resume. env-vars: `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN` "Set to `1` to automatically resume if the previous session ended mid-turn ... Before v2.1.221, Claude Code ignored `0`"; `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS` "Unset or `0` means no bound, except that a turn whose last request failed with an API error resumes only while that error is less than six hours old ... Spawn scripts for long-running agents can set this so a restart against an old transcript doesn't re-run a stale prompt"; `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT` defaults to `Continue from where you left off.`. Changelog: 2.1.212 "Fixed SIGTERM during a running Bash tool orphaning the command's process tree in print/SDK mode; the CLI now aborts the turn, kills the tree, and exits 143"; 2.1.236 "SIGTERM in print/SDK mode no longer records an interrupted turn or synthetic tool denials before exiting; running commands are still terminated and the process still exits with code 143"; 2.1.269 fix for RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN re-running turns older than 6 h; 2.1.274 fix for `claude -p --resume` with RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN not reporting leftover background tasks. Slurm relevance: scancel/wall-time kill delivers SIGTERM, so the worker will exit 143 mid-turn; design a SIGINT-first shutdown (e.g. `scancel --signal=INT` ahead of the kill) and set RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1 plus a MAX_AGE bound on the relaunch. Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.

[8] Stdin cap: headless: "Piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status." This appears under "Pipe data through Claude"; NO doc found stating whether it applies cumulatively to a long-lived `--input-format stream-json` stdin. Unverified either way; treat as a risk for a 30-day worker fed many prompts and test empirically. Also: "If Claude Code can't read stdin ... Claude Code prints a warning to stderr and continues with the prompt from the command line." Background shells are killed ~5 s after the final result once stdin closes; `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default 600000, v2.1.182+) caps waiting on background subagents.

[9] critical=true — Bare mode vs subscription: headless: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release"; "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain. For the Anthropic API, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` ... or supply an `apiKeyHelper` in the `--settings` JSON"; "bare mode doesn't use your subscription login". authentication: "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." env-vars `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` (set by --bare): "OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read". Changelog 2.1.81: "Added `--bare` flag for scripted `-p` calls ... requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` via `--settings` (OAuth and keychain auth disabled)". 2.1.283 --help: "Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ...". Consequence: an Ashley worker on the student's Pro/Max subscription cannot use --bare, and if the future default flips, must pass whatever opt-out exists then. Subscription path for an unattended job: authentication "Generate a long-lived token ... generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token` ... It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable"; env-vars `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` "Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials". On Linux a /login is stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode 0600. Precedence trap: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` "When set, this key is used instead of your Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription ... In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present" — the Singularity job environment must not carry a stray ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Expiry: "A background session ... that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again"; error `Login expired · Please run /login`. Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.

[10] critical=true — Policy: Agent SDK overview: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead." and branding rule "Not permitted: 'Claude Code' or 'Claude Code Agent'". Whether a university VS Code extension that launches the student's own `claude` under their own subscription counts as "offering claude.ai login for a product" is a terms question, not a technical one; flag for the synthesizer. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview.

[11] Other exact strings: `--no-session-persistence` "Disable session persistence so sessions are not saved to disk and cannot be resumed. Print mode only" (do NOT use it for the resumable worker); `--include-partial-messages` "Requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json`"; `-p` rejects `--bg`; `system/init` carries a `capabilities` array (v2.1.205+) e.g. `interrupt_receipt_v1`, `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1`, for feature detection instead of version comparison; `--mcp-config` with -p waits up to `MCP_TIMEOUT` (30 s default) for servers before the first turn (v2.1.221+).

Fetched URLs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (and .md) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (.md) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication (.md) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md. Local test binary: Claude Code 2.1.283 (VS Code extension bundle), Windows; no API requests were made during tests.

findings.claim: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is refused when the process runs as root on Linux/macOS; Anthropic documents it as appropriate for a non-root user inside a container. Apptainer runs the container as the invoking uid, so this works unless --fakeroot is used.
findings.detail: devcontainer: 'Because the container runs Claude Code as a non-root user and confines command execution to the container, you can pass --dangerously-skip-permissions for unattended operation. The CLI rejects this flag when launched as root, so confirm remoteUser is set to a non-root account.' sandbox-environments: 'On Linux and macOS, Claude Code refuses to start with this flag when running as root, so run the container, VM, or sandbox runtime as a non-root user.' Exact CLI error (issue #9184, v2.0.10, closed): '--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons'. Web-search summaries mention an IS_SANDBOX=1 override for uid 0 (not confirmed on any fetched official page; env-vars page has no IS_SANDBOX entry). Admins can block the mode with `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"`. cli-reference: '--dangerously-skip-permissions — Skip permission prompts. Equivalent to --permission-mode bypassPermissions'.

verdict.corrected_claim: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (equivalent to `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) is refused on Linux/macOS when the process's uid is 0 (root or sudo); the CLI prints `--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons` and exits 1. Anthropic documents running it as a non-root user inside a container/VM/sandbox runtime and states the check "is skipped automatically inside a recognized sandbox"; the recognition is an undocumented `IS_SANDBOX=1` (or `CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP=1`) environment check in the shipped cli.js, not listed on the env-vars page. Apptainer/Singularity run the container as the invoking user's uid (`PR_NO_NEW_PRIVS`, no escalation), so the flag works in an unprivileged Apptainer container; `--fakeroot` maps the user to uid 0 inside the container and would trigger the refusal unless `IS_SANDBOX=1` is set. Admins can block the mode entirely with `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"`. First interactive use requires accepting a one-time warning dialog saved to user settings; `-p` runs show no dialog, and a `--bg` session is refused until the dialog has been accepted once interactively.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds; refined, not refuted. Findings (critical=true where the Ashley design depends on it):

1. [critical=true] Official devcontainer page (fetched 2026-09-27, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer), section "Run without permission prompts", verbatim: "Because the container runs Claude Code as a non-root user and confines command execution to the container, you can pass `--dangerously-skip-permissions` for unattended operation. The CLI rejects this flag when launched as root, so confirm `remoteUser` is set to a non-root account." Same page: "To prevent engineers from using `--dangerously-skip-permissions` at all, set `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` to `"disable"` in managed settings."

2. [critical=true] Official sandbox-environments page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments), verbatim: "Always run `--dangerously-skip-permissions` sessions inside a container, a VM, or the sandbox runtime ... On Linux and macOS, Claude Code refuses to start with this flag when running as root, so run the container, VM, or sandbox runtime as a non-root user."

3. [critical=true] Official permission-modes page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes), section "Skip all checks with bypassPermissions mode", verbatim: "On Linux and macOS, Claude Code refuses to start in this mode when running as root or under `sudo`:" followed by code block `--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons`, then: "The check is skipped automatically inside a recognized sandbox. To run autonomously in a container, use the dev container configuration, which runs Claude Code as a non-root user." Also on that page: "Claude Code refuses `bypassPermissions` in a session you start with `--restricted`. `--restricted` requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later." And: "The first time you start an interactive session with this mode enabled, Claude Code shows a warning dialog asking you to accept responsibility ... Claude Code saves your acceptance to user settings, so the dialog appears only once. ... In non-interactive mode no dialog is shown, and a background session started with `--bg` is refused until you've accepted the dialog in an interactive session." Modes table row: "Run fully unattended inside a container | `claude -p "<prompt>" --dangerously-skip-permissions` | Required: a container, VM, or the sandbox runtime; on Linux and macOS, run it as a non-root user | ... In this `-p` run, the few calls that would still prompt are denied instead". Page states "With Claude Code v2.1.283 or later, auto mode is the built-in starting permission mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions."

4. [critical=false] Official cli-reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference), verbatim: "`--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Skip permission prompts. Equivalent to `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. ... For sessions started with `--bg`, the mode persists when the supervisor restarts the session". Also `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`: "Add `bypassPermissions` to the `Shift+Tab` mode cycle without starting in it." `--permission-mode` accepts `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `manual` (alias, v2.1.200+).

5. [critical=true] IS_SANDBOX status. Official env-vars page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars): no variable containing SANDBOX/BYPASS/ROOT/DANGEROUS; "IS_SANDBOX does not appear anywhere on this page." Settings-reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference) lists `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` — "Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode", scope "Any file"; no IS_SANDBOX entry. BUT GitHub issues #58150 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58150, opened 2026-05-11, v2.1.139, closed not planned) and #58197 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58197, opened 2026-05-12, v2.1.139, closed not planned) quote the shipped cli.js check: `if (process.platform !== "win32" && typeof process.getuid === "function" && process.getuid() === 0 && process.env.IS_SANDBOX !== "1" && process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP !== "1") { console.error("--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons"); process.exit(1); }`. So the refusal is a uid==0 test, not a sudo-env test, and the "recognized sandbox" on the official page is these two env vars. Issue #9184 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/9184; API: created 2025-10-08T22:08:02Z, closed 2026-03-09T18:14:41Z, state_reason "completed", 15 comments; reporter version 2.0.10, "Regression: Yes") comments (https://api.github.com/repos/anthropics/claude-code/issues/9184/comments): sammrai 2025-12-01 "`IS_SANDBOX=1 claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` works fine for me."; rgaufman 2026-02-12 same command; xuanswe 2026-03-03 "If I run directly `IS_SANDBOX=1 claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, it works." and persistent config "`skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true` with `IS_SANDBOX` environment variable set to `1`"; Orlando-Richards 2025-12-15: add `{"name": "IS_SANDBOX", "value": "1"}` to `claudeCode.environmentVariables` for the VS Code plugin; original reporter 2025-10-08 said it "doesn't work" (v2.0.10). Issue #3490 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/3490, 2025-07-14, closed not planned) is the original feature request for a root-OK flag. No maintainer confirmation of IS_SANDBOX anywhere; treat as undocumented and subject to removal. CHANGELOG.md (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md, newest 2.1.283) has no entry mentioning root/sudo/IS_SANDBOX; 2.1.280 added "the dangerous `rm` prompt in `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and auto mode to wait 2 minutes for an answer, then deny" and 2.1.281 fixed unprompted `rm -rf "$(pwd)"` in bypass mode — i.e. bypass mode still has a few denials/prompts even unattended.

6. [critical=true] dontAsk is not a substitute as root: #58150/#58197 quote docs "In every mode except bypassPermissions, writes to protected paths are never auto-approved" — `dontAsk` silently denies writes to `.claude/`, `.mcp.json`, dotfiles regardless of `permissions.allow`.

7. [critical=true] Apptainer runs as invoking uid. Apptainer User Guide 1.2 security page (https://apptainer.org/docs/user/1.2/security.html, matches the grid's apptainer/1.2.2 module), verbatim: "When a user runs a container with Apptainer, it is started as a normal process running under the user's account." "processes are started with the `PR_NO_NEW_PRIVS` flag set. This means that even if you run `sudo` inside your container, you won't be able to change to another user, or gain root privileges by other means." "In non-suid mode _all_ operations run as the user who starts the `apptainer` program." Same text on latest (1.5) page https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/security.html. SingularityCE 3.8 (grid's 3.8.6) https://docs.sylabs.io/guides/3.8/user-guide/security.html: "When you run a container, the processes in the container will run as your user account." plus nosuid + PR_NO_NEW_PRIVS. Therefore `process.getuid()` inside the container == the student's grid uid != 0 and the flag is accepted.

8. [critical=true] --fakeroot caveat confirmed. Apptainer fakeroot page (https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/fakeroot.html): "The fakeroot feature allows an unprivileged user to run a container with the appearance of running as root." UID inside container: 0 (root); fallback "root-mapped user namespace" when /etc/subuid absent still maps root id to the user. So under `--fakeroot`, getuid() returns 0 and the CLI refuses unless `IS_SANDBOX=1`/`CLAUDE_CODE_BUBBLEWRAP=1`. Design rule: do NOT use --fakeroot for the persistent Claude Code job; if a container step needs it (e.g. package install at build), do that at build time, not run time.

9. Not verified (web search budget exhausted this session; only WebFetch of known URLs used): whether Anthropic has ever formally named IS_SANDBOX in any official page — every official page fetched omits it. Also not verified: whether the one-time bypass acceptance dialog can be pre-seeded in `~/.claude/settings.json` for a headless Slurm job (user comment names `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true` but it is not on the fetched settings-reference index); design should have the student accept the dialog once in an interactive `srun`/VS Code terminal session before the persistent job, or use `-p` runs where "no dialog is shown".

- claude.com: "claude.ai account sign-in opens a claude.com page in the browser, which redirects to claude.ai; pre-approved WebFetch documentation lookups also reach this host from the CLI"

- mcp-proxy.anthropic.com: "MCP connectors from claude.ai ... connectors are enabled by default for claude.ai-authenticated users. To stop Claude Code from fetching them, set ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false or the disableClaudeAiConnectors setting"
- downloads.claude.ai: "Plugin executable downloads; native installer, native auto-updater, and update version checks"
- storage.googleapis.com: "Plugin install counts and metadata shown in /plugin" AND "Native installer and native auto-updater on versions prior to 2.1.116"  [OMITTED BY CLAIM]
- registry.npmjs.org: "Plugin installs (fetching npm-source plugin packages and installing plugins' Node.js package dependencies), npx-launched MCP servers, and the package registry for npm and bun installs of Claude Code itself"
- bridge.claudeusercontent.com: "Claude in Chrome extension WebSocket bridge"  [OMITTED]
- *.frame.claudeusercontent.com: "Artifact content reads ... only when the Artifact tool is available for your account. To turn the tool off and drop this requirement, set "enableArtifact": false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT=1"  [OMITTED]
- github.com: "Cloning GitHub-hosted plugin marketplaces and plugins, including the official Anthropic marketplace, over HTTPS or SSH. To clone GitHub owner/repo sources over HTTPS only, set CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS=1"
- raw.githubusercontent.com: "Changelog feed for /release-notes. In interactive sessions, Claude Code also fetches it in the background at startup when its cached changelog doesn't yet cover the running version ... non-interactive and cloud sessions never fetch it"  [OMITTED]
- *-review.googlesource.com: Desktop Gerrit lookup only; "Optional: disable with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC"  [OMITTED, irrelevant to our design]
- http-intake.logs.us5.datadoghq.com: "Operational telemetry events, sent only when the CLI uses the Anthropic API directly ... Optional: disable with DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK"
- browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com: "Operational error reports ... Optional: disable with DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING or DISABLE_TELEMETRY"
- formulae.brew.sh: Homebrew only  [OMITTED, irrelevant]
- code.claude.com: "Claude Code documentation lookups ... Blocking this host only affects documentation lookups"  [OMITTED]
Also: "The two Datadog intake hosts carry only optional operational telemetry, and setting CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC disables both." "If you install Claude Code through npm or manage your own binary distribution, end users don't need the native installer and auto-updater uses of downloads.claude.ai, but npm and bun installs need their package registry, registry.npmjs.org". First-run check: "The first-run setup connectivity check points here when it can't reach api.anthropic.com or platform.claude.com".

[critical=true] PROXY, same page: "Claude Code respects standard proxy environment variables" HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY (space- or comma-separated; NO_PROXY="*" bypasses all). "Lowercase variants also work, and Claude Code uses the first one that's set in the order https_proxy, HTTPS_PROXY, http_proxy, HTTP_PROXY." "Claude Code never sends its WebSocket connections to localhost, ::1, or 127.0.0.0/8 through the proxy, so you don't need a loopback entry in NO_PROXY for them." Startup validation: an unparseable proxy URL (e.g. missing http://) "stops launch with an error naming the variable to fix"; other settings are not validated until a request fails. "Set these environment variables before you launch Claude Code. Variables exported in your shell are read once at startup". Background agents/supervisor: "Put the same variables in the env block of ~/.claude/settings.json or managed settings instead" (shell exports reach background agents only if that shell cold-started the supervisor).

[critical=true] CA CERTS, same page: "By default, Claude Code trusts both its bundled Mozilla CA certificates and your operating system's certificate store. Reading the OS store requires a runtime with tls.getCACertificates: the native installer always has it, and npm installs need Node 22.15 or later. On older Node versions, only the bundled set and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS apply." "CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE accepts a comma-separated list ... bundled ... system ... The default is bundled,system." "CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE has no dedicated settings.json schema key. Set it via the env block". Debug log line to confirm: "CA certs: Appended extra certificates from NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (/etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca.pem)" in ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt with `claude --debug`.

[critical=true] CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (row at line 259 of the raw markdown), verbatim: "Set to any non-empty value, such as 1, to disable nonessential network traffic: auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, the /feedback command, Claude-drafted feedback, release notes, the PR and MR status badge checks, and availability checks such as the fast mode check. ... **Setting it to 0 or false still disables this traffic**, unlike most on/off variables; unset the variable to allow it again. verdict.corrected_claim: Environment injection: under Apptainer (module apptainer/1.2.2), export APPTAINERENV_xxx on the host to set xxx inside the container; the legacy SINGULARITYENV_xxx prefix is also honoured but prints "WARNING: DEPRECATED USAGE: Forwarding SINGULARITYENV_FOO as environment variable will not be supported in the future, use APPTAINERENV_FOO instead", and when both are set with different values APPTAINERENV_ wins and Apptainer prints "WARNING: Skipping environment variable [SINGULARITYENV_FOO=BAZ], FOO is already overridden with different value [BAR]". Container PATH is built from the image/default PATH ('/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin'), not the host's; APPTAINERENV_PREPEND_PATH / APPTAINERENV_APPEND_PATH (SINGULARITYENV_* under SingularityCE) edit it. `--env NAME=VALUE[,NAME2=VALUE2]` and `--env-file FILE` exist in both SingularityCE 3.8 and Apptainer 1.2 (single file only in those versions; multiple --env-file allowed from Apptainer 1.3+/1.5 docs) and are the runtime-neutral way to inject variables. `-e/--cleanenv` (and `-C/--containall`) drop host variables; the resulting environment keeps HOME (plus LANG, PATH, LD_LIBRARY_PATH and APPTAINER_COMMAND/APPTAINER_CONTAINER or SINGULARITY_* equivalents) — precedence step 1 is "Clear the environment, keeping just HOME and APPTAINER_APPNAME" (3.8: "HOME and SINGULARITY_APPNAME"), and injected APPTAINERENV_/--env/--env-file variables "override or modify any previous values" at step 8 (3.8: step 7).
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds; all quoted strings verified verbatim on official pages. One critical omission added (APPTAINERENV_ is Apptainer-only).

[1] https://apptainer.org/docs/user/1.2/singularity_compatibility.html (Apptainer 1.2 docs; grid module is apptainer/1.2.2) — critical=true
- Verbatim: "Apptainer respects environment variables with the SINGULARITY_ and SINGULARITYENV_ prefixes when their respective APPTAINER_ and APPTAINERENV_ counterparts are not set."
- Verbatim: "WARNING: DEPRECATED USAGE: Forwarding SINGULARITYENV_FOO as environment variable will not be supported in the future, use APPTAINERENV_FOO instead"
- Verbatim: "Finally, if both are set, the value set by the APPTAINERENV_ variable will take priority over the SINGULARITYENV_ variable."
- Verbatim: "WARNING: Skipping environment variable [SINGULARITYENV_FOO=BAZ], FOO is already overridden with different value [BAR]"
- Verbatim: "Apptainer installations will include a symlink to the apptainer binary named singularity." Example `singularity --version` output in 1.2 docs: "apptainer version 1.2.5".
- Verbatim: "Apptainer will look for a ~/.singularity directory when the ~/.apptainer directory is being created and will migrate user configuration files and keyrings automatically."

[2] https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/singularity_compatibility.html (Apptainer 1.5 docs) — same three sentences and both WARNING strings present unchanged; `singularity --version` example prints "apptainer version 1.5.4"; verbatim: "Apptainer will not migrate cached container data such as OCI blobs and SIF images."

[3] https://apptainer.org/docs/user/1.2/environment_and_metadata.html — critical=true
- Verbatim: "If you export an environment variable on your host called APPTAINERENV_xxx before you run a container, then it will set the environment variable xxx inside the container"
- Default PATH verbatim: "/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
- APPTAINERENV_PREPEND_PATH "prepended (added to the start) of the PATH variable in the container"; APPTAINERENV_APPEND_PATH "appended (added to the end)".
- --env: "allows you to specify environment variables as NAME=VALUE pairs"; --env-file: "lets you provide a file that contains environment variables as NAME=VALUE pairs".
- --cleanenv: "If you do not want the host environment variables to pass into the container you can use the -e or --cleanenv option. This gives a clean environment inside the container, with a minimal set of environment variables for correct operation of most software."
- Precedence list (10 steps) verbatim: 1 "Clear the environment, keeping just HOME and APPTAINER_APPNAME." 2 Docker/OCI env. 3 "If PATH is not defined set the Apptainer default PATH or If PATH is defined, add any missing path parts from Apptainer defaults". 4 %environment. 5 $APPTAINER_ENVIRONMENT from %post. 6 SCIF --app. 7 "Set base environment essential vars (PS1 and LD_LIBRARY_PATH)". 8 "Inject APPTAINERENV_ / --env / --env-file variables so they can override or modify any previous values." 9 "Apply special APPEND_PATH / PREPEND_PATH handling." 10 "Restore environment variables from the host, if they have not already been set in the container, and the --cleanenv / --containall options were not specified."
- --cleanenv example `env` output: HOME=/home/dave, LANG=C, LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/.singularity.d/libs, PATH=/startpath:/usr/local/sbin:..., APPTAINER_COMMAND=exec, APPTAINER_CONTAINER=... (HOME kept, confirmed).

[4] https://apptainer.org/docs/user/1.2/cli/apptainer_exec.html — flags verbatim: "--env stringToString  pass environment variable to contained process (default [])"; "--env-file string  pass environment variables from file to contained process" (single file in 1.2); "-e, --cleanenv  clean environment before running container"; "-C, --containall  contain not only file systems, but also PID, IPC, and environment"; "--no-eval  do not shell evaluate env vars or OCI container CMD/ENTRYPOINT/ARGS" (exists in 1.2).

- Same default PATH; SINGULARITYENV_PREPEND_PATH / SINGULARITYENV_APPEND_PATH same wording.
- --env "specify environment variables as NAME=VALUE pairs", example `--env MYVAR=A,MYVAR2=B`; --env-file example `singularity run --env-file myenvs env.sif`.
- Precedence (8 steps): 1 "Clear the environment, keeping just HOME and SINGULARITY_APPNAME."; 7 "Inject SINGULARITYENV_ / --env / --env-file variables so they can override or modify any previous values"; 8 "Source any remaining scripts from /singularity.d/env".

[6] https://docs.sylabs.io/guides/3.8/user-guide/cli/singularity_exec.html — "--env strings  pass environment variable to contained process"; "--env-file string  pass environment variables from file to contained process"; "-e, --cleanenv  clean environment before running container"; "-C, --containall ...environment". (--no-eval absent in 3.8.)

[8] https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/environment_and_metadata.html (Apptainer 1.5) — same APPTAINERENV_ sentence and PATH default; --env-file now "lets you provide one or more files ... later files taking priority" (multiple --env-file is a post-1.2 change; do not rely on it for apptainer/1.2.2).

DESIGN IMPLICATIONS (critical=true):
- The grid runs three runtimes (SingularityCE 3.8.6 conda, SingularityCE 4.0.2, apptainer/1.2.2 module). APPTAINERENV_xxx is honoured only by the Apptainer runtime; under either SingularityCE it is silently dropped (no warning, no error). SINGULARITYENV_xxx works on all three (with a deprecation WARNING under Apptainer). `--env`/`--env-file` work identically on all three and avoid the prefix question entirely — prefer them for passing the Claude subscription token/config into the container.
- Host PATH is never passed through: PATH inside is image %environment/default, so any node.js placed on the host (e.g. a conda env) must be added via *_PREPEND_PATH or bind-mounted and added via --env PATH=...; otherwise the container will not find it.
- --cleanenv/--containall keep HOME, so a HOME-relative ~/.claude config survives -e; but everything else (including any host-exported ANTHROPIC_*/CLAUDE_* vars) must then be injected explicitly via --env/--env-file/APPTAINERENV_.
- Not verified here (out of scope, no evidence either way): behaviour of --env-file quoting/shell evaluation in 1.2 (docs say nothing); actual runtime behaviour on the grid was not executed, only documentation was checked.

findings.claim: Containers use the host network namespace unless --net is passed; --net/--network/--network-args are root-only by default (admins may allowlist users in setuid installs), so a container on a compute node has exactly the compute node's internet access.
findings.detail: Apptainer networking: 'Passing the --net flag will cause the container to join a new network namespace when it initiates. A bridge interface is also set up by default.' 'The --network option can only be invoked in combination with the --net flag.' 'Many of these options are available only to the root user by default.' Sylabs 3.8: same --net statement plus 'Unrestricted ability to configure networking for containers would allow users to affect networking on the host'; 'SingularityCE 3.8 allows the administrator to permit a list of unprivileged users and/or groups to use specified network configurations'. Neither page states the default in one sentence; the default follows from --net being the only way to create a namespace. /etc/resolv.conf and /etc/hosts are bound from the host by default.

verdict.corrected_claim: By default an Apptainer/SingularityCE container shares the host's network namespace (no network namespace is created unless `--net` is passed), so a container started in a Slurm job shares the compute node's interfaces, routes, hostname, /etc/hosts and (a staged copy of) /etc/resolv.conf, and therefore has the compute node's internet access. Precision fix: `--net` itself is NOT root-only — an unprivileged user may use `--net` but only with `--network none` (loopback-only isolation); every other network (bridge, the default when `--net` is given without `--network`, plus anything named in `--network`/`--network-args`) requires root, or an admin allowlist (`allow net users` / `allow net groups` / `allow net networks` in apptainer.conf, effective ONLY in a setuid install), or `--fakeroot` in a setuid install with /etc/subuid (network `fakeroot`). Non-setuid installs (e.g. the conda SingularityCE 3.8.6 on the grid) cannot use fakeroot networking at all. `--containall`/`-C` does not create a network namespace.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds in substance; refuted=false. Two precision corrections to the DETAIL, plus verified specifics.

[critical=true] ONE-SENTENCE DEFAULT EXISTS in official docs (DETAIL said neither page states it): Apptainer Admin Guide, user_namespace.html (fetched, "latest"=1.5): "Apptainer does not by default make use of network namespaces, but it does have some little-used privileged options beginning with `--net` that do." Apptainer User Guide security.html, BOTH the version-matched 1.2 page and latest: "The process ID space, network, etc., are not isolated in separate namespaces by default." and "Favor integration over isolation: a user is allowed to easily use host resources such as GPUs, network filesystems, and high speed interconnects." Consequence for design: no netns => container uses the compute node's interfaces/routes verbatim.

[critical=true] --net IS USABLE UNPRIVILEGED, BUT ONLY WITH --network none: apptainer.org/docs/user/1.2/networking.html (grid module is apptainer/1.2.2) and /latest, docs.sylabs.io 3.8 and 4.0 all carry the identical sentences: "Passing the `--net` flag will cause the container to join a new network namespace when it initiates." / "A bridge interface is also set up by default." (Sylabs: "New in SingularityCE 3.0, a bridge interface will also be set up by default.") / "The `--network` option can only be invoked in combination with the `--net` flag." / "--network-args ... must be used in conjunction with the `--net` flag." / "Many of these options are available only to the `root` user by default." / "By default, `none` is the only network configuration that can be used by non-privileged users." Sylabs 4.0 adds: "It isolates the container network from the host network with a loopback interface." Sylabs 3.8: "Unrestricted ability to configure networking for containers would allow users to affect networking on the host, or in a cluster." / "SingularityCE 3.8 allows the administrator to permit a list of unprivileged users and/or groups to use specified network configurations." Apptainer: "The administrator of a setuid-root installation of Apptainer is able to permit a list of unprivileged users and/or groups to use specified network configurations."

[critical=true] ALLOWLIST IS SETUID-ONLY. apptainer.conf template embedded in pkg/util/apptainerconf/config.go @ tag v1.2.2 (fetched raw): "# ALLOW NET USERS: [STRING] # DEFAULT: NULL # Allow specified root administered CNI network configurations to be used by the specified list of users. By default only root may use CNI configuration, except in the case of a fakeroot execution where only 40_fakeroot.conflist is used. This feature only applies when Apptainer is running in SUID mode and the user is non-root." Struct fields: `AllowNetUsers []string directive:"allow net users"`, `AllowNetGroups []string directive:"allow net groups"`, `AllowNetNetworks []string directive:"allow net networks"`. Admin guide user_namespace.html: "Unprivileged installations of Apptainer cannot use `fakeroot` network as it requires privilege during container creation to set up the network." User guide fakeroot.html lists the five conditions for fakeroot networking: "1. Apptainer is installed with suid mode enabled 2. Network namespaces are enabled 3. The `-net` option is used 4. The user is listed in `/etc/subuid` and so can use rootless mode 5. The `--fakeroot` option is used". => the conda SingularityCE 3.8.6 (non-setuid) can never get a non-`none` network; apptainer/1.2.2 module and SingularityCE 4.0.2 only if installed setuid AND admins allowlist.

EXACT ERROR STRINGS (internal/pkg/runtime/engine/apptainer/container_linux.go @ v1.2.2, func prepareNetworkSetup): "network requires root or a suid installation with /etc/subuid --fakeroot; non-root users can only use --network=%s unless permitted by the administrator" (condition `(c.userNS || euid != 0) && !fakeroot && !allowedNetUnpriv`); "Network %s is not permitted for unprivileged users." ; warning "Only --network=%s is permitted in --fakeroot mode. You requested '%s'." `--network=none` is always permitted.

[critical=true] -C/--containall DOES NOT TOUCH NETWORKING. apptainer exec CLI reference (latest): "-C, --containall  contain not only file systems, but also PID, IPC, and environment"; "-n, --net  run container in a new network namespace (sets up a bridge network interface by default)"; "-p, --pid run container in a new PID namespace"; "-i, --ipc run container in a new IPC namespace"; "-u, --userns run container in a new user namespace"; "--netns-path join the network namespace at the specified path (as root, or if permitted in apptainer.conf)" — --netns-path / `allow netns paths` exist in 1.5 docs but are ABSENT from the 1.2 networking page (not available on apptainer/1.2.2).

/etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf: User guide bind_paths_and_mounts.html lists "/etc/hosts" among default system bind paths and says "/etc/resolv.conf, /etc/group, and /etc/passwd are mounted into the container" and are "adapted at container startup". There is NO `mount hosts` directive in apptainer.conf (verified against the File struct); /etc/hosts binding is unconditional except under --contain with a netns, where a staged minimal hosts file is used ("Binding staging /etc/hosts as contain is set"). resolv.conf is governed by `ConfigResolvConf bool default:"yes" directive:"config resolv_conf"`; template: "# CONFIG RESOLV_CONF: [BOOL] # DEFAULT: yes # If there is a bind point within the container, use the host's /etc/resolv.conf." Implementation detail: the runtime stages the host's resolv.conf content into a session file and binds that (content identical unless --dns given); if the directive is 'no' it logs "Skipping bind of the host's %s". --dns help: "list of DNS server separated by commas to add in resolv.conf". Requires the file to exist in the image or overlay/underlay support.

Site can disable netns globally (irrelevant to default mode): admin guide: `echo "user.max_net_namespaces = 0" >/etc/sysctl.d/90-max_net_namespaces.conf`; "it recommends disabling network namespaces when possible"; "it is not possible to disable only unprivileged network namespaces".

DESIGN NOTES (not refutations): (a) environment_and_metadata.html: "Most of the environment variables set on your host ... are passed into the container" (PATH modified, LD_LIBRARY_PATH not imported, PS1 reset); "-e or --cleanenv" strips them — so if the grid ever relies on HTTP(S)_PROXY variables, `--cleanenv` would break outbound access even though the netns is shared; use `APPTAINERENV_xxx` or `--env` to reinject. (b) NOT VERIFIED from fetched docs, inference only: TLS trust (CA bundle) comes from the container image, not the host, so "exactly the node's internet access" holds at the network layer but the image must ship ca-certificates for HTTPS to api.anthropic.com/npm.

VERSION MATCH: text identical across Apptainer 1.2 (grid module 1.2.2) and 1.5 (latest) user networking pages, and across SingularityCE 3.8 and 4.0 user guides; only --netns-path is 1.5-only.
