findings.claim: Non-setuid Singularity CE 3.8 (the conda install) must extract every SIF to a temporary sandbox directory on each run and cannot use --writable-tmpfs or overlays; Apptainer 1.1+ instead mounts SIF with bundled squashfuse_ll and supports --writable-tmpfs unprivileged via kernel overlayfs (kernel >=5.11) or fuse-overlayfs.
findings.detail: Sylabs 3.8 admin user_namespace: without setuid or with --userns, 'All containers must be run from sandbox directories. SIF images are extracted to a sandbox directory on the fly, preventing verification at runtime, and potentially allowing external modification of the container at runtime'; unavailable: 'Filesystem image and SIF-embedded persistent overlays', 'Encrypted containers', 'Writable temporary filesystems'. Apptainer CHANGELOG v1.1.0 (2022-09-27): 'Apptainer no longer installs a setuid-root portion by default'; 'Added a squashfuse image driver that enables mounting SIF files without using setuid-root. Uses either a squashfuse_ll command or a squashfuse command and requires unprivileged user namespaces'; later entries 'Update the included squashfuse_ll to have -o uid=N and -o gid=N', 'Avoid failures with --writable-tmpfs in non-setuid mode'. Apptainer 1.2 admin installation: 'Unprivileged user namespaces - (minimum kernel >=3.8, >=4.18 or 3.10.0-1127 on RHEL7 recommended)'; 'OverlayFS mounts - (minimum kernel >=3.18, >=5.11 recommended)'; 'Kernel 5.11 enables support for persistent overlay unprivileged, but otherwise fuse-overlayfs will be used'; relocatable unprivileged install: `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apptainer/apptainer/main/tools/install-unprivileged.sh | bash -s - install-dir`. Grid kernel 5.15 qualifies for unprivileged overlayfs.

findings.claim: Unprivileged (non-setuid) Apptainer/Singularity requires user namespaces: on RHEL/CentOS 7 the sysctl user.max_user_namespaces defaults to 0 and must be set nonzero; --fakeroot additionally needs newuidmap/newgidmap and /etc/subuid (or falls back to a root-only mapping); running as fakeroot makes uid 0 inside, which trips Claude Code's root refusal.
findings.detail: Apptainer admin 1.2 user_namespace: 'sudo sh -c \'echo user.max_user_namespaces=15000 >/etc/sysctl.d/90-max_user_namespaces.conf\''; 'User namespaces are required whenever the setuid-root component of Apptainer is not installed. The default installation of Apptainer does not include a setuid-root component'; 'Apptainer attempts to use external setuid binaries newuidmap and newgidmap'; 'Apptainer requires that a range of at least 65536 IDs is used for each mapping'. Debian also needs kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1; Ubuntu 24.04 kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0. fakeroot page: 'If user namespaces are available without /etc/subuid and /etc/subguid mapping files, Apptainer will map only the root user id to the original unprivileged user'; 'If the fakeroot command is available on the host, Apptainer will use it in addition'. Check on a node: `cat /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces`, `apptainer exec --userns image.sif id -u`.

findings.claim: pam_slurm_adopt denies ssh to a node unless the user has a running job there, adopts the session into the job's 'extern' step (needs PrologFlags=contain + task/cgroup), defaults to the newest job when several exist, only supports publickey/password auth, and disables pam_systemd so XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset; with Slurm X11 it overwrites DISPLAY.
findings.detail: Verbatim strings from pam_slurm_adopt.c: 'Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node' (user_extern_step_cnt == 0 && action_no_jobs=deny), 'Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: unable to determine source job', 'Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: adoption failure', 'Ignoring root user'. Doc: 'PrologFlags=contain must be set in the slurm.conf. This sets up the extern step into which ssh-launched processes will be adopted. You must also enable the task/cgroup plugin'; options 'action_no_jobs ... deny (default)', 'action_unknown ... newest (default) Pick the newest job added to the node', 'action_adopt_failure ... allow (default)'; 'only publickey and password are supported. In particular keyboard-interactive is explicitly unsupported and must be removed from AuthenticationMethods'; 'pam_systemd must be disabled ... which means user session features such as the runtime directory /run/user/$UID and XDG environment variables are not automatically set up'; 'disable_x11 ... 0 (default) If the job the connection is adopted into has Slurm's X11 forwarding enabled, the DISPLAY variable will be overwritten with the X11 tunnel endpoint details'. Adopted ssh processes are killed with the job.

findings.claim: Native Slurm X11 forwarding is `srun --x11[={all|first|last}]` (also salloc) and requires Slurm built with X11 support plus PrologFlags=x11; sbatch has no --x11 option, so a batch job cannot itself forward X11.
findings.detail: srun.html: '--x11[={all|first|last}] Sets up X11 forwarding on "all", "first" or "last" node(s) of the allocation. This option is only enabled if Slurm was compiled with X11 support and PrologFlags=x11 is defined in the slurm.conf. Default is "all". NOTE: This option may not work if --clusters is also provided.' Grep of sbatch.html (fetched 2026-09-27) for 'x11' returned nothing. JHPCE uses 'srun --pty --x11 bash'. For a GUI from a batch-held node, ssh -X into the node (pam_slurm_adopt) or `srun --jobid=<id> --overlap --x11 --pty bash` are the alternatives.

findings.claim: `--signal=B:USR1@120` sends SIGUSR1 to the batch shell only, up to 60 s earlier than requested; without B: all steps but not the batch shell are signalled; the batch script must run its payload in the background and `wait` so the bash trap can fire.
findings.detail: sbatch.html verbatim: '--signal=[{R|B}:]<sig_num>[@sig_time] When a job is within sig_time seconds of its end time, send it the signal sig_num. Due to the resolution of event handling by Slurm, the signal may be sent up to 60 seconds earlier than specified. sig_num may either be a signal number or name (e.g. "10" or "USR1"). sig_time must have an integer value between 0 and 65535. By default, no signal is sent before the job's end time. If a sig_num is specified without any sig_time, the default time will be 60 seconds. Use the "B:" option to signal only the batch shell, none of the other processes will be signaled. By default all job steps will be signaled, but not the batch shell itself. ... To have the signal sent at preemption time see the send_user_signal PreemptParameter.' srun's variant is '--signal=[R:]<sig_num>[@sig_time]' (no B:). NERSC preemptible-job example: '#SBATCH --signal=USR1@60', '#SBATCH --requeue', '#SBATCH --open-mode=append', payload backgrounded with 'pid=$!; trap "timeout_handler '$pid'" USR1; wait' and the handler runs 'scontrol requeue ${SLURM_JOB_ID}'; explanation: the shell would otherwise block on the foreground process and the trap would not run. Claude Code: send SIGINT to end the turn cleanly, then SIGTERM (exit 143); resume with --resume <session-id>.

findings.claim: `--requeue` makes a batch job eligible for requeue by admins, on node failure or on preemption; under PreemptMode=REQUEUE a job is requeued only if it has --requeue or the cluster sets JobRequeue=1, otherwise it is cancelled; a requeued script restarts from the beginning, so use --open-mode=append.
findings.detail: sbatch.html: '--requeue Specifies that the batch job should be eligible for requeuing. The job may be requeued explicitly by a system administrator, after node failure, or upon preemption by a higher priority job. When a job is requeued, the batch script is initiated from its beginning. ... The JobRequeue configuration parameter controls the default behavior on the cluster. NOTE: ForceRequeueOnFail if set as an option to the PrologFlags parameter in slurm.conf can override this setting.' '--no-requeue ... will prevent system administrators from being able to restart the job (for example, after a scheduled downtime), recover from a node failure, or be requeued upon preemption'. '--open-mode={append|truncate} ... The default value is specified by the system configuration parameter JobFileAppend.' preempt.html: PreemptMode 'REQUEUE: Preempts jobs by requeuing them (if possible) or canceling them'; 'For jobs to be requeued they must have the --requeue sbatch option set or the cluster wide JobRequeue parameter in slurm.conf must be set to 1'; 'preempt/qos: Job preemption rules are specified by Quality Of Service (QOS) specifications in the Slurm database'; 'GraceTime ... default value is zero'. Check the grid's QoS with `sacctmgr show qos primary,requeue format=Name,MaxWall,Preempt,PreemptMode,Flags`.

findings.claim: `--dependency=singleton` guarantees at most one running-or-suspended job with a given --job-name per user, which is the Slurm-native exactly-one-worker lock; `srun --jobid=<id> --overlap --pty <cmd>` attaches a new step to a running allocation without ssh.
findings.detail: sbatch.html: 'singleton This job can begin execution after any previously launched jobs sharing the same job name and user have terminated. In other words, only one job by that name and owned by that user can be running or suspended at any point in time. In a federation, a singleton dependency must be fulfilled on all clusters unless DependencyParameters=disable_remote_singleton is used'. Also: 'Once a job dependency fails due to the termination state of a preceding job, the dependent job will never be run, even if the preceding job is requeued'. srun.html: '--jobid=<jobid> Initiate a job step under an already allocated job with job ID id. Using this option will cause srun to behave exactly as if the SLURM_JOB_ID environment variable was set.' Anthropic's HPC write-up uses 'srun --jobid=JOBID --overlap --pty tmux attach -t claude'. Combine: `sbatch --job-name=ashley-claude --dependency=singleton --requeue --signal=B:USR1@300 --open-mode=append --qos=primary --time=30-00:00:00`.

findings.claim: VS Code Server (Remote-SSH) requires glibc >=2.28, libstdc++ >=3.4.25 and kernel >=4.18 since VS Code 1.99 (March 2025); CentOS/RHEL 7 are marked unsupported; the only host-side escape is an unsupported sysroot hack via VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER / VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_PATH / VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH.
findings.detail: Remote FAQ: 'Starting with VS Code release 1.99 (March 2025), the prebuilt servers distributed by VS Code are only compatible with Linux distributions that are based on glibc 2.28 or later.' Requirements: 'kernel >= 4.18, glibc >=2.28, libstdc++ >= 3.4.25, binutils >= 2.29'. Workaround env vars: VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER (dynamic linker in sysroot), VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_PATH (library path), VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH (patchelf on the remote); 'This approach is a technical workaround and is not an officially supported usage scenario.' Linux page: supported 'CentOS / RHEL 64-bit x86 (8+)', 'Debian ... (Buster/10+)', 'Alpine Linux 64-bit x86 containers or WSL hosts (3.16+)'; RHEL/CentOS 7 listed with a cross. Local VS Code is 1.139, so the server it ships needs glibc 2.28 on the target.

findings.claim: Remote-SSH can start the VS Code Server inside a Singularity/Apptainer container by putting `RemoteCommand singularity shell <image>.sif` + `RequestTTY yes` in ~/.ssh/config and enabling `remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand` and `remote.SSH.useLocalServer`; a per-host `remote.SSH.serverInstallPath` keeps the container's server separate; ControlMaster multiplexing and `remoteServerListenOnSocket` can break it.
findings.detail: ICER/MSU lab notebook (2023-11-03): ssh config 'Host <container>~intel18 / HostName dev-intel18 / User <netid> / ProxyJump <netid>@hpcc.msu.edu / RemoteCommand singularity shell <path_to_singularity_image>.sif / RequestTTY yes'; settings.json '"remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand": true, "remote.SSH.useLocalServer": true, "remote.SSH.serverInstallPath": {"<container>~intel18": "~/.vs-code-container/<container>"}, "remote.SSH.configFile": "C:/Users/<Windows_Account_Name>/.ssh/config"'; 'Make sure you edit the JSON files directly ... There is a bug that does not allow you to set the correct settings from the menu'; remove conflicting remote.SSH.remotePlatform entries. CERN ATLAS docs: 'RemoteCommand ~/.local/bin/run_container alma9 / RequestTTY yes', '"remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand": true', '"remote.SSH.remoteServerListenOnSocket" may need to be set to false', ProxyJump via lxplus, and it 'does not work with SSH remote commands' when ControlMaster multiplexing is used. microsoft/vscode-remote-release #6221 confirms the two settings ('remote.SSH.useLocalServer: true' and 'remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand: true'); #6598/#9697 report the feature intermittently ignored. The command must exec a shell in the container so the server (glibc 2.36 in bookworm) runs inside it.

findings.claim: The Claude Code VS Code extension bundles its own native binary at <extension>/resources/native-binary/claude (a linux-x64 Bun ELF), so under Remote-SSH it inherits the same glibc constraint as the CLI; the documented override is the `claudeProcessWrapper` setting, while `claudeCode.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` is reported ignored.
findings.detail: vs-code doc: 'The extension bundles its own copy of the CLI (command-line interface) for the chat panel. To run claude in VS Code's integrated terminal, you also need the standalone CLI install.' Setting table: 'claudeProcessWrapper — Executable used to launch the Claude process. The bundled binary path is passed as an argument when present. Set this to a separately installed claude binary if the extension build doesn't include one for your platform. In a wrapped setup, conversations start in Manual mode unless you set initialPermissionMode'; 'environmentVariables — Set environment variables for the Claude process'. Prereq 'VS Code 1.94.0 or later'. Issue #97022 (ext 2.1.282): hardcoded path '~/.vscode-insiders/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-2.1.282-linux-x64/resources/native-binary/claude'; error 'Claude Code native binary at ... exists but failed to launch. This usually means the binary does not match this system's libc — e.g. spawning a musl-linked binary on a glibc Linux host fails because the musl dynamic loader (/lib/ld-musl-*) is missing. Specify a matching binary with options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable.' Issue #96525 shows the same string is also emitted for unrelated virtual-workspace failures. If the VS Code Server runs inside the bookworm container this problem disappears.

findings.claim: Anthropic's reference devcontainer is the closest official template for a containerised, unattended Claude Code: non-root `node` user, persistent ~/.claude volume + CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, optional CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 (which disables Remote Control), and a pinned `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@X.Y.Z`.
findings.detail: devcontainer: '"mounts": ["source=claude-code-config,target=/home/node/.claude,type=volume"], "containerEnv": {"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR": "/home/node/.claude"}'; '"containerEnv": {"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": "1", "DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER": "1"}'; 'CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC also disables the feature-flag evaluation that Remote Control ... depend on, so sessions in the container can't use them'; 'To pin a specific Claude Code version for reproducible builds, install it from your Dockerfile with npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@X.Y.Z instead of using the feature, and set DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER to 1'; managed policy at '/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json'; warning: 'dev containers do not prevent a malicious project from exfiltrating anything accessible inside the container, including the Claude Code credentials stored in ~/.claude ... Avoid mounting host secrets such as ~/.ssh'. Feature: 'ghcr.io/anthropics/devcontainer-features/claude-code:1.0'.

topics_verified.recommendation: Do not install Claude Code on the CentOS 7 host or attempt a glibc sysroot hack; every current build is a Bun ELF that already needs GLIBC_2.26 and has SIGILLed on glibc 2.17, and the npm path installs the identical binary. Run it inside a container built from docker://node:22-bookworm (glibc 2.36), pulled unprivileged with the apptainer/1.2.2 module (not the conda Singularity 3.8.6, which must unpack the SIF to a sandbox on every run and cannot use --writable-tmpfs); set APPTAINER_CACHEDIR and APPTAINER_TMPDIR to CephFS before pulling. Install Claude Code at runtime rather than baking it in: `apptainer exec node22.sif npm install -g --prefix /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER/claude-prefix @anthropic-ai/claude-code@<pinned>` and export APPTAINERENV_PREPEND_PATH=/rs/.../claude-prefix/bin, APPTAINERENV_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, APPTAINERENV_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/rs/.../claude-config (mode 700; holds .credentials.json and .claude.json), APPTAINERENV_CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR=/dev/shm/$USER, APPTAINERENV_TMPDIR likewise, APPTAINERENV_CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL=/bin/bash, and bind /rs with -B; never use --fakeroot (uid 0 trips the --dangerously-skip-permissions refusal). Authenticate once per student with the paste-code /login inside the container (subscription), or mint `claude setup-token` into CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for the -p worker; remember setup-token cannot start Remote Control and --bare ignores it. For the persistent worker use sbatch with --job-name=ashley-claude --dependency=singleton --qos=primary --time=30-00:00:00 --requeue --open-mode=append --signal=B:USR1@300, run the container in the background under tmux with `wait` and a USR1 trap that SIGINTs then SIGTERMs claude, records the --session-id UUID, and `scontrol requeue`s; on restart `claude -p --resume <uuid> --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --permission-mode acceptEdits|bypassPermissions --permission-prompts none` reading the laptop's prompts from a CephFS inbox (or offer Remote Control / a Telegram channel as the zero-infrastructure alternative for phone use, which needs a full /login and no CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC). Reach the node from the laptop via ProxyJump warrior + pam_slurm_adopt (publickey only) or `srun --jobid=$JOBID --overlap --pty`. For VS Code, glibc 2.28 blocks the server on the host too, so the ssh config for the compute node must use `RemoteCommand apptainer exec -B /rs ... node22.sif bash -l` with RequestTTY yes and `remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand`/`useLocalServer` true plus a per-host serverInstallPath; the Claude Code extension's bundled binary then runs inside the same container and shares CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with the CLI. Verify on the grid before committing: max GLIBC_ symbol of the current binary (objdump -T), /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces > 0 on compute nodes, `apptainer exec node22.sif true` not printing a sandbox-conversion notice, and the actual PreemptMode/MaxWall of QoS primary.
open_questions: What is the exact maximum GLIBC_x.y symbol required by the current linux-x64 binary (2.1.28x)? Issue #89368 gives GLIBC_2.26 for 2.1.243 from a user diff; confirm with `objdump -T` on a downloaded binary, and confirm whether the SIGILL of #69980 was a kernel-3.10 or a glibc-2.17 effect (the grid has glibc 2.17 but kernel 5.15).

topics_verified.topic: Claude Code multi-account / multi-profile management: credential storage, refresh-token rotation, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, claude setup-token, community switchers, rate-limit detection in -p mode, Remote Control vs Claude Code on the web, and Anthropic's policy on accounts and credential handling (state as of 2026-09-27, Claude Code 2.1.28x docs)
topics_verified.summary: On Linux, Claude Code keeps the subscription login in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json` (default `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, mode 0600) under a `claudeAiOauth` object with `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt` (epoch ms, ~8 h), `refreshTokenExpiresAt` (~28-30 days), `scopes`, `subscriptionType` and `rateLimitTier`; macOS uses the Keychain item `Claude Code-credentials` and falls back to the same file when the Keychain is locked (e.g. in an SSH session). Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on every refresh: three independent official-repo issues describe the race in which the second process to present the old refresh token gets `401 Invalid authentication credentials` and Claude Code then clears the stored credential, so a copied `.credentials.json` on a second machine does not keep working alongside the original; refreshing also does not extend the login's ~30-day server-side lifetime. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` gives a fully separate profile (settings, sessions, plugins, `.credentials.json`, and a Keychain entry keyed to that directory), which is the mechanism every community switcher ultimately relies on and the resolution Anthropic accepted for issue #261. `claude setup-token` mints a one-year `sk-ant-oat01-…` OAuth token that is printed, not stored; it is consumed via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, is always used in `-p` mode, is not read in `--bare` mode, can only make model requests (no Remote Control, no claude.ai connectors), and can be revoked only one-by-one at claude.ai → Settings → Claude Code (no CLI; one April-2026 report says revocation did not take effect). The community tools differ: `claude-swap` (PyPI, `pipx install claude-swap`, command `cswap`) swaps the credential file/Keychain item under Claude Code's own credential locks and auto-rotates accounts at 90% of the 5-hour/7-day windows; `cc-switch` (ccswitch.io) is a Tauri GUI that needs glibc 2.35+ and targets API-key/relay providers; `ccswitch` (BNhashem16) is a bash script that backs up and restores the credential file; npm `claude-profiles` swaps settings/MCP/commands only and explicitly shares auth. In `-p` mode a usage-limit hit surfaces as a non-zero exit with `You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm` (or weekly/Opus/Sonnet) in the `result` field, and with `--output-format stream-json` a `system/api_retry` event carries `error: "rate_limit"`; an expired login yields `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` with structured code `authentication_failed`; the interactive auto-wait (`continuing automatically at …`) is not offered in `-p`. Live quota can be polled at `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` (`anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`) returning `five_hour`/`seven_day` `{utilization, resets_at}`. Remote Control (`claude remote-control` server mode, `claude --remote-control`, `/rc`) keeps the session on the local machine, uses outbound HTTPS only to api.anthropic.com, needs a full-scope claude.ai login (not a setup-token, not an API key), and the docs explicitly say to run it inside tmux/screen on a remote SSH machine, so it could steer a Slurm-hosted session, but the login must be renewed interactively every ≤30 days. Claude Code on the web runs on Anthropic-managed VMs cloned from GitHub (self-hosted environments are Team/Enterprise only) and cannot reach an HPC node. Anthropic's consumer terms forbid account sharing and automated access without an API key; the Claude Code legal page says usage limits "assume ordinary, individual usage", that developers "may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow", but that nothing prevents "an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code".

findings.claim: On Linux Claude Code stores the subscription login in ~/.claude/.credentials.json with file mode 0600; on macOS in the Keychain with a documented fallback to the same file when the Keychain rejects the write (e.g. locked in an SSH session); on Windows in %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json.
findings.detail: "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." "On macOS ... When the Keychain rejects the write, such as when it's locked in an SSH session, Claude Code stores your login in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600` instead, the same storage it uses on Linux." Keychain service name reported in issues: `Claude Code-credentials`. "Claude Code manages `.credentials.json` through `/login` and `/logout`."

verdict.evidence:
CLAIM HELD. Verified 2026-09-27 against the live official page https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, section "Credential management", which reads verbatim: "On macOS, credentials are stored in the encrypted macOS Keychain. When the Keychain rejects the write, such as when it's locked in an SSH session, Claude Code stores your login in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600` instead, the same storage it uses on Linux. A Console login that creates an API key fails until the Keychain is writable." / "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." / "On Windows, credentials are stored in `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json` and inherit the access controls of your user profile directory, which restricts the file to your user account by default." / "Claude Code manages `.credentials.json` through `/login` and `/logout`." Note the doc claims 0600 only for Linux and the macOS fallback, NOT Windows (Windows relies on profile-directory ACLs) — consistent with the claim as written.

CRITICAL design-relevant additions from the same page (critical=true): (1) `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead, including the file the macOS fallback writes, and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory too." So in the Singularity/Slurm design the credential file location on the compute node is controllable via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (e.g. point it at a bind-mounted CephFS/Panasas path rather than container $HOME). (2) Login inside SSH/containers uses the paste-code flow: "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers." (3) Alternative for non-interactive nodes: `claude setup-token` prints a one-year OAuth token, "does not save the token anywhere", set as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; it "authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan", but "can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors", and "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`". Auth precedence: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (rank 5) outranks subscription OAuth from /login (rank 7). (4) Expiry: "Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew" warning (v2.1.203+), then "Login expired · Please run /login"; doc explicitly warns that a background/Remote Control session "that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires" — directly relevant to a 30-day persistent Slurm job.

macOS fallback corroborated by https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install (section "Not logged in or token expired"): "On macOS, Claude Code saves credentials to the login Keychain. When the Keychain rejects the write, such as when it's locked in an SSH session or its password is out of sync with your account password, Claude Code saves your login to the plaintext `~/.claude/.credentials.json` file instead." Recovery: `claude doctor` reports a warning starting `macOS Keychain is not writable`; fix with `security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`, then `/logout` + `/login`. Caveat: "Logging out removes all stored credentials, including the plaintext file's contents, saved MCP server logins, and plugin sensitive values."

Keychain service name `Claude Code-credentials` is NOT in the official docs; it is confirmed in GitHub issues only, as the claim stated: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/96310 (opened 2026-09-23, v2.1.278): "Claude Code (subscription / OAuth login) stores its credentials in the login Keychain as a generic-password item labeled `Claude Code-credentials`" and "There is no setting / env var / flag that makes Claude Code store the OAuth token in the file store (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`) while the Keychain is available." https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/95386 (opened 2026-09-18, v2.1.276) uses `security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "Claude Code-credentials"` and quotes the doctor string "macOS Keychain is not writable. Console login will fail to save your API key." Open macOS bugs as of Sep 2026 (#95386, #95425 "ENOTDIR rmdir on stale .storage-write.lock file (2.1.277)") report /login saying "Login successful" while the token is never persisted — laptop-side only, not applicable to the Linux grid node.

verdict.corrected_claim: `.credentials.json` (Linux/macOS-fallback `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, Windows `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`, relocated by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) holds a `claudeAiOauth` object whose fields at login are `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt` (epoch milliseconds), `refreshTokenExpiresAt` (epoch milliseconds), `scopes` (array), `subscriptionType` and `rateLimitTier`; the CLI's persist function also carries an optional `clientId`. Only `accessToken`/`refreshToken` are reliably present: after a token refresh `subscriptionType`/`rateLimitTier` may be null or absent (#94464, CHANGELOG 2.1.69), `expiresAt`/`refreshTokenExpiresAt`/`scopes` can vanish when the refresh response omits `expires_in`/`scope` (#85262, closed not planned), and a failed refresh rewrites `accessToken`/`refreshToken` to "" with `expiresAt: 0` (#91571). A top-level `mcpOAuth` block appears only when remote MCP servers have been OAuth-authorized (present with 27 entries in #94464; absent on a machine with none). `subscriptionType`/`rateLimitTier` are cached at login and not refreshed on plan upgrade (#43639, closed not planned). The login gate `if(!t.scopes?.includes("user:inference")) return "oauth_no_inference_scope";` exists in the shipped bundle and was verified in Claude Code 2.1.224-2.1.226 with the behavior predating them; the earliest enforcing version is NOT established by any source, and "2.1.81" is unsupported (that release's changelog entry adds `--bare` and fixes concurrent-session re-auth). The only scope error documented in the official errors reference is `OAuth token does not meet scope requirement: user:profile` (fix: run `/login`, no logout needed); `oauth_no_inference_scope` is an internal code, not a documented string.

findings.claim: OAuth refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on each refresh; a second holder of the same refresh token gets a 401 and Claude Code then overwrites the shared store with a logged-out stub, so two independent copies of one credential cannot both keep working.
findings.detail: #80085 (v2.1.216): "instance A rotates the refresh token → instance B refreshes with the now-consumed token → 401 → destructive logged-out write"; error `401 Invalid authentication credentials`. #25609: "Anthropic issues a new token for A, invalidating the old refresh token ... All sessions lose authentication". #94464: "rotation → old refresh token revoked". #91571: after a failed refresh the file is rewritten with `accessToken: ""`, `refreshToken: ""`, `expiresAt: 0`. Same-machine processes are serialised by a shared refresh lock (errors doc: `Could not refresh your login because another Claude Code process is refreshing it`), which does not protect two hosts.

verdict.corrected_claim: Claude Code's claude.ai subscription login uses rotating refresh tokens: when one process refreshes, the previously stored refresh token is consumed/revoked server-side. A second holder that later refreshes with that consumed token is rejected (reported as `401 Invalid authentication credentials` in #80085/#76561; one Windows report in #24317 says the replay gets a 400; one report in #80085 says the WINNER's still-valid access token was also revoked, i.e. reuse detection can revoke the whole token family, so neither copy is guaranteed to survive). On a rejected refresh Claude Code, by documented design (errors doc "Login expired": "the OAuth service rejected the stored refresh token, so Claude Code cleared the saved credentials"), rewrites its credential store to a logged-out stub (`accessToken: ""`, `refreshToken: ""`, `expiresAt: 0`, per #91571; `{"claudeAiOauth": {..., "expiresAt": 0}}` per #76561). Consequently two independent copies of one `/login` credential (e.g. laptop and grid node) cannot both keep working across an access-token expiry; this is still the behaviour at v2.1.283 (no CHANGELOG fix; #76561, #80085, #91571, #94464 open, no maintainer response). Same-machine processes are serialised by a shared refresh lock (errors doc: "Another Claude Code process on the same machine held the shared refresh lock"; strings `Could not refresh your login because another Claude Code process is refreshing it` and `Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh`; lock fixes in 2.1.211, 2.1.248, 2.1.282). The docs scope this lock to one machine; whether it protects two grid nodes sharing one Panasas/CephFS home is not established by any source found. Documented escape hatches: `claude setup-token` -> `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (one-year token, never subject to refresh rotation, "can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors"; not read under `--bare`); `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` gives each directory its own credential store; `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` + `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES` let `claude auth login` exchange a refresh token headlessly (which, given rotation, would consume the copy it was taken from).

This is usually transient; retry in a minute, and if it persists close other Claude Code processes or sign in again` (code `server_error`). "Signing in again doesn't wait on the refresh lock." Section "API Error: 401 Invalid authentication credentials": "Anthropic returns this message when a credential was recently revoked ... so an expired token isn't the cause." Section "OAuth token revoked or expired": strings `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login`, `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`; "When the saved login has already been cleared after a failed refresh, you see Login expired instead."

It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable ... requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. No maintainer statement.

[10] https://api.github.com/repos/anthropics/claude-code/issues/94464 (open, 2026-09-15, CLI 2.1.270, labels bug/has repro/area:auth/area:desktop): "The engine consumed the shared refresh token (rotation → old refresh token revoked), persisted the successor only to `.credentials.json`" while Keychain stayed stale, so the terminal CLI gets `Login expired` daily. Comment User0856 2026-09-16 confirms on CLI 2.1.273.

[11] https://api.github.com/repos/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91571 (open, 2026-09-02, Windows, 2.1.220, labels bug/has repro/area:auth): after a failed refresh "`.credentials.json` mtime updates: `accessToken` and `refreshToken` now empty strings (`expiresAt: 0`), other fields (scopes, subscriptionType, `refreshTokenExpiresAt`) retained"; "It converts one failed refresh into 'every future process is locked out'". NOT ESTABLISHED: (a) no Anthropic OAuth-server document states refresh-token rotation in those words; the official confirmation is the consequence described in [2] and the word "rotated" in [5]/2.1.216; (b) whether the same-machine refresh lock (a lock in the credential store's directory) is effective between two grid nodes that share one Panasas/CephFS `~/.claude` — no source addresses NFS-style shared homes; (c) whether reuse detection ALWAYS revokes the whole family (one report, [6]) or only sometimes. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE (critical): do not copy a laptop `/login` credential to the grid; give the grid job either its own `/login` under its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/home (never shared with the laptop copy) or a `claude setup-token`-minted `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, accepting that the latter cannot use Remote Control or claude.ai connectors and is not read under `--bare`. findings.claim: Copying ~/.claude/.credentials.json to a headless machine is explicitly unsupported: the copy fails with a 401 once the access token expires, and the issue was closed as not planned.
findings.detail: Issue #21765 (opened 2026-01-29, closed not planned, labels area:auth, bug, has repro): after scp of the file, `API Error: 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"OAuth token has expired. Please obtain a new token or refresh your existing token."}}`.

verdict.corrected_claim: Copying ~/.claude/.credentials.json to a headless machine is undocumented, not "explicitly unsupported": the official authentication docs never mention copying the file (they say only "Claude Code manages `.credentials.json` through `/login` and `/logout`") and give `claude setup-token` -> `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (a one-year subscription OAuth token) as the path for environments without browser login. Issue #21765 (opened 2026-01-29, labels bug / has repro / platform:linux / area:auth / stale) reports that after scp the remote copy fails once the access token expires with `API Error: 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"OAuth token has expired. Please obtain a new token or refresh your existing token."}}`. The issue was closed with state_reason `not_planned` on 2026-03-28 by `github-actions[bot]` as stale ("Closing for now — inactive for too long"), then locked 2026-04-06; no Anthropic maintainer ever commented, so the closure is not an Anthropic verdict. The failure mechanism, documented by community forensics across #21765, #12447 and #24317 and consistent with the docs' statement that only "parallel sessions on one machine share a saved login and coordinate its renewal", is refresh-token rotation (RFC 9700 s2.2.2): two copies of one rotating refresh token cannot coexist, so a laptop copy and a grid copy invalidate each other. Copying the file therefore does break in practice, but because of rotation, not policy; the supported headless credential is `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token`.
verdict.evidence:
METHOD: WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before this task, so every finding below comes from direct fetches of GitHub (web page + REST API via curl) and code.claude.com docs. `gh` CLI is not installed locally.

--- WHAT HOLDS (from https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/21765 and https://api.github.com/repos/anthropics/claude-code/issues/21765 + /comments + /timeline) ---
- Title: "OAuth refresh token not used when credentials are copied to remote/headless machines". Opened by khaledfouad0, created_at 2026-01-29T18:43:25Z. state=closed, state_reason="not_planned", closed_at 2026-03-28T22:12:43Z. Labels (actual): bug, has repro, platform:linux, area:auth, stale (the claim omitted platform:linux and stale).
- Repro verbatim: (1) `claude login` on workstation (Max, OAuth); (2) copy `~/.claude/.credentials.json` to remote headless machine via `scp`; (3) run `claude` after `accessToken` expired. File shape: `{"claudeAiOauth": {"accessToken", "refreshToken", "expiresAt", "scopes", "subscriptionType": "max", "rateLimitTier"}}`.
- Error verbatim: `API Error: 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"OAuth token has expired. Please obtain a new token or refresh your existing token."},"request_id":"req_011CXc8h3VFKY9jGum2N2rTZ"}`.

--- WHAT IS WRONG IN THE CLAIM ---
1. "Explicitly unsupported" - no official source says so. Timeline shows closed_by=github-actions[bot] (type Bot) at 2026-03-28T22:12:43Z; closing comment: "Closing for now — inactive for too long. Please open a new issue if this is still relevant." Stale label applied 2026-02-14, removed 2026-02-28 after a comment, re-applied 2026-03-14, auto-close 2026-03-28, auto-lock 2026-04-06T14:32:30Z. Zero maintainer comments. The two human commenters are NOT Anthropic: fahreddinozcan (company @Upstash; api.github.com/orgs/anthropics/public_members/fahreddinozcan -> 404) and lonetis (Louis Jannett, Ruhr University Bochum, PhD student on SSO; -> 404). fahreddinozcan's 2026-01-30 line "I've verified our refresh token flow to be working, however Claude Code doesn't use refresh tokens" refers to Upstash's MCP server, not Anthropic's backend.
2. Official docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, fetched 2026-09-27) never mention copying the file. Verbatim: "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." "Claude Code manages `.credentials.json` through `/login` and `/logout`." "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead". Supported headless path, verbatim: "For CI pipelines, scripts, or other environments where interactive browser login isn't available, generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`" ... "It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable" ... "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." ... "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." Precedence order: 1 cloud provider (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY), 2 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, 3 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, 4 apiKeyHelper, 5 CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, 6 Anthropic profile/WIF, 7 subscription OAuth from /login. [critical=true for the Ashley design: the supported credential for a Slurm/Singularity job is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, and it must not be combined with --bare.]
3. Docs also show Claude Code DOES refresh the /login credential (contradicting the Jan-2026 commenter): "Once the stored login expires and can't be refreshed, each model request fails with `Login expired · Please run /login`" and "Claude Code refreshes the profile's login automatically". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install "Not logged in or token expired": "Parallel sessions on one machine share a saved login and coordinate its renewal so that only one process refreshes the token at a time. Before v2.1.211, waking the machine from sleep could cause two sessions to renew with the same token, which revoked the saved login". Coordination is same-machine only; nothing coordinates two machines holding separate copies. That page's only headless/SSH guidance is the login-code flow: "When Claude Code runs in WSL2, on a remote machine over SSH, or inside a container ... the browser shows a login code ... Paste that code into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt".
4. Mechanism (community, consistent across three issues; not confirmed by Anthropic): lonetis on #21765 2026-02-28 and #12447 2026-02-28: "Claude uses refresh token rotation ... RFC 9700 section 2.2.2 ... When a client redeems a refresh token, the server invalidates it and issues a new one. As a result, two machines can't share the same refresh token. One machine redeems it and stores the rotated token, while the other keeps using the old token and fails." #24317 body (https://api.github.com/repos/anthropics/claude-code/issues/24317): accessToken "short-lived (~15 hour expiry)", refresh tokens "single-use". kynbeen on #24317 2026-09-03, reading the shipped v2.1.258 bundle: 5-minute pre-expiry window (`FD4 = 300000`), in-process-only dedup (`if (this.pendingRefresh) return this.pendingRefresh; // no cross-process lock`), losers "replay a consumed refresh token and get a 400, which under RFC 9700 reuse detection takes the whole token family down — the 27-day refresh token"; also "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_401_WAIT_MS` ... does not apply to file-store setups" (gated on `process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`). Ryzodus-RB42 on #12447 2026-09-08: 7 headless systemd agents + desktop app on one Max account "all agents dying overnight with `OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`, and the credentials file left zeroed". [critical=true: a student's laptop VS Code extension and the grid job would hold two copies of one rotating refresh token; one side WILL be logged out.]
5. Version-specific error wording: the raw `API Error: 401 {...}` string is Jan-2026 vintage. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors now lists `Login expired · Please run /login` and `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`; authentication doc: "Before v2.1.206, Claude Code reported an expired login on model requests as a model error instead." `/status` shows a `Login` row `Expired — log in again` (v2.1.210+); startup warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (v2.1.203+; five days before v2.1.217). Local extension is 2.1.283, so students will see the new wording.

[critical=true for a persistent interactive Claude Code in Singularity; community-only, unverified by me.] One commenter there (samodadela 2025-10-23) says "copying the credentials works... For some reason you need `~/.claude.json` too" - i.e. copying is not blocked, it works until rotation bites.

--- NET ---
Dates, labels (minus two), repro and error string in the claim are accurate. "Explicitly unsupported" and the implication that "closed as not planned" was a maintainer decision are wrong. The practical conclusion for the design stands for a different reason: copying the file fails because of refresh-token rotation shared with the laptop, and the documented remedy is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from claude setup-token (one year, model requests only, not read in --bare, no Remote Control / claude.ai connectors). Not known: whether Anthropic considers cross-machine file copying a policy violation (no statement found either way), and the exact current access-token lifetime (reports range 8-15 h; the docs give no number).

findings.claim: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates the whole ~/.claude tree including .credentials.json and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory, giving a fully separate profile; project/local settings cannot set it.
findings.detail: env-vars: "`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — Directory where Claude Code stores configuration, cache, and logs (default: `~/.claude`). Project and local settings can't set this variable". authentication: "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead ... and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory too, so a session with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` reads a different entry." claude-directory: "If you set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, every `~/.claude` path on this page lives under that directory instead." verdict.corrected_claim: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.claude) relocates Claude Code's settings, session history/transcripts, plugins, backups, the IDE lock files, the background-session supervisor state, `.credentials.json` (including the macOS fallback file), and, in practice, `~/.claude.json` (confirmed empirically on 2.1.278 Linux/WSL and 2.1.283 Windows, though the docs never say so explicitly); on macOS the Keychain entry is keyed to the directory so a different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR reads a different entry. It is NOT a guarantee that the whole tree moves or that the profile is fully isolated: as of 2.1.280 an open, reproduced bug (#97680, 2026-09-27) shows `daemon.json`/`daemon.log` paths and trailing session-metadata records still written under `~/.claude` and `~/.claude.json` reappearing in $HOME; #79952 (open since 2026-07-21) shows config-editing skills writing `~/.claude/settings.json` regardless; and on v2.1.251+ `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1` strips CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from Bash-tool, hook and MCP-stdio children, which then fall back to `~/.claude`. Project and local settings `env` blocks cannot set it (dropped with a `--debug` warning; changed in 2.1.251); set it in the shell, user settings, managed settings, or the VS Code extension's `environmentVariables` setting (never as an empty value). The current env-vars row reads "Override the configuration directory (default: `~/.claude`). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path ... Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings", not the "configuration, cache, and logs" wording quoted in the claim.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core mechanics hold; "whole ~/.claude tree" and "fully separate profile" are overstated, and the quoted env-vars text is not the current wording. Details, all from pages fetched 2026-09-27 (raw markdown via curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/<page>.md unless noted):

[HOLDS, critical=true] authentication.md (Credential management, verbatim): "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead, including the file the macOS fallback writes, and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory too, so a session with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` reads a different entry." Also: Linux stores "`~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`"; Windows "`%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`"; macOS uses the Keychain, falling back to the file "when it's locked in an SSH session". URL: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication

[HOLDS, critical=true] Project/local settings can't set it. env-vars.md row (verbatim): "`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | Override the configuration directory (default: `~/.claude`). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path. For credentials, see [where Claude Code stores credentials]. Useful for running multiple accounts side by side: for example, `alias claude-work='CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work claude'`. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in [project and local settings]". settings-reference.md "Variables Claude Code ignores in `env`" (verbatim): "Project and local settings can't set variables that a checked-out repository shouldn't control; set those in your shell, user settings, or managed settings instead. Claude Code drops each one, apart from a few values that turn telemetry off, and logs a warning you can see with `claude --debug`. They include: Variables that choose where Claude Code stores or writes its own files: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR`, and the operating-system directory variables such as `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP`, and the `XDG_*` family." CHANGELOG 2.1.251: "Changed project-level `.claude/settings.json` `env` to no longer set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR`, or `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`; set them in your shell, user, or managed settings instead" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md). Version-specific: before 2.1.251 a project file could set it.

[MISQUOTE] The claim's env-vars quote "Directory where Claude Code stores configuration, cache, and logs (default: `~/.claude`). Project and local settings can't set this variable" does not appear on the page; the actual row is quoted above. The page's prose does say: "Project and local settings can't set some variables, such as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and the OpenTelemetry exporter variables."

[HOLDS BY TEST, docs silent, critical=true] Where `~/.claude.json` goes. Docs: claude-directory.md says only "If you set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, every `~/.claude` path on this page lives under that directory instead." and lists `~/.claude.json` ("Global only ... App state, OAuth, UI toggles, personal MCP servers") in its File reference table; settings.md calls it "a fifth file ... It holds your sign-in session, MCP server configurations, per-project state such as trust decisions, and the global config keys". No page states its location under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Empirical test run by this verifier: (a) WSL Ubuntu, npm install, `claude --version` = "2.1.278 (Claude Code)", `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/ashley_cfgtest claude config list` then `claude mcp list` with a fresh empty dir created `/tmp/ashley_cfgtest/.claude.json` (423 bytes; keys firstStartTime, firstStartVersion "2.1.278", machineID, userID, migrationVersion 14), `backups/.claude.json.backup.<ts>`, `projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl`, `projects/<slug>/memory/`, `sessions/`; `$HOME/.claude.json` mtime unchanged (2026-09-19 10:48:01) and no new files under `~/.claude`. The CLI's own warning even names the path: "set projects[...].hasTrustDialogAccepted: true in /tmp/ashley_cfgtest/.claude.json". ADDITIONAL FACTS THAT BEAR ON THE DESIGN (all official, all fetched):
1. Token is per-person: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions: "an OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran `claude setup-token`". Each student mints their own; never share one token across students. [critical=true]
2. Browser flow in SSH/WSL/containers: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install "OAuth login fails in WSL2, SSH, or containers": "the browser usually opens on a different host and its redirect can't reach Claude Code's local callback server. After you sign in, the browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back automatically. Paste that code into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt to complete login." Also "press `c` to copy the OAuth URL to your clipboard". Error string if the code is stale/truncated: "OAuth error: Invalid code. Please make sure the full code was copied". So `claude setup-token` can be run either on the laptop (simplest) or on the grid via the paste-code fallback. [critical=true]
3. Expiry/revocation behaviour with the env token (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors, "OAuth token revoked or expired"): "If you authenticate with a long-lived token in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, you see the same messages when that token expires or is revoked." Strings: "OAuth token revoked · Please run /login" and "Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...". "If you authenticate with the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable, Claude Code keeps sending the value you set after a request fails with a 401, rather than switching to a stored login's token. `/status` shows this credential as an `Auth token` row reading `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Generate a fresh token with `claude setup-token` and restart with it, or unset the variable and run `/login`. Before v2.1.225, Claude Code could replace the variable's value mid-session with the short-lived access token from a stored login". A persistent 30-day Slurm session does not auto-renew this token; the design needs a rotate-and-restart path. Errors page also says (line ~869): "Confirm `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or your cloud provider credentials are set in the environment that launches the worker, not only in your interactive shell" -- i.e. the sbatch script / singularity exec env must carry the variable. Note Singularity/Apptainer passes host env by default unless --cleanenv; use SINGULARITYENV_/APPTAINERENV_ prefixes if cleaning.
4. Non-interactive expired-login string (saved /login, not env token): "Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed", structured error code `authentication_failed`. Sessions using CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN "never see this message".
5. Org restriction: authentication page: "`claude setup-token` and `/install-github-app`: enforce only `forceLoginMethod`, so they can mint a token in a different organization" (forceLoginOrgUUID not checked). Every path applies forceLoginMethod on v2.1.212+.
6. Override trap: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, apiKeyHelper and any CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* var all outrank CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; env-vars page: "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present." A stray ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in a student's ~/.bashrc on the grid silently switches billing off the subscription. [critical=true]
7. Credential file fallback (authentication page, Credential management): on Linux `/login` credentials live in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode 0600; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates it. The setup-token path avoids writing this file at all (token is env-only), which is preferable on a shared Panasas home.
8. Cloud sessions / Remote Control / claude.ai connectors / `/schedule` need a full claude.ai login, not this token (authentication page: "It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors"). Our SSH/shared-filesystem prompt relay is therefore the right transport; Remote Control is not available under this token.

verdict.corrected_claim: Credential precedence (code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, "Authentication precedence", fetched 2026-09-27): (1) cloud provider credentials when CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY is set > (2) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (sent as `Authorization: Bearer`) > (3) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (sent as `X-Api-Key`) > (4) apiKeyHelper script output > (5) CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (one-year token from `claude setup-token`) > (6) Anthropic profile / Workload Identity Federation credentials > (7) subscription OAuth from /login. Two documented exceptions: a signed-in Claude apps gateway session sits outside this list and outranks even the cloud providers; and item 6 is conditional: a profile named by ANTHROPIC_PROFILE, or federation variables (ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID + ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID), or an active profile with auth mode `oidc_federation` rank above /login, but an ACTIVE profile with auth mode `user_oauth` (from `ant auth login` or keyless Console sign-in) ranks BELOW a working /login credential. In non-interactive mode (`-p`): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "is always used when present" with no approval prompt (the one-time approve/decline prompt and the `/config` "Use custom API key" toggle are interactive-only). CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN has no approval prompt in any mode and, per the env-vars row, "Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials" and is used "for the whole session" unless you run /login; but the sentence the claim quotes for it ("When set, this token is used instead of your stored login. In non-interactive mode (-p), the token is always used when present.") does NOT appear in the current env-vars page. Design-critical omission: with `--bare`, Claude Code "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain" and "does not read CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN" (nor profiles/federation vars); `--bare` is "the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release", so a subscription-backed `-p` runner must not pass `--bare` and must pin/verify this when the default flips. After a 401 with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set, Claude Code (v2.1.225+) keeps sending the env value rather than switching to a stored login's token; before v2.1.225 it could swap in the stored login's short-lived access token mid-session and fail again when that expired.

findings.claim: Over SSH/WSL/containers the browser login completes through a paste-code fallback rather than the localhost callback, so a login can be performed on a grid node from the laptop's browser.
findings.detail: "When Claude Code runs in WSL2, on a remote machine over SSH, or inside a container, the browser usually opens on a different host and its redirect can't reach Claude Code's local callback server. verdict.corrected_claim: Over SSH, WSL2, or inside a container, Claude Code's claude.ai OAuth login "usually" (docs' word, not "always") cannot complete via the localhost callback; after sign-in the browser shows a login code, which is pasted into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt (or into `claude auth login`, which reads the code from stdin). Press `c` at the interactive login prompt to copy the OAuth URL. Therefore a Pro/Max login CAN be performed for a Claude Code instance running on a grid compute node using the laptop's browser, provided the node itself can reach `platform.claude.com` (token exchange), `claude.ai` and `api.anthropic.com`, and the code is pasted promptly (it expires: `OAuth error: Invalid code. Please make sure the full code was copied`).
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim HOLDS as of 2026-09-27; verbatim wording confirmed on the cited page and corroborated on two other official pages. Refinements below are additions, not corrections.

[1] EXACT QUOTE, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install, section heading "OAuth login fails in WSL2, SSH, or containers": "When Claude Code runs in WSL2, on a remote machine over SSH, or inside a container, the browser usually opens on a different host and its redirect can't reach Claude Code's local callback server. After you sign in, the browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back automatically. Paste that code into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt to complete login." Then: "Alternatively, press `c` at the interactive login prompt to copy the OAuth URL, or copy the URL that `claude auth login` prints, and open it in a browser on your local machine." critical=true.

[2] CORROBORATION, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, "Log in to Claude Code": "If the browser doesn't open automatically, press `c` to copy the login URL to your clipboard, then paste it into your browser. If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers. When login completes, the terminal shows `Login successful` and prompts you to press `Enter` to continue." Account types accepted: "Claude Pro or Max subscription: log in with your claude.ai account." critical=true.

[3] CORROBORATION (containers), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer, Note: "If the browser sign-in completes but the callback never reaches the container, copy the code shown in the browser and paste it at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt in the terminal. This can happen when the editor's port forwarding doesn't route the localhost callback." NUANCE: this implies that when an editor (VS Code Remote-SSH/Dev Containers) DOES auto-forward the callback port, the localhost redirect can succeed instead; the extension must handle both outcomes (auto-redirect success OR code paste). critical=true.

[4] EXPLICIT REMOTE/SSH GUIDANCE, troubleshoot-install, "OAuth error: Invalid code": "If you see `OAuth error: Invalid code. Please make sure the full code was copied`, the login code expired or was truncated during copy-paste." Solutions: "Press Enter to retry and complete the login quickly after the browser opens"; "Type `c` to copy the full URL if the browser doesn't open automatically"; "If using a remote/SSH session, the browser may open on the wrong machine. Copy the URL displayed in the terminal and open it in your local browser instead." DESIGN: the code is time-limited; relay URL to laptop and code back to node without delay. critical=true.

[5] SCRIPTABLE PATH (stdin), troubleshoot-install: "If pasting the code into the interactive prompt does nothing, your terminal's paste binding likely isn't reaching the input field. ... or use `claude auth login` instead, which reads the pasted code from standard input". CLI reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference): `claude auth login` flags `--email`, `--sso`, `--console`; `claude auth status` "Shows authentication status as JSON. Use `--text` for human-readable output. Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not." DESIGN: drive login over an SSH exec channel with `claude auth login` (prints URL to stdout, reads code from stdin) rather than scraping the TUI; poll `claude auth status`. critical=true.

[6] NODE-SIDE NETWORK REQUIREMENT (implicit in claim, made explicit), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config, "Network access requirements": `platform.claude.com` -- "OAuth token exchange, refresh, and revocation also go to this host for claude.ai accounts, so both Console and claude.ai sign-ins require it"; `claude.ai` -- "claude.ai account authentication"; `claude.com` -- "claude.ai account sign-in opens a `claude.com` page in the browser, which redirects to `claude.ai`"; `api.anthropic.com` -- "Claude API requests". The code->token exchange is performed by the CLI on the compute node, so the node (already verified to have internet) must reach `platform.claude.com`; the laptop browser needs `claude.com`/`claude.ai`. critical=true.

[7] CREDENTIAL PERSISTENCE IN THE SINGULARITY JOB, authentication page "Credential management": "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." devcontainer page: "It stores your OAuth account, personal MCP servers, and per-project trust in `~/.claude.json`, a separate file outside that directory, so mounting a volume at `~/.claude` alone doesn't keep you signed in. Mount a named volume at `~/.claude` and set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to the same path so Claude Code writes `.claude.json` inside the volume." Authentication page: "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead". DESIGN: with Singularity binding $HOME (Panasas) by default a one-time login persists across jobs; set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to a bound persistent path if $HOME is not bound; never place it under swept /tmp. critical=true.

[8] ALTERNATIVE WITHOUT BROWSER ON THE NODE, authentication page "Generate a long-lived token": "`claude setup-token` ... generate a one-year OAuth token ... It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable ... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors." Also: "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`." Precedence: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (rank 5) outranks `/login` subscription OAuth (rank 7). DESIGN OPTION: run `claude setup-token` on the laptop (where the callback works), ship the token to the node. critical=false.

[9] LOGIN EXPIRY FOR A LONG-RUNNING JOB, authentication page "Renew an expiring login": warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (v2.1.203+); after expiry each request fails with `Login expired · Please run /login`; "A background session ... or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." Login lifetime itself is not stated in the docs. headless page: "Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available" in `-p` mode. DESIGN: a 30-day persistent job needs a re-login path or a setup-token; the docs do not state the /login token lifetime. critical=true.

[10] VERSION/DATE: no version gate is attached to the login-code fallback on any of the three pages; the same doc set references Claude Code v2.1.283 (headless page) and 2.1.246 (troubleshoot page), so the text is current for the installed 2.1.283. The callback port number is not documented on these pages. WebSearch budget was exhausted for this session, so no third-party/GitHub-issue corroboration was gathered; all evidence is from code.claude.com pages actually fetched.

findings.claim: In -p mode Claude Code exits 0 on success and non-zero on failure, and prints an in-run failure (including auth failures) as the result on stdout; with --output-format json the text is in `result`; result subtypes are success, error_max_turns, error_during_execution, error_max_budget_usd, error_max_structured_output_retries with is_error, errors, total_cost_usd, usage, permission_denials, session_id, num_turns.
findings.detail: headless: "Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails ... When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout." SIGTERM exits 143. `--output-format` options `text|json|stream-json`; `--input-format stream-json` for a long-lived stdin-driven session; `--continue`/`--resume <id>` to keep one conversation across invocations (`--resume` finds the id from any directory since v2.1.223). Python SDK ResultMessage subtype list as stated.

verdict.corrected_claim: In -p mode Claude Code exits 0 on success and non-zero (observed: 1) when the run fails; an invalid flag is reported on stderr before the run starts (`error: unknown option '--no-such-flag'`, exit 1), while a failure inside the run, including missing or invalid authentication, is printed as the RESULT on stdout (stderr empty) and the process exits 1. With `--output-format json` the text is in `result`. Result subtypes are `success` (SDKResultSuccess) and the four error subtypes `error_max_turns`, `error_during_execution`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_max_structured_output_retries` (SDKResultError). CRITICAL PRECISION: an API/auth failure is NOT an error subtype; it is `subtype:"success"` with `is_error:true`, `terminal_reason:"api_error"`, `api_error_status` (401 or null) and the error text in `result` — branch on `is_error` or the exit code, never on `subtype` alone. Fields on every result: `is_error`, `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, `session_id`, `num_turns`, `stop_reason`, `uuid`; `result` (string) only on `success`; `errors: string[]` only on the error subtypes (absent from the success JSON). SIGTERM exits 143 and records no result for the in-progress turn. `--output-format text|json|stream-json`; `--input-format text|stream-json` (stream-json keeps the process alive across turns; single-prompt mode exits after the turn). `--continue` / `--resume <session-id|name|/abs/path.jsonl>` continue a conversation; `claude -p --resume <id>` works from any directory on the machine since v2.1.223 (cross-project lookup resolves only when exactly one other project holds the transcript). Python SDK docs list the five subtypes as a Literal, but the shipped dataclass types `subtype: str`, `errors: list[str] | None`, `total_cost_usd: float | None` — treat the list as non-exhaustive and null-check.

findings.claim: With --output-format stream-json every retryable API failure emits a `system/api_retry` event whose `error` field is one of a fixed category set including `rate_limit`, `authentication_failed`, `account_on_hold`, `billing_error`, `overloaded`; a wrapper can key off this to fail over or sleep.
findings.detail: Fields: `type: "system"`, `subtype: "api_retry"`, `attempt` (from 1), `max_retries`, `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status` (HTTP status or null), `error` ∈ {`authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `account_on_hold`, `billing_error`, `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `cloud_credential_error`, `unknown`}, `uuid`, `session_id`. On v2.1.246+ a 401/403 against an apiKeyHelper credential is retried twice silently before the event appears.

verdict.corrected_claim: With `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose` (the `--verbose` flag is still mandatory: the 2.1.283 binary exits with `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`), Claude Code emits a `system/api_retry` event before each retry of a retryable API failure in the main thread, with fields `type:"system"`, `subtype:"api_retry"`, `attempt` (from 1), `max_retries` (per-cause, can be below the session budget), `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status` (HTTP status or null), optional `no_response{waited_ms,retry_wait_ms}` (v2.1.261+), `error`, `uuid`, `session_id`. The docs list twelve `error` values, but the emitter in the shipped 2.1.283 binary maps a failure to only six: `overloaded` (529 / overloaded_error), `rate_limit` (429), `authentication_failed` (401/403), `server_error` (status >= 408), `cloud_credential_error`, `unknown`; `account_on_hold`, `billing_error`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `max_output_tokens` never appear on an `api_retry` event, because those conditions are not retried at all (account hold and expired login stop locally before any request). They surface instead as `error` on the `assistant` message (`SDKAssistantMessageError`) and on the terminal `result` (`is_error:true`, `terminal_reason:"api_error"`, `api_error_status`). Not every retry produces the event: on v2.1.246+ the first two 401/403 retries against an `apiKeyHelper` credential are silent (still counted in `attempt`), retries inside subagents are reported as `tool_progress.subagent_retry` (same six `error_category` values) rather than `system/api_retry`, and the binary contains an undocumented 13th enum value `verification_required`, so a wrapper must treat unrecognised values as `unknown`. A wrapper that wants to sleep through 429/529 should set `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1` (indefinite capacity retries, back-off up to 5 min or until the reset time the response carries) rather than re-implement it, and detect a used-up Pro/Max window from the `rate_limit_event` message (`rate_limit_info.status:"rejected"`, `resetsAt`, `errorCode:"credits_required"`, v2.1.181+), not from `api_retry`.

The interactive auto-continue feature (v2.1.234+, setting `autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, footer `Usage limit reached · continuing automatically at 3:45pm · esc to cancel`, menu `/rate-limit-options`) is NOT offered in `-p` runs or background sessions, does not auto-start for Remote Control or agent-team teammate sessions or for a reset more than 24 hours away (weekly limit), re-arms at most twice, needs Enter after a >30 min computer sleep, and ends when Claude Code exits. HOWEVER, a documented non-interactive wait-through mechanism does exist: `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1` (v2.1.186+), "for unattended sessions such as eval harnesses, CI jobs, or remote workers", retries 429/529 indefinitely and "backs off up to 5 minutes between attempts, or until the limit resets when the response carries a rate-limit reset time, so a session that hits a usage limit waits out the remaining window" (but fails at once on a 429 reporting a spend limit or exhausted usage credits, v2.1.239+). Without the watchdog, plan-limit 429s that carry quota headers are not retried and a `-p` run fails with a non-zero exit and the failure printed as the result; in `stream-json`/SDK the hit surfaces as a `rate_limit_event` (`rate_limit_info.status: "rejected"`, `resetsAt`, `utilization`). DESIGN IMPLICATIONS (critical=true): for a persistent Claude Code worker in a Slurm job, (a) do not count on the interactive auto-continue — it is unavailable in `-p`/background sessions, and even in an interactive tmux session it will not auto-start for a weekly-limit reset >24 h away and stops after two re-arms; (b) set `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1` (v2.1.186+, fix in 2.1.281) so the unattended session waits out a session-window reset instead of exiting, and treat spend-limit/credits-exhausted 429s as terminal; (c) parse `rate_limit_event` (`status: "rejected"`, `resetsAt`) from `--output-format stream-json` to surface the reset time to the student's laptop; (d) `--bare` disables subscription login, so do not use it with the student's Pro/Max account.
