findings.claim: An expired/unrefreshable login in -p mode is reported as `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` with structured error code `authentication_failed`, after Claude Code has already cleared the stored credential; sessions using CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or an API key never see this.
findings.detail: errors "Login expired": interactive `Login expired · Please run /login`; "In non-interactive mode (`-p`) and the Agent SDK, the message reads as follows, and the structured error code is `authentication_failed`: `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`"; "Claude Code tried to renew your saved ... login and the OAuth service rejected the stored refresh token, so Claude Code cleared the saved credentials"; "For automation that can't sign in interactively, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or generate a long-lived token with `claude setup-token`".

verdict.corrected_claim: An expired/unrefreshable login in -p mode is reported as `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` with structured error code `authentication_failed`, after Claude Code has already cleared the stored credential; sessions using CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or an API key never see this.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim CONFIRMED verbatim against the official errors page (fetched raw markdown https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md, 528 KB, section "### Login expired", lines 1164-1190). Page carries no visible last-updated date; it references Claude Code versions up to v2.1.283, so it is current as of 2026-09-27.

EXACT TEXT (errors.md, "### Login expired"):
- "Claude Code tried to renew your saved claude.ai or Claude Console login and the OAuth service rejected the stored refresh token, so Claude Code cleared the saved credentials. After that, each model request stops locally with this message before it reaches the API, because only `/login` can create new credentials."
- Interactive message: `Login expired · Please run /login`
- "In non-interactive mode (`-p`) and the Agent SDK, the message reads as follows, and the structured error code is `authentication_failed`:" -> `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`
- "Sessions authenticated with an API key, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or a third-party provider don't use the saved login and never see this message." (claim omits "third-party provider"; subset, not wrong)
- Recovery: "In non-interactive mode, run `claude` in the same environment, complete `/login`, then rerun your command. For automation that can't sign in interactively, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or generate a long-lived token with `claude setup-token`."
- "/status shows a `Login` row reading `Expired — log in again`" (requires v2.1.210+).

QUALIFIERS THE DESIGN DEPENDS ON (critical=true):
1. Version gate: "Before v2.1.206, Claude Code sent the model request anyway with whatever credential remained in the environment, and every model then failed with There's an issue with the selected model or a 401 instead of a prompt to sign in." Also "Before v2.1.235, Claude Code reported a held account as Login expired" (now `account_on_hold`). => the CLI pinned inside the Singularity image must be >= v2.1.206 (ideally >= 2.1.235) for this error string/code to be reliable. critical=true.
2. "Never see this" applies only to THIS message. A `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (setup-token, one-year) session that expires/is revoked gets a DIFFERENT failure, from the "### OAuth token revoked or expired" section: "If you authenticate with a long-lived token in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, you see the same messages when that token expires or is revoked." Messages: `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` and `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`. "Claude Code keeps sending the value you set after a request fails with a 401, rather than switching to a stored login's token" (v2.1.225+); fix = "Generate a fresh token with `claude setup-token` and restart with it". => the persistent grid worker must also handle 401 `OAuth token has expired`, not only `authentication_failed`. critical=true.
3. `--bare` breaks subscription auth entirely: headless page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless) "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain"; authentication page: "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." and headless notes "`--bare` ... will become the default for `-p` in a future release." => a Pro/Max-backed `-p` worker must NOT pass `--bare`, and a future default flip would surface as `Not logged in · Please run /login` rather than `authentication_failed`. critical=true.
4. Sibling transient error, same surface, different code: "### Could not refresh your login because another Claude Code process is refreshing it" -> in `-p`/SDK the message is `Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh. This is usually transient; retry in a minute...` with structured code `server_error`. Relevant because parallel sessions on one shared home (Panasas) "share a saved login and coordinate its renewal so that only one process refreshes the token at a time" (troubleshoot-install, "### Not logged in or token expired"). critical=true (retry, do not treat as auth death).
5. In `-p` mode "/login" is unavailable: headless page: "Built-in commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/login`, aren't available." Failure surfaces as the run's result on stdout with non-zero exit: "When a failure happens inside the run, such as missing authentication, Claude Code prints the failure as the result on stdout." `authentication_failed` is also an `error` category value in `system/api_retry` stream-json events.
6. Credential storage on Linux (authentication page): `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode `0600`; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates it. Expiry warning `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (v2.1.203+, 5 days before v2.1.217) appears only for a claude.ai/Console login, "not when a cloud provider, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` supplies the credential."
7. setup-token facts (authentication page "Generate a long-lived token"): one-year OAuth token; "requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan"; "It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work."; precedence rank 5 (below `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `apiKeyHelper`; above `/login` subscription OAuth at rank 7).

verdict.corrected_claim: Remote Control keeps the Claude Code session running on the machine where `claude` is launched (execution and filesystem access stay there) and exposes it at claude.ai/code and in the Claude iOS/Android app. It is started with `claude remote-control` (server mode: no local interactive session), `claude --remote-control [name]` / `--rc` (interactive session also reachable remotely), `/remote-control` / `/rc` inside a running CLI, VS Code extension or Desktop-app session, or automatically via `remoteControlAtStartup: true` in user or managed settings. It requires a full-scope claude.ai login on a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan (API keys, `apiKeyHelper`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, and long-lived tokens from `claude setup-token` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` are all rejected), talking directly to api.anthropic.com (blocked on Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, a non-default `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_UNIX_SOCKET`, or an enterprise Claude apps gateway login). Server-mode flags, given AFTER the `remote-control` verb: `--name`, `--remote-control-session-name-prefix` (env `CLAUDE_REMOTE_CONTROL_SESSION_NAME_PREFIX`), `-c/--continue` and `--session-id <id>` (v2.1.200+), `--spawn same-dir|worktree|session` (default `same-dir`), `--capacity <N>` (default 32), `--[no-]create-session-in-dir` (on by default), `--permission-mode <mode>`, `--sandbox/--no-sandbox` (off by default), `--verbose`, `-d/--debug[=<filter>]` (v2.1.282+), `--debug-file <path>`. One-time confirmation `Enable Remote Control? (y/n)`; declining exits without starting the server. Settings: `remoteControlAtStartup`, `disableRemoteControl`. The `claude remote-control` subcommand shipped in v2.1.51 on 2026-02-24 per the official changelog ("Expand Remote Control to more users" in v2.1.58, 2026-02-25).

Requires a git repository. `session`: single-session mode. Serves exactly one session and rejects additional connections. Set at startup only. Press `w` at runtime to toggle between `same-dir` and `worktree`." `--capacity <N>` "Maximum number of concurrent sessions. Default is 32. If you pass a global `claude` flag before `remote-control`, or a wrapper script adds one, Claude Code doesn't carry the flag over to the sessions the server creates ... For any other flag, such as `--settings`, Claude Code refuses to start and names the flag to remove." findings.claim: Remote Control needs only outbound HTTPS (port 443) to the Anthropic API, opens no inbound port, and the docs explicitly cover running it on a remote SSH machine inside tmux/screen, so a Slurm compute node with internet can host a Remote Control session.
findings.detail: "Your local Claude Code session makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports on your machine. When you start Remote Control, it registers with the Anthropic API and polls for work." "Remote Control requires access to the Anthropic API on port 443." Limitations: "Local process must keep running ... To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside `tmux` or `screen`." Server mode: sessions can be brought back "for about four hours after the server stopped"; on sustained HTTP 403 "Server mode: Claude Code gives up after roughly 10 minutes and the `claude remote-control` process exits". verdict.corrected_claim: Remote Control makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens an inbound port; it registers with the Anthropic API and polls for work, and "requires access to the Anthropic API on port 443" (for a strict allowlist, `claude.ai` and `platform.claude.com` are also required on 443, because the claude.ai sign-in and the OAuth token exchange/refresh that renew Remote Control's short-lived credentials go there). The docs explicitly say: "To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside `tmux` or `screen`." So a Slurm compute node with outbound internet can host a `claude remote-control` server, PROVIDED: (1) the account is Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise and signed in via `/login` on that node (the paste-code flow works over SSH); API keys, `claude setup-token`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` cannot establish Remote Control; (2) `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` and `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK` are unset; (3) the one-time `Enable Remote Control? (y/n)` confirmation and the workspace-trust dialog have been accepted once from a TTY in the project directory (trust is never saved for $HOME); (4) the saved claude.ai login is renewed before it expires (lifetime not stated in the docs; a 3-day warning appears at startup on v2.1.203+), because a Remote Control session that outlives the login "stops making progress ... and can't recover until you sign in again". Stopped servers can be brought back for about four hours; in an extended network outage (not specifically HTTP 403) server mode "gives up after roughly 10 minutes and the `claude remote-control` process exits", while the interactive-session 403 retry window is three minutes. The transcript is stored on Anthropic servers and Zero Data Retention orgs cannot enable it.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: headline claim holds; all quoted sentences found verbatim on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control (fetched 2026-09-27). One DETAIL mis-attribution and several design-critical qualifications the claim omits.

VERBATIM MATCHES (remote-control page):
- critical=true | "Your local Claude Code session makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports on your machine. When you start Remote Control, it registers with the Anthropic API and polls for work. When you connect from another device, the server routes messages between the web or mobile client and your local session over a streaming connection." (section "Connection and security")
- critical=true | Troubleshooting > "Remote credentials fetch failed": "Network or proxy issue: a firewall or proxy may be blocking the outbound HTTPS request. Remote Control requires access to the Anthropic API on port 443." Also: "API key authentication is not supported for Remote Control."
- critical=true | Limitations: "**Local process must keep running**: Remote Control runs as a local process. If you close the terminal, quit the Desktop app or VS Code, or otherwise stop the `claude` process, the session goes offline until you bring it back. To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside `tmux` or `screen`."
- critical=true | "These commands work for about four hours after the server stopped. After that, run `claude remote-control` to start a new session. If you archived a session in the meantime, `--continue` and `--session-id` unarchive it on Claude Code v2.1.228 or later." (`claude remote-control`, `claude remote-control --continue`, `claude remote-control --session-id <id>`; `--continue`/`--session-id` require v2.1.200+)
- "While Remote Control is connected, the session transcript, including your messages, Claude's responses, and tool activity, is stored on Anthropic servers." / "Organizations with compliance requirements such as Zero Data Retention can't enable Remote Control." / setting `disableRemoteControl` turns it off.

DETAIL INACCURACY (minor):
- The "10 minutes" sentence is under the bullet "**Extended network outage**: if your machine is awake but can't reach the network" -> "**Server mode**: Claude Code gives up after roughly 10 minutes and the `claude remote-control` process exits. Run `claude remote-control` again to start a new session." / "**Interactive session**: keep working locally. Claude Code retries for as long as the outage lasts and reconnects on its own when the network returns." The separate 403 bullet reads: "**HTTP 403 refusals on a connected session**: once an interactive session is connected, Claude Code keeps retrying for up to three minutes when something between your machine and Anthropic's servers answers with HTTP 403 ... If the refusals last longer, Claude Code disconnects, and the reason names what refused: a network edge, or a proxy, VPN, or firewall on your own network." The docs give no server-mode-specific 403 number.
- Also: "**Presence heartbeats failing**: if an interactive session disconnects with `could not reach the Remote Control server for about 30 minutes`, run `/remote-control` to reconnect."

DESIGN-CRITICAL QUALIFICATIONS THE CLAIM OMITS:
- critical=true | Requirements: "**Subscription**: available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported." "**Authentication**: run `claude` and use `/login` to sign in through claude.ai ... Without an eligible login, `claude remote-control` exits with an error". "**API endpoint**: not available ... You point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at a host other than `api.anthropic.com` ... Unset the variable to use Remote Control." "If you set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` or `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK`, Remote Control is unavailable." "If you set only `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` or `DO_NOT_TRACK`, Remote Control stays available unless your organization requires Trusted Devices ... requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later." (CHANGELOG 2.1.283: "Fixed Remote Control being unavailable on paid plans when telemetry is turned off"; latest version 2.1.283, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- critical=true | "**Workspace trust**: run `claude` in your project directory at least once to accept the workspace trust dialog. The startup trust dialog never saves trust for your home directory, so start Remote Control from a project directory."
- critical=true | Server mode first run needs a TTY answer: "Until you accept Remote Control's one-time confirmation, `claude remote-control` explains what it does and asks `Enable Remote Control? (y/n)` before starting the server ... If you decline, Claude Code exits without starting the server". Server-mode flags: `--name`, `--remote-control-session-name-prefix <prefix>` (env `CLAUDE_REMOTE_CONTROL_SESSION_NAME_PREFIX`, default = hostname), `-c/--continue`, `--session-id <id>`, `--spawn same-dir|worktree|session`, `--capacity <N>` (default 32), `--[no-]create-session-in-dir`, `--permission-mode <mode>`, `-d/--debug[=<filter>]` (v2.1.282+), `--debug-file <path>`, `--verbose`, `--sandbox`/`--no-sandbox` (off by default). "Give these flags after `remote-control`." Global flags before `remote-control` such as `--settings` make it refuse to start. Crashed sessions in server mode are re-served on next message (v2.1.238+).
- critical=true | Long-lived tokens do NOT work for Remote Control (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md, "Generate a long-lived token"): `claude setup-token` mints a one-year OAuth token that "requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions". So the compute-node login must be an interactive `/login`. Same page: "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers." Linux credentials live in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode 0600 (or under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`).
- critical=true | Login lifetime bounds a 30-day Slurm job (authentication.md "Renew an expiring login"): "When the login you created with `/login` is within three days of expiring, Claude Code shows a warning at startup: `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later." "Renewing early matters most for sessions that run unattended. A background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." The numeric lifetime is NOT stated anywhere I fetched ("The login lifetime itself is unchanged"). Errors page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md, "Remote Control couldn't refresh your login"): "Claude Code runs a live Remote Control connection on short-lived credentials that it obtains and renews using your saved claude.ai login ... If the login service still isn't answering when that credential expires, Claude Code stops Remote Control and reports `OAuth token refresh failed`." Exact disconnect strings: `Remote Control disconnected — Claude.ai login expired — run /login to restore Remote Control`, `... — OAuth token refresh failed — run /login to re-authenticate`, `... — JWT refresh failed: no OAuth token — run /login`, `... — Signed out of Claude — run /login, then /remote-control`.
- Allowlist is wider than api.anthropic.com (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/network-config, "Network access requirements"): `api.anthropic.com` (API, feature flags), `claude.ai` ("claude.ai account authentication"), `claude.com` (sign-in redirect), `platform.claude.com` ("OAuth token exchange, refresh, and revocation also go to this host for claude.ai accounts, so both Console and claude.ai sign-ins require it"), `downloads.claude.ai` (native installer/updater), `registry.npmjs.org` (npm installs). All outbound; "Claude Code does not support SOCKS proxies"; `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` honored.
- Trusted Devices (beta, off by default on Pro/Max; if the student turns on "Require trusted devices", sign-in must be < 18 hours old): "Your organization requires Trusted Devices for Remote Control, but this device is not enrolled" -> run `/login`.
- Not fetched/unknown: no independent third-party confirmation of running `claude remote-control` under Slurm/Singularity specifically; WebSearch budget was exhausted, so only official docs were used. Nothing found that contradicts the tmux/screen guidance for a batch-job context, but the docs never mention Slurm, a non-TTY batch start, or a container.

findings.claim: A Remote Control or background session that outlives its login simply stops making progress; the login (~30 days) cannot be renewed unattended, so Remote Control alone cannot carry a 30-day Slurm job.
findings.detail: authentication: "A background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." #92127 requests "a revocable machine/agent credential with `user:sessions:claude_code`" and confirms an external refresh script cannot extend the 30-day lifetime; #96076 says the choice is "long-lived token → Remote Control stops working" or "normal interactive login → expires after ~28 days with no background refresh daemon".

verdict.corrected_claim: A background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and cannot recover until an interactive `/login` is performed (official, verbatim). Claude Code auto-refreshes a subscription login unattended WITHIN its lifetime, but it cannot extend the login's maximum lifetime, and no unattended/device-code login exists (`claude auth login` takes only `--email`, `--sso`, `--console`). The maximum lifetime is NOT stated in any official doc; the "~30 days" (issue #92127) and "~28 days" (issue #96076) figures are community-measured and unanswered by Anthropic. The 1-year `claude setup-token` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` credential carries model requests for a 30-day job but "can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions" (error: `Remote Control requires a full-scope login token`), and `--bare` mode does not read it. Separately, server-mode `claude remote-control` exits after roughly 10 minutes of network outage. Conclusion stands: Remote Control alone cannot carry a 30-day Slurm job unattended.
verdict.evidence:
VERIFIED (official, critical=true) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, section "Renew an expiring login": "Renewing early matters most for sessions that run unattended. A background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again." Same section: "When the login you created with `/login` is within three days of expiring, Claude Code shows a warning at startup: `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. Before v2.1.217, the warning appeared five days out." "Once the stored login expires and can't be refreshed, each model request fails with `Login expired · Please run /login` until you sign in again. Before v2.1.206, Claude Code reported an expired login on model requests as a model error instead." "`/status` shows a `Login` row reading `Expired — log in again` ... requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later." NOTE: "The login lifetime itself is unchanged" — the page never gives the lifetime in days.

VERIFIED (official, critical=true) — same page, "Generate a long-lived token": "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token` ... set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable ... This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work." "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead." Precedence: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is #5, above subscription OAuth from `/login` (#7), so if the env var is set it wins over the interactive login (this is the mechanism behind issue #96076's "mutually exclusive").

VERIFIED (official, critical=true) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control: "Subscription: available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported." "Without an eligible login, `claude remote-control` exits with an error, while `claude --remote-control` still starts an interactive session and shows a Remote Control failure notification shortly after launch." Error section "Remote Control requires a full-scope login token": "You're authenticated with a long-lived token from `claude setup-token` or the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. These tokens can only make model requests, so they can't establish Remote Control sessions. Run `claude auth login` to authenticate with a full-scope session token instead." Other exact strings: `Remote Control requires a claude.ai subscription.`, `You must be logged in to use Remote Control. Remote Control is only available with claude.ai subscriptions.`, `Remote Control requires claude.ai subscription auth.` followed by e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, so this session is using API-key auth`. Also: "The connection uses multiple short-lived credentials, each scoped to a single purpose and expiring independently." Design-relevant failure modes on the same page (critical=true for a Slurm-node deployment): "Local process must keep running ... To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside `tmux` or `screen`." "Extended network outage — Server mode: Claude Code gives up after roughly 10 minutes and the `claude remote-control` process exits. Run `claude remote-control` again to start a new session." "Presence heartbeats failing: if an interactive session disconnects with `could not reach the Remote Control server for about 30 minutes`, run `/remote-control` to reconnect." Session resume after server stop: "These commands work for about four hours after the server stopped." Trusted Devices: "session expired for trusted-device check — Your sign-in is more than 18 hours old" applies to viewer devices; "the machine running Claude Code receives its own credential automatically when the developer signs in to the CLI."

VERIFIED (official) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors lists the Remote Control auth error strings: `OAuth token refresh failed — run /login to re-authenticate`, `JWT refresh failed: no OAuth token — run /login`, `Claude.ai login expired`, `OAuth token unavailable — run /login to restore Remote Control`, `Signed out of Claude — run /login, then /remote-control`, and the scope error `does not meet scope requirement user:profile`. Every fix is an interactive `/login`; none is automatable.

VERIFIED (official) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install, "Not logged in or token expired": "If Claude Code prompts you to log in again after a session, your OAuth token may have expired. Run `/login` to re-authenticate." "Parallel sessions on one machine share a saved login and coordinate its renewal so that only one process refreshes the token at a time. Before v2.1.211, waking the machine from sleep could cause two sessions to renew with the same token, which revoked the saved login." — confirms unattended refresh exists within the lifetime; no lifetime in days stated.

VERIFIED (official) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference: `claude auth login` flags are `--email`, `--sso`, `--console` only; `claude auth status` (`--text`, exit 0/1); `claude auth logout`; `claude setup-token` "Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it." No device-code or unattended login flag exists. The only `--no-browser` is for `claude mcp login <name>`.

VERIFIED (official) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view: "The supervisor and its sessions authenticate with the same stored credentials as your interactive sessions." "Shutting down or restarting your machine stops running background sessions." "Finished or waiting for your next message, and unattached for about an hour: the supervisor stops the process to free resources."

COMMUNITY (not official; no Anthropic response as of 2026-09-27) — https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/92127 (opened 2026-09-04, OPEN, labels `area:auth`, `enhancement`, title "Support unattended authentication for Remote Control on long-running Claude Code instances"): "`user:sessions:claude_code` appears to have a server-side maximum lifetime of 30 days. Refreshing the credential does not extend that lifetime." "The refresh token rotates, but the returned lifetime continues counting down towards the expiry of the original login. Claude Code already refreshes these credentials automatically, so implementing an external refresh-token script doesn't solve this." "a long-lived credential without `user:sessions:claude_code` gets through the Claude Code client-side checks, but Remote Control registration fails with a 403 because the required scope is missing." "`setup-token` remains a good solution for unattended inference, but cannot be used with Remote Control." Requests: opt-in Remote Control on setup-token; "a revocable machine/agent credential with `user:sessions:claude_code`"; a device authorization flow.

COMMUNITY (not official; no Anthropic response) — https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/96076 (opened 2026-09-22, OPEN, labels `area:auth`, `bug`, title "[BUG] Long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (setup-token) and Remote Control are mutually exclusive with no documented workaround"): "as soon as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set (globally or per-session), Remote Control stops working, regardless of how recently a full interactive `/login` was performed — the env token always wins over the session's own credentials." "`claude doctor` reports that Remote Control requires a full-scope login token, and that a `setup-token`-issued token is missing the `user:profile` scope." "Use the normal interactive OAuth login → refresh token expires after inactivity or after ~28 days, and without a background daemon to proactively refresh it (no longer present in recent CLI versions — no daemon process, no `daemon.log`), the session silently falls back to being logged out and needs a manual `/login`." Choices stated: "1) Use a long-lived token → lose Remote Control entirely. 2) Use the normal interactive OAuth login → ... ~28 days ... There's no supported way to get both."

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: the actual maximum lifetime of a `/login` credential is not published anywhere on code.claude.com; 28 vs 30 days are two user measurements that differ. Whether the "after inactivity" expiry in #96076 applies to a continuously active Slurm job is unverified. Note the two issues name different missing scopes (`user:sessions:claude_code` vs `user:profile`); the official docs say only "full-scope login token".

findings.claim: Claude Code on the web (cloud sessions) runs on Anthropic-managed VMs cloned from GitHub, is started with `claude --cloud "task"` (`--remote` deprecated alias), steered with `claude -p "msg" --cloud <session-id>`, pulled back with `claude --teleport <id>`, always uses subscription credentials, and cannot execute on the user's own HPC node.
findings.detail: "A cloud session is a Claude Code session that runs on cloud infrastructure instead of on your machine. By default it runs on infrastructure Anthropic manages, or on your organization's self-hosted environment" (self-hosted environments: "on Team and Enterprise plans"). Plans: Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise premium seats. "Cloud sessions always use your subscription credentials." Repo requirement: GitHub, or a local bundle < 100 MB with `CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1`. `--cloud` needs org policy `allow_remote_sessions`; `--teleport` "requires claude.ai subscription authentication" and "connects through the same Remote Control session infrastructure". Sessions share account rate limits; VMs are reclaimed after inactivity ("Environment expired").

verdict.corrected_claim: A Claude Code cloud session "runs on cloud infrastructure instead of on your machine. By default it runs on infrastructure Anthropic manages, or on your organization's self-hosted environment when routed there." Anthropic-hosted sessions each get "a fresh virtual machine (VM) running Ubuntu 24.04 on x86_64" that "clones your current directory's GitHub remote at your current branch, not your local checkout", or receives a local git bundle (<100 MB; forced with `CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1`). Start from the terminal with `claude --cloud "task"` ("The older `--remote` spelling still works as a deprecated alias for `--cloud`"); queue a follow-up with `claude -p "your message" --cloud <session-id>` (bare `session_...`/`cse_...` id or claude.ai/code URL; `--output-format json` gives `{ok, session_id, url}`); pull back with `claude --teleport <session-id>` (or `/teleport`, `/tp`, `/tasks` then `t`), which needs clean git state, a checkout of the same repository, the branch pushed, and the same claude.ai account. Availability: "Pro, Max, and Team plans, and for Enterprise users with premium seats or Chat + Claude Code seats"; the CLI forms need a claude.ai sign-in (API-key auth fails with `Unable to get organization UUID`; Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry are refused) and the org policy `allow_remote_sessions`; `--teleport` "requires claude.ai subscription authentication" and "connects through the same Remote Control session infrastructure that cloud sessions use". The sentence "Cloud sessions always use your subscription credentials" is NOT on the cited page; what the docs state is that sessions "share rate limits with all other Claude and Claude Code usage within your account", "There is no separate compute charge for the cloud VM", and self-hosted sessions authenticate inference "with an Anthropic-issued, session-scoped OAuth token". Sessions are not persistent processes: "Cloud sessions stop after a period of inactivity and the session's VM is reclaimed" (heading "Environment expired"); reopening restores the conversation but "Background work that was still running when the VM was reclaimed, such as subagents and shell commands, isn't restored." CORRECTION to the last part of the claim: a cloud session CAN execute on the user's own Linux host, including an HPC node or container, via a self-hosted environment (`claude self-hosted-runner --environment-secret-file <file> --base-dir <dir>`, Claude Code >= v2.1.224, Linux/macOS host or container, outbound HTTPS only), but this is "public beta on Team and Enterprise plans", "off by default", and requires an org Owner to enable "Allow self-hosted environments". For an individual student on Pro or Max it is unavailable, so for the Ashley design the practical conclusion stands: an Anthropic-hosted cloud session cannot run on the WSU grid. The documented route for "run Claude Code on your own always-on machine and drive it from other devices" on Pro/Max is Remote Control (`claude remote-control` server mode, `claude --remote-control`/`--rc`, or `/remote-control`/`/rc`), which "executes on your machine", "makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports", requires a claude.ai subscription ("API keys are not supported"), and per the docs should be started "inside `tmux` or `screen`" to survive an SSH disconnect on a remote machine.

findings.claim: Cross-session messaging lets one Claude Code session send plain-text messages to another session, including to a `-p` worker on another machine, but the cross-machine path rides on Remote Control (claude.ai login on both ends) and a message can never approve a permission prompt.
findings.detail: v2.1.224+ (Windows v2.1.234+). Tools `ListAgents`/`SendMessage`; `/list-agents` (`/peers`). Same machine: Unix socket at `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` (private dir `/tmp/cc-socks-<uid>`), token `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`; a script can post `{"type":"auth","token":"..."}` then a line. Other machine: "Through Anthropic servers, arriving over that machine's Remote Control connection". "Claude Code binds an inbox socket for a `claude -p` session like an interactive one ... "A session inside a container and a session on the host can't reach each other." "It can't approve anything".

VERIFIED against the live page https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance fetched 2026-09-27 (no last-updated date shown on the page). Every quoted sentence in the DETAIL appears verbatim. Section-by-section:

[Usage policy > Acceptable use] "Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK." — exact match.

[Usage policy > Authentication and credential use] "**OAuth authentication** is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications." — exact match. Same section: "Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users. Moreover, developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." — exact match. Same section, carve-out: "Nor does it prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code as described under *Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?* above." — exact match. Same section: "Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice." — exact match.

[Legal agreements > Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?] "Unless we've mutually agreed otherwise, preinstalling or running Claude Code in your products or services (e.g. in hosted sandboxes or other agent infrastructure) requires agreeing to our Commercial Terms of Service and complying with the conditions below:" then "**The Claude Code binary must not be modified.** Claude Code must be installed and run as published by Anthropic, and customers may not remove, disable, or restrict any authentication method built into it (including methods that permit signing in with a Claude account or the user's own API key)." and "**Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf.** Each end user must authenticate with their own Anthropic API key, Claude subscription plan credentials, or 3P inference provider credential (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry). That usage is billed directly to the end user under their own agreement with Anthropic or, for third-party inference providers, with the applicable provider." — exact matches.

NUANCES THE CLAIM OMITS (critical=true for the Ashley design):
(a) The hosting permission is conditional: the hoster must agree to the Commercial Terms of Service ("Unless we've mutually agreed otherwise ... requires agreeing to our Commercial Terms of Service"). The end-user carve-out cross-references that section, so it applies to a platform that meets those conditions.
(b) The page also states developers "building products or services that interact with Claude's capabilities, including those using the Agent SDK, should use API key authentication" — so an extension that itself calls Claude on the student's behalf (rather than launching the unmodified `claude` binary for the student to log into) falls on the forbidden side.
(c) Name/logo: "You can accurately say, in plain text, that your product has Claude Code preinstalled or that it runs Claude Code. But you can't use the Claude Code or Anthropic names or logos as part of your own product, feature, or company name, in your own logo..."
(d) Design consequence: Ashley must NOT collect, store, transmit or proxy the student's Claude.ai OAuth token or `~/.claude/.credentials.json`. The permitted pattern is: the unmodified binary runs in the container on the compute node and the STUDENT completes `/login` through Anthropic's own flow there. The Authentication page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication, fetched 2026-09-27) confirms this works headless: "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers." Press `c` to copy the login URL. On Linux credentials land in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mode `0600`, or under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if set (relevant: Panasas home vs CephFS). For an unattended Slurm job the student themselves may run `claude setup-token` (opens the same browser flow, prints a one-year OAuth token, "does not save the token anywhere") and set `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; it "authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan", "can only make model requests", cannot establish Remote Control sessions, and is NOT read in `--bare` mode. Note the `/login` credential expires and shows "Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew" (v2.1.203+); "A background session ... that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires" — so a 30-day persistent job needs the setup-token route or periodic re-login by the student. Precedence: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `apiKeyHelper` outrank `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, which outranks subscription `/login` credentials.

Caveat on method: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200), so no secondary sources were searched; verification rests on direct fetches of the two official pages, which is the authoritative check for this claim.

topics_verified.recommendation: 1. Never collect, copy or relay the student's Claude credential. Ashley must not scp `.credentials.json` to the grid, must not store the OAuth token in its own settings, and must not put a token-pooling proxy in front of api.anthropic.com. The legal page allows exactly one thing: the student signs in to the unmodified `claude` binary with their own subscription, through Anthropic's own flow. Design the extension to open a terminal on the compute node (inside the Singularity container) and let the student run the flow themselves; over SSH the browser shows a paste-code, which the docs cover. 2. Use two credentials on the grid, both minted by the student, both isolated with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a per-student directory on CephFS or home (never /tmp) so the grid never shares a refresh-token family with the laptop: (a) for the persistent `-p` worker, `claude setup-token` → `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the job's environment (one year, always used in -p, do not pass `--bare`, do not route it through apiKeyHelper); (b) only if Remote Control is wanted, a full `claude auth login` in that same `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, run inside tmux/screen in the Slurm job with `claude remote-control --name <student>-<jobid>`; tell the student it dies at ≤30 days and must be renewed by hand. 3. Do not treat Remote Control or Claude Code on the web as a replacement for the SSH bridge. Web/cloud sessions run on Anthropic VMs and cannot reach the grid. Remote Control can steer a grid session from a phone (outbound 443 only, docs sanction the tmux-on-SSH case) but is subscription-only, unattended-renewal-impossible, and stores transcripts on Anthropic servers; keep the SSH/shared-filesystem bridge as the primary channel and offer `/rc` as an optional extra. If a push channel into the container is wanted without SSH polling, a custom Channels webhook server (`--dangerously-load-development-channels server:<name>`, port 8788 reached through the existing SSH tunnel) works with a setup-token or API key and can relay permission prompts; note it is research-preview and container/host socket sharing is undocumented for Singularity. 4. Run the worker with `--output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json` (or `--resume <session_id>` per prompt) and implement failover on three signals: `system/api_retry` with `error` in {`rate_limit`, `overloaded`}; a final `result` with `is_error: true` whose `result` matches `You've hit your (session|weekly|Opus|Sonnet) limit · resets (.+)`; and `authentication_failed` / `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`. On a plan limit, parse the reset time or poll `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` (`anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`) for `five_hour`/`seven_day.resets_at`, then either sleep until reset or restart the worker with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set (it outranks OAuth in -p) using a lab or student Console key; on `authentication_failed`, stop and notify the student to re-run setup-token. Never fail over to a second subscription account of the same student: that is the limit-evasion pattern Anthropic acts on. 5. Do not depend on community switchers on the grid. cc-switch needs glibc 2.35 and a GUI; claude-swap/ccswitch swap the live credential file and would fight the running worker's refresh; npm claude-profiles does not switch accounts. For laptop-side profile separation, ship shell aliases over `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. 6. Surface `claude auth status` (exit 1 when not logged in; JSON `subscriptionType`, `email`) in the extension's health check, and warn students not to sign in to Desktop, VS Code and CLI on the same machine with different accounts because they share one `oauthAccount` slot.

topics_verified.topic: Persistent Claude Code worker accepting remote prompts (stream-json bidirectional mode), orchestration tools, IPC over shared/parallel filesystems vs sockets vs ssh tunnels, and orchestrator-to-N-worker fan-out/join, for the Ashley VS Code extension on the WSU grid
topics_verified.summary: The bidirectional protocol is real, stable and used by Anthropic's own Agent SDK: start `claude` with `--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose` (the docs describe both flags as print-mode flags and third parties report `-p` is now mandatory, so pass `-p`), feed one NDJSON line per user turn shaped `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."},"parent_tool_use_id":null}` (the Python SDK also sends `"session_id":""`), and treat `{"type":"result",...}` as end of turn; the same process accepts unlimited further turns until stdin EOF, and Anthropic's SDK source says explicitly that "a result ends a turn, not necessarily the run." No official cold-start number exists; measured points range from ~0.7 s process boot (`claude -p` boot-to-ready 679 ms median, v2.1.251) to 20-74 s wall clock for a trivial `claude -p` on slow or unlucky hosts, with a documented 12.5 s stall from a failed startup config fetch, so a warm long-lived process is the only reliable way to get low latency, and the `result` event itself now carries `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `ttft_ms` and `time_to_request_from_spawn_ms` for measuring it. `--resume` re-sends the whole transcript; it is cheap only while the prompt cache is warm (1 h on a subscription within plan usage, 5 min on API billing), otherwise the full history is reprocessed. Of the orchestration tools, Agent Teams are interactive-only ("In non-interactive mode with the -p flag, including Agent SDK sessions, Claude doesn't spawn teammates") and single-machine (JSON mailboxes under `~/.claude/teams/`), claude-squad and ccmanager drive TTYs with tmux/PTY and worktrees, and claude-flow/Ruflo is a large MCP/CLI layer with 667 open issues; the built-in mechanisms that do work headless are subagents (in-process, 20 concurrent default) and dynamic workflows (`agent()/parallel()/pipeline()`, 16 concurrent default, allowed in `-p` via a `Workflow` permission rule). Anthropic's own same-machine IPC is a per-session Unix domain socket that even `claude -p` workers bind (not in `--bare`), and its cross-machine path goes through Anthropic servers via Remote Control, which requires an interactive claude.ai login and is not available to a `claude setup-token` token. For a shared-filesystem inbox, NFS is the weak case (close-to-open consistency, 3-60 s attribute cache, inotify blind to remote writes, O_EXCL atomic only on NFSv3+), whereas CephFS documents "strong cache coherency across clients" and PanFS DirectFlow claims "fully POSIX-compliant and cache-coherent" behaviour; an atomic rename plus polling is the portable pattern, and a `/dev/shm` Unix socket reached via `ssh -J warrior node socat STDIO UNIX-CONNECT:...` or an `ssh -L` tunnel (OpenSSH 6.7+ forwards Unix sockets, 7.3+ has ProxyJump) gives millisecond delivery. Authentication for the worker is `claude setup-token` -> `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (one-year, Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise), which `--bare` does not read; and the Agent SDK's license note forbids third parties from offering claude.ai login in their own products, which the design must weigh. The native Claude Code binary is a Bun single executable that has crashed (SIGILL/Bus error) on CentOS 7.9 glibc 2.17, so it must run inside the Singularity image with its own glibc, never on the host.

findings.claim: (1 latency) No official Anthropic benchmark of `claude -p` cold start exists; the only measured process-boot figure found is 679 ms median for `claude -p boot-to-ready` on Claude Code 2.1.251 in an 8 CPU / 8 GB container (range 563-825 ms, 3 runs), with `claude --version` 3 ms and `node -e ''` 14 ms on the same host.
findings.detail: Per-stage numbers from issue: `claude -p boot-to-ready`: 679ms median (563-825ms); `claude update` (up to date): 669ms; `claude --help`: 120ms. Whole warm launch of their agent container estimated 7-8.5 s end-to-end. Version 2.1.251, August 2026.

verdict.corrected_claim: (1 latency) The per-stage numbers are transcribed correctly from couetilc/agentic-coding issue #8 (opened and closed 2026-08-30): `claude -p boot-to-ready` [679 563 825] ms, median 679, 3 runs; `claude --version` [9 4 3 3 3] median 3 ms; `node -e ''` [64 13 14 20 14] median 14 ms; `claude --help` median 120 ms; `claude update` (already current) median 669 ms; conditions "inside an agent container at c09e31d, 8 CPU / 8GB, warm npm cache volume, `claude` 2.1.251". But the claim mislabels and over-generalises it. (a) It is a WARM-launch figure, not a cold start: the issue title is "~7-8.5s warm", the container had a "warm shared npm cache volume — the same conditions any fresh container gets after the first launch", and C8 is "679ms to ready (then first API round-trip)", i.e. the API call is excluded; the body never says what command or stop condition timed "boot-to-ready". (b) It is version-specific to 2.1.251 and stale: the current release is 2.1.283 (npm latest, 26 releases later) and Anthropic's CHANGELOG lists `-p`-specific startup changes in 2.1.277 (headless first turn no longer waits on per-directory CLAUDE.md lookup; background Haiku auto-title request removed from `claude -p`), 2.1.281 (managed-settings fetch "about 80 ms, 17+ seconds when the network is unreachable" moved off startup; git reads, startup telemetry, model-upgrade checks moved off the first frame), and 2.1.283 (`claude -p` "no longer load[s] the interactive UI"; classifier rules and Artifact tool load on first use; "up to 1.5 s" Artifact check removed; preconnected API connection reused), plus 2.1.243 and 2.1.238 before it; 679 ms cannot be carried to 2.1.283 in either direction without re-measuring. (c) "No official Anthropic benchmark" is only narrowly true: Anthropic publishes no absolute end-to-end ms figure, but its CHANGELOG does publish an official relative `-p` startup figure, 2.1.83 "`--bare -p` (SDK pattern) is ~14% faster to the API request", and component figures (80 ms / 17+ s, 1.5 s, "up to 2s" first-turn MCP wait in `--input-format stream-json` sessions before 2.1.274, update check "about 10 seconds after launch" since 2.1.238). (d) It is not the only measured figure: anthropics/claude-code issues report measured `-p`/CLI startup times under fault conditions (#17974 "8+ seconds", #66395 `claude -p` slow/hanging on Windows 2.1.161–2.1.168, #91987 `claude -p` hanging indefinitely at startup on a version-directory lock, SIGKILLed at 480 s, 2.1.259, open 2026-09-04). (e) For the Ashley design the number only matters if a new `claude -p` process is spawned per prompt; the documented persistent pattern (Agent SDK streaming input / `--input-format stream-json`, one long-lived `claude` subprocess per session, `startup()` to pre-warm) pays boot once per Slurm job. The official startup lever `--bare` is unusable with a Pro/Max subscription ("bare mode doesn't use your subscription login", "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", "does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`") and "will become the default for `-p` in a future release". No measurement exists for a native `claude` binary executed from a Singularity image on Panasas/CephFS on the WSU grid; that cold-start figure is unknown.

findings.claim: (1 resume cost) `--resume`/`--continue` re-send the entire conversation on the next request; it is cheap only while the prompt cache is warm. Claude Code's main-conversation cache TTL (including `-p` runs and Agent SDK turns) is one hour on a Claude subscription within plan usage and five minutes on API-key/credit billing; subagents, workflows and teammates get five minutes regardless unless `subagentPromptCacheTtl`/`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL` is set to `1h`.
findings.detail: prompt-caching: 'When you resume a session, Claude Code sends the whole conversation again, and the request reads from the cache whatever part of its prefix is unchanged and still within the cache lifetime.' TTL table: Main conversation (interactive turns, non-interactive -p runs, Agent SDK turns) = One hour on subscription within plan usage, Five minutes on usage credits/API key/cloud. Controls: `promptCacheTtl` / `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL` (5m|1h), `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1`, `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1`, require v2.1.242+. Verify with `claude -p "hello" --output-format json` -> `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` vs `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`. Also: 'the cache is effectively scoped to one machine and directory'.

verdict.corrected_claim: (1 resume cost) `--resume`/`--continue` re-send the whole conversation on the next request, but so does every ordinary turn: Claude Code re-sends the full context (system prompt, project context, every prior message and tool result) on each API request, and the API serves whatever prefix is unchanged and still within the cache TTL from cache. Resume is therefore only "expensive" when the cache has expired, and a long-lived process that idles past the TTL pays exactly the same full uncached re-read on its next prompt as a cold `--resume` does — keeping the process alive does not keep the cache warm; the TTL is a server-side inactivity timer reset by each cache hit, measured from the start of the request that wrote or read the entry. Default TTL per request bucket: Main conversation (interactive turns, non-interactive `-p` runs, Agent SDK turns, plus inline helpers) = one hour on a Claude subscription while within the plan's included usage, five minutes on usage credits (extra usage past the plan limit), an API key, or a cloud provider (Bedrock / Google Cloud Agent Platform / Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS). Everything else (subagents, workflows, in-process teammates, forks, compaction, session titles) = five minutes on every billing type, except a small set of server-controlled helper requests that get one hour on a subscription. Controls, each taking only `5m` or `1h`: `promptCacheTtl` setting / `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL` env var for the main conversation; `subagentPromptCacheTtl` / `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL` for everything else; the docs say all four require Claude Code v2.1.242 or later, while the GitHub CHANGELOG has no 2.1.242 entry and lists the two settings under 2.1.243 (so require >=2.1.243 to be safe; the local 2.1.283 is fine). Additional levers not in the original claim: `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` requests one hour for BOTH buckets (added in 2.1.108, lower precedence than the bucket-specific controls), `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` forces five minutes for both and overrides everything, and a subagent's `experimental.cacheTtl` frontmatter (v2.1.248+) sets its own TTL but a `1h` there is ignored while the subscription is on usage credits. Precedence: FORCE_5M > bucket env var > bucket setting > subagent frontmatter > ENABLE_1H > bucket default. Verify with `claude -p "hello" --output-format json` and read `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` vs `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`. Price: 1-hour cache writes bill at 2x base input (5-minute writes 1.25x; reads 0.1x, 0.025x on Fable 5.1), so 1h is not "cheaper" for short bursts that never idle past five minutes. Scope: "the cache is effectively scoped to one machine and directory" (working directory, platform, shell, OS version and auto-memory paths are in the prefix; worktrees differ; parallel sessions in the same directory share it, sequential ones only if the startup git-status snapshot matches). Caveats for the Ashley design: the 1h TTL is unavailable through the Claude apps gateway and, through an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway, needs the `anthropic-beta` header forwarded unchanged; on Pro/Max an interactive resume of a session idle >~1 hour and >100,000 tokens opens a "Resume from summary" dialog before the first message; and `claude --bare` never reads OAuth credentials (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), so the subscription-billed `-p` path must not use `--bare` — the docs also state `--bare` "will become the default for `-p` in a future release".
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds on every load-bearing point; corrections are refinements (version number source, extra TTL levers, and the fact that re-sending is not specific to resume). critical=true for the design: TTL defaults, subscription-vs-credits drop, per-machine-and-directory scope, and the `--bare`/OAuth exclusion.

Options: "Resume from summary", "Resume full session as-is", "Don't ask me again". Also: "Claude Code leaves sessions created with `claude -p` or the Agent SDK out of the session picker and out of `claude --continue`. You can still resume one by passing its session ID to `claude --resume <session-id>` ... When you run `claude -p --continue`, Claude Code includes `-p`, SDK, and `/loop` sessions." Transcripts: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves storage; `--no-session-persistence` (print mode) / `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` suppress writes.

[H] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless — `claude -p "Now focus on the database queries" --continue`; `session_id=$(claude -p "Start a review" --output-format json | jq -r '.session_id')`; `claude -p "Continue that review" --resume "$session_id"`; "You can run the two commands from different directories ... Before v2.1.223 ... same directory." Bare mode: "Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before running it, because bare mode doesn't use your subscription login" / "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain." / "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." SIGTERM: exit code 143, turn left unfinished; `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1` continues it on resume.

[I] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (raw page) — `--continue`, `-c`: "Load the most recent conversation in the current directory ... Skips sessions created with `claude -p` or the Agent SDK ... `claude -p --continue` includes `-p`, SDK, and `/loop` sessions"; `--resume`, `-r`: "Resume a specific session by ID or name ... In place of an ID, you can pass the absolute path to a session's `.jsonl` transcript file"; `--fork-session`: "When resuming, create a new session ID instead of reusing the original"; `--session-id`: "(must be a valid UUID)"; `--no-session-persistence`: "Print mode only". No `--force-prompt-caching-5m` flag exists.

NOT FOUND / UNKNOWN: no official statement on how cache-read vs cache-write tokens are weighted against a Pro/Max plan's usage allowance; no statement on whether the "Resume from summary" dialog can appear on a `claude -p --resume` path (the doc describes it as an interactive dialog). WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted); all evidence is from directly fetched official pages and the official changelog.

findings.claim: (1 resume cost) On Pro/Max, resuming a session idle >~1 h and >100,000 tokens triggers a 'Resume from summary' dialog because the cache has expired and 'the next request processes the full history once no matter which of the dialog's options you pick'; `-p --continue/--resume` runs report the whole conversation's accumulated `total_cost_usd` including earlier runs.
findings.detail: sessions: 'when you resume a session that has been inactive for more than about an hour and is over 100,000 tokens, Claude Code restores the conversation and then opens a dialog before you send your first message. The session's prompt cache has expired by then'. headless: 'When you continue an earlier conversation with --continue or --resume, the run reports the conversation's whole total, earlier runs' spend included.' Transcripts live at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`; `claude --resume <session-id>` finds the ID in any project on the machine (v2.1.223+); `--resume` also accepts the absolute .jsonl path; sessions from `claude -p` are excluded from the picker and from `claude --continue` but included by `claude -p --continue`.

findings.claim: (2 protocol) The exact stdin envelope the official Python Agent SDK writes for each user turn is `{"type":"user","session_id":"","message":{"role":"user","content":<prompt>},"parent_tool_use_id":null}` serialised with json.dumps and a trailing "\n"; the official docs example omits session_id and shows `content` may be a string or an array of `text`/`image` blocks.
findings.detail: client.py: `user_message = {"type": "user", "session_id": "", "message": {"role": "user", "content": prompt}, "parent_tool_use_id": None}` then `json.dumps(stamp_user_message(...)) + "\n"`. Docs (streaming-vs-single-mode) TypeScript: `yield { type: "user", message: { role: "user", content: "Analyze this codebase for security issues" }, parent_tool_use_id: null }` and image block `{type:"image", source:{type:"base64", media_type:"image/png", data}}`. TS type: `SDKUserMessage = { type: 'user'; message: MessageParam; parent_tool_use_id: string | null; isSynthetic?: boolean; tool_use_result?: unknown; priority?: 'now' | 'next' | 'later'; origin?: SDKMessageOrigin; shouldQuery?: boolean; ... }`.

verdict.corrected_claim: (2 protocol) The Python Agent SDK (0.2.160, main @ 2026-09-27) writes each user turn to the CLI's stdin as one JSON line: json.dumps(stamp_user_message(msg, verbatim_prompts)) + "\n", over a subprocess started with `--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose`. The dict is NOT one fixed envelope: (a) the one-shot `query()` function path (_internal/client.py L184-197) writes `{"type":"user","session_id":"","message":{"role":"user","content":<prompt>},"parent_tool_use_id":null}`; (b) the persistent `ClaudeSDKClient` path (client.py L248-256 in connect(), L289-297 in query()) writes `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":<prompt>},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"default"}` because `query(self, prompt, session_id: str = "default")`; (c) for an AsyncIterable prompt, `ClaudeSDKClient.query()` writes the caller's dict, injecting `msg["session_id"] = session_id` only if the key is absent (L300-306), while `Query.stream_input()` (_internal/query.py L1112-1115) writes the caller's dict untouched; (d) when `ClaudeAgentOptions.verbatim_prompts=True` (SDK >=0.2.158, CLI >=v2.1.248) `stamp_user_message` adds top-level `"client_composed": true` (_internal/query.py L132-143). `session_id` is therefore optional and free-form on the wire (TS d.ts: `session_id?: string`); the minimal accepted envelope, as the official docs example shows, is `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":<string | [text|image blocks]>}}` (TS example adds `parent_tool_use_id: null`; the Python docs example omits both `session_id` and `parent_tool_use_id`). Image blocks: `{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":"image/png","data":<b64>}}`. TS type (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.283 sdk.d.ts L6149-6236): `SDKUserMessage = { type:'user'; message: MessageParam; parent_tool_use_id: string|null; isSynthetic?: boolean; tool_use_result?: unknown; priority?: 'now'|'next'|'later'; origin?: SDKMessageOrigin; shouldQuery?: boolean; timestamp?: string; client_composed?: true; uuid?: UUID; pasted_content?: MessageParam['content'][]; inline_pastes?: string[]; session_id?: string; subagent_type?: string; task_description?: string }`.
verdict.evidence: critical=true (Ashley's laptop->grid prompt relay will write this envelope to a containerised `claude` stdin, so the exact keys matter). (8) CLI reference https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference: `--input-format` "Specify input format for print mode (options: text, stream-json)", example `claude -p --output-format json --input-format stream-json`; `--include-partial-messages` "Requires --print and --output-format stream-json". findings.claim: (2 protocol) The official Python SDK launches the CLI as `claude --output-format stream-json --verbose ... --input-format stream-json` (always streaming; `--input-format stream-json` is unconditional) and does NOT pass `--print`/`-p`; it sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py`, requires Claude Code >= 2.0.0, limits one NDJSON line to 1 MB by default, and closes stdin to end the run.

verdict.corrected_claim: (2 protocol) The official Python SDK (claude-agent-sdk 0.2.160, HEAD of main on 2026-09-27) launches the CLI as `claude --output-format stream-json --verbose ... --input-format stream-json` — always streaming, `--input-format stream-json` unconditional — and does NOT pass `--print`/`-p`; the CLI (2.1.283) accepts this because it selects print mode itself when stdin is not a TTY. It sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py` (overridable via `options.env`), `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION` (not overridable), `CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE=1` (unless caller set it), removes `CLAUDECODE`, and limits one NDJSON line to 1 MB by default (`max_buffer_size` option). It does NOT enforce Claude Code >= 2.0.0: `_check_claude_version()` runs `claude -v` with a 2 s timeout and only `logger.warning`s below `MINIMUM_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION = "2.0.0"` (and below 2.1.248 when `verbatim_prompts` is on), swallows all exceptions, and is skipped when `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK` is set. It ends the run by closing stdin (`end_input()` / `close()`), but since 0.2.160 it first waits for the CLI's `session_state_changed` `idle` frame on runs that serve control requests (ceiling `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`, default 10 min; older CLIs fall back to close-at-first-result); `close()` then waits for exit after stdin EOF before terminating. Resume/session are passed as `--resume=<v>`, `--session-id=<v>` (also `--resume-session-at=`, `--resume-drops-turn=`). The bundled binary `claude_agent_sdk/_bundled/claude` (`claude.exe` on Windows) is looked up first; the POSIX not-found error is 'Claude Code not found. Install with:\n  npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ...' while Windows gets a different message recommending `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` and refusing npm's `claude.cmd` shim.

"claude_code_version":"2.1.283","apiKeySource":"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY","permissionMode":"default","model":"claude-opus-5-5",...}` then `{"type":"system","subtype":"api_retry","attempt":1,"max_retries":10,"retry_delay_ms":615,"error_status":401,"error":"authentication_failed",...}` repeated until the 45 s timeout (note for design: a 401 is retried up to 10 times, it does not fail fast). If pip installs the Python SDK's source distribution instead of a platform wheel ... no binary is bundled." The `manylinux_2_17` tag matches the grid's glibc 2.17 nominally, but whether the Bun-compiled native `claude` actually runs on CentOS 7.9/glibc 2.17 was NOT tested here. Please use the API key authentication methods described in this document instead." — this bears directly on driving the CLI via the SDK with a student's Claude Pro/Max subscription. findings.claim: (2 protocol) Official docs define `--input-format` and `--output-format` as print-mode flags, and a third-party report on Claude Code 2.1.261 says `--input-format stream-json` is rejected unless `--print` is present, while `--print` with a PTY stdin fails with 'Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument'; so a daemon should pass `-p` and give the process a pipe, not a pseudo-terminal, as stdin.
findings.detail: cli-reference: `--input-format` 'Specify input format for print mode (options: text, stream-json)'; `--output-format` 'Specify output format for print mode (options: text, json, stream-json)'; `--include-partial-messages` 'Requires --print and --output-format stream-json'. OpenCompany #134 (2026-09-06, CLI 2.1.261, Windows 11): newer CLI 'reject[s] this flag unless --print is also included'; with --print on PTY stdin: 'Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument'. Working third-party invocations: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose` (cockpit, verified on 2.1.281) and `tail -f input.jsonl | claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --replay-user-messages` (ludics-lite, 2.1.258).

findings.claim: (2 protocol) End of a turn is signalled by a line `{"type":"result", "subtype": "success" | "error_during_execution" | "error_max_turns" | "error_max_budget_usd" | "error_max_structured_output_retries", ...}` carrying `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `is_error`, `num_turns`, `result`, `stop_reason`, `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, `session_id`; the SDK's own comment states 'A result ends a turn, not necessarily the run'.
findings.detail: query.py lines 455-470: `if msg_type == "result": ... self._result_received = True; self._turn_in_progress = False  # A result ends a turn, not necessarily the run: a background agent that finished just before it still wakes the session for another turn ... A CLI that reports session state stays "running" while such a turn is owed, so wait for "idle"`. sdk.d.ts: `SDKResultMessage = SDKResultSuccess | SDKResultError`; SDKResultError subtypes 'error_during_execution' | 'error_max_turns' | 'error_max_budget_usd' | 'error_max_structured_output_retries', fields duration_ms, duration_api_ms, is_error, num_turns, stop_reason, total_cost_usd, usage, modelUsage, permission_denials, queued_turn_count?, errors: string[], startup_failure_reason?. Python SDK 0.2.160 changelog: listens for `session_state_changed` and keeps stdin open until CLI reports `idle`, ceiling `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default 10 min).

verdict.corrected_claim: (2 protocol) Each turn ends with one line `{"type":"result", "subtype": "success" | "error_during_execution" | "error_max_turns" | "error_max_budget_usd" | "error_max_structured_output_retries", ...}`. Both variants carry `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms` (required, number), `is_error` (boolean), `num_turns`, `stop_reason` (string|null), `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `modelUsage`, `permission_denials`, `queued_turn_count?`, `uuid`, `session_id`. Idle waiting starts over each time Claude takes a turn to handle a background result. Default: `600000`, or 10 minutes. ... Set to `0` to wait indefinitely. This cap is separate from the five-second grace period that applies to plain background shells. No evidence found contradicting any part of the claim; refinements above are additions, not corrections of fact. Note: the small-model summary of one WebFetch (unpkg sdk.d.ts) misreported `subtype: 'error'` and `duration_api_ms?` — discarded in favor of the raw file at lines 5610-5700.

findings.claim: (2 protocol) Multiple turns to one process are officially supported: the Python `ClaudeSDKClient` calls `query()` repeatedly on one connection ('Reuses same session', 'Multiple exchanges in same context'), TypeScript exposes `Query.streamInput(stream: AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>)`, and the CLI reference states that with `--input-format stream-json` a queued message 'stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit'.
findings.detail: Python docs example: `async with ClaudeSDKClient() as client: await client.query("What's the capital of France?"); async for message in client.receive_response(): ...; await client.query("What's the population of that city?"); ...` (`receive_response()` ends at the first result message). Table: query() 'Creates a new session by default' vs ClaudeSDKClient 'Reuses same session', interrupts supported only by ClaudeSDKClient. cli-reference `--max-turns`: 'With --input-format stream-json, a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit'. sdk.d.ts line 3205: `streamInput(stream: AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>): Promise<void>;`.
