VERDICT: claim holds on all three legs; verified 2026-09-27 against official docs and the shipped packages. critical=true for the design (persistent Claude Code process on the grid accepting prompts over time).

[1] PYTHON (critical=true) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python, fetched. Package is `claude-agent-sdk` (`pip install claude-agent-sdk`; import `from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeSDKClient`), PyPI latest 0.2.160 (https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json). Comparison table verbatim: Session: query() "Creates a new session by default" vs ClaudeSDKClient "Reuses same session"; Conversation: "Single exchange" vs "Multiple exchanges in same context"; Interrupts: query() "❌ Not supported" vs ClaudeSDKClient "✅ Supported"; Continue Chat: "Manual via `continue_conversation` or `resume`" vs "✅ Automatic"; Use Case: "One-off tasks" vs "Continuous conversations". The "Example - Continuing a conversation" code is exactly as claimed: one `async with ClaudeSDKClient() as client:` block, `await client.query("What's the capital of France?")`, `async for message in client.receive_response()`, then `await client.query("What's the population of that city?")`, then a third `query("What are some famous landmarks there?")`, comment "the session retains the previous context". Methods table: `receive_response()` = "Receive messages until and including a ResultMessage". Source confirms (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/client.py): `async def query(self, prompt: str | AsyncIterable[dict[str, Any]], session_id: str = "default") -> None` docstring "Send a new request in streaming mode."; it writes a `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":...},"parent_tool_use_id":None,"session_id":...}` JSON line to the CLI transport per call; `receive_response()` docstring: "Terminates immediately after yielding a ResultMessage ... If no ResultMessage is received, the iterator continues indefinitely"; `interrupt()` docstring: "Send interrupt signal (only works with streaming mode)." Under the hood ClaudeSDKClient IS the CLI with `--input-format stream-json`, so leg [3] is the same mechanism.

[2] TYPESCRIPT (critical=true) — `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.283 (https://unpkg.com/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/package.json), file https://unpkg.com/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts downloaded: line 2843 `export declare interface Query extends AsyncGenerator<SDKMessage, void> {`; line 3205 exactly `streamInput(stream: AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>): Promise<void>;` (line number in the claim is correct for 0.3.283); line 2857 `interrupt(): Promise<SDKControlInterruptResponse | undefined>;`; line 2864 `setPermissionMode(mode: PermissionMode): Promise<void>;`; line 3238 `prompt: string | AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>;`. NUANCE: the .d.ts JSDoc above streamInput reads "Stream input messages to the query. Used internally for multi-turn conversations." — but the official TS reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript, section "`Query` object") lists it in the public interface and in the Methods table as "`streamInput(stream)` | Stream input messages to the query for multi-turn conversations", and the `clientComposed` option JSDoc (sdk.d.ts ~line 1872) names "`Query.streamInput()`" as a caller-facing path ("Covers string prompts, streamed messages and `Query.streamInput()`"). So it is documented-public, not merely leaked-internal. Same docs table: `interrupt()` "Only available in streaming input mode"; `setPermissionMode()` / `setModel()` "(only available in streaming input mode)". DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: start the TS query with an `AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>` prompt (streaming input mode), not a string, or mid-session control is unavailable. The officially recommended multi-turn pattern in TS is the async-generator prompt: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode ("Streaming input mode is the **preferred** way to use the Claude Agent SDK ... a long lived process that takes in user input, handles interruptions ... Queued messages: send multiple messages that process sequentially, with ability to interrupt ... Context persistence: maintain conversation context across multiple turns naturally"; Single Message Input "does **not** support: ... Dynamic message queueing, Real-time interruption, Natural multi-turn conversations"). That page also states verbatim: "The Python version's `receive_response()` loop ends at the first result message ... to read both responses, use one `query()` and `receive_response()` pair per message" — confirming the claim's parenthetical. Warning on that page: TS generator exceptions surface as `Claude Code process aborted by user`; Python generator exceptions are logged at debug level and "the session stalls without raising".

[3] CLI (critical=true) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference, fetched; `--max-turns` row verbatim: "Limit the number of agentic turns (print mode only). Exits with an error when the limit is reached. No limit by default. With `--input-format stream-json`, a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit". `--input-format`: "Specify input format for print mode (options: `text`, `stream-json`)". `--replay-user-messages`: "Re-emit user messages from stdin back on stdout for acknowledgment. Requires `--input-format stream-json` and `--output-format stream-json`" (example `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --replay-user-messages`) — useful as an ack in a laptop-to-grid relay. Related from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless (fetched): SIGTERM on `claude -p` exits code 143 and leaves the turn unfinished — "send SIGINT, or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()`, before you stop the process"; `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1` resumes the interrupted turn; piped stdin capped at 10MB; `--bare` "doesn't use your subscription login" and "never reads OAuth credentials" (do NOT use `--bare` for the Pro/Max-subscription design); background bash tasks are terminated ~5 s after the final result when stdin closes (keep stdin open for persistence); `system/init` carries a `capabilities` array (`interrupt_receipt_v1`, `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1`, requires v2.1.205+) for feature detection.

NOT FOUND / NOT CLAIMED: no official statement of a maximum session lifetime for one streaming process; no deprecation notice for ClaudeSDKClient. Local host versions in the task (Claude Code extension 2.1.283) match the SDK 0.3.283 bundle line.

findings.claim: (2 protocol) Empirically (Claude Code 2.1.281, 2026-09-24) a stream-json process stays alive after a `result` while stdin is open; if a background task is pending it later emits `background_tasks_changed`, `task_updated`, `task_notification` and then a NEW `system/init` + `assistant` + `result` on its own; a worker design that keeps stdin open and appends NDJSON lines ('unstick appends a message instead of kill-and-resume') is in production use on 2.1.258.
findings.detail: cockpit PR #608: 'after result, if a background task is still pending, the process stays alive; when it completes the CLI emits background_tasks_changed, task_updated, task_notification, then on its own a NEW system/init + assistant + result' (haiku model, backgrounded `sleep 20`, ~19 s). ludics-lite #259 (2026-09-18): `tail -f input.jsonl | claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --replay-user-messages`; append with `printf '%s\n' "$json" >> input.jsonl` over ssh; 'each turn ends with a result event in the JSONL while the process lives'; `--replay-user-messages` echoes stdin into output so delivery is verifiable; advantages: 'no kill, no resume, no new process', idle distinguishable from dead, context and cache persist.

verdict.corrected_claim: (2 protocol) With `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`, the process stays alive after a `result` for as long as stdin is open (official docs: background shells are killed ~5 s after "Claude has returned its final result and stdin has closed"; `--max-turns` doc: a queued stream-json message "starts a new turn with its own limit"). If a background task (Bash run_in_background, subagent, monitor, workflow) is pending at `result`, the CLI later emits `system` events with subtypes `background_tasks_changed`, `task_updated`, `task_notification`, then on its own starts a fresh turn: a NEW `system/init` + `assistant` + `result`, the second `result` carrying `"origin": {"kind": "task-notification"}` (cockpit PR #608, tested on Claude Code 2.1.281, haiku, backgrounded `sleep 20`, ~19 s, merged 2026-09-24; independently shown in anthropics/claude-code#86103 on 2.1.226/2.1.228). `--replay-user-messages` ("Re-emit user messages from stdin back on stdout for acknowledgment (only works with --input-format=stream-json and --output-format=stream-json)") exists in the CLI (verified on 2.1.278 `--help`) but is absent from the CLI reference page. The `tail -f input.jsonl | claude -p ... --replay-user-messages` worker with `printf '%s\n' "$json" >> input.jsonl` over ssh was a PROPOSAL in ludics-lite issue #259 (2026-09-18, citing 2.1.258); it was implemented and merged on 2026-09-26 in ludics-lite PR #416 (`issue-wave/scripts/fleet-worker.sh`), verified against Claude Code 2.1.282, not 2.1.258, and is a merged shell script in a small skills repo rather than "production use". Unverified: whether the 10-minute idle ceiling (`CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`) that ends a `-p` wait on stuck subagents/workflows also applies while stdin is held open.

findings.claim: (2 protocol) The SDK<->CLI control channel is in-band NDJSON: the client writes `{"type":"control_request","request_id":"req_<n>_<hex>","request":{"subtype":...}}` with subtypes `initialize`, `interrupt`, `set_permission_mode`, `set_model`, `mcp_status`, `get_context_usage`, `rewind_files`; the CLI answers `{"type":"control_response","response":{"subtype":"success"|"error","request_id":...}}`; the CLI can send its own `control_request` (permission prompts, hooks) and `control_cancel_request`.
findings.detail: query.py: `request_id = f"req_{self._request_counter}_{os.urandom(4).hex()}"`; `control_request = {"type": "control_request", "request_id": request_id, "request": request}`; initialize request `{"subtype": "initialize", "hooks": ..., "agents": ..., "excludeDynamicSections": ..., "systemPromptSnapshot": ..., "skills": ..., "forwardSubagentText": True}`; responses `{"type": "control_response", "response": {"subtype": "success", "request_id": ...}}` / `"subtype": "error"`; `interrupt()` -> `{"subtype": "interrupt"}`. system/init `capabilities` (v2.1.205+) feature-detects e.g. `interrupt_receipt_v1`, `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1`, `queued_notifications`, `mcp_read_resource_v1`.

findings.claim: (2 protocol) Process lifecycle rules for a headless worker: after the final result and stdin close, background Bash tasks are killed ~5 s later; background subagents/workflows keep `claude -p` open up to `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default 600000); SIGTERM exits 143 leaving the turn unfinished (send SIGINT or SDK `interrupt()` first); output drain at exit is capped at 30 s (was 2 s before v2.1.214); piped stdin (text mode) is capped at 10 MB.
findings.detail: headless: 'that shell is terminated about five seconds after Claude has returned its final result and stdin has closed'; 'By default the wait ends after 10 minutes of continuous idle waiting ... set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS, or set it to 0 to wait without one'; 'If you stop a claude -p run with SIGTERM ... Claude Code exits with code 143 ... To end the turn instead, send SIGINT, or call the Agent SDK's interrupt()'; 'CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1' to continue an interrupted turn on resume; 'Piped stdin is capped at 10MB'. CHANGELOG: 2.1.153 'Fixed a hang where the CLI could fail to exit when stdin was closed without EOF in stream-json mode'; 2.1.257 'non-JSONL data piped into claude -p --input-format stream-json ... now fails fast with a clear error'; 2.1.208 blank CRLF lines no longer kill the session; 2.1.94 UTF-8 split fix.

verdict.corrected_claim: (2 protocol) Process lifecycle rules for a headless `claude -p` worker, per code.claude.com/docs/en/headless as of 2026-09-27 (doc tracks CLI 2.1.283): (a) A background Bash task started during the run "is terminated about five seconds after Claude has returned its final result and stdin has closed" (behaviour introduced in 2.1.163; before that `claude -p` could hang forever on a never-exiting backgrounded command). (b) A background subagent or workflow instead keeps `claude -p` open until it completes; the wait is an IDLE ceiling that "starts over each time Claude takes a turn to handle a background result", default `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=600000` (10 min), `0` = wait indefinitely, requires Claude Code v2.1.182 or later, and is "separate from the five-second grace period that applies to plain background shells". A Monitor watch also holds the process open until it fires/times out (default watch timeout 5 min) or the 10-min ceiling ends the wait (2.1.257+; before that `-p` exited ~5 s after the result with a Monitor still armed). (c) SIGTERM -> exit code 143, turn left unfinished with no result recorded (2.1.236 stopped writing interrupted-turn/synthetic-denial records); the Bash command's process tree is killed (fixed in 2.1.212), `SessionEnd` hooks run, nothing else starts. To end the turn cleanly send SIGINT or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()` first (Python: `async def interrupt(self) -> None`, "only works in streaming mode"). `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1` continues the interrupted turn on resume (`0` honoured only from 2.1.221; `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS` bounds it; default continuation prompt "Continue from where you left off."). (d) Exit output drain for slow stream-json consumers scales with queued bytes, capped at 30 s; before v2.1.214 it was a flat ~2 s cap. (e) "Piped stdin is capped at 10MB" (exits non-zero with a clear error; 2.1.128 fixed the >10 MB crash loop). The doc does NOT qualify this as text-mode only; the stream-json input path has its own documented limit: any single line over 256M characters (268,435,456) with no newline -> `Error: stream-json input carried over 256M characters with no newline...`, exit 1, v2.1.257+. Whether the 10 MB cap also applies to cumulative stream-json input is not stated anywhere fetched. (f) Cited CHANGELOG entries 2.1.153 (stdin closed without EOF hang), 2.1.257 (non-JSONL fails fast), 2.1.208 (blank CRLF lines), 2.1.94 (UTF-8 split) are verbatim-confirmed. Design note: rules (a) and (b) trigger only after the final result AND stdin close, so a persistent worker that holds stdin open in `--input-format stream-json` is not subject to them; `--bg` cannot be combined with `-p` ("--bg and --print conflict").
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds on every point; refinements below are version/precision additions, not contradictions. Sources actually fetched 2026-09-27: [H] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless (WebFetch + curl of headless.md, 37,679 B); [E] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (env-vars.md, 507,134 B); [R] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors (errors.md, 528,617 B); [C] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md (821,156 B, 7,640 lines, top version 2.1.283, sha256 ae8f617c...; re-downloaded, identical); [P] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python (python.md); [CLI] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (cli-reference.md).

1. ~5 s grace for background Bash [critical=true]. [H] line 67 verbatim: "If Claude starts a background Bash task during a `claude -p` run, for example a dev server or a watch build, that shell is terminated about five seconds after Claude has returned its final result and stdin has closed. The grace period lets a task that finishes right after the result still deliver its output." [C] 2.1.163: "Fixed `claude -p` hanging forever after its final result when a backgrounded command never exits — background shells are now stopped ~5s after the result once stdin closes". [E] row: "This cap is separate from the five-second grace period that applies to plain background shells."

2. Background subagents/workflows + ceiling [critical=true]. [H] lines 69-71: "If Claude starts a background subagent or workflow, `claude -p` instead stays open until that work completes, because its result is part of the final output. By default the wait ends after 10 minutes of continuous idle waiting, so a stuck subagent or workflow can't hold the process open indefinitely. At that point Claude Code stops whatever is still running and drops its partial result. To change the limit, set `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`, or set it to `0` to wait without one." [E] verbatim row: "`CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` | Ceiling in milliseconds on idle waiting for background subagents and workflows after the final turn in non-interactive mode with the `-p` flag. Idle waiting starts over each time Claude takes a turn to handle a background result. Default: `600000`, or 10 minutes. When idle waiting reaches the ceiling, Claude Code stops waiting for the remaining background tasks and exits. Set to `0` to wait indefinitely. This cap is separate from the five-second grace period that applies to plain background shells. Requires Claude Code v2.1.182 or later". REFINEMENT: it is an idle ceiling that resets per background-result turn, not a total wall cap; requires >=2.1.182. [H] also: "If Claude starts a Monitor watch during a `claude -p` run, Claude Code waits for the watch until it times out or the ten-minute cap ends the wait, whichever comes first ... By default, a watch times out five minutes after Claude starts it." [C] 2.1.257: "Fixed `claude -p` exiting about 5 seconds after its final result while a Monitor the model armed was still running; it now waits for the watch to fire or time out". [C] 2.1.161: "Fixed background subagent output corrupting `claude -p` stdout when using `--output-format text` or `json`". No CHANGELOG entry names CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS (grep 'PRINT_BG_WAIT' = 0 hits); the v2.1.182 requirement comes from [E] only.

3. SIGTERM / 143 / SIGINT / interrupt() [critical=true]. [H] line 77: "If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example with `kill` or from a process supervisor, Claude Code exits with code 143. Claude Code leaves the turn that was in progress unfinished and records no result for it. To end the turn instead, send SIGINT, or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()`, before you stop the process." Then: "On SIGTERM, Claude Code terminates the process tree of any Bash command that is still running. Claude Code then runs `SessionEnd` hooks and exits. While exiting, Claude Code starts no new tool call, sends no new model request, and runs no hook other than `SessionEnd`." Permission-prompt case: "if you send SIGTERM to the process, Claude Code leaves the prompt unanswered. If your program closes the session through the Agent SDK, the SDK ends Claude Code's input before sending any signal, and Claude Code cancels the prompt as soon as the input ends." [C] 2.1.212: "Fixed SIGTERM during a running Bash tool orphaning the command's process tree in print/SDK mode; the CLI now aborts the turn, kills the tree, and exits 143". [C] 2.1.236: "SIGTERM in print/SDK mode no longer records an interrupted turn or synthetic tool denials before exiting; running commands are still terminated and the process still exits with code 143". [C] 2.1.160: "Improved background-session teardown (`claude rm`/`stop`, idle reap) to send SIGTERM to running shell subprocesses before SIGKILL, so cleanup handlers run". [P] line 443 `async def interrupt(self) -> None`; table: "`interrupt()` | Send interrupt signal (only works in streaming mode)"; "`interrupt()` sends a stop signal but does not clear the message buffer. Messages already produced by the interrupted task, including its `ResultMessage`, remain in the stream. You must drain them with `receive_response()`". Errors page [R] does not list 143 (only 137 for installer kill).

4. CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN [critical=false]. [H] line 84: "When you resume the session, Claude Code leaves the interrupted turn as it is, and your next prompt drives the conversation. To have Claude Code continue the interrupted turn on resume instead, set `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=1`." [E]: "Set to `1` to automatically resume if the previous session ended mid-turn. Used in SDK mode ... To turn this off, unset the variable or set it to `0`. Before v2.1.221, Claude Code ignored `0` and other falsy values"; `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN_MAX_AGE_MS` ("Unset or `0` means no bound, except that a turn whose last request failed with an API error resumes only while that error is less than six hours old"); `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_PROMPT` "Defaults to `Continue from where you left off.`". [C] 2.1.221, 2.1.269, 2.1.274 entries confirm.

5. Exit drain 30 s / 2.1.214 [critical=true]. [H] line 179: "If your consumer reads the stream slowly, Claude Code waits for the queued output to drain before exiting, scaling the wait with how much is still queued, capped at 30 seconds. Before v2.1.214 the exit wait was capped at about two seconds, which could cut off the end of a large response." [C] 2.1.214: "Fixed stream-json output truncation at exit for slow-reading SDK/pipeline consumers; the exit drain now scales with queued bytes instead of a flat 2s cap". (Note: `--drain-wait-sec` in [C] 2.1.275 is a `claude self-hosted-runner` flag, unrelated to `-p`.)

6. Piped stdin 10 MB [critical=true, one imprecision]. [H] line 107 verbatim: "Piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status. To work with larger inputs, write the content to a file and reference the file path in your prompt instead of piping it." The doc does NOT say "text mode"; the claim's qualifier is an inference. [C] 2.1.128: "Fixed crash loop when piping very large input (>10 MB) to `claude -p` via stdin". Separate stream-json limit [R] lines 3026-3029: "Your program sent more than 268,435,456 characters on stdin without a newline to a `claude -p --input-format stream-json` run, so Claude Code prints this error to stderr and exits with code 1 ... Before v2.1.257, Claude Code buffered such input without limit"; exact string: "Error: stream-json input carried over 256M characters with no newline. Each stream-json message must be a single newline-terminated JSON line: either the producer is not newline-terminating its messages, or one message exceeded this budget." [CLI], agent-sdk/overview, agent-sdk/streaming-vs-single-mode, agent-sdk/typescript: zero hits for a 10 MB stdin cap. UNKNOWN: whether the 10 MB cap applies to cumulative stream-json input over a long-lived session; no fetched source says either way. The exact error string for the 10 MB cap is not given on [H] or [R].

7. Cited CHANGELOG entries, verbatim-confirmed [C]: 2.1.153 "Fixed a hang where the CLI could fail to exit when stdin was closed without EOF in stream-json mode, leaving a stale session marker behind"; 2.1.257 "Fixed unbounded memory growth when non-JSONL data is piped into `claude -p --input-format stream-json`; it now fails fast with a clear error"; 2.1.208 "Fixed stream-json input killing the session on blank CRLF or whitespace-only lines from Windows-style SDK hosts"; 2.1.94 "Fixed CJK and other multibyte text being corrupted with U+FFFD in stream-json input/output when chunk boundaries split a UTF-8 sequence".

8. Adjacent facts for the design [critical=true]: [H] line 110: "If Claude Code can't read stdin ... Claude Code prints a warning to stderr and continues with the prompt from the command line. Before v2.1.211, an unreadable stdin on Windows crashed the session or made it exit silently with no output." [H]: "Claude Code rejects `--bg`" with `-p`; [R] line 2596: "--bg and --print conflict: --print never starts the interactive session that `claude agents` attaches to". [R]: `Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print`; `Error: Input contained only whitespace...`. [CLI] `--input-format` options: `text`, `stream-json`; `--max-turns` with stream-json: "a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit". Implication: the 5 s and 10 min rules are keyed on "final result AND stdin closed"; a persistent worker holding stdin open in stream-json mode never reaches that state, so those rules are not the mechanism that would end it. Minimum versions our design leans on: 2.1.163 (5 s grace), 2.1.182 (ceiling var), 2.1.212 (SIGTERM tree kill), 2.1.214 (30 s drain), 2.1.257 (non-JSONL fail-fast, Monitor hold); local extension is 2.1.283 so all satisfied if the grid-side CLI matches.

findings.claim: (2 protocol) Other stream-json flags: `--verbose` is required for token-level streaming ('With --output-format stream-json, also includes partial streaming events'), `--include-partial-messages` emits `stream_event` deltas, `--session-id` must be a valid UUID (v2.1.206+), `--fork-session` branches on resume, `--no-session-persistence` disables transcript writes, `--forward-subagent-text` adds subagent text with `parent_tool_use_id`, and `--replay-user-messages` (v2.1.209+) echoes user messages to stdout.
findings.detail: cli-reference verbatim: `--replay-user-messages` 'Replay user messages from a resumed session without re-running the agent. Print mode only. Requires Claude Code v2.1.209 or later'; CHANGELOG 1.0.86: 'SDK: Added --replay-user-messages to replay user messages back to stdout' (descriptions disagree on scope). `--session-id` 'Set a session ID instead of generating one. Must be a valid UUID. Requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later'. `--verbose` 'Print verbose output, including token counts, model information, and hook lifecycle events. With --output-format stream-json, also includes partial streaming events'. jq filter for text: `select(.type == "stream_event" and .event.delta.type? == "text_delta") | .event.delta.text`. `system/api_retry` events carry attempt, max_retries, retry_delay_ms, error_status, error category.

verdict.corrected_claim: (2 auth, critical) A headless worker can use a student's Claude Pro/Max subscription via `claude setup-token`, which opens the same browser flow as `/login`, prints a one-year OAuth token to the terminal without saving it, and is meant to be set as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; it "requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan", "can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors" (locally configured MCP servers still work), and is not read in `--bare` mode (`--bare` = `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`; bare mode "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", so it ignores both `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `.credentials.json`; `--bare` is not yet the default for `-p` in v2.1.283 but "will become the default for `-p` in a future release"). On Linux, `/login` credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`, relocated under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when that variable is set. Precedence: 1 cloud provider vars, 2 `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, 3 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` ("In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present"), 4 `apiKeyHelper`, 5 `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, 6 Anthropic profile/WIF, 7 subscription OAuth from `/login`. The 3-day expiry warning applies to the `/login` credential only (v2.1.217+; 5 days on v2.1.203–2.1.216); an expired `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` instead surfaces as `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` or `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...` with no advance warning, and must be replaced by generating a new token and restarting.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim holds; every quoted string in the claim appears verbatim in the official docs (fetched 2026-09-27; docs describe Claude Code through v2.1.283, matching the installed extension).

CONFIRMED VERBATIM from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication:
- "generate a one-year OAuth token with `claude setup-token`" ... "The command opens the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, and the token prints to the terminal after you approve access in the browser. It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable wherever you want to authenticate"
- "This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work."
- "Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. If your script passes `--bare`, authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead."
- Storage: "On Linux, credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`." macOS: Keychain, falling back to the same file "when it's locked in an SSH session". Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`. "If you've set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, Claude Code keeps the `.credentials.json` file under that directory instead".
- Precedence list 1–7 exactly as the claim states, including item 3's "In non-interactive mode (`-p`), the key is always used when present." and item 5 "`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. A long-lived OAuth token generated by `claude setup-token`. Use this for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login isn't available."
- SSH/container: "If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers."
- Expiry: "When the login you created with `/login` is within three days of expiring, Claude Code shows a warning at startup: `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. Before v2.1.217, the warning appeared five days out." and "A background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again."
- Extra: "`claude setup-token` and `/install-github-app`: enforce only `forceLoginMethod`, so they can mint a token in a different organization" (irrelevant for personal Pro/Max).

CORROBORATION from other official pages:
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference: "`claude setup-token` | Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription." and "`--bare` | Minimal mode ... Sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`".
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless: "In bare mode, Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain." and NOTE: "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release." Also: "Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before running it, because bare mode doesn't use your subscription login".
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars (env-vars.md): `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` = "OAuth access token for claude.ai authentication. Alternative to `/login` for SDK and automated environments. Takes precedence over keychain-stored credentials. Generate one with `claude setup-token`. Unless you run `/login`, Claude Code uses the token you set for the whole session. To replace an expired token, generate a new one and restart". `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` = "Set to `1` ... OAuth tokens and keychain credentials are not read, so Anthropic authentication must come from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` in `--settings`. Equivalent to passing `--bare`". `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` = "Override the configuration directory (default: `~/.claude`) ... Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings".
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control: error section "Remote Control requires a full-scope login token": "You're authenticated with a long-lived token from `claude setup-token` or the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. These tokens can only make model requests, so they can't establish Remote Control sessions. Run `claude auth login` to authenticate with a full-scope session token instead." Also "API keys are not supported" for Remote Control.
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors (errors.md): "Sessions authenticated with an API key, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or a third-party provider don't use the saved login and never see this message [`Login expired · Please run /login`]"; expired setup-token shows `OAuth token revoked · Please run /login` / `Please run /login · API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired ...`; "Generate a fresh token with `claude setup-token` and restart with it ... Before v2.1.225, Claude Code could replace the variable's value mid-session with the short-lived access token from a stored login, and the session failed with 401 errors again once that token expired." Background-worker guidance: "Confirm `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or your cloud provider credentials are set in the environment that launches the worker, not only in your interactive shell".
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install: "### OAuth login fails in WSL2, SSH, or containers ... Paste that code into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt to complete login."; macOS locked-Keychain fallback to "the plaintext `~/.claude/.credentials.json` file".
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md (top = 2.1.283): 2.1.81 "Added `--bare` flag for scripted `-p` calls ... requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` via `--settings` (OAuth and keychain auth disabled)"; entry "Fixed a transient 401 replacing a long-lived `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` with a stored login's short-lived token, breaking headless sessions until restart" (docs date it v2.1.225); 2.1.86 notes the /login OAuth access token "refreshes (8 hours after login)". No changelog entry through 2.1.283 makes `--bare` the default for `-p`.

DESIGN-CRITICAL NUANCES (critical=true):
1. The persistent grid worker must NOT pass `--bare` and must not set `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`, or subscription auth (both the token and `.credentials.json`) is silently ignored. Because `--bare` "will become the default for `-p` in a future release", pin the Claude Code version in the Singularity image and re-test auth on every bump; when that flips, subscription-backed `-p` may need an explicit opt-out flag that does not exist yet in the docs.
2. Two viable subscription routes: (a) `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token` (documented one-year lifetime; must be present in the environment that launches the Slurm job / container, not just the login shell; no advance expiry warning; replace by regenerating and restarting); (b) copying/relocating `.credentials.json` via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (gets the 3-day warning and auto-refresh, but the refresh-token lifetime is NOT documented anywhere fetched; access token refreshes ~8 h). For a 30-day QoS job, (a) has the documented lifetime.
3. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (precedence 5) beats `.credentials.json` (7) but loses to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (3) and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (2); in `-p` an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment is "always used when present" with no prompt, so scrub those from the job environment.
4. Remote Control and claude.ai connectors are unavailable on the setup-token path; the design's SSH/shared-filesystem prompt relay is therefore the right transport.

LIMITS OF THIS CHECK: WebSearch budget was exhausted before this task, so no third-party corroboration was gathered; all evidence is Anthropic's own docs and changelog. The one-year lifetime is asserted by the docs and was not independently tested.

verdict.corrected_claim: Agent Teams (experimental, disabled by default, enabled by CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in the environment or settings.json "env") cannot spawn teammates in a `claude -p` / `--print` or Agent SDK session: "Spawning teammates also requires an interactive session. That constraint is on -p/SDK specifically, NOT on "headless" in the sense of no human at the keyboard: an interactive `claude` running under tmux on the compute node (the pattern the Remote Control docs themselves recommend for a remote machine after SSH disconnect) is an interactive session, and the default in-process display mode "Works in any terminal, no extra setup required", so teams ARE usable there. Teams are session-scoped and stored on the lead's local filesystem (mailbox `~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/{agent-name}.json`, team config `~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json`, task list `~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/`, team-name = `session-` + first 8 chars of session ID); "single-machine" is a sound inference from that but is not stated verbatim in the docs. Task claiming "uses file locking to prevent race conditions", but the shared task list exists only for agents that have the Task tools (TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate/TaskList), which are on by default only for Claude 3.x, Opus 4-4.7, Sonnet 4-4.6, Haiku 4.5; on newer models set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1, otherwise teammates coordinate by messages only. Limitations verbatim: "One team per session", "No nested teams", "Lead is fixed", "Split panes require tmux or iTerm2 ... Split-pane mode isn't supported in VS Code's integrated terminal, Windows Terminal, or Ghostty." In-process teammate cache TTL is 5 min by default "including on a Claude subscription"; `subagentPromptCacheTtl` ("5m"|"1h", requires v2.1.242+) raises it to 1h. Hooks TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted exist (exit code 2 = keep working / roll back creation / block completion). The former TeamCreate/TeamDelete tools were removed in v2.1.178; every session now has one implicit team.

VERDICT: every verbatim quote in the claim is present, word-for-word, on the live page today (2026-09-27; page references v2.1.281 behaviour and the changelog tops out at 2.1.283, matching the user's extension). Two framing statements are corrected, one of them design-critical.

CONFIRMED VERBATIM (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams, fetched 2026-09-27):
- Warning banner: "Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default. Enable them by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` in your settings.json or environment. Without that variable, no team is set up at session start, no team directories are written, and Claude does not spawn or propose teammates."
- "Spawning teammates also requires an interactive session. In non-interactive mode with the `-p` flag, including Agent SDK sessions, Claude doesn't spawn teammates, and a subagent that Claude names runs as an ordinary subagent even with agent teams enabled." [critical=true]
- "Each agent's mailbox is a JSON file at `~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/{agent-name}.json`." Also: "Claude Code reports a message as sent only when the write to the recipient's mailbox file succeeds"; "Before v2.1.207, a single malformed mailbox entry caused a repeated error every second and blocked delivery."
- "Task claiming uses file locking to prevent race conditions when multiple teammates try to claim the same task simultaneously."
- "Teams and tasks are stored locally under a session-derived name. The name is `session-` followed by the first eight characters of the session ID: Team config: `~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json`; Task list: `~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/`". "The team config directory is removed when the session ends. The task list directory persists locally and is never uploaded". "There is no project-level equivalent of the team config."
- Limitations section: "One team per session: a session has exactly one team, scoped to that session. You can't create additional named teams or share a team across sessions." "No nested teams: teammates cannot spawn their own teammates. Only the lead can manage the team." "Lead is fixed: the main session is the lead for its lifetime." "Split panes require tmux or iTerm2: the default in-process mode works in any terminal. Split-pane mode isn't supported in VS Code's integrated terminal, Windows Terminal, or Ghostty." Also: "No session resumption with in-process teammates: `/resume` and `/rewind` do not restore in-process teammates." "No background subagents from in-process teammates ... a teammate's background work can't outlive the lead's process."
- Display modes: "In-process: all teammates run inside your main terminal ... Works in any terminal, no extra setup required." "Split panes ... Requires tmux, or iTerm2." `teammateMode` values per settings-reference: "in-process" (default), "auto", "tmux", "iterm2"; per-session flag `--teammate-mode` ("experimental and doesn't appear in `claude --help`").
- Cache: "An in-process teammate's requests fall outside the main conversation's cache TTL bucket, so its cache holds for five minutes by default, including on a Claude subscription. To keep it for an hour, set `subagentPromptCacheTtl` to `1h`. The API bills 1-hour cache writes at a higher rate." Settings-reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md): type string "5m"|"1h", Default unset, "Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later"; override order FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M > CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL > key > ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H.
- Hooks (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md): table rows `TaskCreated` "When a task is being created via `TaskCreate`", `TaskCompleted` "When a task is being marked as completed", `TeammateIdle` "When an agent team teammate is about to go idle"; exit-2 column: "Prevents the teammate from going idle, so it continues working" / "Rolls back the task creation" / "Prevents the task from being marked as completed". All three "don't support matchers and fire on every occurrence". Hook input carries `teammate_name` and `team_name` ("Deprecated. Session-derived team name; will be removed in a future release").

CORRECTION 1 (design-critical, critical=true): "unusable for a headless worker" is over-broad. The docs' restriction is on `-p`/`--print` and SDK sessions only (the agent-teams page links "non-interactive mode" to /docs/en/headless, which is the `-p` page: "Add the `-p` (or `--print`) flag to any `claude` command to run it non-interactively"). A persistent interactive `claude` under tmux on a compute node has a PTY and is an interactive session; in-process teammates work "in any terminal". The Remote Control page explicitly recommends this pattern: "To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside `tmux` or `screen`." (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md, Limitations). So: if Ashley's grid worker is `claude -p ... --resume` or an SDK `query()` loop, teams are off; if it is an interactive `claude` in tmux fed by tmux send-keys / cross-session messaging / channels, teams are available. Changelog v2.1.71: "Fixed `--print` hanging forever when team agents are configured — the exit loop no longer waits on long-lived `in_process_teammate` tasks" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog.md).

CORRECTION 2 (minor): "single-machine" is not a verbatim doc statement; it is an inference from local file paths, "scoped to that session", "never uploaded", and "a teammate's background work can't outlive the lead's process". Cross-session messaging page adds: "Structured agent team protocol messages stay within a team." (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging). The inference is sound.

CORRECTION 3 (minor): the shared task list applies only to "agents that have the Task tools". tools-reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md): "The task-tracking tools, `TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskList`, and `TodoWrite`, are available by default only on Claude 3.x models, Opus 4 through 4.7, Sonnet 4 through 4.6, and Haiku 4.5." Opt in with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`, `--allowedTools TaskCreate`, or `--tools`. Agent-teams page: "Agents without the Task tools coordinate through messages instead of the shared task list."

VERSION HISTORY (changelog.md, `## x.y.z` headers): 2.1.32 "Added research preview agent teams feature ... requires setting CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1"; 2.1.33 "Added `TeammateIdle` and `TaskCompleted` hook events"; 2.1.69 "Fixed teammates accidentally spawning nested teammates via the Agent tool's `name` parameter"; 2.1.71 `--print` hang fix above; 2.1.178 "Agent teams: removed the `TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete` tools. With `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` set, every session now has one implicit team — spawn teammates directly with the Agent tool's `name` parameter ... The `team_name` parameter on the Agent tool is still accepted but ignored." If the claim's "(3 tools)" meant TeamCreate/TeamDelete/SendMessage, only SendMessage remains. The env var name is unchanged through 2.1.283; the page still labels the feature "experimental" (agents overview page: "Experimental and disabled by default").

ADJACENT FINDINGS FOR THE ASHLEY DESIGN (from pages fetched, not part of the claim):
- A `-p` worker CAN receive messages even though it cannot spawn teammates: "Claude Code binds an inbox socket for a `claude -p` session like an interactive one, so a long-running `-p` worker can receive messages and appears in the listing." Not with `--bare`. Start it with `crossSessionInbound` set to `accept` in `--settings` "to let a `-p` worker take messages unattended"; a default-held message in `-p` expires after `dialogExpiry` (5 min) unless set to "never". (cross-session-messaging page) [critical=true]

verdict.corrected_claim: (3/4 IPC) Claude Code's inter-session IPC, as documented 2026-09-27 at code.claude.com: every session with messaging on — including a `claude -p` session, but NOT one started with `--bare` — binds a per-session inbox (Unix domain socket on macOS/Linux/WSL 2; named pipe on native Windows). The path is exported to hooks and Bash commands as `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` (exported before any hook, including `SessionStart`) and shown in `/status` under `Peer address` prefixed `uds:`. Other sessions deliver over that socket "never through Anthropic servers". A script or hook can post into a session by connecting and writing line-delimited JSON; the ONLY line format the docs publish is the optional (Linux/macOS) / required (native Windows) first line `{"type":"auth","token":"<CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN>"}` — the schema of the message line itself is undocumented. Claude Code "closes a connection that hasn't sent a complete line within 30 seconds". "When the receiving session is idle, Claude Code starts a new turn with the message"; during a turn it is read between tool calls. Inbound control is the setting `crossSessionInbound` = `accept` | `hold` | `refuse` (default unset → decided per message by permission-mode class: a receiver that bypasses permission prompts HOLDS messages from senders that do not assert bypass, including scripts, and a `-p` session cannot show the approval dialog, so held messages expire after `dialogExpiry`, 5 min default, unless `dialogExpiry: "never"`). Hence "To let a -p worker take messages unattended, start it with crossSessionInbound set to accept in its --settings value." Precedence: managed settings → `--settings` → user settings, first value found; project/local values apply only when stricter (hold/refuse). Same-machine limits: refuse at sender when serialized message exceeds 1,048,576 characters ("about a million"); rapid bursts refused at sender (error example: "30 were sent recently"); receiver queues at most 50 accepted messages, holds at most 100, drops identical repeats, rate-limits per sender. Isolation: "A session inside a container and a session on the host can't reach each other"; WSL 2 and native Windows on one computer can't either; sockets are restricted to the OS user; if the default socket dir is unusable Claude Code falls back to `/tmp/cc-socks-<uid>` (the default dir is not named in the docs), and if no dir is acceptable the session runs with no inbox (`/status` shows `unavailable`). Cross-machine: "Through Anthropic servers, arriving over that machine's Remote Control connection" (or straight to a cloud session); listing/finding those sessions requires the sending session to be connected to Remote Control, which needs a claude.ai sign-in (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise; "API keys are not supported"; not available on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry or behind a non-api.anthropic.com `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`); sending without Remote Control still goes through but one-way (no reply address). Versions: v2.1.224+ on macOS/Linux/WSL 2 (feature + `crossSessionInbound` + `dialogExpiry` added there); v2.1.234+ native Windows; v2.1.225+ to initiate to another machine; v2.1.228+ for `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`; v2.1.243+ for the 30-s idle-connection close and the fix for messaging "silently turning off inside user namespaces and rootless containers"; v2.1.248+ for the `/tmp/cc-socks-<uid>` fallback and for same-machine messaging on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry or with feature-flag fetching off. Tools `ListAgents`/`SendMessage` (deny both by bare name to stop sending); command `/list-agents` (alias `/peers`). Design caveats: `--bare` also "never reads OAuth credentials", so a bare worker cannot use a Pro/Max subscription at all; and a plain `claude -p "prompt"` exits after its result, so a persistent idle `-p` receiver must be kept resident (e.g. Agent SDK streaming input mode, `--input-format stream-json`, "a long lived process"); the docs do not state whether a socket message alone keeps a `-p` process alive.

findings.claim: (4 IPC) NFS mounts give close-to-open consistency only: attributes are cached 3-60 s for files (acregmin=3, acregmax=60) and 30-60 s for directories (acdirmin=30, acdirmax=60); `actimeo`/`noac` shorten or disable it; `lookupcache=none` makes the client revalidate directory entries 'permit[ting] quick detection of files that were created or removed by other clients, but can impact application and server performance'; flock() is converted to advisory NLM locks; `nocto` disables close-to-open.
findings.detail: nfs(5): 'When an application opens a file stored on an NFS version 3 server, the NFS client checks that the file exists on the server ... When the application closes the file, the NFS client writes back any pending changes'; defaults acregmin 3 / acregmax 60 / acdirmin 30 / acdirmax 60; `noac` 'to achieve attribute cache coherence among multiple clients'; `lookupcache=none` quoted; 'The NFS client converts file locks obtained via flock(2) to advisory locks'; 'cto/nocto Selects whether to use close-to-open cache coherence semantics'. Delayed writes flushed on close, sync(), memory pressure or lock ops; `sync` mount option forces immediate writes.

verdict.corrected_claim: (4 IPC) Linux NFS mounts give close-to-open (CTO) consistency only, and the defaults in nfs(5) are as stated: acregmin=3, acregmax=60, acdirmin=30, acdirmax=60 (seconds); `actimeo=n` sets all four at once; `noac` disables the attribute cache and also "forces application writes to become synchronous"; `lookupcache=none` makes the client "revalidate[] both types of directory cache entries before an application can use them. This permits quick detection of files that were created or removed by other clients, but can impact application and server performance" — but it "has no effect on how the NFS client caches the attributes of files". Two parts of the original claim are version-specific and need correcting: (a) flock(2) is NOT "converted to advisory NLM locks" in general — nfs(5) says only "The NFS client converts file locks obtained via flock(2) to advisory locks" and that "NFS clients > 2.6.12 implement flock by emulating POSIX locks"; those emulated byte-range locks travel over NLM only on NFSv3 ("The Network Lock Manager protocol is a separate sideband protocol used to manage file locks in NFS version 3"), whereas "In NFS version 4, file locking is supported directly in the main NFS protocol, and the NLM and NSM sideband protocols are not used." (b) `nocto` does not simply "disable close-to-open" on every mount: under "Options for NFS versions 2 and 3 only" `nocto` makes the client use "a non-standard heuristic to determine when files on the server have changed", while under "Options for NFS version 4 only" a separate `cto / nocto` applies "for NFS directories on this mount point" and "File data caching behavior is not affected by this option." Neither `cto/nocto` nor `local_lock` is listed under "Options supported by all versions" (ac/noac, acreg*/acdir*, actimeo and lookupcache are). Delayed writes are flushed on memory pressure, sync(2)/msync(2)/fsync(3), close(2), or fcntl(2) lock/unlock; the `sync` mount option (or O_SYNC) forces each write to the server before the syscall returns. nfs(5) also warns that even `noac` leaves "races that may result in data cache incoherence between client and server" and that "If absolute cache coherence among clients is required, applications should use file locking." All of these are root-set mount options, so an unprivileged student cannot apply them on the grid; and the CONTEXT's "Panasas home + CephFS" are not shown to be NFS mounts at all — CephFS "maintains strong cache coherency across clients" (docs.ceph.com), so the NFS caveats apply only to paths verified (e.g. `findmnt -T <path>`) to be nfs/nfs4.
verdict.evidence:
SOURCE FETCHED: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/nfs.5.html (colophon: "obtained from the project's upstream Git repository <git://git.linux-nfs.org/projects/steved/nfs-utils.git> on 2026-08-04 ... most recent commit ... 2026-07-23"). Fetched twice via WebFetch and once raw via curl; the raw text was grepped for section placement because the WebFetch summariser mis-placed one option.

CONFIRMED VERBATIM (claim holds):
- acregmin: "If this option is not specified, the NFS client uses a 3-second minimum." acregmax: "...a 60-second maximum." acdirmin: "...a 30-second minimum." acdirmax: "...a 60-second maximum."
- actimeo=n: "Using actimeo sets all of acregmin, acregmax, acdirmin, and acdirmax to the same value. If this option is not specified, the NFS client uses the defaults for each of these options listed above."
- noac: "Use the noac mount option to achieve attribute cache coherence among multiple clients." Also: "the noac option forces application writes to become synchronous so that local changes to a file become visible on the server immediately."
- lookupcache=mode: "mode can be one of all, none, pos, or positive. This option is supported in kernels 2.6.28 and later." ... "If none is specified, the client revalidates both types of directory cache entries before an application can use them. This permits quick detection of files that were created or removed by other clients, but can impact application and server performance." Default: "If this option is not specified, or if all is specified, the client assumes both types of directory cache entries are valid until their parent directory's cached attributes expire." (i.e. a NEGATIVE lookup for a not-yet-existing file is cached up to acdirmax=60 s by default — critical=true for any poll-for-new-file IPC.)
- CTO: "When an application opens a file stored on an NFS version 3 server, the NFS client checks that the file exists on the server and is permitted to the opener by sending a GETATTR or ACCESS request. The NFS client sends these requests regardless of the freshness of the file's cached attributes." ... "When the application closes the file, the NFS client writes back any pending changes to the file so that the next opener can view the changes." ... "referred to as close-to-open cache consistency, or CTO. It can be disabled for an entire mount point using the nocto mount option."
- Delayed writes: default (async) client "delays sending application writes to the server until any of these events occur: Memory pressure forces reclamation of system memory resources. An application flushes file data explicitly with sync(2), msync(2), or fsync(3). An application closes a file with close(2). The file is locked/unlocked via fcntl(2)." sync option: "any system call that writes data to files on that mount point causes that data to be flushed to the server before the system call returns control to user space." "Applications can use the O_SYNC open flag to force application writes to individual files to go to the server immediately without the use of the sync mount option."
- flock: "NLM supports advisory file locks only. To lock NFS files, use fcntl(2) with the F_GETLK and F_SETLK commands. The NFS client converts file locks obtained via flock(2) to advisory locks."

REFUTED / CORRECTED (version-specific or subtly wrong):
1. "advisory NLM locks": the man page never says flock becomes an NLM lock. "The Network Lock Manager protocol is a separate sideband protocol used to manage file locks in NFS version 3." "In NFS version 4, file locking is supported directly in the main NFS protocol, and the NLM and NSM sideband protocols are not used." local_lock text: "Since NFS clients > 2.6.12 implement flock by emulating POSIX locks, this will result in conflicting locks." So flock -> emulated POSIX byte-range lock; NLM is the v3 transport only. (Note: current upstream text says "NFS version 3", not "version 2 and version 3" as older copies did.)
2. "`nocto` disables close-to-open": raw text shows `cto / nocto` appears TWICE — once under "Options for NFS versions 2 and 3 only" ("If the nocto option is specified, the client uses a non-standard heuristic to determine when files on the server have changed. Using the nocto option may improve performance for read-only mounts, but should be used only if the data on the server changes only occasionally.") and once under "Options for NFS version 4 only" ("Selects whether to use close-to-open cache coherence semantics for NFS directories on this mount point. ... File data caching behavior is not affected by this option."). It is NOT under "Options supported by all versions" (grep: heading at line 118; v2/3 heading at 521; cto/nocto at 651 and 762; v4 heading at 716; local_lock at 680 -> also v2/3-only).
3. Missing caveats that matter for IPC over a shared FS: "Disabling lookup caching should result in less of a performance penalty than using noac, and has no effect on how the NFS client caches the attributes of files." "The noac mount option prevents the client from caching file metadata, but there are still races that may result in data cache incoherence between client and server. The NFS protocol is not designed to support true cluster file system cache coherence without some type of application serialization. If absolute cache coherence among clients is required, applications should use file locking. Alternatively, applications can also open their files with the O_DIRECT flag to disable data caching entirely." Directory-entry caching: "To detect when directory entries have been added or removed on the server, the Linux NFS client watches a directory's mtime. ... Since the directory's mtime is a cached attribute, it may take some time before a client notices it has changed."

DESIGN APPLICABILITY (critical=true): (i) actimeo/noac/lookupcache/nocto/local_lock/sync are mount(8) options set by root; the Ashley extension cannot change them for a student on the grid — the IPC design must live with defaults (write temp+fsync+rename; reader re-opens the file each poll; do not poll for a not-yet-existing filename; or use SSH-delivered prompts instead of FS polling). (ii) NOT VERIFIED: that the grid's Panasas home or CephFS volume is an NFS mount at all. Panasas is normally mounted by its own DirectFlow client (no fetch obtained; WebSearch budget exhausted this session), and https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/cephfs/posix/ (fetched) states "CephFS maintains strong cache coherency across clients" and that NFS "has extremely weak consistency semantics when multiple clients are interacting with the same files or directories, opting instead for 'close-to-open'", ranking "HDFS < NFS < CephFS < {XFS, ext4}". Verify with `findmnt -T ~` and `findmnt -T /rs/rs_grp_oschome/go2432` (fstype nfs/nfs4 vs panfs vs ceph) before applying the NFS caveats. If /rs/rs_grp_oschome is a native ceph kernel mount, the 3-60 s attribute lag in this claim does not apply there, which would favour placing the prompt/response exchange under CephFS rather than Panasas home.

findings.claim: (4 IPC) Atomic primitives on shared filesystems: rename(2) atomically replaces `newpath` ('no point at which another process attempting to access newpath will find it missing') but 'On NFS filesystems, you can not assume that if the operation failed, the file was not renamed'; O_CREAT|O_EXCL is atomic on NFS 'only when using NFSv3 or later on kernel 2.6 or later', and open(2) recommends link(2) + stat(2) link-count==2 as the portable lockfile; inotify 'does not catch remote events that occur on network filesystems', so a remote inbox must be polled.
findings.detail: rename(2): 'If newpath already exists, it will be atomically replaced, so that there is no point at which another process attempting to access newpath will find it missing.' and the NFS retransmitted-RPC caveat; EXDEV across mount points. open(2): 'On NFS, O_EXCL is supported only when using NFSv3 or later on kernel 2.6 or later. In NFS environments where O_EXCL support is not provided, programs that rely on it for performing locking tasks will contain a race condition'; portable technique: 'create a unique file on the same filesystem (e.g., incorporating hostname and PID), and use link(2) to make a link to the lockfile. If link(2) returns 0, the lock is successful. Otherwise, use stat(2) on the unique file to check if its link count has increased to 2'. inotify(7): 'Inotify reports only events that a user-space program triggers through the filesystem API. As a result, it does not catch remote events that occur on network filesystems.'

verdict.corrected_claim: (4 IPC) Atomic primitives on shared filesystems — all quoted man-page text verified verbatim in Linux man-pages 6.19. rename(2) (2026-02-08): "If newpath already exists, it will be atomically replaced, so that there is no point at which another process attempting to access newpath will find it missing." NFS caveat: "On NFS filesystems, you can not assume that if the operation failed, the file was not renamed. If the server does the rename operation and then crashes, the retransmitted RPC which will be processed when the server is up again causes a failure. The application is expected to deal with this." EXDEV: "oldpath and newpath are not on the same mounted filesystem" (rename does not work across different mount points even for the same filesystem). open(2) (2026-02-08): O_CREAT|O_EXCL "is SUPPORTED only when using NFSv3 or later on kernel 2.6 or later" (the page says "supported", not "atomic"); "In NFS environments where O_EXCL support is not provided, programs that rely on it for performing locking tasks will contain a race condition." The link(2)+stat(2) link-count==2 lockfile is described as a technique portable programs "can" use to avoid reliance on NFS O_EXCL, not as a recommendation over O_EXCL; link(2) BUGS gives the reason: "On NFS filesystems, the return code may be wrong in case the NFS server performs the link creation and dies before it can say so." inotify(7) (2026-02-14): "Inotify reports only events that a user-space program triggers through the filesystem API. As a result, it does not catch remote events that occur on network filesystems." REFINEMENT of the inference: an inbox on a network filesystem must be polled only when the file is written from ANOTHER host (e.g. on warrior or via SFTP to the login node); a write executed on the compute node itself (ssh warrior -> node, `cat > inbox/file`) goes through that node's VFS and inotify on the node does fire. On NFS mounts a further polling lag applies: with the default lookupcache=all, a file created by another client may stay invisible until the directory attribute cache expires (acdirmin default 30 s, acdirmax default 60 s). These NFS caveats apply only if the grid home/CephFS volume is an NFS mount; CephFS via its native client documents strong cross-client cache coherence ("in contrast to many other common network file systems like NFS"), and Panasas/PanFS coherence was not verified — check the mount type on the grid (findmnt -T ~ ; stat -f -c %T ~) before choosing the primitive.
