VERIFIED VERBATIM (all fetched 2026-09-27):
[1] rename(2), Linux man-pages 6.19, 2026-02-08, https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/rename.2.html — critical=true. "If newpath already exists, it will be atomically replaced, so that there is no point at which another process attempting to access newpath will find it missing." | "On NFS filesystems, you can not assume that if the operation failed, the file was not renamed. If the server does the rename operation and then crashes, the retransmitted RPC which will be processed when the server is up again causes a failure. The application is expected to deal with this." (no workaround prescribed) | EXDEV: "oldpath and newpath are not on the same mounted filesystem. (Linux permits a filesystem to be mounted at multiple points, but rename() does not work across different mount points, even if the same filesystem is mounted on both.)" -> design consequence: write the temp file and rename within the same mount (same inbox directory), never /tmp -> /rs or ~ -> /rs.
[2] open(2), Linux man-pages 6.19, 2026-02-08, https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html — critical=true. "Ensure that this call creates the file: if this flag is specified in conjunction with O_CREAT, and path already exists, then open() fails with the error EEXIST." | "On NFS, O_EXCL is supported only when using NFSv3 or later on kernel 2.6 or later. In NFS environments where O_EXCL support is not provided, programs that rely on it for performing locking tasks will contain a race condition. Portable programs that want to perform atomic file locking using a lockfile, and need to avoid reliance on NFS support for O_EXCL, can create a unique file on the same filesystem (e.g., incorporating hostname and PID), and use link(2) to make a link to the lockfile. If link(2) returns 0, the lock is successful. Otherwise, use stat(2) on the unique file to check if its link count has increased to 2, in which case the lock is also successful." Wording nuance vs claim: page says "supported", not "atomic"; and "can", not "recommends". Grid kernel 5.15 satisfies ">= 2.6"; any NFSv3/v4 mount satisfies the protocol condition, so O_CREAT|O_EXCL is usable on the grid unless a mount is NFSv2 (unlikely).
[3] inotify(7), Linux man-pages 6.19, 2026-02-14, https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html — critical=true. "Inotify reports only events that a user-space program triggers through the filesystem API. As a result, it does not catch remote events that occur on network filesystems." Also: "various pseudo-filesystems such as /proc, /sys, and /dev/pts are not monitorable with inotify"; "the event queue can overflow. In this case, events are lost" -> IN_Q_OVERFLOW; "robust applications should handle the possibility of lost events gracefully." The limitation is generic to every network filesystem (NFS, CephFS kernel client, PanFS) — but it only bites when the WRITER is on a different host. Since grid users can ssh from warrior to a node holding their job, the laptop can deliver a prompt with `ssh -J warrior.grid.wayne.edu <node> 'cat > $INBOX/<id>.tmp && mv $INBOX/<id>.tmp $INBOX/<id>.json'`; that write is local to the node, so inotifywait on the node sees IN_MOVED_TO. Polling is required only if prompts land on the shared FS from warrior/SFTP/laptop-side mounts. Ceph tracker Feature #62215 "libcephfs: Allow monitoring for any file changes like inotify" (status New) confirms no remote-change notification exists in CephFS (https://tracker.ceph.com/search?q=inotify&issues=1).
[4] link(2), Linux man-pages 6.19, 2026-02-11, https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/link.2.html — critical=false. BUGS: "On NFS filesystems, the return code may be wrong in case the NFS server performs the link creation and dies before it can say so." — this is the reason for the stat(2) st_nlink==2 fallback in [2]. EXDEV: link() "does not work across different mounts, even if the same filesystem is mounted on both." The page does not itself assert link() atomicity.
[5] nfs(5), man7 copy (nfs-utils, dated 9 October 2012), https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/nfs.5.html — critical=true IF the grid mount is NFS. Close-to-open (CTO) consistency, disabled by mount option `nocto`. Directory entry caching: "To detect when directory entries have been added or removed on the server, the Linux NFS client watches a directory's mtime." `lookupcache=all` (default) caches positive AND negative lookups until the parent directory's attribute cache expires; `lookupcache=pos`/`positive` revalidates negative entries; `lookupcache=none` revalidates both. Defaults: acregmin=3 s, acregmax=60 s, acdirmin=30 s, acdirmax=60 s; `actimeo` sets all four. Consequence: on NFS a polled inbox can lag up to acdirmax (60 s) for a file created on another client. Locking: "NLM supports advisory file locks only. To lock NFS files, use fcntl(2) with the F_GETLK and F_SETLK commands"; `nolock` mount option disables NLM.
[6] flock(2), Linux man-pages 6.19, 2026-02-08, https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html — critical=false. "Up to Linux 2.6.11, flock() does not lock files over NFS"; "Since Linux 2.6.12, NFS clients support flock() locks by emulating them as fcntl(2) byte-range locks on the entire file. This means that fcntl(2) and flock() locks do interact with one another over NFS."; "Since Linux 2.6.37, the kernel supports a compatibility mode that allows flock() locks (and also fcntl(2) byte region locks) to be treated as local; see the discussion of the local_lock option in nfs(5)." If a mount uses `local_lock=all|flock|posix`, locks are NOT visible to other hosts.
[7] CephFS "Differences from POSIX", https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/cephfs/posix/ — critical=true for the /rs/rs_grp_oschome CephFS volume. "CephFS aims to adhere to POSIX semantics wherever possible. For example, in contrast to many other common network file systems like NFS, CephFS maintains strong cache coherency across clients." Documented exceptions: writes by a failed client are not necessarily atomic; a write crossing object boundaries with simultaneous writers is not necessarily atomic; st_blocks wrong for sparse files; mmap writes not coherently propagated across hosts; hidden `.snap` directory; atime not maintained. Stated ordering: "HDFS < NFS < CephFS < {XFS, ext4}". The page says nothing about inotify, rename or O_EXCL specifically. So on the CephFS volume the NFS-specific caveats (retransmitted-RPC rename, lookupcache staleness, O_EXCL-only-on-NFSv3+) do not apply as such, but the inotify remote-event limitation in [3] still does.
NOT VERIFIED: Panasas PanFS (grid home) cache-coherence / rename / O_EXCL semantics — WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted (200/200) before this could be checked; no official Panasas page was fetched. Action item: on the grid run `findmnt -T ~` and `findmnt -T /rs/rs_grp_oschome/go2432` (or `stat -f -c %T`) to learn whether each path is panfs, ceph, or nfs/nfs4 and pick the primitive accordingly. All man-page quotes are from the current release (6.19) and are not version-specific in any way that affects kernel 5.15 / CentOS 7.9 userland; nfs(5) on man7 is the 2012 nfs-utils text but the options quoted (lookupcache, acdirmin/acdirmax, local_lock, nocto) are still current.

findings.claim: (4 IPC) CephFS documents 'strong cache coherency across clients' and places itself above NFS in consistency ('HDFS < NFS < CephFS < {XFS, ext4}'), characterising NFS as having 'extremely weak consistency semantics when multiple clients are interacting with the same files or directories, opting instead for close-to-open'; the caveat is that concurrent writes crossing object boundaries can interleave, and st_blocks is estimated.
findings.detail: docs.ceph.com/cephfs/posix: 'CephFS maintains strong cache coherency across clients ... processes behave the same when they are on different hosts as when they are on the same host'; NFS 'writes will be significantly more time-shifted than CephFS, leading to less predictable results'; example 'writer A write aa|aa and writer B write bb|bb simultaneously ... end up with aa|bb'. The grid's `/rs/rs_grp_oschome` CephFS volume is therefore the better shared-FS choice for cross-node handoff files than an NFS-gateway mount.

findings.claim: (4 IPC) Panasas PanFS claims that its DirectFlow client 'work[s] with the Director Nodes and Storage Nodes to deliver fully POSIX-compliant and cache-coherent file system behavior, from a single namespace, across all the servers in the compute cluster'; the same whitepaper has a separate section for 'NFS and SMB/CIFS Gateway on Director Nodes', i.e. NFS-gateway access does not get the DirectFlow guarantees. Whether the WSU home directory is mounted via DirectFlow or an NFS gateway was not verified.
findings.detail: PanFS 9 Architectural Overview PDF (text extracted): '• The DirectFlow Client driver is a loadable file system implementation installed on compute servers ... to deliver fully POSIX-compliant and cache-coherent file system behavior, from a single namespace, across all the servers in the compute cluster.' Section headings: 'Full POSIX Semantics with Cache Coherency', 'NFS and SMB/CIFS Gateway on Director Nodes'. Check on the grid with `mount | grep -E 'panfs|nfs'` or `stat -f -c %T ~`.

findings.claim: (4 IPC) OpenSSH supports the socket-based alternatives natively: 6.7 added 'Unix domain socket forwarding. A remote TCP port may be forwarded to a local Unix domain socket and vice versa or both ends may be a Unix domain socket'; ssh(1) `-L` accepts `[bind_address:]port:remote_socket`, `local_socket:host:hostport`, `local_socket:remote_socket`; 7.3 added `ProxyJump`/`-J` 'to allow simplified indirection through one or more SSH bastions or jump hosts'; `-N`/`-T` for forward-only sessions; `-W host:port` for stdio tunnelling.
findings.detail: release-6.7 quote as given; release-7.3: 'ssh(1): Add a ProxyJump option and corresponding -J command-line flag to allow simplified indirection through a one or more SSH bastions or "jump hosts".'; ssh(1) -L forms: `[bind_address:]port:host:hostport`, `[bind_address:]port:remote_socket`, `local_socket:host:hostport`, `local_socket:remote_socket`; `-J destination` chains with commas. ssh_config: `ControlMaster auto` + `ControlPath` (include %h,%p,%r or %C, non-world-writable dir) + `ControlPersist <seconds|yes>` keep one authenticated connection open so later ssh commands skip the handshake; `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` (default 3) detect dead links; `ExitOnForwardFailure`; `StreamLocalBindUnlink` removes a stale Unix socket file before forwarding.

findings.claim: (4 IPC) socat provides the shim for 'ssh node socat STDIO UNIX-CONNECT:/dev/shm/worker.sock': `UNIX-CONNECT:<filename>` errors if the file is missing, not a socket, or nobody listens; `UNIX-LISTEN:<filename>` needs `unlink-early` to rebind and `fork` to serve multiple connections; `-t` (default 0.5 s) delays close after one side's EOF and `-T` is a total inactivity timeout.
findings.detail: socat(1): UNIX-CONNECT 'Connects to <filename> assuming it is a UNIX domain socket. If <filename> does not exist, this is an error; ... if <filename> is a UNIX domain socket, but no process is listening, this is an error.'; UNIX-LISTEN 'If <filename> exists and is a UNIX domain socket, binding to the address fails (use option unlink-early!)'; fork 'handles its channel in a child process and keeps the parent process attempting to produce more connections'; STDIO 'Uses file descriptor 0 for reading, and 1 for writing'; `-t` 'socat waits <timeout> seconds before terminating. Default is 0.5 seconds'; `-T` 'Total inactivity timeout'.

findings.claim: (5 fan-out, HPC) Anthropic's own HPC integration (Claude Science 'Remote compute clusters') keeps Claude OFF the cluster: it uses `~/.ssh/config` aliases including `ProxyJump`, 'installs nothing on the host', probes for `sbatch`/Apptainer/conda/modules/GPUs, submits via `sbatch`, states 'Jobs survive connection loss', requires the scratch directory to be 'on a shared filesystem for SLURM', defaults the job timeout to 30 minutes and the concurrent job limit to 100, and pulls outputs back into the session (files >~100 MB stay on the host).
findings.detail: 'Claude Science uses your existing ~/.ssh/config, authenticates with your key or ssh-agent, and installs nothing on the host itself.' 'The address, user, port, and any ProxyJump come from that file.' 'Adding a host runs a read-only probe that records CPUs, memory, GPUs, CUDA driver, presence of conda/modules/Apptainer, scratch directories, and whether sbatch exists.' 'SLURM clusters receive jobs via sbatch. Jobs survive connection loss.' 'Scratch directory (must be on a shared filesystem for SLURM) and Concurrent job limit (default 100).' 'Default job timeout is 30 minutes'. Warning: 'Remote jobs run outside the sandbox, as your user on the host'.

findings.claim: (5 fan-out, HPC) The one open-source Slurm+Claude example with a working loop (xgenius) also keeps Claude Code on the dev machine: it calls `claude -p` / `claude --continue` non-interactively (auth via `claude setup-token`), submits with `sbatch`, runs jobs inside Singularity, and a watcher polls the cluster for `.done` marker files every 60 s (`poll_interval_seconds = 60`, `max_concurrent_jobs = 50`), running one Claude session per cycle. The nextflow-io/agent-skills plugin gives Claude Nextflow skills only; it does not orchestrate Claude workers.
findings.detail: xgenius README: 'xgenius watch needs to invoke claude --continue non-interactively. This requires a long-lived auth token' (claude setup-token); diagram 'Claude Code <---- xgenius watch' on dev machine, 'SLURM Cluster (Singularity container, sandboxed)'; jobs write '.done marker on completion'; watcher 'polls clusters for completed jobs'. nextflow-io/agent-skills: skills install-nextflow, create-workflow, run-module, launch-workflow, migrate-nextflow-code; `/plugin marketplace add nextflow-io/agent-skills`; requires Nextflow 26.04+; 'enhances a single Claude instance'.

findings.claim: (5 fan-out, Slurm) Slurm primitives for a worker fleet: `--signal=[{R|B}:]<sig_num>[@sig_time]` sends a signal (default 60 s) before the time limit and 'Use the B: option to signal only the batch shell' (default signals job steps, not the batch shell); `--time` limit kills with SIGTERM then SIGKILL after KillWait; `--requeue` restarts 'the batch script ... from its beginning with the same job ID'; `--array=<indexes>` with `%` to cap simultaneous tasks; `--dependency=afterany|afterok|singleton`; `srun --jobid <id>` 'Initiate a job step under an already allocated job' and `--overlap` lets steps share resources.
findings.detail: sbatch.html: '--signal ... When a job is within sig_time seconds of its end time, send it the signal sig_num ... default of 60 seconds ... Use the "B:" option to signal only the batch shell, none of the other processes will be signaled. By default all job steps will be signaled, but not the batch shell itself.' '--requeue ... the batch script is initiated from its beginning with the same job ID'. '--array ... A "%" separator limits simultaneous running tasks'. srun.html: '--jobid=<id> Initiate a job step under an already allocated job with job ID id'; 'Parallel steps will either be blocked or rejected until requested step resources are available unless --overlap is specified'; '--exclusive ... within a running job, it is a synonym for --exact'. Env: SLURM_JOB_ID, SLURM_JOB_NODELIST, SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID.

findings.claim: (5 fan-out, cost) For a fleet of workers on different nodes/directories, the `claude_code` system-prompt preset embeds per-session context (cwd, git flag, platform, shell, OS version, auto-memory paths) that defeats cross-machine prompt-cache sharing; set `excludeDynamicSections: true` (TS >=0.2.98 / Python `exclude_dynamic_sections` >=0.1.58, or CLI `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`) to move it into the first user message so identical workers share one cache entry.
findings.detail: modifying-system-prompts: 'two sessions that use the same claude_code preset and append text still cannot share a prompt cache entry if they run from different working directories ... set excludeDynamicSections: true ... leaving only the static preset and your append text in the system prompt so identical configurations share a cache entry across users and machines'. 'For the equivalent flag in non-interactive CLI mode, see --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections'. Also: 'The Python SDK passes a string prompt as one command-line argument to the CLI subprocess, so a prompt that exceeds the OS argument-length limit fails at process spawn ... Argument list too long'.

findings.claim: (platform, critical) The native Claude Code binary is a Bun single-executable (2.1.112 was 'the last Node-based release'); Bun documents glibc 2.17 / kernel 3.10 as the floor with SSE4.2 required, yet Claude Code 2.1.176 (Bun 1.3.14) crashed at launch on CentOS 7.9 / glibc 2.17 with 'panic(main thread): Bus error ... Illegal instruction, exit: 132' while 2.1.170 worked, and 2.1.113-2.1.161 SIGILL'd on an Emerald Rapids Kubernetes host; official system requirements list Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, Alpine 3.19+, not RHEL/CentOS 7. Run the CLI inside the Singularity image (its own glibc), never on the host.

verdict.corrected_claim: (platform, critical) The native Claude Code binary is a Bun-compiled single executable: the official changelog says "Upgraded the bundled Bun runtime to 1.4" (2.1.181), and 2.1.176 embedded Bun v1.3.14. 2.1.112 was the last release whose npm package ran as bundled JavaScript under Node (changelog 2.1.113: "Changed the CLI to spawn a native Claude Code binary (via a per-platform optional dependency) instead of bundled JavaScript"); the install.sh native binary was already Bun before that (2.1.30 native worked on Ivy Bridge, later versions SIGILL, #62244). Bun documents "glibc 2.17 or newer", kernel 3.10 minimum / 5.6 recommended, and "does not support x64 CPUs without the SSE4.2 extension", BUT the CPU floor of the Claude binary is higher than Bun's documented SSE4.2: Anthropic's troubleshooting page says "your CPU likely lacks AVX or another instruction the binary requires. This affects roughly pre-2013 Intel and AMD processors ... There is no native-binary workaround; track issue #50384", Bun's build hardcodes -march=haswell (oven-sh/bun #35964), and Ivy Bridge CPUs with AVX1 but no AVX2/BMI2 die on a VEX-encoded BMI2 instruction (#50466, #62244). Treat the practical x86-64 floor as Haswell-class (AVX2+BMI2, 2013+); kvm64-style VMs lacking SSE4.2/POPCNT hang at 100% CPU instead of crashing (#95566). #69980 (CentOS 7.9.2009, kernel 3.10.0-1160, glibc 2.17, Xeon E5-2697A v4 with AVX2): 2.1.176 failed with "panic(main thread): Bus error at address 0xF0D0358 / oh no: Bun has crashed ... Illegal instruction ... exit: 132" while 2.1.170 ran; closed "not planned" with no maintainer diagnosis, so glibc 2.17 vs kernel 3.10 was never separated and later versions are untested on that host. Official supported Linux: "Ubuntu 20.04+", "Debian 10+", "Alpine Linux 3.19+"; RHEL appears only as a dnf repository target with no version floor; CentOS 7 is unsupported. glibc-version bugs exist at both ends (startup crash on glibc 2.44 fixed in 2.1.245). Design: run claude inside the Singularity/Apptainer image built from a supported distro (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 or Debian 12; or Alpine 3.19+ with the linux-x64-musl binary plus libgcc, libstdc++, ripgrep and USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0). The image supplies glibc but NOT the CPU or kernel: the container executes on the host CPU and the host kernel (grid 5.15, above Bun's 5.6 recommendation), so gate the Slurm job on nodes advertising avx2 and bmi2 in /proc/cpuinfo (or a Slurm --constraint) and test `claude --version` in the job prologue. Pin the version at image build with `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s <version>` (or npm with Node 22+ used only at install time: the package "downloads a native binary that doesn't use your Node.js at runtime"; platforms linux-x64, linux-x64-musl, linux-arm64, linux-arm64-musl), set DISABLE_UPDATES=1 (blocks background and manual `claude update`/`claude install`; DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 only stops the background check), and keep the binary out of the bind-mounted Panasas $HOME: the native installer manages ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ and on NFS leaves .nfs* silly-rename ghosts (#69980). Separate risk: the VS Code Claude Code extension "bundles a private copy of the CLI inside the extension directory for its own chat panel", so under Remote-SSH that Bun binary runs on the CentOS 7.9 host, not in the container.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core facts hold, but the claim is subtly wrong in three load-bearing places: (1) it takes Bun's documented CPU floor (SSE4.2) as the binary's floor, while Anthropic's own docs say AVX and field evidence shows AVX2/BMI2 (Haswell) instructions faulting; (2) "2.1.112 last Node-based release" is true only of the npm package, the install.sh binary was Bun well before 2.1.113; (3) the remedy "Singularity image (its own glibc)" is incomplete, a container does not change the CPU or kernel, and #69980's host ran kernel 3.10 so it never isolated glibc 2.17 as the cause.

Haswell = AVX2+BMI1/BMI2, contradicting the Nehalem/SSE4.2 wording for at least part of the runtime.

12. Claude Code CPU-floor issues (GitHub search https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue+%22Illegal+instruction%22): #50384 (2026-04-18, closed not planned; the issue the official docs point to): "[BUG] Illegal instruction crash on CPUs without AVX after 2.1.112 (native binary regression)", AMD A4-3310MX (sse, sse2, sse4a; no avx), broken 2.1.113+, working 2.1.112, no maintainer comment. #50466 (2026-04-18, closed not planned): "[BUG] 2.1.113 crashes with SIGILL \"illegal hardware instruction\" on Ivy Bridge (AVX2-less) Intel Macs — regression from 2.1.112", Core i5-3470S, hw.optional.avx1_0=1, hw.optional.avx2_0=0. #62244 (2026-05-25, closed duplicate): "[BUG] Illegal instruction: 4 (SIGILL/BMI2) on 2013 Mac Pro (Xeon E5 v2 / Ivy Bridge) — regression after 2.1.30", faulting bytes "c4 e2 f9 f7 d1" = VEX-encoded BMI2; works 2.1.30 (native installer, so the native Bun binary predates 2.1.113). #89033 (2026-08-23, open): "Claude Code v2.1.241 native binary crashes with SIGILL on CPUs without SSE4.1", Xeon 5130, fault "pinsrq $0x0,%rsi,%xmm1" (SSE4.1); works 2.1.92 via cli.js. #95566 (2026-09-19, open): "Native binary hangs silently at 100% CPU on VMs with the kvm64 CPU model (no SSE4/POPCNT) — needs a CPU feature pre-flight check", versions 2.1.217-2.1.278, both linux-x64 and linux-x64-musl; under "qemu-x86_64 -cpu Nehalem" completes normally; workaround Proxmox "qm set <vmid> --cpu host". #96402 (2026-09-23, open): "[BUG] SIGILL on x86-64 CPU without AVX (Linux, bare metal) — native installer 2.1.280 and npm 2.1.197 both crash; 2.1.112 (last JS bundle) on Node 22 works"; kernel trap "traps: claude-2.1.280-[81617] trap invalid opcode"; installer output "Installation was killed before it could finish (exit code 132)."; pins 2.1.112 with DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 and calls it fragile. Also #91914 (open): "Native Linux build crashes (SIGILL/SIGSEGV) in JSC GC HeapHelper thread, 8x/day on 2.1.258, same Bun 1.4.1 in 2.1.259" and #89437: startup SIGILL in 2.1.241 (Bun v1.4.0) 71% of launches, 2.1.243 clean, showing per-release Bun regressions that a pinned version plus DISABLE_UPDATES avoids. No Anthropic maintainer comment appears on any of these issues; the only official position is the troubleshoot-install text.

13. GitHub search https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue+glibc+2.17 returns only #69980 as relevant: no report of a newer Claude Code version succeeding or failing on glibc 2.17, so behaviour of 2.1.28x on the CentOS 7.9 host is unknown (not tested; do not assume either way).

WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED: no official Anthropic statement gives a glibc floor or a CPU instruction-set floor beyond "AVX"; the root cause of #69980 (glibc 2.17 vs kernel 3.10 vs a 2.1.176-specific Bun bug) was never diagnosed; whether the current single-binary Bun x64 build (runtime AVX2 dispatch) has removed the Haswell requirement from Claude Code binaries is unknown, and the open 2026-08/09 issues (#89033, #95566, #96402) say it has not. Web search budget was exhausted; all evidence above is from direct fetches of the URLs listed.

findings.claim: (1/2 docs gap) Anthropic has twice closed as 'not planned' requests to document the `--input-format stream-json` stdin format (issues #24594, 2026-02-10 and #44911, 2026-04-07); the only official specification of the envelope is the Agent SDK documentation and source, so the design should treat the SDK's wire format as the contract and pin the CLI version in the container image.
findings.detail: #24594: 'There is no documentation explaining how to use --input-format stream-json. Specifically: What message format should be sent on stdin?' Closed as not planned, no maintainer reply. #44911: asks for docs with `--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --replay-user-messages`; notes v2.1.94 UTF-8 fix; closed as not planned.

findings.claim: (3 tools) Official taxonomy of parallelism: subagents (in-session), agent view/background sessions (`claude agents`, research preview), agent teams (experimental), dynamic workflows (script-driven, 'Dozens to hundreds of agents per run'), and projects (cloud threads); plus worktrees, cross-session messaging and `/batch` (5-30 worktree-isolated subagents). 'In every approach the workers are Claude sessions.'
findings.detail: agents page table and 'Choose an approach': 'Claude delegates and collects results inside one conversation: subagents'; 'A script holds the plan instead of Claude's turn-by-turn judgment: dynamic workflows'; workflows table: Scale 'Dozens to hundreds of agents per run', Interruption 'Resumable in the same session', intermediate results 'Script variables'. `/batch` 'has Claude split one large change into 5 to 30 worktree-isolated subagents'.

topics_verified.recommendation: Run ONE long-lived Claude Code process per student inside the Singularity image in the Slurm job, started as `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --session-id <uuid> [--replay-user-messages] [--permission-mode acceptEdits|--allowedTools ...] --settings '{"crossSessionInbound":"accept"}'` with stdin attached to a PIPE held open by a small shim (never a PTY, never `--bare`, since `--bare` disables OAuth and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`). Authenticate with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token` (one-year, Pro/Max), stored 0600 on the shared home; set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, pin the CLI version in the image (glibc 2.17 on the host is unsafe for the Bun binary), and set `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_MS=0` unless MCP servers are needed. Each prompt from the laptop is one NDJSON line `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."},"parent_tool_use_id":null}`; the extension streams `stream_event`/`assistant` lines to the UI and marks the turn done on `{"type":"result"}` (then waits briefly for a possible follow-on `system/init` if background tasks exist, or for a `session_state_changed: idle` event). For the laptop-to-node channel, prefer a Unix socket (or FIFO pair) in node-local `/dev/shm` owned by the shim, reached with `ssh -J warrior.grid.wayne.edu <node> socat STDIO UNIX-CONNECT:/dev/shm/ashley/<jobid>.sock`, using `ControlMaster auto`/`ControlPersist` so each send skips the double handshake; the equivalent `ssh -L <local>:/dev/shm/ashley/<jobid>.sock` Unix-socket forward through ProxyJump is a fine alternative if VS Code's Remote-SSH connection is already up. Use the shared filesystem only for durability and discovery (job registry, session id, transcript in `~/.claude/projects/...`, result JSON written to CephFS via write-to-temp then `rename()`, plus a `.done` marker), never as the low-latency prompt path: NFS attribute caches are 3-60 s, inotify is blind to remote writes, and Anthropic itself uses a Unix socket locally and its own servers cross-machine. Do not depend on Agent Teams (interactive-only) or on cross-machine Claude messaging (needs Remote Control, unavailable with setup-token). For fan-out, keep it inside the single worker first (subagents, 20 concurrent; dynamic workflows with `parallel()`/`pipeline()` approved via a `Workflow` allow rule in `-p`), and reach for multi-node only with Slurm job arrays (`--array`, `%N` cap) whose tasks run one-shot `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema ...` and drop results by atomic rename for the orchestrator to poll and join; guard every job with `--signal=B:USR1@120` so the shim can flush and stop cleanly before walltime. Measure cold start on the grid before design freeze: `time claude -p ok --output-format json` and read `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `ttft_ms`, `time_to_request_from_spawn_ms`; expect roughly 0.7 s process boot plus network fetches plus several seconds to first token, and treat any first-turn number under 3 s as unproven.
open_questions: Does Claude Code 2.1.283 actually refuse `--input-format stream-json` without `-p`? The Python SDK omits `--print` (but sets CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py), while a third-party report on 2.1.261 says it is required; test both on the grid.

Exact semantics of `--replay-user-messages`: the CLI reference says 'Replay user messages from a resumed session without re-running the agent. Print mode only. Requires v2.1.209+', but the 1.0.86 changelog and third-party workers use it to echo stdin messages into the output stream; confirm which behaviour 2.1.283 has.

Measured cold start on WSU compute nodes (Singularity, CephFS/Panasas home): no published figure applies; measure `time_to_request_from_spawn_ms`/`ttft_ms` with the OAuth token and with feature-flag fetching on and off.

Where does Claude Code place its per-session inbox Unix socket on Linux (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR? TMPDIR? `/tmp/cc-socks-<uid>` fallback), and will the grid's /tmp sweeper delete a long-running worker's socket file? Does TMPDIR=/dev/shm redirect it?

Does `--bare` become the default for `-p` in a future release (Anthropic says it will)? If so, OAuth/subscription auth in `-p` breaks unless the extension passes an explicit opt-out; watch the changelog and pin the CLI version.

Is the WSU Panasas home mounted through the DirectFlow client (documented cache-coherent) or an NFS gateway (close-to-open only)? `mount | grep -Ei 'panfs|nfs'` on a compute node decides whether shared-file handoff can be trusted for anything latency-sensitive.

Terms of service: the Agent SDK note forbids third parties offering claude.ai login in their products; an extension that launches the official CLI under each student's own subscription token on university hardware is not explicitly covered. Needs a policy check with Anthropic before rollout.

Does a worker authenticated with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN emit `session_state_changed`/`idle` events by default, or only with CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS set? The Python SDK relies on them to know when a run is truly idle after a `result`.

Whether the current native binary (Bun 1.3.x) runs on the host's glibc 2.17 + kernel 5.15 at all is unverified (the documented crash was glibc 2.17 + kernel 3.10); irrelevant inside the container, but any host-side use of `claude` (e.g. on warrior) must be tested.

Rate limits: how a Pro/Max plan's 5-hour and 7-day usage windows behave with many subagents/workflow agents running from one persistent worker (the result event exposes `rateLimitType` values 'five_hour', 'seven_day', 'seven_day_opus'); no published numbers.

topics_verified.topic: VS Code extension engineering facts for the "Ashley" extension (vsce/bundling, extensionKind, extensionDependencies, SecretStorage, environmentVariableCollection, programmatic Remote-SSH, VS Code Server on glibc 2.17, headless tests on Windows, SSH FS alternative, Windows OpenSSH client)
topics_verified.summary: The current @vscode/vsce is 4.0.0 (released 2026-09-14) and, like @vscode/test-cli 0.0.15 and @vscode/test-electron 3.1.0, requires Node >= 22, not 20; `vsce package --no-dependencies` ("Disable dependency detection via npm or yarn") is the documented pairing with an esbuild bundle that externalises only 'vscode' and .vscodeignores node_modules. An extension with a `main` entry and no `extensionKind` is deduced as `['workspace']` in VS Code's source, so Ashley must declare `"extensionKind": ["ui"]` or it will be installed onto the compute node's VS Code Server instead of the laptop; a `ui` extension's SecretStorage lives on the laptop (Electron safeStorage: DPAPI on Windows, Keychain on macOS, libsecret/kwallet or insecure basic_text on Linux; keytar removed in 1.83) and is "not synced across multiple machines". Source inspection shows a UI extension's `environmentVariableCollection` does reach remote terminals: every extension host's MainThreadTerminalService writes into one workbench EnvironmentVariableService whose `mergedCollection` is applied in TerminalProcessManager._resolveEnvironment for both local and remote `backend.createProcess` paths; `persistent` defaults to true and the collection is invalidated on uninstall, which is better than writing tokens into plain-text `terminal.integrated.env.linux`. For programmatic connection the only documented, collaborator-endorsed route is `vscode.openFolder` with `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+<user@host>/<path>` (or `vscode.newWindow` with `remoteAuthority`); `opensshremotesexplorer.emptyWindowInNewWindow` was removed in Remote-SSH 0.92.0 and the argument shape of `opensshremotes.openEmptyWindow` is undocumented. On glibc 2.17 the official FAQ workaround is real but "not an officially supported usage scenario": since VS Code 1.99 (PR #235232, merged 2025-03-10) `check-requirements-linux.sh` skips its glibc check whenever `VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER` is non-empty and `code-server-linux.sh` runs `patchelf --set-rpath` then `--set-interpreter` on `$ROOT/node` only, requiring patchelf >= 0.18; the docs never say which shell file must export the variables, one 1.99.2 user with them in ~/.bashrc and useExecServer=true failed (closed not-planned), while Red Hat's bash carries the SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC patch so ~/.bashrc is plausibly read by Remote-SSH's non-interactive shell. Two premises in the task are wrong: CentOS 7.9's sshd (OpenSSH 7.4) has negotiated hmac-sha2 MACs since 5.9 and RSA/SHA-2 signatures since 7.2, so neither `MACs +hmac-sha1` nor `+ssh-rsa` is needed from a Windows 9.x client, and the Windows client's default MAC list still contains hmac-sha1 anyway. Headless testing on Windows does not exist as such: the CI recipe uses xvfb only on Linux and runs `npm test` bare on windows-latest, which has an interactive desktop session. SSH FS (Kelvin.vscode-sshfs) is alive (v1.27.0 published 2026-06-07, 78 open issues, ~790k installs) and needs no server binary, so it sidesteps glibc entirely, at the cost of having no remote extension host.

findings.claim: @vscode/vsce latest is 4.0.0 and requires Node.js >= 22 (not 20).
findings.detail: registry.npmjs.org/@vscode/vsce/latest: "version": "4.0.0", "engines": {"node": ">= 22"}, "bin": {"vsce": "vsce"}. GitHub release v4.0.0 published_at 2026-09-14T18:53:48Z; release notes include the breaking line "Raise Node.js baseline to 22". README Requirements: "Node.js at least 22.x.x" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vscode-vsce/main/README.md).

findings.claim: `vsce package --no-dependencies` is the exact flag and it only disables npm/yarn dependency detection; bundling still has to exclude node_modules via .vscodeignore.
findings.detail: src/main.ts option strings: "--no-dependencies", 'Disable dependency detection via npm or yarn'; "--dependencies", 'Enable dependency detection via npm or yarn'; "--pre-release", 'Mark this package as a pre-release'; "-t, --target <target>", 'Target architecture. Valid targets: ${ValidTargets}'; "-o, --out <path>", 'Output .vsix extension file to <path> location (defaults to <name>-<version>.vsix)'; "--no-yarn", 'Use npm instead of yarn (default inferred from absence of yarn.lock or .yarnrc)'; ls command: "--tree", 'Prints the files in a tree format'.

findings.claim: The official esbuild bundling recipe externalises only 'vscode', emits dist/extension.js, and .vscodeignore drops node_modules and src/.
findings.detail: esbuild.js: entryPoints: ['src/extension.ts'], bundle: true, format: 'cjs', platform: 'node', external: ['vscode'], outfile: 'dist/extension.js'; the doc says external "exclude[s] the 'vscode' module from the bundle (since it's provided by the VS Code runtime)"; "vscode:prepublish" runs "npm run package" (esbuild with --production); .vscodeignore: "Everything that's now bundled into the dist/extension.js file can be excluded, usually the out folder...and most importantly, the node_modules folder" with sample entries `node_modules` and `src/`.

findings.claim: `"extensionKind": ["ui"]` makes the extension run in the local extension host even in a Remote-SSH window; `["workspace"]` makes it run where the workspace (the compute node) is.
findings.detail: extension-host doc: "extensionKind": ["ui"] means the extension "must run close to the UI because it requires access to local assets, devices, or capabilities or because low latency is required"; ["workspace"] "requires access to workspace contents and therefore needs to run where the workspace is located"; ["ui","workspace"] "will run in VS Code's local extension host if it exists locally...Otherwise, the extension will run in VS Code's workspace extension host". remote-extensions doc: UI extensions "cannot directly access files in the remote workspace, or run scripts/tools installed in that workspace."

findings.claim: If extensionKind is omitted, an extension that has a `main` entry is deduced as ['workspace'] — i.e. Ashley would be installed onto the compute node's VS Code Server, not the laptop.
findings.detail: extensionManifestPropertiesService.ts deduceExtensionKind: "if (manifest.main) { if (manifest.browser) { return isWeb ? ['workspace', 'web'] : ['workspace']; } return ['workspace']; }"; "if (manifest.browser) { return ['web']; }"; with neither, start from ['ui','workspace','web'] filtered by contribution points. Override precedence in getConfiguredExtensionKind: user setting "remote.extensionKind" -> productService.extensionKind -> manifest.extensionKind (filtered to ui/workspace).

findings.claim: Users can override an extension's kind with the `remote.extensionKind` setting; extensions running on different hosts cannot share an exported API and must talk via commands.
findings.detail: remote-extensions doc example: {"remote.extensionKind": {"ms-azuretools.vscode-cosmosdb": ["ui"], "ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh-edit": ["workspace"]}}; "it is possible that an extension running remotely has an extension dependency on an extension running locally... the providing extension give up entirely the ability to export any APIs by using "api": "none" in their extension's package.json"; "extensions can still communicate using VS Code commands (which are asynchronous)"; vscode.env.remoteName is undefined for local workspaces and e.g. 'ssh-remote' for SSH.

findings.claim: `extensionDependencies` is an array of `${publisher}.${name}` ids; at install time VS Code resolves the dependencies from the Marketplace gallery unless `donotIncludePackAndDependencies` is set, and it blocks uninstalling a dependency.
findings.detail: Manifest ref: "An array with the ids of extensions that this extension depends on. The id of an extension is always ${publisher}.${name}." Source abstractExtensionManagementService.ts: getAllDepsAndPackExtensions()/collectDependenciesAndPackExtensionsToInstall() recurse through the gallery; option donotIncludePackAndDependencies; error strings: "Can't install '{0}' extension because it is not compatible with the current version" (notFoundCompatibleDependency) and "Cannot uninstall '{0}' extension. '{1}' extension depends on this." No string says a missing dependency is ignored.

findings.claim: Side-loading a VSIX whose extensionDependency is not installed and not resolvable fails with an opaque error from the CLI.
findings.detail: Issue #233375: `code --install-extension path/to/file.vsix` on VS Code 1.94.2 fails with "Error: Unable to resolve nonexistent file '/Users/jvilk/.vscode/extensions/$dependency'" when the dependency is not installed; reporter asked that the message say "the dependency must be installed first"; closed as not planned (reported 2024-11-08). The extension-manifest page itself does not describe missing-dependency behaviour.

findings.claim: SecretStorage (context.secrets) is per-machine and explicitly not synced; from a UI extension it is stored on the laptop, and even remote extensions store secrets client-side.
findings.detail: vscode-api: SecretStorage "Secrets are stored securely on the machine. They are not synced across multiple machines."; methods get(key), store(key, value), delete(key), onDidChange; ExtensionContext.secrets: "The SecretStorage instance of the current extension. Use it to store secrets like API tokens securely." remote-extensions doc: the API stores secrets "on the client side" regardless of where the extension runs and "is the recommended way to persist passwords & secrets".

findings.claim: SecretStorage's backend is Electron safeStorage (keytar removed in VS Code 1.83): DPAPI on Windows, Keychain on macOS, libsecret/kwallet on Linux with an insecure basic_text fallback.
findings.detail: VS Code 1.83 notes, section "keytar removed from VS Code": "Back in June, we moved the SecretStorage API over to using Electron's safeStorage"; extensions should "Use the SecretStorage API that VS Code provides on the ExtensionContext"; `--disable-keytar` deprecated in favour of `--use-inmemory-secretstorage`. Electron safe-storage doc: Windows "Encryption keys are generated via DPAPI"; macOS "Encryption keys are stored for your app in Keychain Access"; getSelectedStorageBackend() returns basic_text | gnome_libsecret | kwallet | kwallet5 | kwallet6 | unknown, selectable with --password-store="gnome-libsecret" etc.; with no store "items stored in using the safeStorage API will be unprotected as they are encrypted via hardcoded plaintext password". vscode-discussions #748: ciphertext lives in the SQLite state DB under the user data dir; macOS key item "Code Safe Storage".

findings.claim: On Linux (WSL GUI or Linux laptops) the keyring must be unlocked or forced; VS Code documents `--password-store` / argv.json values kwallet5, gnome-libsecret, kwallet, basic.
findings.detail: Settings Sync doc, keychain troubleshooting: error "Cannot create an item in a locked collection" means unlock the default `Login` keyring; specify a backend "by running VS Code with the --password-store flag or by editing the argv.json file through Preferences: Configure Runtime Arguments"; values "kwallet5", "gnome-libsecret", "kwallet", "basic" ("basic" = text encryption, not recommended). Also: Settings Sync does not synchronize extensions to or from remote windows.

findings.claim: context.environmentVariableCollection.persistent defaults to true, survives window reloads, and is invalidated when the extension is uninstalled or the collection is cleared; `description` labels the change in the terminal UI.
findings.detail: vscode.d.ts (via vshaxe mirror) GlobalEnvironmentVariableCollection.persistent: "Whether the collection should be cached for the workspace and applied to the terminal across window reloads. When true the collection will be active immediately such when the window reloads. Additionally, this API will return the cached version if it exists. The collection will be invalidated when the extension is uninstalled or when the collection is cleared. Defaults to true." getScoped: "Gets scope-specific environment variable collection for the extension... applied in addition to (and after) the global collection." vscode-api page: description = "A description for the mutator to be shown in the UI"; methods replace/append/prepend(variable, value, options?) with EnvironmentVariableMutatorOptions applyAtProcessCreation / applyAtShellIntegration, default { applyAtProcessCreation: true }.

findings.claim: A UI (local) extension's environmentVariableCollection IS applied to terminals in a Remote-SSH window: collections from every extension host are merged in the workbench renderer and applied on both local and remote terminal-creation paths.
findings.detail: mainThreadTerminalService.ts (@extHostNamedCustomer(MainContext.MainThreadTerminalService), one per extension host): $setEnvironmentVariableCollection(extensionIdentifier, persistent, collection, descriptionMap) -> this._environmentVariableService.set(extensionIdentifier, translatedCollection). terminalProcessManager.ts: this._extEnvironmentVariableCollection = this._environmentVariableService.mergedCollection; _resolveEnvironment awaits this._extEnvironmentVariableCollection.applyToProcessEnvironment(env, { workspaceFolder }, variableResolver) and is used by both _launchLocalProcess and the remote-authority backend.createProcess path.

findings.claim: Extension env contributions relaunch idle terminals automatically or show a warning icon with a hover listing `extensionName: description`; two settings govern this.
findings.detail: Terminal advanced doc: "If an extension changes the terminal environment, any existing terminals will be relaunched if it is safe to do so, otherwise a warning will show in the terminal status." Settings: terminal.integrated.environmentChangesIndicator; terminal.integrated.environmentChangesRelaunch (source default true: "Whether to relaunch terminals automatically if extensions want to contribute to their environment and have not been interacted with yet."). environmentVariableInfo.ts strings: "The following extensions want to relaunch the terminal to contribute to its environment:", "The following extensions have contributed to this terminal's environment:", action "Relaunch Terminal", "Show Environment Contributions"; hover renders `${extensionName}`: ${description}. Example given: the built-in Git extension injects GIT_ASKPASS.

findings.claim: The alternative, `terminal.integrated.env.linux/windows/osx`, is a plain-text settings.json object and is the wrong place for tokens.
findings.detail: terminalConfiguration.ts: terminal.integrated.env.linux — "Object with environment variables that will be added to the VS Code process to be used by the terminal on Linux. Set to `null` to delete the environment variable." (same wording for windows/osx). Profiles doc: profile `env`: "A map defining environment variables and their values, set the variable to null to delete it from the environment"; `terminal.integrated.inheritEnv: false` strips most inherited variables.

findings.claim: The collaborator-endorsed way to open a Remote-SSH window programmatically is `vscode.openFolder` with a `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+<user@host>/<path>` URI; `opensshremotes.openEmptyWindow`'s argument shape is undocumented.
findings.detail: vscode-discussions #58 (answer by VS Code collaborator Alessandro Fragnani, 2022-07-08): const uri = vscode.Uri.parse(`vscode-remote://ssh-remote+${machineAddress}/home/folder/sub-folder`); vscode.commands.executeCommand("vscode.openFolder", uri, {forceNewWindow: true}); asker reported the address had to be "username@machineAddress". Issue #3552 (opened 2020-08-21, milestone November 2020, closed, labels feature-request/verified, assignee roblourens) asked to pass a host to opensshremotes.openEmptyWindow instead of the quick pick; no parameter shape is documented there. Issue #1888 proposed executeCommand("opensshremotes.openEmptyWindow", "ssh://user@hostname:port") with no confirmed resolution.

findings.claim: `opensshremotesexplorer.emptyWindowInNewWindow` was removed in Remote-SSH 0.92.0; the Remote Explorer's `remote-explorer.connectToRemoteInNewWindow` takes different, undocumented parameters.
findings.detail: Issue #7529 title: "Command opensshremotesexplorer.emptyWindowInNewWindow not anymore available in version 0.92.0" (opened 2022-11-15, labels info-needed, ssh); poster: "the remote-explorer extension provides a command remote-explorer.connectToRemoteInNewWindow" but "the parameters expected by this function are not the same". The Remote Explorer wiki documents only the `remote` view container, `contributes.remoteHelp`, and view groups, not that command's arguments.

findings.claim: `vscode.newWindow` with `{ remoteAuthority: 'ssh-remote+<host>', reuseWindow }` and `vscode.openFolder` with `Uri.from({scheme:'vscode-remote', authority, path})` are the two built-in commands an open-source Remote-SSH reimplementation uses; `vscode.openFolder` accepts forceNewWindow/forceReuseWindow/noRecentEntry.
findings.detail: open-remote-ssh src/commands.ts: openRemoteSSHWindow -> vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.newWindow', { remoteAuthority: getRemoteAuthority(host), reuseWindow }); openRemoteSSHLocationWindow -> vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.openFolder', vscode.Uri.from({ scheme: 'vscode-remote', authority: getRemoteAuthority(host), path })). Built-in commands ref: vscode.openFolder "Open a folder or workspace in the current window or new window depending on the newWindow argument" with options forceNewWindow, forceReuseWindow, noRecentEntry; vscode.newWindow options { reuseWindow }.

findings.claim: The VS Code CLI can open a Remote-SSH folder directly: `code --remote ssh-remote+<remote_server> <path on remote>`.
findings.detail: Command line doc: `--remote <authority>` — "Connect to a remote development environment. The authority specifies the remote connection for WSL (wsl+<distro name> <path in WSL>) or for SSH (ssh-remote+<remote_server> <path on remote>)." Also -n/--new-window and -r/--reuse-window.

findings.claim: Remote-SSH settings: `remote.SSH.configFile` points at an alternate ssh config; `remote.SSH.remotePlatform` is a host->platform map; `remote.SSH.path` overrides the ssh binary; `remote.SSH.showLoginTerminal` exposes the login; hosts need bash, tar and curl/wget.
findings.detail: ssh.md: "You can also set the remote.SSH.configFile property in your User settings.json file"; "Once you select a platform, it will be stored in VS Code settings under the remote.SSH.remotePlatform property"; "Linux hosts need to have Bash (/bin/bash), tar, and either curl or wget installed"; remote.SSH.defaultExtensions. troubleshooting.md: "remote.SSH.remotePlatform": { "host-in-ssh-config-or-fqdn": "windows" }; "VS Code will look for the ssh command in the PATH. Failing that, on Windows it will attempt to find ssh.exe in the default Git for Windows install path. You can also specifically tell VS Code where to find the SSH client by adding the remote.SSH.path property"; "Enable the remote.SSH.showLoginTerminal setting".

findings.claim: `remote.SSH.useLocalServer` defaults to true (one shared SSH process, "Local Server Mode"); `remote.SSH.useExecServer` bootstraps a minimal control server and is being enabled by default; disabling it is the first troubleshooting step.
findings.detail: Remote-SSH troubleshooting wiki: "The Remote-SSH extension has a setting called remote.SSH.useLocalServer which provides two different modes for connecting. The default value is true..." true = "Local Server Mode": "spawns an SSH process which will then be reused by all VS Code windows connected to that remote"; false = "Terminal Mode": "runs the SSH connection command in a hidden terminal". Exec server: "The Remote-SSH extension can establish itself by bootstrapping with a minimal control server before launching the full VS Code Server... This is gradually being enabled by default for users." "If remote.SSH.useExecServer is enabled on your machine, try disabling it and see whether that is successful." Also: "Kill VS Code Server on Host..." "will kill running VS Code Server processes on your remote machine and remove server files from the remote."

findings.claim: `RemoteCommand` in ssh config (e.g. to land inside a Slurm allocation) is honoured only with `remote.SSH.useLocalServer: true` AND `remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand: true`.
findings.detail: Test-plan issue #6221 (2022-01-25): set `remote.SSH.useLocalServer` to true and `remote.SSH.enableRemoteCommand` to true, then "Edit your SSH config for your remote to include RemoteCommand field" and verify the terminal starts under that command. No OpenSSH version or ProxyJump caveat stated there.

findings.claim: `remote.SSH.serverInstallPath` is a host->absolute-path map and, since VS Code 1.86, does not expand `${HOME}` or `~`; use it to move ~/.vscode-server off the Panasas home onto CephFS.
findings.detail: Issue #9474: "Prior to VSCode 1.86.0, I've been using ${HOME} in my remote.SSH.serverInstallPath without any problem"; with ${HOME} or ~ the extension creates a literal directory; absolute paths such as /home/alice work; labels info-needed/ssh, assigned roblourens, closed not planned. Issue #8065 (how the key is matched: alias vs FQDN) received no maintainer answer.

findings.claim: An HPC centre's published Remote-SSH-to-Slurm recipe: ProxyJump through the login host to a node obtained with salloc, connectTimeout raised to 60 s, reconnection attempts 0, and no VS Code Server on login nodes.
findings.detail:
MIT ORCD (page dated 2026-02-12) ssh config: `Host orcd-login
  HostName orcd-login.mit.edu
  User USERNAME

Host orcd-compute
  User USERNAME
  HostName nodename
  ProxyJump orcd-login`; obtain a node with `salloc -t 1:00:00 -p mit_normal`, find it with `hostname` or `squeue --me`; settings "Remote.SSH: Connect Timeout — Set to 60 seconds" and "Remote.SSH: Max Reconnection Attempts — Set to 0"; "Avoid running VSCode through RemoteSSH on the login nodes."

findings.claim: Since VS Code 1.99 the prebuilt VS Code Server requires glibc >= 2.28; CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17) is listed as unsupported, and the only official escape is the custom-glibc/patchelf workaround, which is declared unsupported.
findings.detail: FAQ: "Starting with VS Code release 1.99 (March 2025), the prebuilt servers distributed by VS Code are only compatible with Linux distributions that are based on glibc 2.28 or later." Requirements: "kernel >= 4.18, glibc >=2.28, libstdc++ >= 3.4.25, binutils >= 2.29". Variables: VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER "path to the dynamic linker in the sysroot"; VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_PATH "path to the library locations in the sysroot"; VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH "path to the patchelf binary on the remote host". "patchelf v0.17.x is known to cause segfaults with the remote server, we recommend using patchelf >=v0.18.x". "This approach is a technical workaround and is not an officially supported usage scenario." "VS Code will show a dialog and banner message about the connection not being supported." The FAQ does not say which shell file must export them. linux.md marks "❌ CentOS 7 Server (64-bit)" and "❌ RedHat Enterprise Linux 7 (64-bit)".

findings.claim: Mechanism: the server's requirements check is skipped whenever VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER is non-empty (or /tmp/vscode-skip-server-requirements-check exists), and the launcher patchelf's only the `node` binary — rpath first, interpreter second — with no LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
findings.detail: check-requirements-linux.sh: `if [ -f "/tmp/vscode-skip-server-requirements-check" ] || [ -n "$VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER" ]` -> warnings, exit 0; otherwise MIN_GLIBCXX_VERSION="3.4.25", glibc "2.28", "Warning: Missing GLIBC >= 2.28!", "Error: Missing required dependencies..." exit 99. code-server-linux.sh: `if [ -n "$VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER" ] && [ -n "$VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_PATH" ] && [ -n "$VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH" ]; then "$VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH" --set-rpath "$VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_PATH" "$ROOT/node"; "$VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH" --set-interpreter "$VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER" "$ROOT/node"; echo "Patching complete."; fi`. Because /tmp on the grid is swept, the marker-file route is not durable; the env-var route is.

findings.claim: The env-var workaround shipped with VS Code 1.99 (PR #235232 'build: remove legacy server support', merged 2025-03-10, milestone March 2025); 1.98 was the last release with a legacy (glibc 2.17) server.
findings.detail: PR #235232 introduced the three variables and the patchelf --set-interpreter/--set-rpath calls with the comment that "the order of the calls matter otherwise it can lead to corrupted binaries". Remote release notes v1_98 (Remote-SSH 0.118.0): "VS Code release v1.98 (February 2025) is the last release that supports Linux servers with glibc < 2.28 or libstdc++ < 3.4.25. As of release 1.99, you can no longer connect to these servers." v1_97 (Remote-SSH 0.117.0) pre-announced it. 1.99 release notes: "users that require additional time to complete migration to a supported Linux distro can provide custom builds of glibc and libstdc++ as a workaround." Dev Containers does not honour the variables (vscode-remote-release #10822, closed not planned).

findings.claim: Where the variables must be exported is undocumented and is the known failure point: a 1.99.2 user with them in ~/.bashrc and useExecServer=true still got exit 207 / 'found GLIBC 2.27'; community guides split between ~/.bashrc and ~/.bash_profile.
findings.detail: Issue #246375 (VS Code 1.99.2, 2025-04-10 build): vars VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER/PATH and VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH in ~/.bashrc; settings remote.SSH.useExecServer = true, remote.SSH.useLocalServer = false; log "find GLIBC >= v2.28.0 (but found v2.27.0 instead)", exit code 207; closed not planned, no fix. dev.to guide (2025-04-15): "For the bash shell, add the above lines to the remote ~/.bash_profile. For the zsh shell, add them to ~/.zprofile." hsfzxjy/vscode-remote-glibc-patch: "modify ~/.bashrc/~/.bash_profile (for yourself only) or /etc/bashrc//etc/profile (for all users)" via `eval "$(your/custom/path/init.sh)"`; requires "VSCode 1.99". physicsuniverse/vscode-centos7-remote-patcher targets "CentOS 7.9 (Core)", glibc 2.28+ from AlmaLinux 8 repos, "No root access required - all operations are in user space".

findings.claim: Red Hat-family bash is compiled with SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC, so ~/.bashrc is sourced even for non-interactive ssh commands — which is how Remote-SSH's install script runs — provided the exports precede any interactive-only `return` guard.
findings.detail: CentOS Stream bash.spec: `Patch107: bash-3.2-ssh_source_bash.patch` with comment "# Source bashrc file when bash is run under ssh." and changelog "- Enabling #define SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC, because ssh changed. Resolves: #458839" (2008). The el7 spec itself could not be fetched (git.centos.org archive 404), so this is inferred from the shared Fedora/RHEL lineage; verify with `ssh <node> 'echo $VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER'`.

findings.claim: @vscode/test-cli is 0.0.15 and @vscode/test-electron is 3.1.0; both require Node >= 22; config is `.vscode-test.(js|mjs|cjs)` with defineConfig.
findings.detail: registry.npmjs.org: @vscode/test-cli "version": "0.0.15", "engines": {"node": ">=22"}, "bin": {"vscode-test": "out/bin.mjs"}, deps mocha ^11.7.6, c8 ^11.0.0; @vscode/test-electron "version": "3.1.0", engines ">=22". Testing doc: `npm install --save-dev @vscode/test-cli @vscode/test-electron`; defineConfig options files (required), version (defaults to `stable`), workspaceFolder, extensionDevelopmentPath, mocha, launchArgs; multiple configs filtered with `vscode-test --label unitTests`; README options also env, useInstallation, installExtensions, skipExtensionDependencies, download, platform, label, srcDir; flags --label, --coverage, --watch, --code-version.

findings.claim: There is no headless mode on Windows: the official CI recipe uses xvfb-run only on Linux and runs `npm test` bare on windows-latest; @vscode/test-electron downloads a full VS Code (platform 'win32-x64-archive') into .vscode-test and launches its window.
findings.detail: continuous-integration.md GitHub Actions: `strategy: matrix: os: [macos-latest, ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]`; `- run: xvfb-run -a npm test\n  if: runner.os == 'Linux'`; `- run: npm test\n  if: runner.os != 'Linux'`. vscode-test README: runTests({ extensionDevelopmentPath, extensionTestsPath, launchArgs, version ('1.36.1' | 'insiders'), platform e.g. 'win32-x64-archive', vscodeExecutablePath, extensionTestsEnv }); downloads cached in ".vscode-test"; Linux requires "xvfb-run". Testing doc: pass `--disable-extensions` in launchArgs to keep other installed extensions out of the test host.

findings.claim: SSH FS (Kelvin.vscode-sshfs) needs no server-side install, supports ProxyJump-style hops, and is still maintained: v1.27.0 was published 2026-06-07 and the repo is not archived.
findings.detail: Marketplace: "File system, terminal and task provider using SSH", 789,682 installs, publisher Kelvin Schoofs; features: SSH hopping, HTTP/SOCKS 4/5 proxies, private key, agent, remote terminals and `ssh-shell` tasks. README: "SSH Hop refers to using another configuration to hop through, similar to OpenSSH's ProxyJump". GitHub API: latest release tag_name "v1.27.0", published_at "2026-06-07T22:39:35Z" ("Update from patched ssh2@^1.11.0 to ssh@^1.17.0", "Removed the OPENSSH-SHA1 flag"); repo pushed_at 2026-06-07T22:37:18Z, open_issues_count 78, archived false, 618 stars. Earlier 1.26.1 (2024-04-16) patched for "OpenSSH 8.8+ disabling ssh-rsa by default". Because it is a FileSystemProvider it has no remote extension host, so no Claude Code extension, debugger or language server runs on the node.

findings.claim: Windows OpenSSH client install/check commands and key locations; ssh-keygen defaults to Ed25519; ssh-agent is a Windows service.
findings.detail: `Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object Name -like 'OpenSSH*'` returns `OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0` / `OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0`; install `Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0`. Overview table: "Windows 10 build 1809 + | Not installed, install and enable using optional features" (doc dated 2025-02-20). Key doc (2025-10-03): "If you don't specify an algorithm, Ed25519 is used"; default path `C:\Users\username/.ssh/id_ecdsa`; `Get-Service ssh-agent | Set-Service -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service ssh-agent; ssh-add $env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ecdsa`. Inbox version on 24H2 reported by users as `OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p2, LibreSSL 3.8.2` (search snippets only; verify with `ssh -V`).

findings.claim: Windows OpenSSH enforces NTFS ACLs on private keys and on ~/.ssh/config: only the owner (plus SYSTEM/Administrators) may have access; VS Code's documented fix is `icacls "privateKeyPath" /grant <username>:R`.
findings.detail: Win32-OpenSSH wiki: "User's private keys are user's credentials. To prevent unauthorized access to these files, private keys need to be owned by the user and no other user should have access to user's key files." ssh_config has "similar restrictions as the user's private keys". Repair helpers: FixUserFilePermissions.ps1 ("fix permissions of client side files": ~/.ssh/config, id_rsa...), module functions Repair-UserKeyPermission, Repair-UserSshConfigPermission. VS Code troubleshooting.md: "For Windows, run the following command in PowerShell to grant explicit read access to your username: icacls "privateKeyPath" /grant <username>:R". A safer full form seen in the field is `icacls .\id_ed25519 /inheritance:r /grant:r "%username%:R"` (search results, not an official page).

findings.claim: ProxyJump is native OpenSSH syntax (`[user@]host[:port]`, comma-separated hops) and is mutually exclusive with ProxyCommand; on Windows, a ProxyCommand must name `ssh.exe` (full path is the safe form) but ProxyJump avoids the issue.
findings.detail: ssh_config(5): ProxyJump takes "one or more jump proxies as either [user@]host[:port] or an ssh URI. Multiple proxies may be separated by comma characters and will be visited sequentially"; ProxyJump and ProxyCommand are mutually exclusive (whichever appears first wins). Imperial College post (2025-03-03): "If you are on Windows, you might need to replace ssh inside the ProxyCommand with ssh.exe depending on which is available in your shell." VS Code troubleshooting.md: "you may need to use the ProxyCommand parameter for your host in a local SSH config file".

findings.claim: `MACs +hmac-sha1` is NOT needed for CentOS 7.9's sshd: hmac-sha2-256/512 have been default in both ssh and sshd since OpenSSH 5.9, and the modern client's default MAC list still contains hmac-sha1 anyway.
findings.detail: OpenSSH 5.9 release notes: "Add new SHA256-based HMAC transport integrity modes... These modes are hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-256-96, hmac-sha2-512, and hmac-sha2-512-96, and are available by default in ssh(1) and sshd(8)". Current ssh_config(5) default MACs: "umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha1-etm@openssh.com,umac-64@openssh.com,umac-128@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha1". CentOS 7.9 ships openssh-7.4p1-22.el7_9 (package index seen in search results; not fetched).

findings.claim: `+ssh-rsa` is also not needed: OpenSSH 8.8+ clients disable only RSA/SHA-1 signatures, and RSA/SHA-256/512 has been supported since OpenSSH 7.2, so a 9.x Windows client negotiates rsa-sha2-* with a 7.4 CentOS 7 sshd; ssh-rsa is absent from the client's default HostKeyAlgorithms.
findings.detail: OpenSSH 8.8 notes: "This release disables RSA signatures using the SHA-1 hash algorithm by default"; "existing ssh-rsa keys will automatically use the stronger algorithm where possible" (RFC 8332 RSA/SHA-256/512, supported "since release 7.2"); legacy directives `HostkeyAlgorithms +ssh-rsa` / `PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms +ssh-rsa`. OpenSSH 7.2 notes: "all: add support for RSA signatures using SHA-256/512 hash algorithms". ssh_config(5) default HostKeyAlgorithms includes rsa-sha2-512/rsa-sha2-256 and not ssh-rsa. Microsoft troubleshooting (2026-02-12) lists the same `+ssh-rsa` lines only as the fix for "Unable to negotiate with <server>: no matching host key type found" against truly legacy peers and recommends "stronger algorithms such as ED25519 or ECDSA".

topics_verified.recommendation: Build Ashley as a Node-22 toolchain project (vsce 4.0.0, test-cli 0.0.15, test-electron 3.1.0), bundle with esbuild (external: ['vscode']) and package with `vsce package --no-dependencies`. Declare `"extensionKind": ["ui"]` explicitly — with a `main` entry and no declaration VS Code deduces `['workspace']` and would install Ashley onto the compute node's server. Declare `"extensionDependencies": ["ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh"]` and ship through the Marketplace (dependencies are resolved from the gallery); for VSIX side-loads, install Remote-SSH first. Keep all five credentials in `context.secrets` (laptop-side safeStorage; on Linux/WSL guard against the basic_text fallback) and never in settings.json. Inject `HF_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` etc. via `context.environmentVariableCollection` with `persistent=true` and a `description`; source inspection says a UI extension's collection is applied to remote terminals too, but verify on the first Remote-SSH window (and check whether the hover reveals values) before relying on it. Open the compute-node window with `vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.openFolder', Uri.parse('vscode-remote://ssh-remote+<accessid>@<node>/<path>'), {forceNewWindow:true})` (or `vscode.newWindow` with `remoteAuthority`), not the undocumented `opensshremotes.*` commands; write a `Host wsu-node-*` block with `ProxyJump warrior.grid.wayne.edu` into `%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config` (or a file named by `remote.SSH.configFile`), set `remote.SSH.remotePlatform` to linux for those hosts, raise `remote.SSH.connectTimeout` to 60, and set `remote.SSH.serverInstallPath` to an absolute CephFS path (no `${HOME}`/`~`). For glibc 2.17 the design must assume the unsupported-workaround path: Ashley's grid bootstrap should install patchelf >= 0.18 and a glibc-2.28 sysroot in user space, export the three `VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_*` variables in BOTH `~/.bashrc` (above any interactive-return guard) and `~/.bash_profile`, verify with `ssh node 'echo $VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER'`, try `remote.SSH.useExecServer=false` if the banner still reports the prerequisite failure, and pin the student's VS Code version in the docs since the workaround is officially unsupported; keep SSH FS as the documented fallback for file editing because it needs no server binary. Do not add `MACs +hmac-sha1` or `+ssh-rsa` to the Windows config; generate Ed25519 keys, fix ACLs with `icacls <key> /inheritance:r /grant:r "<user>:R"`, and load them into the Windows ssh-agent service. Run integration tests on windows-latest without xvfb (an interactive session is present) and on Linux with `xvfb-run -a`.
open_questions: Exact argument shape (if any) of `opensshremotes.openEmptyWindow` and of `remote-explorer.connectToRemoteInNewWindow`: both closed-source and undocumented; only `vscode.openFolder`/`vscode.newWindow` are confirmed.

Does the terminal hover for an extension env contribution display the variable VALUE (which would show a token on screen)? environmentVariableInfo.ts only renders `extensionName: description`; the mutator-level strings were not found and should be checked in a live window.

Which shell file Remote-SSH's non-interactive install shell reads on CentOS 7.9: the Red Hat SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC patch was confirmed in the c9s spec but the el7 spec and the GNU bash manual could not be fetched; issue #246375 shows ~/.bashrc failing for one 1.99.2 user with useExecServer=true. Needs an empirical test on warrior and on a compute node.
How `remote.SSH.serverInstallPath` keys are matched (ssh-config alias vs resolved hostname) — issue #8065 was never answered by maintainers; with per-job node names a wildcard may not work.

The default of `remote.SSH.connectTimeout` (15 s per HPC-centre pages and issues) and the semantics of `remote.SSH.lockfilesInTmp` on a node whose /tmp is swept were seen only in search snippets, not fetched official pages.

Whether patching only `$ROOT/node` suffices for all native components of the current server (node-pty spawn-helper, @parcel/watcher, ripgrep) on glibc 2.17 with kernel 5.15 — the FAQ claims it works but community reports include unresolved failures.
The inbox OpenSSH version on the students' Windows 11 builds (users report OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p2 on 24H2) and whether WSU's warrior sshd has been hardened away from OpenSSH 7.4 defaults.

Whether a Marketplace install of Ashley in a window that is already Remote-SSH-connected installs Remote-SSH locally as expected, and what happens on a machine without Marketplace access (VSIX side-load).
SSH FS marketplace 'last updated' could not be read from the listing; GitHub API dates (2026-06-07) are the basis for the maintenance claim.

topics_verified.topic: Xcode as a second host for the Ashley tool: Xcode 26.x/27 agentic coding, Source Editor Extension limits, Claude Code/Agent SDK in Xcode, and porting strategies (as of 2026-09-27)
topics_verified.summary: Xcode 26.3 (RC 2026-02-03, macOS Sequoia 15.6+) added agentic coding with Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI Codex built in, and exposed Xcode's own tools to any external agent over MCP via `xcrun mcpbridge`; Anthropic confirmed the in-Xcode agent runs on the Claude Agent SDK ("the same underlying harness that powers Claude Code", with subagents, background tasks and plugins). Xcode 26.6 (17F113, 2026-06-25) added Gemini and the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) so any ACP-speaking agent can be added via Intelligence > Agents > "Add an Agent"; Xcode 27 (27A266a, 2026-09-14, macOS Tahoe 26.6+, Apple silicon only) added agent plug-ins that bundle skills, MCP servers and ACP agent configurations, a filesystem security layer, and a preview `xcrun mcp-server` that works without an open workspace. Xcode has no general extension API for third-party wizards or commands: the only sanctioned extension point is the Source Editor Extension, which Apple documents as able to "read and modify the contents of a source file" and the selection, invoked from the Editor menu, one file at a time, sandboxed, no UI; tools like Copilot for Xcode escape this only through a non-sandboxed XPC service plus the Accessibility permission. Claude Code's official docs have no Xcode page (only VS Code and JetBrains), Xcode has no integrated terminal in any 26.3–27 release note, and Apple's documented path is to run Claude Code in Terminal.app and give it Xcode's tools with `claude mcp add --transport stdio xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge`. Custom MCP servers for Xcode's built-in Claude Agent are configured only via files under `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig` (community-verified filename `.claude.json`, project-keyed `mcpServers`), not via the CLI's `~/.claude.json`, and Apple says these "only affect agents when you launch them in Xcode". Two Anthropic terms findings shape the design: the Agent SDK docs say third parties may not offer claude.ai login unless approved, and since 2026-06-15 subscription plans get only a small monthly Agent SDK credit ($20 Pro, $100/$200 Max) that also covers `claude -p`, so the persistent grid-side process should be the interactive `claude` CLI with a real `/login`, not an SDK or `-p` harness. Claude Code does not speak ACP natively (anthropics/claude-code#6686 closed as not planned); the maintained adapter is `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`. The realistic Xcode port is a Developer-ID-signed, notarized Swift `MenuBarExtra` app embedding the shared TypeScript core compiled with `bun build --compile`, which (a) runs the credential/SSH/Slurm wizard, (b) registers an "ashley" MCP server for Xcode's Claude Agent and as an Xcode 27 plug-in, and (c) exposes the grid session as an ACP agent added through "Add an Agent" (26.6+). Shortcuts/Automator are viable only as launchers (`shortcuts run`), not as a credential UI.

findings.claim: Xcode 26.3 introduced agentic coding with Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex built in, plus MCP exposure of Xcode capabilities, and requires macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later.
findings.detail: Release notes: "Xcode 26.3 introduces support for agentic coding ... powered by coding agents from Anthropic and OpenAI ... In addition to Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex integrations, Xcode 26.3 makes its capabilities available through the Model Context Protocol" (169448160); "a comprehensive permissions system that gives you fine-grained control over what external agentic coding tools can do" (170740647); "Xcode 26.3 requires a Mac running macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later." Apple newsroom: RC "available as a release candidate for all members of the Apple Developer Program starting today" (Feb 3, 2026).

verdict.corrected_claim: Xcode 26.3 introduced agentic coding with Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex built in, plus MCP exposure of Xcode capabilities, and requires macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: claim HELD on every point; all quoted fragments and reference numbers verified verbatim against Apple's own pages. critical=false for the Ashley design (Xcode is macOS-only; our target is VS Code on Windows 11/WSL -> Linux grid), but the Anthropic-side facts below are useful analogues.

1) RELEASE NOTES (fetched https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes/xcode-26_3-release-notes.md; the non-.md HTML URL is a JS shell that returns only the title, so cite the .md URL). Verbatim, under "Coding Intelligence > New Features":
- "Xcode 26.3 introduces support for agentic coding, a new way in Xcode for developers to build apps, powered by coding agents from Anthropic and OpenAI. ... In addition to Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex integrations, Xcode 26.3 makes its capabilities available through the Model Context Protocol, an open standard that gives developers the flexibility to use any compatible agent or tool with Xcode." (169448160) -- matches claim.
- "Xcode 26.3 introduces a comprehensive permissions system that gives you fine-grained control over what external agentic coding tools can do in your development environment." (170740647) -- matches claim.
- Overview: "Xcode 26.3 requires a Mac running macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later." -- matches claim. Also: "Xcode 26.3 includes Swift 6.2.3 and SDKs for iOS 26.2, iPadOS 26.2, tvOS 26.2, macOS 26.2, and visionOS 26.2."
- Related verbatim items showing the Anthropic integration is the Claude Code CLI under the hood: "Fixed: Resolved agent indicator not showing if Claude CLI was launched before opening a project. (170492975)"; "Fixed: Added support for Claude 4.6. (170562239)"; "Fixed: Upgraded to Codex version 0.98.0 for improved stability and features. (170586680)"; "Fixed OpenCode compatibility for accepting MCP responses from Xcode. (170565579)"; Known issue 166387271: denying Claude/Codex access to Desktop/Downloads/Documents cannot be reversed in-app.

2) macOS REQUIREMENT cross-check (fetched https://developer.apple.com/support/xcode/): table row "Xcode 26.3 — Minimum macOS Required: macOS Sequoia 15.6 - macOS Tahoe 26.x". verdict.corrected_claim: The in-Xcode Claude Agent (Xcode 26.3, announced 2026-02-03) is built on the Claude Agent SDK, "the same underlying harness that powers Claude Code," with subagents, background tasks and plugins — that half holds verbatim. The second half is wrong as stated: Xcode is not closed to third-party code. The same Anthropic article says Xcode 26.3 "also makes its capabilities available through the Model Context Protocol" so "Developers using Claude Code can integrate with Xcode over MCP"; Apple documents the exact mechanism (`claude mcp add --transport stdio xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge`, after turning on "Allow external agents to use Xcode tools" in Intelligence settings) and calls it "external agents, that you launch outside of Xcode." What remains true is narrow: Apple publishes no API for third-party code to script the bundled Claude Agent itself; it is configured only through files in `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig`, and "These configurations only affect agents when you launch them in Xcode." The claim is also version-specific and now outdated: Xcode 27 (current as of 2026-09-27) "adds support for the Agent Client protocol," lets you "Add an Agent" for any ACP agent, ships plugins with "ACP agent configurations," adds Google Gemini and Antigravity to the coding assistant, and adds `sudo xcrun mcp-server enable [--unsafe-always-allow-all-agents]` for unattended use. Enablement steps exist in Apple's docs (Intelligence settings > Agents > Get > Install; Account row > (…) > sign in); plan requirements for the Agent are stated nowhere I could find, though the Sep 2025 Claude-in-Xcode chat integration was limited to "all plans that include Claude Code—Pro and Max, plus premium seats for Team and Enterprise plans."
