verdict.corrected_claim: Apple's page "Extending and customizing agents" (undated, copyright 2026) says the agent-specific folders under ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant (ClaudeAgentConfig, codex, gemini) let you "customize agents beyond the options available in Intelligence settings and the coding assistant" (e.g. set a default model, add MCP servers, create skills) and that "These configurations only affect agents when you launch them in Xcode." They are NOT the only route: the default model is also a "Model" row in the Claude Agent pane of Intelligence settings, and MCP servers and skills can also be added by installing plug-ins (Intelligence > Agents > Plug-ins row > Add Plug-in > "choose an import option", one of which is "Add from URL"). The Plug-ins row, ACP agents and the gemini folder are Xcode 27 features (Xcode 27 release notes 178289210, 178294840, 171990272; Xcode 27 is still an RC dated 2026-09-09 and requires macOS Tahoe 26.6); Xcode 26.3 (2026-02-26) shipped only Claude Agent and Codex plus the permissions system (170740647). The Permissions row (Allowed Commands +/-, Allowed Tools -) is as stated. The isolation is bidirectional: the in-Xcode Claude agent runs with its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and does not read ~/.claude (Apple Product Manager, forum thread 814959; anthropics/claude-code#22996 closed not-planned; Hacking with Swift 2026-03-11). Apple names no file names; third-party sources use ClaudeAgentConfig/.claude.json for MCP servers, ClaudeAgentConfig/settings.json for the model, ClaudeAgentConfig/skills/ and /commands/, and codex/config.toml.

verdict.corrected_claim: Confirmed (Apple docs + Apple staff on forums + community): Xcode launches its bundled Claude Agent (stock Claude Code CLI) via `xcrun mcpbridge run-agent claude` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig`, so it uses `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig/.claude.json` (third-party MCP servers, community-documented under `"projects": {"/abs/project/path": {"mcpServers": {...}}}`, i.e. Claude Code's local scope; a root-level `mcpServers` = user scope is valid per the CLI schema but untested in Xcode), `ClaudeAgentConfig/skills`, `ClaudeAgentConfig/commands`, `ClaudeAgentConfig/settings.json`, `ClaudeAgentConfig/debug/latest`. Apple: the folder is one "that Xcode uses exclusively" and "These configurations only affect agents when you launch them in Xcode"; an Apple Product Manager: Claude Agent in Xcode uses "a specific config.json file, different from a global json file" from a prior Claude Code install. So Xcode does not read `~/.claude.json` or `~/.claude/*`; copying `~/.claude/settings.json` into `ClaudeAgentConfig/` (Apple forum user tip) carries CLI settings over. Restart: close/reopen Xcode (or at least the Claude chat panel); Apple's 26.3 release notes give "Relaunch Xcode" as the workaround for agent settings not being respected. Version-specific details to drop or date: "2.1.14" was the CLI bundled with the Xcode 26.3 RC (Fatbobman, 2026-02-06; CLI 2.1.14 released 2026-01-20), not necessarily 26.3 GA (whose release notes add Claude 4.6 support, which Fatbobman says needed CLI 2.1.32); the binary path `Agents/Versions/26.3/claude` changed in Xcode 27.0 to `Agents/XcodeVersions/<build>/claude/claude` (gist, re-verified 2026-06-16); the "custom commands do not appear in / autocomplete" note is a Feb-2026 26.3 observation, and Apple's 26.3 known issue 169214412 says direct "/skill" invocation "can be rejected" (workaround: "use the {skill-name} skill"). Fatbobman's article itself writes the path as `ClaudeAgentConfig/.claude` (no `.json`, zero occurrences of `.claude.json` in the page); the gist's `.claude.json` is the correct filename.

verdict.corrected_claim: On macOS with Xcode 26.3 or later (Xcode 26.3 requires macOS Sequoia 15.6+; 26.4–26.6 require macOS Tahoe 26.2+; Xcode 27 requires macOS Tahoe 26.6+), external agents get Xcode's MCP tools by turning on "Allow external agents to use Xcode tools" under Xcode > Settings > Intelligence > Model Context Protocol and registering the stdio bridge with `claude mcp add --transport stdio xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge` (Claude Code) or `codex mcp add xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge` (Codex); verify with `claude mcp list` / `codex mcp list`. Apple names only Claude Code and Codex on the page (release notes also mention OpenCode compatibility fixes); "Cursor" is not named by Apple, though the release notes describe MCP as usable by "any compatible agent or tool". With `xcrun mcpbridge`, the project must be open in Xcode and Xcode alerts you when the agent connects and is active. This open-workspace requirement is version-specific: Xcode 27 (Beta 5 onward) adds a preview MCP server enabled with `sudo xcrun mcp-server enable` (status: `xcrun mcp-server status`; unattended: `sudo xcrun mcp-server enable --unsafe-always-allow-all-agents`) that "runs without requiring an open Xcode workspace". Hints go in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. Note `claude mcp add` defaults to local scope (~/.claude.json, current project only), so run it in the project directory or pass `--scope user`. Irrelevant to the Ashley design: xcrun/mcpbridge exist only on macOS, not on Windows/WSL or the CentOS 7.9 grid.

verdict.corrected_claim: Xcode 27 (GA; requires macOS Tahoe 26.6+) adds "Agent Plug-ins" containing skills, MCP servers and ACP agent configurations (178289210). The only Apple-published example of the plug-in JSON (release note 178470032) has top-level `name`/`description`/`version`/`mcpServers`, and each server entry has `"type": "http"`, `"url"`, `"tools": ["*"]` and an optional `"_meta"` block with `ideToolIconPath`, `ideToolIconRendersAsTemplate` and `ideToolTitles`. Apple documents NO `command`/stdio server form, never calls the file a "manifest", never names the file or its on-disk layout, and publishes no schema page. The top-level shape mirrors Claude Code's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, but `tools` and `_meta` on a server entry are Apple-specific and are not fields in Claude Code's plugin/MCP server schema, so compatibility between an Xcode plug-in and a Claude Code plugin is unstated by either vendor. The documented install path is UI-only: Xcode > Settings > Intelligence > Agents > Plug-ins > "Add Plug-in" > choose an import option (e.g. "Add from URL") > select components > Install. The docs page is `/documentation/Xcode/extending-and-customizing-agents` (section "Install agentic coding plug-ins"), not `extending-and-customizing-coding-intelligence` (404); the real index is `/documentation/Xcode/coding-intelligence`. ACP support (178294840) already shipped in Xcode 26.6; only plug-ins and `_meta` are Xcode-27-new. Xcode 27.1 beta and 27.2 beta notes change nothing here. For an "ashley" MCP server this is a macOS-only side channel: it cannot serve the Windows 11 + WSL student laptops the design targets, and the documented external-agent path (`claude mcp add --transport stdio xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge`) runs in the opposite direction (Xcode as MCP server to an external Claude Code).

[5] Claude Code schema comparison (critical=false). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md: manifest is ".claude-plugin/plugin.json"; top-level fields include `name` (only required key), `displayName`, `version`, `description`, `author`, `mcpServers` ("Path, object, or array of either — .json MCP config files, .mcpb or .dxt bundles, or inline server configs keyed by name"); inline example `{"deploy-api":{"command":"node","args":["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/server.js"]}}`; MCP validation "require Claude Code v2.1.281 or later". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md "Plugin-provided MCP servers": server fields are `type` (stdio/http/sse/ws), `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `headers`, `headersHelper`, `oauth`, `timeout`, `alwaysLoad`; a per-server `"tools"` key is NOT present; `_meta` appears only on tool definitions in tools/list responses (`"_meta": {"anthropic/maxResultSizeChars": 200000}`), not on server config; `ideToolIconPath` not present. Conclusion: Apple's top-level shape equals plugin.json's, but `tools` and `_meta` per server are Apple extensions; neither vendor states that an Xcode plug-in and a Claude Code plugin are interchangeable.

Xcode is macOS-only and the design's stated local environment is Windows 11 + WSL Ubuntu with VS Code 1.139, so an Xcode agent plug-in cannot be the distribution vehicle for the student population; at most it is an optional macOS side channel.

findings.claim: Xcode's 'Add an Agent' (ACP) sheet takes a display name, an absolute path to the agent executable, and arguments; Xcode does not expand ~ or use the shell PATH; the model cannot be switched from Xcode's UI for third-party ACP agents.
findings.detail: Devin docs (third-party ACP agent in Xcode): requires "Xcode 26.6 or later"; fields Name, Command ("the absolute path to your `devin` binary ... for example `/Users/you/.local/bin/devin`"), Arguments (e.g. `acp --model <name>`); "Xcode requires an absolute path—it does not expand `~` or use your shell's `PATH`"; "The model can't be switched from Xcode's UI." verdict.corrected_claim: Xcode's sheet is titled "Add an ACP Agent" (Xcode > Settings > Intelligence > Agents > "Add an Agent"; ACP support shipped in Xcode 26.6, 17F113, 2026-06-25, and remains in Xcode 27). Apple's own screenshot shows FOUR fields, not three: "Name" (placeholder "My Agent"), "Executable" (placeholder "/absolute/path/to/agent" — Devin's docs call this field "Command", which is not its label), "Interpreter" ("Optional — Specify an interpreter if the executable is a script. The interpreter runs the executable as its argument."), and "Arguments". The sheet is cropped below "Arguments" in Apple's screenshot and Apple's text says only "enter information in the next sheet", so whether an environment-variables field exists is UNKNOWN, not established-absent. The absolute-path requirement is corroborated by Apple's placeholder; the specific statements that Xcode "does not expand ~ or use your shell's PATH" appear only in Devin's docs (Apple is silent) and are consistent with, but not proven by, the existence of the Interpreter field. "The model can't be switched from Xcode's UI" is Devin's statement about Devin in Xcode; Apple documents a "Model" dropdown only for the built-in Claude Agent, and does not say whether its ACP client implements ACP's session/set_config_option model selector, so the generalisation to all third-party ACP agents is unverified. Devin's own workaround is `acp --model <name>` in Arguments (equivalently env `DEVIN_MODEL`).

(178289210)" — i.e., since Xcode 27 an ACP agent can also be registered via an Agent Plug-in, not only the sheet (details of that config format not documented on the fetched pages). Xcode 27.1 beta notes: no ACP mentions.

4. Model switching — DEVIN-SPECIFIC, UNVERIFIED AS GENERAL. Devin verbatim: "The model can't be switched from Xcode's UI. To use something other than your team's default model, pass `--model <name>` in the agent's **Arguments** field … which sets the model for every session Xcode starts." Devin command reference (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/commands): `devin acp` flags `--agent-type <TYPE>`, `--model <MODEL>` (env `DEVIN_MODEL`, "Default model for every new ACP session, overriding the enterprise-configured default"); credentials from `WINDSURF_API_KEY` or `devin auth login`; description names "Windsurf or Zed" as ACP clients. Apple's built-in Claude Agent settings screenshot (https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/images/com.apple.Xcode/intelligence-settings-claude-agent@2x.png; alt "showing the Model and Account rows") shows a "Model: Default" dropdown and "Sign in to a Claude.ai account, or provide an API Key to use Claude Agent up to your limit." — built-in agents only. ACP spec: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-config-options — "Agents can provide an arbitrary list of configuration options for a session, allowing Clients to offer users customizable selectors for things like models, modes, reasoning levels, and more." via `session/set_config_option`; "Session Config Options supersede the older Session Modes API" (`session/set_mode`, https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-modes). Whether Xcode's ACP client renders config options is not stated in any Apple page fetched. Apple's "Extending and customizing agents" (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/extending-and-customizing-agents): for built-in agents "you can set a default model" via files under `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig`, `…/codex`, `…/gemini` — "These configurations only affect agents when you launch them in Xcode."

5. Other exact strings from the Devin page (Troubleshooting): `xcrun: error: unable to find utility "mcpbridge"` → `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer` ; `sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch` ; verify `xcrun --find mcpbridge`. Requires "Allow external agents to use Xcode tools" (Apple: Intelligence settings > Model Context Protocol; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/giving-external-agents-access-to-xcode, which also gives `claude mcp add --transport stdio xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge`). Devin limitations: "Xcode's coding assistant does not surface Devin's slash commands."

6. Negative checks: https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/clients does not list Xcode among ACP clients (Zed, JetBrains, neovim, VS Code, Sublime, Qt Creator, Emacs, Obsidian, Unity, Visual Studio, Pulsar). Claude Code docs index https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt has no Xcode or ACP page (only vs-code.md, jetbrains.md); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/xcode → HTTP 404. Zed's Claude ACP adapter is npm `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` (https://github.com/zed-industries/claude-code-acp; README has no Xcode mention and no model env var). https://opencode.ai/docs/xcode/ → 404 (no second vendor corroboration obtained).

Feature request anthropics/claude-code#6686 (opened 2025-08-27) was NOT closed by an Anthropic decision: github-actions[bot] auto-closed it on 2026-02-09 for 60 days of inactivity (state_reason "not_planned"), no Anthropic member ever commented, and a successor request #24411 (opened 2026-02-09) remains OPEN with no Anthropic reply as of 2026-09-27. The maintained bridge is @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp (latest 0.81.2 published 2026-09-24; preview 0.81.3-preview.1; bin `claude-agent-acp`; pins @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.280 and @agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.5.0; Apache-2.0; maintained by Zed staff), created 2026-03-26 as the rename of @zed-industries/claude-code-acp (last version 0.16.2, 2026-02-17; all 73 versions deprecated with "This package has been renamed to @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp. The README's `npm install @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@preview` is the PREVIEW channel ("changes that have landed on `main` but are not released yet"); the stable install is `npm install @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`. Also: the Agent SDK is "A library that runs the Claude Code binary" — the adapter therefore needs Node.js AND the Claude Code binary inside the Singularity image (host has no node.js; container must supply it).
- Implication for Ashley: driving a student's Pro/Max subscription through claude-agent-acp makes Ashley a third-party SDK product offering claude.ai login (disallowed unless approved; Zed/JetBrains are presumably approved partners). Running the real `claude` CLI in the container, with the student logging in themselves (`claude auth login` / `claude setup-token`, both in the CLI reference), is the surface that legitimately uses a Pro/Max subscription. Choose between: (i) ACP via adapter + API key, or (ii) plain Claude Code CLI + subscription with a non-ACP prompt channel (e.g. `--input-format stream-json`/`--output-format stream-json`, `claude remote-control`, or `claude attach`).

- https://agentclientprotocol.com/overview/clients: Anycode; Chrome ACP; ACP Sidebar; Emacs (agent-shell.el); Exo for VSCode; JetBrains; Neovim (CodeCompanion, agentic.nvim, avante.nvim, hermes.nvim); Obsidian (4 plugins); Open Knowledge; Pulsar; Qt Creator; Sublime Text; Unity; Visual Studio (Poolside Assistant); Visual Studio Code — "ACP Client", "ACP Patchbay", "ACP Pro Extension" (also Cursor/Windsurf/Trae via Open VSX), "Multicoder", "Poolside Assistant"; Zed. Not confirmed either way.

findings.claim: Zed's Claude Agent ACP integration prompts for an Anthropic API key, not a claude.ai login; this is consistent with Anthropic's Agent SDK terms that third parties may not offer claude.ai login unless approved (Apple is an approved exception).
findings.detail: Zed: "If this is your first time using Claude Agent, you'll be prompted to add your Anthropic API key." Agent SDK overview: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead." Branding: "Not permitted: “Claude Code” or “Claude Code Agent”"; allowed "Claude Agent". Terms: "governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service".

verdict.corrected_claim: Zed's Claude Agent (ACP adapter @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp, formerly claude-code-acp) does NOT prompt only for an Anthropic API key. Since Zed 0.202.7 its docs say to run `/login` inside a Claude Agent thread and "authenticate either via API key, or via `Log in with Claude Code` to use a Claude Pro/Max subscription" (Feb 2026 wording; current wording: "authenticate with an API key or with Claude Code where supported"). The adapter's ACP `initialize` advertises auth methods `claude-ai-login` ("Claude Subscription", runs `claude auth login --claudeai`) and `console-login` ("Anthropic Console (API usage billing)", runs `claude auth login --console`), or in remote/SSH environments `claude-login` ("Log in with Claude": "Run `claude /login` in the terminal"). The sentence "If this is your first time using Claude Agent, you'll be prompted to add your Anthropic API key" does not appear in Zed's docs in the Feb-2026, Jun-2026 or current (Sep-2026) revisions. The Agent SDK quotes themselves are accurate verbatim: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK"; branding forbids "Claude Code"/"Claude Code Agent" and allows "Claude Agent"; the SDK is "governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service". But no Anthropic document names Apple (or Zed) as an approved exception; Xcode 26.3's Claude Agent uses a browser "Sign In" (consistent with a claude.ai login) and the adapter exposes a `--hide-claude-auth` flag ("This integration does not support using claude.ai subscriptions.") for clients that must not bill a subscription, which neither Zed nor JetBrains passes by default. The operative, more specific policy is on the Claude Code Legal and compliance page: third parties may not offer claude.ai login "into their own applications", route requests through Free/Pro/Max credentials, or "collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow"; but this "does not prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code", and hosts "may not remove, disable, or restrict any authentication method built into it".
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: Agent SDK quotes HOLD verbatim; the Zed half of the claim is REFUTED (outdated/wrong); the "Apple is an approved exception" half is UNSUPPORTED by any fetched Anthropic source (not refuted, not confirmed).

[1] critical=true — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview (fetched 2026-09-27). Verbatim: "Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the Quickstart instead." Branding — Allowed: "Claude Agent", preferred for dropdown menus; "Claude", when within a menu already labeled "Agents"; "{YourAgentName} Powered by Claude". Not permitted: "Claude Code" or "Claude Code Agent"; "Claude Code-branded ASCII art or visual elements that mimic Claude Code". License: "Use of the Claude Agent SDK is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service, including when you use it to power products and services that you make available to your own customers and end users". The page names NO approved party (no Apple, no Zed).

[2] critical=true — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart. Same note, wording "Please use the API key authentication methods described in this document instead." Auth env vars listed: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`; `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1` + `ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID`; `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`; `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1`. Error strings: `Not logged in`, `Invalid API key`. Packages: `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (npm), `claude-agent-sdk` (PyPI); "Both the TypeScript and Python SDKs bundle a native Claude Code binary"; Node.js 18+ or Python 3.10+.

[3] critical=true — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance (the more specific, operative policy for our design). License: "Commercial Terms of Service - for Team, Enterprise, and Claude API users"; "Consumer Terms of Service - for Free, Pro, and Max users". "Can customers offer Claude Code in their products?": "preinstalling or running Claude Code in your products or services (e.g. in hosted sandboxes or other agent infrastructure) requires agreeing to our Commercial Terms of Service and complying with the conditions below: The Claude Code binary must not be modified. ... customers may not remove, disable, or restrict any authentication method built into it (including methods that permit signing in with a Claude account or the user's own API key). Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf. Each end user must authenticate with their own Anthropic API key, Claude subscription plan credentials, or 3P inference provider credential". "Authentication and credential use": "OAuth authentication is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications." "Developers building products or services that interact with Claude's capabilities, including those using the Agent SDK, should use API key authentication ... Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users. Moreover, developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens — sign-in to a Claude account must complete through Anthropic's own flow." Carve-out: "Nor does it prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription, including where a platform hosts Claude Code as described under Can customers offer Claude Code in their products? above." "Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK." "Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice." Name/logo: "You can accurately say, in plain text, that your product has Claude Code preinstalled or that it runs Claude Code. But you can't use the Claude Code or Anthropic names or logos as part of your own product, feature, or company name". DESIGN IMPLICATION: Ashley must NOT "collect" the student's Claude subscription credential/session token; it may launch the unmodified `claude` CLI and let the student complete `/login` through Anthropic's own browser flow; and it must not disable the API-key or Claude-account login paths.

findings.claim: Since 2026-06-15, Claude subscriptions receive a separate, small monthly Agent SDK credit that covers Agent SDK usage, `claude -p`, GitHub Actions and third-party apps authenticating via the SDK; when it is exhausted SDK requests stop unless usage credits are enabled. A `-p`-driven grid daemon would therefore run on $20/month (Pro) rather than normal subscription limits.
findings.detail: "Pro: $20, Max 5x: $100, Max 20x: $200, Team (Standard): $20, Team (Premium): $100, Enterprise (usage-based): $20, Enterprise (Premium seats): $200" per month; covers "Claude Agent SDK usage in your own projects (Python or TypeScript)", "the `claude -p` command", GitHub Actions, and "third-party apps that authenticate with your Claude subscription through the Agent SDK". "If you use the Agent SDK with an API key from the Claude Platform, nothing changes." "If usage credits aren't enabled, Agent SDK requests stop until your credit refreshes." Article last updated June 16, 2026.

verdict.corrected_claim: The Agent SDK monthly credit never took effect. Anthropic paused the change on the day it was to start: as of the article's last update (June 16, 2026) and still as of 2026-09-27, Agent SDK usage, `claude -p`, GitHub Actions run on a subscription OAuth token, and third-party apps authenticating with a Claude subscription all draw from the subscription's normal usage limits (the rolling 5-hour and weekly windows shared with claude.ai and interactive Claude Code). There is no separate $20/$100/$200 credit to claim. A `-p`-driven grid daemon on a Pro plan therefore competes with the student's interactive use for the same Pro limits; once those are hit it either stops until the window resets or, if the student has enabled usage credits under claude.ai Settings > Usage, bills at standard API rates. Separately, the Agent SDK overview docs state that Anthropic does not allow third-party developers to offer claude.ai login or plan rate limits in their products unless previously approved, which bears directly on an extension that drives Claude Code with the student's subscription.

findings.claim: Xcode Source Editor Extensions (XcodeKit) can only read/modify the current source file's text and selection, invoked from the Editor menu, from a sandboxed app extension inside a containing macOS app; they cannot add windows, wizards, settings UI, project access, network-driven flows or terminal integration.
findings.detail: Apple: "Source editor extensions can read and modify the contents of a source file, as well as read and modify the current text selection within the editor." "Add a new Xcode Source Editor Extension target to your project"; "you must enable development signing"; entry point `perform(with invocation: XCSourceEditorCommandInvocation, completionHandler: @escaping (Error?) -> Void)` "called each time a user selects one of your extension's commands from the Editor menu"; data via `invocation.buffer.lines`; commands defined in the target's `Info.plist` (`XCSourceEditorCommandDefinitionKey`). NSHipster (2019-03-25): "pure text manipulation, instigated by the user from a menu command, on one source file at a time"; "a file of text, but not any of its context within a project"; "no way to dynamically disable individual menu commands"; sandboxed, own process; "remained unchanged since introduction" (Xcode 8, 2016, after unsigned plugins were banned). Xcode 26.4 still maintains them: "Xcode source editor extensions display the localized name via the CFBundleName (139574330)".

verdict.corrected_claim: Xcode Source Editor Extensions (XcodeKit, macOS 10.12+/Xcode 8, 2016) give the extension process exactly one surface: an XCSourceTextBuffer for the active editor (lines, selections, completeBuffer, contentUTI, tabWidth, indentationWidth, usesTabsForIndentation; no file URL, path or project data), handed to perform(with:completionHandler:) when the user picks a command from the Editor menu OR a user-assigned key binding (no default bindings, no per-context disabling). Commands come from the Info.plist array `XCSourceEditorCommandDefinitions` (keys XCSourceEditorCommandClassName / XCSourceEditorCommandIdentifierKey / XCSourceEditorCommandNameKey) or, at runtime, the `commandDefinitions` property. The extension is a sandboxed app extension inside a containing macOS app, development-signed, and cannot present windows/wizards/settings UI, read the project, or run long-lived/background tasks. However: (a) it MAY make outgoing network calls inside perform() if the App Sandbox `com.apple.security.network.client` entitlement is added (Apple: "You might need to define additional capabilities for your extension if it needs to do things like use the network"), so a synchronous network-driven text transform is possible; (b) all UI, settings, auth and background work belongs to the containing/host app, which talks to the extension only indirectly (App Group shared container/NSUserDefaults), and shipping products (GitHub Copilot for Xcode) add the macOS Accessibility permission to read the editor "in real-time" precisely because "The XcodeKit API ... only provides information when manually triggered by the user"; (c) since Xcode 26.3 (2026) XcodeKit is no longer the only integration path: Xcode has built-in agentic coding with Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI Codex (browser sign-in under Xcode > Settings > Intelligence, per-agent config in ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig), accepts ACP agents, and exposes its own tools to terminal-run agents over MCP via `claude mcp add --transport stdio xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge` after enabling "Allow external agents to use Xcode tools". XcodeKit itself is unchanged and still maintained (Xcode 26.4 note 139574330 on CFBundleName display).
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core claim holds; refuted on three sub-points (network possible with entitlement; invocation also via key bindings + runtime commandDefinitions; "no terminal integration / no wizards" is true of the XcodeKit process but obsolete as a statement about Xcode since 26.3). Claim's plist key name is slightly off: the Info.plist array key is `XCSourceEditorCommandDefinitions` (under NSExtensionAttributes); `XCSourceEditorCommandDefinitionKey` is the Swift enum type for the per-command dictionary keys.

A host process (Swift or otherwise) can shell out to `~/.local/bin/claude` ONLY for a native-installer install; Homebrew (`brew install --cask claude-code` / `claude-code@latest`) and `npm -g` installs put `claude` elsewhere, so resolve via PATH (`which -a claude`) rather than hardcoding the path. Auth: "Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account. The free claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code access." Supported platform packages: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64-musl, linux-arm64-musl, win32-x64, win32-arm64. Current release: 2.1.283 (2026-09-25).

verdict.corrected_claim: Subscription OAuth for unattended/remote machines: `claude setup-token` mints a one-year OAuth token, printed to the terminal and not saved anywhere, used via the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable (requires Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). It can only make model requests: it cannot establish Remote Control sessions (Claude Code reports `Remote Control requires a full-scope login token`) or fetch claude.ai connectors; locally configured MCP servers still work. `--bare` (equivalently `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`) does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, OAuth credentials or the keychain; it needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper`. On Linux credentials live in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (mode `0600`); on macOS the same file is the fallback when the Keychain rejects the write, such as when it is locked in an SSH session; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates the file. In SSH/WSL2/containers the browser shows a code to paste at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. Precedence: `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` > `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` > `apiKeyHelper` > `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` > Anthropic profiles > `/login` subscription OAuth; in `-p` mode `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is always used when present. A `/login` login warns `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` (v2.1.203+; five days before v2.1.217) and a background or Remote Control session that outlives the login stops making progress until you sign in again; the `/login` lifetime itself is not stated in the docs. A `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` session never sees `Login expired`; when the one-year token expires it gets `API Error: 401 OAuth token has expired`, Claude Code keeps sending the stale value, and you must mint a fresh token and restart.

verdict.corrected_claim: Remote Control lets claude.ai/code or the Claude iOS/Android app drive a Claude Code session that keeps running on another machine (the docs explicitly say: on a remote machine, start it inside tmux or screen so it survives SSH disconnect). The Claude Code process "makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports", "registers with the Anthropic API and polls for work", and needs port 443 to api.anthropic.com. It requires a claude.ai login on Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise made with `/login` / `claude auth login` (a "full-scope session token"); API keys are not supported, and neither are `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `apiKeyHelper`, nor the long-lived `claude setup-token` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` token ("These tokens can only make model requests, so they can't establish Remote Control sessions"). On Team/Enterprise the feature is off by default and an Owner must enable the toggle; HIPAA-configured orgs cannot use it. Server mode `claude remote-control` (flags go AFTER the subcommand): `--name`, `--capacity <N>` = "Maximum number of concurrent sessions. Default is 32" (a configurable default, not a hard ceiling), `--spawn same-dir|worktree|session`, `--[no-]create-session-in-dir`, `--permission-mode <mode>`, `-c/--continue` and `--session-id <id>` (v2.1.200+), `--sandbox/--no-sandbox` (off by default), `--verbose`, `-d/--debug` (v2.1.282+), `--debug-file`. Before its first start it asks a one-time TTY prompt `Enable Remote Control? (y/n)`; no non-interactive pre-acceptance flag is documented. After Ctrl+C, sessions can be brought back for "about four hours after the server stopped": plain `claude remote-control` brings back every session, `--continue` / `--session-id` bring back one and exit when it ends; nothing is resumable if the server was started with `--no-create-session-in-dir`. In server mode the process exits after roughly 10 minutes without network. Interactive modes: `claude --remote-control` / `--rc`, `/remote-control` / `/rc`; auto-connect via `remoteControlAtStartup: true` is honored only in user `~/.claude/settings.json` or managed settings (project/local files honor `false`, ignore `true`). Ineligible when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a host other than `api.anthropic.com` (since v2.1.196), on Amazon Bedrock / Google Cloud Agent Platform / Microsoft Foundry, behind an enterprise Claude apps gateway, or when `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` or `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK` is set; `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` / `DO_NOT_TRACK` are allowed from v2.1.283 (2026-09-25) unless the org requires Trusted Devices. Run `claude` in the project directory once to accept workspace trust ("The startup trust dialog never saves trust for your home directory, so start Remote Control from a project directory"). A Remote Control session that outlives the stored login "stops making progress once the credential expires and can't recover until you sign in again".

findings.claim: Headless/programmatic driving of the CLI uses `-p` with `--output-format stream-json` and `--input-format stream-json`; `--bare` is recommended for scripts but does not use subscription login; `--permission-prompts none` (v2.1.259+) and `--permission-prompt-tool` handle unattended permission decisions; SIGTERM exits 143.
findings.detail: `--input-format` "options: `text`, `stream-json`" ("structured streaming input parsing for the Agent SDK"); `--output-format` "`text`, `json`, `stream-json`"; `--continue`, `--resume <id or .jsonl path>`; "`--bare` ... Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before running it, because bare mode doesn't use your subscription login"; "`--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release"; `--permission-prompts none` "requires Claude Code v2.1.259 or later"; `--permission-prompt-tool` "Specify an MCP tool to handle permission prompts in non-interactive mode"; "If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM ... exits with code 143"; stdin "capped at 10MB"; `system/init` event lists `mcp_servers`/`mcp_server_errors`. Subcommands: `claude mcp`, `claude setup-token`, `claude remote-control`, `claude update`, `claude doctor`.

findings.claim: Claude Code MCP servers are registered with `claude mcp add --transport stdio <name> -- <command> [args]` at local/project/user scope (~/.claude.json or project .mcp.json); the stdio command is arbitrary, so an ssh-launched process on the grid can be a stdio server, and `--mcp-config`/`--strict-mcp-config` pin a session to a given server set.
findings.detail: "For stdio servers, the `--` (double dash) separates Claude's own options, such as `--transport`, `--env`, and `--scope`, from the command and arguments that run the server. Everything after `--` is passed to the server untouched." Scopes: `local` (default, `~/.claude.json` under `projects`), `project` (`.mcp.json` at project root, `{"mcpServers": {...}}`), `user` (`~/.claude.json`). `--env KEY=value`; `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expansion in `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `headers`; `MCP_TIMEOUT=10000 claude`; "Use `--strict-mcp-config` to use only the MCP servers you pass with `--mcp-config`"; tool names `mcp__server__tool`. The docs do not mention ssh explicitly; community SSH MCP servers use e.g. `claude mcp add --transport stdio ssh-mcp -- npx -y ssh-mcp -- --host=example.com --user=root --key=/path/to/private/key`.

verdict.corrected_claim: Claude Code MCP servers are registered with `claude mcp add [options] <name> -- <command> [args...]`; `--transport stdio` is accepted but is also the default ("Defaults to stdio if not specified" in `claude mcp add --help`, v2.1.283). Scopes: `-s/--scope` local (default; written into `~/.claude.json` under `projects` -> `<absolute project path>` -> `mcpServers`), project (`.mcp.json` at project root, `{"mcpServers": {...}}`, requires per-user approval), user (`~/.claude.json`). Everything after `--` is "passed to the server untouched", and the docs' own examples run arbitrary commands (`npx server`, `python server.py --port 8080`, `my-command --some-flag arg1`), so `ssh <host> <remote-server-cmd>` is a legal stdio command — BUT the docs never show ssh as a stdio command, I did not execute an ssh-backed server, and the community `ssh-mcp` package is a LOCAL server that opens SSH sessions to run remote commands, not an MCP server running on the grid; its current README installs it as `claude mcp add --transport stdio ssh-mcp -- ssh-mcp` (the `npx -y ssh-mcp -- --host=… --key=…` form in the claim is not what the README shows today). CRITICAL design caveat the claim omits: "Stdio servers are local processes, and Claude Code doesn't reconnect them automatically" — a dropped SSH/ProxyJump connection kills the server for the session until a manual `/mcp` reconnect; only HTTP/SSE servers get exponential-backoff auto-reconnect (5 attempts, 1 s doubling). `--mcp-config <configs...>` ("Load MCP servers from JSON files or strings (space-separated)") plus `--strict-mcp-config` ("Only use MCP servers from --mcp-config, ignoring all other MCP configurations") pin a session to a server set; skipping approval prompts for unloaded project-scoped servers under strict mode requires Claude Code >= v2.1.246 (earlier versions left background sessions waiting at startup), and `--mcp-config` with `-p` waits for pending servers up to `MCP_TIMEOUT` (>= v2.1.221). `MCP_TIMEOUT` is in milliseconds (`MCP_TIMEOUT=10000 claude`), but the two official pages disagree on its default (env-vars page: 5000 ms; cli-reference page: 30 s) — set it explicitly for an ssh-bastion-launched server. `--env KEY=value` works but the server name must not immediately follow `--env` (put `--transport stdio` between them). `${VAR}` / `${VAR:-default}` expand in `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `headers`; an unset variable without a default is warned about and left unexpanded. Tool names are `mcp__<server>__<tool>` (plugin-bundled servers use `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`). `~/.claude.json` is a file Claude Code "writes for itself; you don't need to edit it" — an extension should register servers via `claude mcp add`, `claude mcp add-json <name> '<inner object>'`, `.mcp.json`, or `--mcp-config`, not by editing `~/.claude.json`.
verdict.evidence:
VERIFIED against three independent sources: raw markdown of the official docs (curl via WSL, grep by line), the shipped Claude Code 2.1.283 binary bundled with the VS Code extension (C:\Users\grego\.vscode\extensions\anthropic.claude-code-2.1.283-win32-x64\resources\native-binary\claude.exe, `--help` and `mcp add --help`), and the tufantunc/ssh-mcp README.

[1] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md (fetched 2026-09-27; line numbers from the raw .md):
- L115: "Stdio servers run as local processes on your machine. They're ideal for tools that need direct system access or custom scripts."
- L128: `claude mcp add --env AIRTABLE_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY --transport stdio airtable -- npx -y airtable-mcp-server`
- L135 (verbatim, matches the claim's DETAIL exactly): "For stdio servers, the `--` (double dash) separates Claude's own options, such as `--transport`, `--env`, and `--scope`, from the command and arguments that run the server. Everything after `--` is passed to the server untouched."
- L139-140: "`claude mcp add --transport stdio myserver -- npx server` → runs `npx server`"; "`claude mcp add --env KEY=value --transport stdio myserver -- python server.py --port 8080` → runs `python server.py --port 8080` with `KEY=value` in environment"
- `--env` gotcha: "`--env` accepts multiple `KEY=value` pairs. If the server name comes directly after `--env`, the CLI reads the name as another pair and rejects it, so place at least one other option, such as `--transport stdio`, between `--env` and the server name."
- L168: "Each command writes to [local scope] unless you add `--scope project` or `--scope user`."
- L524: "Local scope is the default. A local-scoped server loads only in the project where you added it and stays private to you. Claude Code stores it in `~/.claude.json` under that project's path, so the same server won't appear in your other projects." Example JSON shows `{"projects": {"/path/to/your/project": {"mcpServers": {...}}}}`.
- `.mcp.json` format: `{"mcpServers": {"shared-server": {"type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/mcp"}}}`; stdio entry shape from the `claude mcp serve` example: `{"type": "stdio", "command": "claude", "args": ["mcp","serve"], "env": {}}`.
- `claude mcp add-json` takes "the object inside `mcpServers`, not the wrapper."
- L363 (critical=true for an ssh-launched server): "Claude Code reconnects a remote server that drops mid-session and retries an HTTP or SSE server's first connection after a transient error. Stdio servers are local processes, and Claude Code doesn't reconnect them automatically." L367: remote reconnect is "up to five attempts, starting at a one-second delay and doubling it each time"; failure shows `MCP server "<name>" disconnected · open /mcp to reconnect`.
- L407: "Configure MCP server startup timeout using the `MCP_TIMEOUT` environment variable (for example, `MCP_TIMEOUT=10000 claude` sets a 10-second timeout)". L413: per-server `timeout` field in ms; "Values below 1000 are ignored and fall through to `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, or to its default of about 28 hours when that variable is unset" (requires v2.1.203+). "Stdio and WebSocket servers have no per-request timer."
- L583 (critical=true): "Start the session with `--strict-mcp-config`. Claude Code then uses only the MCP servers you pass with `--mcp-config`. Skipping the approval prompt for the project-scoped servers Claude Code isn't loading requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later; before v2.1.246, a strict session still waited on approval for them, which left background sessions waiting at startup." Section heading: "Exclusive control with managed-mcp.json".
- L621: "`${VAR:-default}`: expands to `VAR` if set, otherwise uses `default`"; supported fields listed as `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `headers`. L296: a missing variable with no `:-default` is warned about in `claude mcp list` and `/mcp` and the server "still loads ... with the `${VAR}` text unexpanded."
- L500-506: `mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool-name>` for plugin servers; bare form `mcp__database-tools__.*`; prompts `/mcp__github__list_prs`. Regular tool example `mcp__database-tools__query`.
- ssh mentions (L799, L1164, L1169, L1173): ONLY in `claude mcp login` OAuth context ("detects when no local browser is available, such as during an SSH session ... connect with `ssh -t`. Pass `--no-browser`") and desktop-app "local and SSH sessions". No mention of ssh as a stdio command — claim's statement "The docs do not mention ssh explicitly" is correct.
- SSE transport: "The SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport is deprecated. Use HTTP servers instead, where available."

[2] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference.md (raw grep; the WebFetch summarizer had wrongly reported `--strict-mcp-config` absent):
- L104: "`--mcp-config` | Load MCP servers from JSON files or strings (space-separated). When you pass this flag with `-p`, Claude Code waits for still-pending servers to connect before running the first turn, up to the `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup timeout, 30 seconds by default; a server with a cached tool list skips the wait and connects on first use. findings.claim: A Swift menu-bar host is straightforward: SwiftUI `MenuBarExtra` (macOS 13.0+) with `LSUIElement` for a Dock-less utility and `.menuBarExtraStyle(.window)` for a rich popover; Developer-ID distribution requires notarization with hardened runtime but not App Sandbox.
findings.detail: `nonisolated struct MenuBarExtra<Label, Content> where Label : View, Content : View`, availability "macOS: 13.0.0 -"; "set the LSUIElement flag in your app's Information Property List file to `true`"; "An app that only shows in the menu bar will be automatically terminated if the user removes the extra from the menu bar." Notarization: "Beginning in macOS 10.15, all software built after June 1, 2019, and distributed with Developer ID must be notarized"; requirements: valid code signature, Developer ID certificate, "Enable the Hardened Runtime capability", secure timestamp, no `com.apple.security.get-task-allow`; tools `notarytool` and `stapler` (altool no longer accepted since 2023-11-01). App Sandbox is not among the listed requirements.

findings.claim: The shared TypeScript core can be shipped inside a Swift app as a single native executable via Bun (`bun build --compile`, cross-compiles to bun-darwin-arm64/x64 and bun-linux-x64[-musl], codesignable with a JIT entitlement) or Node SEA (`node --build-sea`, Stability 1.1, macOS tested arm64 only).
findings.detail: Bun: `bun build ./cli.ts --compile --outfile mycli`; targets `bun-darwin-arm64`, `bun-darwin-x64`, `bun-linux-x64`, `bun-linux-arm64`, `bun-linux-x64-musl`, `bun-linux-arm64-musl`, `bun-windows-x64`, `bun-windows-arm64` ("`-baseline` and `-modern` ... resolve to the same binary"); `--minify --sourcemap --bytecode`; `codesign --deep --force -vvvv --sign "XXXXXXXXXX" --entitlements entitlements.plist ./myapp` with `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit`; "Codesign support requires Bun v1.2.4 or newer." Node SEA: "Stability: 1.1 - Active development"; `node --build-sea sea-config.json` (added v25.5.0), then `codesign --sign - sea`; legacy `postject ... --sentinel-fuse NODE_SEA_FUSE_fce680ab2cc467b6e072b8b5df1996b2 --macho-segment-name NODE_SEA`; "macOS (arm64 only; x64 is not currently supported)"; "By default, both `require()` and `import` statements would only be able to load the built-in modules", ESM needs `"mainFormat": "module"`.

findings.claim: macOS Shortcuts and Automator remain available (Automator guide covers macOS 27) and can launch scripts, but they are launchers, not a credential/wizard UI; Shortcuts has a documented CLI (`shortcuts run`) and App Intents (macOS 13+) let a Swift app expose actions to Shortcuts/Spotlight/Siri.
findings.detail: `shortcuts run "Combine Images" -i ~/Desktop/*.jpg -o ~/Desktop/combined.png`, `shortcuts list`, `shortcuts list --folders`, `shortcuts view`, `shortcuts sign --mode people-who-know-me --input ... --output ...`; flags `-i/--input-path`, `-o/--output-path`, `--output-type`. Automator: guide version selector lists "macOS 27 Golden Gate"; "You can easily import Automator workflows into Shortcuts"; Run Shell Script action: "string several bash shell commands together to perform complex tasks, and then pass the results to a window." App Intents: availability "macOS: 13.0.0 -"; "The Shortcuts app helps people configure workflows that include your app's actions." An official Shortcuts-guide page for the 'Run Shell Script' action itself was not located.

topics_verified.recommendation: Treat Xcode as a *shell* host, not an extension host. Do not build an Xcode Source Editor Extension for Ashley: Apple limits it to text edits of one open file from the Editor menu, with no windows, settings, project or network flow. Recommended porting path, in order: (1) Keep the credential wizard, SSH ProxyJump writer and Slurm launcher in the shared TypeScript core and compile it once per platform with `bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64` (add `bun-darwin-x64` only if Intel Macs on Xcode 26.x matter; Xcode 27 is Apple-silicon only). Wrap it in a Swift `MenuBarExtra` app (macOS 13+, `LSUIElement`, `.menuBarExtraStyle(.window)`), signed with Developer ID, hardened runtime and notarized via `notarytool`; do not enable App Sandbox because the app must write `~/.ssh/config`, run `ssh`/`sbatch`, and write into `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/`. (2) Have the app install an "ashley" MCP server (stdio; tools such as provision_credentials, write_ssh_config, submit_grid_job, send_prompt, read_reply) for Xcode's built-in Claude Agent by writing `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/CodingAssistant/ClaudeAgentConfig/.claude.json` (project-keyed `mcpServers`, absolute paths, restart Xcode) and, for Xcode 27+, package the same server as an agent plug-in (JSON with `mcpServers`, `_meta.ideToolIconPath`) installable via Intelligence > Plug-ins > Add from URL; also register it for the student's terminal Claude Code with `claude mcp add --transport stdio ashley --scope user -- /abs/path/ashley-core mcp`. (3) On Xcode 26.6+, expose the grid-side Claude Code as an ACP agent: ship an `ashley-acp` binary (JSON-RPC over stdio, forwards prompts over the existing ProxyJump SSH to the grid session and streams results back) and register it through Intelligence > Agents > Add an Agent with an absolute Command path and Arguments; this gives students a "Grid Claude" entry in the coding-assistant picker without any Accessibility hacks. (4) For the grid-side persistent process, run the interactive `claude` CLI (tmux/`script`, `/login` with the paste-code flow, credentials in `~/.claude/.credentials.json`), and offer Remote Control (`claude remote-control --name`, outbound HTTPS only, Pro/Max) as the second prompt channel; do NOT build the daemon on the Agent SDK or on `claude -p`/`--input-format stream-json` with subscription auth until the Agent-SDK-credit accounting is confirmed, since Anthropic's terms forbid third-party claude.ai login on the SDK and the June-2026 credit is only $20/month on Pro; use `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` only for model-request-only helpers, never for Remote Control. (5) Skip Automator; use Shortcuts/App Intents only as optional launchers (`shortcuts run`), and tell students that "Claude Code in Xcode's terminal" means Terminal.app with `claude mcp add --transport stdio xcode -- xcrun mcpbridge` and the project open in Xcode.

topics_verified.topic: Programmatic literature-access credentials for a PRISMA-style review pipeline run from the WSU grid (compute nodes have internet), plus Wayne State library proxy/VPN coverage
topics_verified.summary: Every metadata source a PRISMA pipeline needs (PubMed E-utilities, Europe PMC, Crossref, Unpaywall, NIH RePORTER, ClinicalTrials.gov v2, arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv) is reachable from any internet-connected node with no institutional key; the only credentials that materially change throughput are a free NCBI API key (3 -> 10 requests/s) and, new in 2026, an OpenAlex API key (OpenAlex retired the mailto polite pool and moved to a metered daily budget: $1/day free with a key, roughly a tenth of that without one, 429 on overrun). Semantic Scholar's key is free but paradoxically slow (1 request/s introductory), so it is optional. The two subscription indexes, Scopus (Elsevier) and Web of Science, both appear in WSU library guides behind proxy.lib.wayne.edu, so WSU is a subscriber; their APIs are keyed per user for free but full data only flows from a WSU IP range (Elsevier IP-based auth) or with an institution token, and Elsevier's policy forbids storing retrieved records except temporarily, which constrains a systematic-review cache. Google Scholar has no API; SerpAPI's Google Scholar engine costs $25/month for 1,000 searches (250/month free). GitHub push needs a fine-grained PAT with Contents: Read and write on the target repo (org-owned repos may sit 'pending' until approved; personal tokens may have no expiry, org policy defaults to 366 days). Hugging Face push needs a 'write' or fine-grained token, read via HF_TOKEN. For Wayne State, the EZproxy prefix is https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login?url= with AccessID login; on campus 'you typically won't need to sign in', and the GlobalProtect VPN (protect.wayne.edu, MFA) is limited to 'a current student or employee'. School of Medicine students authenticate to EZproxy with their AccessID like any WSU student; what ended 2026-06-30 was Tenet/DMC-sponsored residents' access, by Tenet's 'sole decision'. The binding constraint is WSU's acceptable-use policy, which prohibits robots/crawlers and systematic downloading of licensed resources, so the pipeline must pull full text from open-access routes or vendor TDM APIs, never by scripting EZproxy with a student's credentials. Whether the grid's compute-node egress IPs fall inside the publisher-registered WSU ranges was not verifiable from outside and must be probed from a node.

findings.claim: PubMed E-utilities allow 3 requests/second without an API key and 10 requests/second with one; the key is passed as the api_key parameter.
findings.detail: NLM KA-05317: 'the number of requests per second (rps) to 3' by default, 'increase the rate to 10 rps' with a key; example 'https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/einfo.fcgi?db=pubmed&api_key=ABCD123'. Key created at NCBI account -> Account settings -> 'API Key Management' -> Create an API Key. NCBI Insights: 'Requests without an API key have a rate limit of 3 requests/second' / 'Requests with an API key have a default rate limit of 10 requests/second (or a higher rate limit that you've negotiated with us)', in force since 2018-12-01.

verdict.corrected_claim: PubMed E-utilities allow 3 requests/second without an API key and 10 requests/second with one; the key is passed as the api_key parameter.
verdict.evidence:
CLAIM HELD on every point; verified 2026-09-27 against official NLM/NCBI pages and a live test of the endpoint.

[1] NLM KB KA-05317 (fetched, https://support.nlm.nih.gov/kbArticle/?pn=KA-05317): "NCBI E-Utilities API service limits the number of requests per second (rps) to 3." / "You can increase the rate to 10 rps if you obtain and use an API Key." Example URL exactly as claimed: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/einfo.fcgi?db=pubmed&api_key=ABCD123 . Key-creation path exactly as claimed: Sign in to NCBI -> click username (top right) -> "Account settings" -> "API Key Management" section -> "Create an API Key" button. Also states the same key works for both E-Utilities and the NCBI Datasets API. Article shows no last-updated date.

[2] NCBI Insights 2018-08-14 "Release Plan for E-utility API Keys" (fetched, https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2018/08/14/release-plan-for-e-utility-api-keys/): this is the actual source of the two Insights sentences the claim quotes, verbatim: "Requests without an API key have a rate limit of 3 requests/second." / "Requests with an API key have a default rate limit of 10 requests/second (or a higher rate limit that you've negotiated with us)." Enforcement date: "At 12:00 AM EST on December 1, 2018, API keys will become fully active in our production environment." -> the claim's 2018-12-01 is correct.

[3] Date history (so nobody "corrects" 2018-12-01 back to an earlier date): NCBI Insights 2017-11-02 "New API Keys for the E-utilities" (fetched, https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2017/11/02/new-api-keys-for-the-e-utilities/) originally said "After May 1, 2018, NCBI will limit your access to the E-utilities unless you have one of these keys." and "your key will increase the limit to 10 requests/second for all activity from that key", limit without key "three requests per second" per IP, parameter "&api_key=ABCD123", "If you need higher rates of access, please contact us and we can discuss your situation." NCBI Insights 2018-04-19 "Testing Periods for New API Keys" (fetched, https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2018/04/19/testing-periods-for-new-api-keys/) postponed it: "We will not be activating API keys on May 1, 2018 as originally announced. That date is being moved to be no earlier than September 1, 2018." and states the three tiers: "If you don't have an API key, then any IP you use that generates more than 3 requests/second will receive an error message"; "default API key (rate max = 10 requests/second)"; "high-rate API key (rate max > 10 requests/second, obtained by negotiating with us)". Final activation = 2018-12-01 per [2].

[4] LIVE TEST 2026-09-27 (critical=true for the design): 8 concurrent keyless GETs to https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/einfo.fcgi?db=pubmed&retmode=json from one IP returned 3x HTTP 200 and 5x HTTP 429 with body exactly: {"error":"API rate limit exceeded","api-key":"68.41.128.254","count":"4","limit":"3"} . Confirms (a) the keyless limit is 3/s and is enforced today, (b) the over-limit response is HTTP 429 with JSON key "error":"API rate limit exceeded", (c) keyless limiting is per source IP (the "api-key" field echoes the client IP when no key is sent) - relevant if many students share a grid/NAT egress: a keyless design shares one 3 rps bucket per IP, so each student should supply their own api_key (10 rps per key).

[5] Independent implementation: Biopython Bio.Entrez tutorial (fetched, https://biopython.org/docs/latest/Tutorial/chapter_entrez.html): "If you are using a API key, you can make at most 10 queries per second, otherwise at most 3 queries per second." "This is automatically enforced by Biopython." Set via Entrez.api_key = "MyAPIkey" or api_key= argument. Also: "For any series of more than 100 requests, do this at weekends or outside USA peak times."

[6] Do-not-conflate note: NCBI Insights 2024-10-08 "New API Key System Coming Soon to NCBI Datasets" (fetched, https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2024/10/08/new-api-key-system-coming-ncbi-datasets/) gives DIFFERENT numbers for the NCBI Datasets API: "You will be limited to 5 requests per second" without a key, "10 requests per second" with one, effective January 2025. Those are Datasets limits, not E-utilities; the claim (E-utilities: 3/10) remains correct.

NOT VERIFIED: the canonical Bookshelf chapter NBK25497 (Entrez Programming Utilities Help, Usage Guidelines) returned a reCAPTCHA page to both WebFetch and WSL curl (HTTP 200, ~20 KB, 28x "recaptcha"), so no quote from it; the KB article and Insights posts above are official NLM/NCBI statements and the live test agrees with them. WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before this task; all lookups were direct fetches.

findings.claim: Exceeding the E-utilities limit returns a JSON error body, and NCBI asks that large jobs run off-peak; tool and email parameters identify the caller.
findings.detail: Error string: {"error":"API rate limit exceeded","count":"11"}. Guidance: 'Post no more than three URL requests per second' without a key, 'up to 10 requests per second by default' with one; 'Limit large jobs to either weekends or between 9:00 PM and 5:00 AM Eastern time during weekdays'. Register tool name + developer email; higher rates via eutilities@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov. Note: the NCBI Bookshelf page NBK25497 served a reCAPTCHA to the automated fetcher; the eutils endpoint itself is not captcha-gated.

verdict.corrected_claim: Exceeding the E-utilities limit returns HTTP 429 with Content-Type application/json, headers Retry-After: 2, X-RateLimit-Limit: 3 and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, and a JSON body of the form {"error":"API rate limit exceeded","api-key":"<client IP or key>","count":"<n>","limit":"<limit>"} — e.g. live on 2026-09-27: {"error":"API rate limit exceeded","api-key":"68.41.128.254","count":"4","limit":"3"}. The string {"error":"API rate limit exceeded","count":"11"} is only the documentation's abbreviated example; the real body carries two extra fields ("api-key", which echoes the caller's IP address when no key is sent, and "limit"), so clients must parse the "error" field, not match the whole string. Limits are 3 requests/second per IP without a key and 10/second per key by default (enforced since 1 May 2018); an invalid api_key returns HTTP 400 {"error":"API key invalid","api-key":"<value>","type":"invalid","status":"unknown"}. NCBI asks that large jobs be limited to weekends or 9:00 PM–5:00 AM Eastern on weekdays. The tool and email parameters identify the caller but do not raise the limit, and NCBI states that supplying them in requests "is not sufficient": the software name (no internal spaces) and developer e-mail must be registered by mailing eutilities@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, which is also the address for higher rates. The Bookshelf pages NBK25497/NBK25499 serve a reCAPTCHA to non-browser fetchers even from a residential IP; the eutils endpoint itself is not captcha-gated.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: substance holds (JSON error, 3/10 rps, off-peak window, tool+email, eutilities@ contact); the quoted error string is the documentation example, not the literal body the server returns, and the claim omits the HTTP status/headers and understates the registration requirement. Details, with URLs actually fetched:

[1] LIVE PROBE, critical=true. URL: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/einfo.fcgi?retmode=json&tool=ashley_verifier&email=<addr> — 20 concurrent GETs from one residential IP (Detroit, via WSL curl) at 2026-09-28 00:30 GMT (= 2026-09-27 20:30 EDT, i.e. inside NCBI's off-peak window). Result: 3 x "HTTP/2 200", 17 x "HTTP/2 429". Every 429 body (86 bytes) was exactly: {"error":"API rate limit exceeded","api-key":"68.41.128.254","count":"4","limit":"3"}. 429 headers: server: Finatra; content-type: application/json; retry-after: 2; x-ratelimit-limit: 3; x-ratelimit-remaining: 0; access-control-expose-headers: X-RateLimit-Limit,X-RateLimit-Remaining,Retry-After. Findings: (a) body has fields api-key + limit that the claim's string lacks; "api-key" carries the CLIENT IP when no key is sent (the IP is echoed back to the caller); (b) tool= and email= were present and the limit stayed at 3, so they do not raise the rate; (c) the endpoint is not captcha-gated (clean JSON on 200/429/400).

[2] INVALID KEY PROBE, critical=true. Same endpoint with api_key=NOTAREALKEY -> "HTTP/2 400", content-type: application/json, x-ratelimit-limit: 3, x-ratelimit-remaining: 3, body: {"error":"API key invalid","api-key":"NOTAREALKEY","type":"invalid","status":"unknown"}. Design note: a mistyped student key yields 400 not 429; the counter still shows the no-key limit of 3.

[3] NCBI-run documentation (MkDocs site; landing page reads "Welcome to NCBI EUtilities (site in progress)" and directs to eutilities@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). URL: https://eutilities.github.io/site/API_Key/usageandkey/ (full raw HTML fetched; no date/version on page). Verbatim: "Post no more than three URL requests per second"; "Limit large jobs to either weekends or between 9:00 PM and 5:00 AM Eastern time during weekdays"; "Failure to comply with this policy may result in an IP address being blocked from accessing NCBI."; "Without an API key, IP address posting more than 3 requests per second to the EUtilities will receive an error message."; "Example Error Message if Rates are Exceeded {"error":"API rate limit exceeded","count":"11"}" (note the word "Example"); "By including an API key, a site can post up to 10 requests per second by default. Higher rates are available by request at eutilities@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov."; "Only one API key is allowed per NCBI account... Requests for new API Keys invalidate any existing API key associated with that NCBI account."; parameter is api_key={API key value}; "The name of the software and email must be registered with NCBI. To register, e-mail eutilities@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov"; software name "should be a string with no internal spaces that uniquely identifies the software producing the request For example: Microsoft-Office"; email is "the software developer and not that of a third-party end user"; "The information must be registered with NCBI - providing it in requests is not sufficient to comply with this policy."; "use the History parameter, which works in batches". Site index https://eutilities.github.io/site/ (fetched) says ~25 million EUtilities calls/day from ~100,000 IPs; sitemap.xml is empty; the Reference_Guide pages (about/, esearch/, a_reference/) and Quick_Start/eu_quick/ contain no separate tool/email parameter definitions.

[4] NLM official support KB, URL: https://support.nlm.nih.gov/kbArticle/?pn=KA-05317 ("What is an API Key and how can I get it?", no date shown). Verbatim: "NCBI E-Utilities API service limits the number of requests per second (rps) to 3. You can increase the rate to 10 rps if you obtain and use an API Key." Key is made under NCBI account -> Account settings -> "API Key Management" -> "Create an API Key". No error text, no rate-increase contact given there.

[5] NCBI Insights (official NCBI blog), URL: https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2017/11/02/new-api-keys-for-the-e-utilities/ (posted 2 Nov 2017). Verbatim: "After May 1, 2018, any computer (IP address) that submits more than three E-utility requests per second will receive an error message"; "By default, your key will increase the limit to 10 requests/second for all activity from that key"; "all requests using that key will receive an error message" when the key's rate is exceeded; "If you need higher rates of access, please contact us"; contact eutilities@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov. Confirms the limit is per IP without a key and per key with one.

[6] 2026 change check, URL: https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2026/01/06/updated-pmc-e-utilities/ (6 Jan 2026): "PMC is moving to an updated version of the E-utilities API in early February 2026"; "This update only affects E-utility calls when the request specifies the PMC database, &db=pmc."; ESearch limited to first 10,000 records (&retmax <= 10,000; &retstart + &retmax <= 10,000); EPost up to 10,000 PMCIDs. No change to rates, keys, tool/email or error format. Tag listing https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/tag/e-utilities/ shows no other 2024-2026 E-utilities policy post.

[7] Bookshelf captcha, confirmed both ways: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25497/ and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25499/ returned a reCAPTCHA page to the WebFetch proxy AND to curl from a residential IP with a Chrome UA (HTTP 200, ~20.4 KB, 6 "recaptcha" hits, none of the guideline text). web.archive.org is not reachable from this tool ("Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org"), and the WebSearch budget for this session was already exhausted (200/200) before this task, so no search was run. Consequently the "9:00 PM and 5:00 AM Eastern" sentence is verified only from the NCBI-run eutilities.github.io page (not independently from the Bookshelf); the 3/10 rps figures and the contact address are triply verified (NCBI site, NLM KB, NCBI Insights) plus the live x-ratelimit-limit: 3 header.

DESIGN IMPLICATIONS (critical=true): parse JSON field "error" and the HTTP status (429 rate / 400 bad key), never string-match the documented example; honour Retry-After (observed 2 s) and X-RateLimit-Remaining; the no-key budget is per IP, so every student process sharing one egress IP (a login node, or compute nodes behind one NAT — inference, not verified for warrior.grid.wayne.edu) shares a single 3 rps allowance, which is the practical reason each student needs their own api_key (10 rps per key, one key per NCBI account); send tool=<NoSpaces> and email=<developer>, and register them by e-mail with NCBI since per-request inclusion alone does not satisfy the policy; schedule bulk jobs in the stated off-peak window and use the History server for batches.

findings.claim: NCBI's own command-line tooling reads the key from the NCBI_API_KEY environment variable, so that is the env var name to standardise on.
findings.detail: 'Set the NCBI_API_KEY environment variable and the command-line tool will use the API key automatically.' Also accepts header 'api-key: <KEY>' or '?api_key=<KEY>'. (The Datasets API's keyless default is 5 rps, keyed 10 rps; E-utilities' keyless default is 3 rps.)

findings.claim: Europe PMC REST API needs no key or registration; a live unauthenticated call succeeded.
findings.detail: GET https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=lumbosacral%20transitional%20vertebra&format=json&pageSize=1 returned JSON with version "6.9" and hitCount 1097. Note europepmc.org (the website, /developers, /RestfulWebService) returned HTTP 403 to the automated fetcher; the ebi.ac.uk API host did not.

findings.claim: Europe PMC throttles at 10 requests/second and 500 requests/minute, applied per IP address.
findings.detail: Staff (Mohamed Selim, 2020-03-24): 'Currently we apply some throttling of 10 requests per second and 500 requests per minute.' Staff (Mariia Levchenko, 2024-12-11, thread cZLnV1JhCj8): 'The API limit is applied per IP address.' No API key exists; increases are requested on the epmc-webservices forum. Per-IP matters on a shared login/compute node.

findings.claim: Semantic Scholar API is free; unauthenticated traffic shares one pool of 1000 requests/second, while a personal key gets an introductory 1 request/second on all endpoints.
findings.detail: 'Most Semantic Scholar endpoints are available to the public without authentication, but they are rate-limited to 1000 requests per second shared among all unauthenticated users.' 'The introductory rate limit for an API key is 1 RPS on all endpoints.' Key requested via the form at https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api#api-key-form; 'You will receive your private API key via email.'

findings.claim: Semantic Scholar key goes in the x-api-key header; base URL is https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1 and bulk search is /paper/search/bulk.
findings.detail: Tutorial code uses headers {"x-api-key": api_key}; 'using an individual API key automatically gives a user a 1 request per second rate across all endpoints'. Env var: not defined officially; S2_API_KEY is the de-facto community name (seen in third-party clients via search, not on semanticscholar.org).

findings.claim: OpenAlex announced that API calls require a key from 2026-02-13 and that the mailto polite pool is discontinued.
findings.detail: Jason Priem, openalex-users, 2026-01-13: 'API calls will require a key starting one month from today (Feb 13).' Keyless: '100 credits per day' for testing; keyed: '100,000 credits per day'. Credit costs: singleton 1, list 10, content 100, vector search 1,000. Key usage 'api.openalex.org/works?api_key=YOUR_KEY'; key from openalex.org settings/api; after Feb 13 keyless calls get '100 free credits for testing, then 409 errors' (current docs say 429). Email-based polite pool 'discontinued entirely'.

verdict.corrected_claim: OpenAlex did announce on 2026-01-13 (Jason Priem, openalex-users) that API keys would be required from 2026-02-13, with a credit system (keyless 100 credits/day, keyed 100,000/day; singleton 1, list 10, content 100, vector search 1,000; '409 errors' after the free credits) and that the email/mailto polite pool was discontinued. That announcement is accurate as history but is OUTDATED as a description of the API: on 2026-02-24 OpenAlex replaced credits with USD usage-based pricing, and the current official docs (help.openalex.org, Authentication page updated 2026-08-19; docs.openalex.org now 301-redirects there) state that basic queries work with NO key at all on a keyless budget of $0.10 of usage per day, a free key raises it to $1.00/day ('10× the keyless budget'), singleton lookups by ID/DOI are free, list+filter costs $0.10 per 1,000 calls, search and semantic search $1 per 1,000, content download $10 per 1,000; the key is sent as `?api_key=YOUR_KEY` or `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY` and obtained from openalex.org/settings/api; exhausting the daily budget or exceeding 100 requests/second returns `429 Too Many Requests` (the Errors page documents no 409). The polite pool part holds: the `mailto` parameter is now ignored (calls with it still return 200 but earn nothing). Live keyless calls on 2026-09-27 returned HTTP 200 with `"cost_usd": 0.0001` in `meta`. Not critical to the Ashley design: an OpenAlex key is not one of the credentials the extension collects.
verdict.evidence:
ORIGINAL SOURCE (fetched, confirms the claim's wording, thread has no replies): https://groups.google.com/g/openalex-users/c/rI1GIAySpVQ — Jason Priem, Jan 13 2026 9:54:16 PM: "API calls will require a key starting one month from today (Feb 13)."; "Without a key you get 100 credits per day, which is fine for testing and demos but not for real work."; "You get 100,000 credits per day with your API key"; singleton "1 credit", list "10 credits", content "100 credits", vector search "1,000 credits"; "api.openalex.org/works?api_key=YOUR_KEY"; "Copy your API key from https://openalex.org/settings/api"; "you'll get 100 free credits for testing, then 409 errors."; "No more polite pool! No more email parameter in your calls—it was never secure and couldn't scale."

SUPERSEDING ANNOUNCEMENT (fetched): https://groups.google.com/g/openalex-users/c/6kwRTtqUcnU — Jason Priem, Feb 24 2026 10:06:42 PM, "new features and usage-based pricing": "API keys are now required for all requests. Getting one is free and takes 30 seconds"; "Your free API key gets $1 of free usage per day."; "Searching costs $1 per thousand calls."; "looking up a single work (or millions of them) by DOI or ID is now free."; "Grabbing all 694k works by Finnish authors costs about $0.70 — well within your daily free allowance." The credit system in the Jan 13 post does not appear.

CURRENT OFFICIAL DOCS (fetched): (1) https://help.openalex.org/api/authentication/ (last updated August 19, 2026): "OpenAlex data is free, and so is casual use of the API — you can make basic queries with no key at all."; "a free key gives you 10× the keyless budget"; `curl "https://api.openalex.org/works?api_key=YOUR_KEY"` and `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" "https://api.openalex.org/works"`; "Make an account (about 30 seconds) and copy your key from openalex.org/settings/api"; "Two things return `429 Too Many Requests`: exceeding your daily budget, or making more" than 100 requests per second.
