findings.claim: Elsevier API keys are free to anyone, but full Scopus/ScienceDirect data only flows to users at subscribing institutions.
findings.detail: dev.elsevier.com: 'Anyone can request an API Key to use Elsevier APIs.' Key management at https://dev.elsevier.com/apikey/manage. 'Full API access is only granted to researchers affiliated to organisations that have subscriptions to the corresponding Elsevier product.'

verdict.corrected_claim: Anyone can request an Elsevier API key (registration at https://dev.elsevier.com/apikey/manage, which redirects to an id.elsevier.com OAuth sign-in, so a free Elsevier account is required), but keys are free only for non-commercial use by "researchers in academic and public-sector institutions, charities and charitable foundations", and SciVal and Embase APIs are excluded from no-charge access; commercial use needs "an API license and subscription". Full Scopus/ScienceDirect data flows only when the caller is recognised as a subscriber, and subscriber status is determined by the request's source IP being inside a subscribing institution's network ("only when you're making calls from within your institutional network are you considered a subscriber"; "API access through proxies is not supported"); off-network or proxied access requires an Institutional Token (X-ELS-Insttoken header) obtained by contacting Elsevier API support. Keys also carry weekly quotas (e.g. Scopus Search 20,000 req/week at 9 req/s; ScienceDirect Article Retrieval 50,000 req/week at 10 req/s) and several APIs (Scopus Citation Overview, ScienceDirect Full-Text Entitlement, Embase, Engineering Village, SUSHI COP5) are access-controlled and need explicit approval.
verdict.evidence:
VERDICT: core claim holds; "free to anyone" is subtly wrong; the mechanism by which "full data flows to subscribing institutions" is IP-based, which is critical for the Ashley design (critical=true).

1. https://dev.elsevier.com/ (fetched 2026-09-27) — verbatim: "Anyone can request an API Key to use Elsevier APIs." AND "Except for Scival and Embase APIs, access at no charge is available to researchers in academic and public-sector institutions, charities and charitable foundations." AND "Free access is only available for non-commercial use and provided Elsevier's policies for using APIs and the data are honoured." AND "Full API access is only granted to researchers affiliated to organisations that have subscriptions to the corresponding Elsevier product." Key management link is /apikey/manage. So: anyone may REQUEST a key; FREE access is scoped to non-commercial academic/public-sector/charity users and excludes SciVal/Embase — the claim's "free to anyone" overstates this.

2. https://dev.elsevier.com/apikey/manage (fetched) — HTTP 302 to https://id.elsevier.com/as/authorization.oauth2?platSite=EAPI%2Felsapi&...&client_id=ELSAPI-PROD&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fdev.elsevier.com%2Fauthenticate. Key management requires an Elsevier ID sign-in (the free Elsevier account); the URL in the claim is correct.

3. https://dev.elsevier.com/support.html (fetched) — verbatim: "Most APIs (except SciVal APIs) are available for no charge, for non-commercial use, subject to Elsevier's policies and limits on usage." AND "only when you're making calls from within your institutional network are you considered a subscriber." AND "Elsevier Research Products APIs rely primarily on Institutional IP address for authentication. API access through proxies is not supported." AND "If you are working away from your main institutional network or your institution accesses Scopus.com, Scival.com, or ScienceDirect.com through a proxy, please contact us to enquire about Institutional Token access." AND commercial: "APIs are available (for commercial use), with an API license and subscription." DESIGN IMPLICATION (critical=true): subscriber-level data depends on the SOURCE IP of the HTTP request, not on the student's WSU AccessID. Calls made by Claude Code running on a grid compute node (WSU IP space, compute nodes have internet) should be treated as on-network; calls from a student laptop off campus, or through a VPN/proxy, will return non-subscriber views unless an Institutional Token is provisioned by WSU library/Elsevier support. Do not model an Elsevier key as a personal credential that carries entitlements.

4. https://dev.elsevier.com/tecdoc_api_authentication.html (fetched) — verbatim: "IP address based authentication for institutional subscribers of Scopus/ScienceDirect" is the default; "Clients authenticating this way get access to all content associated with their institutional account." Headers: "X-ELS-APIKey: [apikey]" on every request; "X-ELS-Insttoken" for institutional tokens, which "must be kept secure server-side in a password protected environment" and "may be revoked at any time, without notice"; insttoken requests require HTTPS. An authtoken from the Authentication API "expires two hours after issuance by the Authentication API" (for multi-account IP conflicts).

5. https://dev.elsevier.com/api_key_settings.html (fetched) — verbatim: "Quotas, meaning the number of requests run, are reset every seven days." Response headers X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Sample weekly quotas: Scopus Search 20,000 req/week at 9 req/s; Scopus Author Retrieval 5,000/week at 3 req/s; ScienceDirect Article Retrieval 50,000/week (unlimited for Text Mining keys) at 10 req/s; SciVal 5,000/week at 6 req/s. Over-rate returns "http 429 TOO MANY REQUESTS". Access-controlled APIs needing explicit approval from API Support: Scopus Citation Overview, Scopus Author Feedback, ScienceDirect Full-Text Entitlement, Embase Search and Retrieval, Engineering Village Search and Retrieval, SUSHI COP5.

6. https://dev.elsevier.com/policy.html (fetched) — use-case policies: Scopus IR use requires "The application needs to be operated by, or on behalf of an academic institution that has a subscription for Scopus."; SciVal requires a SciVal license; ScienceDirect IR/CRIS/VIVO use case "available to all IRs free of charge upon acceptance of a click-through agreement when registering for an API key"; repeated "The client application needs to be free of use and non-commercial."

7. https://dev.elsevier.com/sc_apis.html and https://dev.elsevier.com/sd_apis.html (fetched) — both state the APIs "are available for no charge, for non-commercial use, subject to Elsevier's policies and limits on usage."; commercial use requires "an API license and subscription".

8. https://dev.elsevier.com/documentation/ArticleRetrievalAPI.wadl (fetched) — view values META, META_ABS, META_ABS_REF, FULL, ENTITLED; "The presence of a bearer token implies the request will be executed against user-based entitlements." https://dev.elsevier.com/sc_search_views.html and ScopusSearchAPI.wadl list STANDARD vs COMPLETE views but the fetched text did not itself state which view non-subscribers receive — that specific subscriber/non-subscriber view mapping is NOT verified here beyond the general "considered a subscriber" rule in item 3.

findings.detail: 'X-ELS-APIKey: [apikey]' or '?apiKey=[apikey]'. IP-based: 'This is the default for any newly registered APIKey. Clients authenticating this way get access to all content associated with their institutional account.' Insttoken 'an additional security token submitted in tandem with your APIKey', header 'X-ELS-Insttoken', 'must be kept secure server-side', 'All requests using insttoken must come over https.' Authtoken 'expires two hours after issuance'. Implication: from a grid node, access works only if the node's egress IP is in WSU's registered range, else the library must issue an insttoken.

verdict.corrected_claim: Elsevier Research Product APIs authenticate every request by an APIKey sent either as the HTTP header `X-ELS-APIKey: [apikey]` or as the query parameter `apiKey=[apikey]` (exact case). Entitlement is IP-based by default: "This is the default for any newly registered APIKey. Clients authenticating this way get access to all content associated with their institutional account", and "only when you're making calls from within your institutional network are you considered a subscriber." Off the institutional IP range the key does NOT stop working; it falls back to the key's default, non-subscriber entitlements ("Each APIKey provides access to a limited amount of content by default"), and subscriber-only content/features return an error. "API access through proxies is not supported"; remote access is granted only via an Institutional Token ("insttoken"), which Elsevier's integration support team creates on request from the customer institution (the library/institution requests it from Elsevier Research Product APIs Support; it does not mint it itself). The insttoken is "an additional security token submitted in tandem with your APIKey", sent in header `X-ELS-Insttoken` (the WADL also documents a query override `insttoken`, but the policy says it "can't appear in the address bar"), "must be kept secure server-side in a password protected environment", "may be revoked at any time, without notice", and "All requests using insttoken must come over https." The authtoken (header `X-ELS-Authtoken`, from GET https://api.elsevier.com/authenticate?platform=SCOPUS|SCIDIR|EV|EMBASE) "expires two hours after issuance" but only resolves multiple-account IP conflicts and still requires the caller's IP to map to a known customer account, so it is not an off-campus route; OAuth (`access_token`) is the user-level alternative. Design implication: from a grid compute node, subscribed ScienceDirect/Scopus content is reachable only if the node's egress IP is inside WSU's registered range (not verified here); otherwise the WSU library must obtain an insttoken from Elsevier and the extension must hold it server-side and call over https.

Verbatim: "You either submit the APIKey within a request URL parameter: http://api.elsevier.com/content/search/scopus?query=heart&apiKey=[apikey] Or use this http header with each request: X-ELS-APIKey: [apikey]"; "IP address based authentication for institutional subscribers of Scopus/ScienceDirect: This is the default for any newly registered APIKey. Clients authenticating this way get access to all content associated with their institutional account."; "Each APIKey provides access to a limited amount of content by default"; "Using tokens from our Authentication API to resolve IP address conflicts for institutional subscribers"; "C) The API then checks that your IP address maps to a known customer account."; "Note: An authtoken expires two hours after issuance by the Authentication API."; "Insttokens are only available to customers or partners working on behalf of a customer. If Elsevier grants you an insttoken, there are restrictions to follow: The insttoken must be kept secure server-side in a password protected environment. It can't appear in any browser side code. It can't appear in the address bar. The insttoken represents full access to a customer account ... It may be revoked at any time, without notice. All requests using insttoken must come over https. You submit insttokens in header: X-ELS-Insttoken"; also "Using a proprietary token (an 'Institutional Token') created for you by our integration support team". Page carries no date/last-updated notice. If you attempt to access a subscriber-only feature from home, you're likely to receive such an error response. API access through proxies is not supported, however Elsevier will provide remote access direct to the APIs using a special access credential ('Institutional Token'). If you are working away from your main institutional network or your institution accesses Scopus.com, Scival.com, or ScienceDirect.com through a proxy, please contact us to enquire about Institutional Token access." If provided, this key (in combination with its associated APIKey) is used to establish the credentials"; query params apiKey, access_token ("Override for HTTP header Authorization ... OAuth bearer access token"), insttoken ("Override for HTTP header X-ELS-Insttoken"). Fetched https://dev.elsevier.com/documentation/AuthenticationAPI.wadl: GET https://api.elsevier.com/authenticate/, headers X-ELS-APIKey, X-ELS-Authtoken, X-ELS-Insttoken, X-ELS-ReqId, X-ELS-ResourceVersion, Authorization; params platform (default SCIDIR; SCIDIR, SCOPUS, EV, EMBASE), choice, apiKey, access_token, insttoken; status 300 = multiple choices, 401 = authentication failure, 429 = quota. Fetched https://dev.elsevier.com/policy.html: "The APIs have a built-in authorization mechanism that checks if the application's user has a Scopus license based on its client IP address." Fetched https://dev.elsevier.com/api_key_settings.html: Article Retrieval default = "All Subscribed, OpenAccess and Complimentary Articles", 50,000/week, and "ScienceDirect Full-Text Entitlement" is an access-controlled API. findings.claim: Elsevier's API policy forbids mining the whole Scopus dataset and, for some use cases, storing retrieved records beyond a temporary cache; TDM of full text is allowed for non-commercial research at subscribing institutions.
findings.detail: 'The application needs to be operated by, or on behalf of an academic institution that has a subscription for Scopus.' Academic research: no 'mining of the entire Scopus dataset'. Federated search: 'Data retrieved through the APIs cannot be indexed or stored in a data repository, other than temporarily for performance reasons.' TDM: 'Researchers at subscribing academic institutions can text mine subscribed full-text ScienceDirect content via the Elsevier APIs for non-commercial purposes.' Elsevier TDM policy page: 'Researchers are able to obtain an API key via our developers portal'.

verdict.corrected_claim: Elsevier's API Use Policies (dev.elsevier.com/policy.html, "Policy updated: 06-Sep-2017", still the live page on 2026-09-27) forbid mining the whole Scopus dataset under the Academic Research use case ("Research is limited in scope to a specific discipline - no mining of the entire Scopus dataset is permitted"; also "non-commercial, academic purposes only - no commercial, government or funding body access is permitted"; retention of the research dataset "limited to archival purposes and reproduction of the research results"). Storage beyond a temporary cache is forbidden specifically for the Federated Search use case ("Data retrieved through the APIs cannot be indexed or stored in a data repository, other than temporarily for performance reasons (e.g. non-permanent caching)"), whereas the IR/CRIS/VIVO use case explicitly allows perpetual storage of permitted Scopus metadata. TDM of full text is allowed for non-commercial research at subscribing institutions ("Researchers at subscribing academic institutions can text mine subscribed full-text ScienceDirect content via the Elsevier APIs for non-commercial purposes"), with full-text XML (FULL view) served only when the client IP is recognised as a subscribing institution's; the API key is obtained via the developers portal by registering a text-mining project.
verdict.evidence: Fetched https://dev.elsevier.com/policy.html (2026-09-27): every quoted sentence in the claim is present verbatim. Academic Research: "Research is for non-commercial, academic purposes only - no commercial, government or funding body access is permitted." / "Research is limited in scope to a specific discipline - no mining of the entire Scopus dataset is permitted." / "Retention of original research dataset is limited to archival purposes and reproduction of the research results." Federated Search: "The developer of the federated search application must be affiliated with an organization that has a subscription for the product." / "Data retrieved through the APIs cannot be indexed or stored in a data repository, other than temporarily for performance reasons (e.g. non-permanent caching)." / "For Scopus and Engineering Village, the application can only show the core bibliographic data for each search result; abstracts and references are off-limits." Scopus IR/CRIS/VIVO: "The application needs to be operated by, or on behalf of an academic institution that has a subscription for Scopus." and "The institution is allowed to store this metadata in its IR/CRIS in perpetuity even after it has cancelled its Scopus license." Text mining: "Researchers at subscribing academic institutions can text mine subscribed full-text ScienceDirect content via the Elsevier APIs for non-commercial purposes." Footer: "Policy updated: 06-Sep-2017". Fetched https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/text-and-data-mining: "text mine full-text content hosted on Science Direct for non-commercial research purposes", "automatically enables researchers at subscribing academic institutions to text mine", "Researchers are able to obtain an API key via our developers portal", "gain access to full-text content in XML for this purpose", "All researchers at subscribing academic institutions can download articles to text mine"; page links TDM_Glossary_2025.pdf. Fetched https://dev.elsevier.com/tecdoc_text_mining.html: FULL view returned only "if your client IP address is recognized as that of a subscribing institute that has access to that article"; must "register your text mining project" at the API key management page; key passed as header "X-ELS-APIKey: [APIKey]"; storage/redistribution terms deferred to /api_service_agreement.html (not fetched). Caveats: the claim's phrasing "for some use cases" is accurate because the temporary-cache rule is scoped to Federated Search only; the policy page is dated 2017 but is the current live page. Design implication (critical=true if Ashley ever calls Elsevier APIs from the grid): full-text TDM entitlement is IP-recognised, so calls must originate from a WSU-recognised IP range (grid compute nodes may or may not be in Scopus/ScienceDirect's registered range; not verified). findings.claim: To push with a GitHub fine-grained PAT the token needs repository permission Contents: Read and write (contents=write); the token is used in place of the password over HTTPS and is limited to one resource owner.
findings.detail: 'Push access to repositories' maps to 'contents=write'; Metadata read is implicit. 'Once you have a personal access token, you can enter it instead of your password when performing Git operations over HTTPS.' 'Each token is limited to access resources owned by a single user or organization.' 'If you selected an organization as the resource owner and the organization requires approval for fine-grained personal access tokens, then your token will be marked as pending.' Default expiration 'is 30 days'; 'Infinite lifetimes are allowed but may be blocked by a maximum lifetime policy'. Relevant: the OpenSpineConsortium org copy needs an org-scoped token or a second token.

verdict.corrected_claim: To push over HTTPS with a GitHub fine-grained PAT the token needs the repository permission "Contents" at the write level (API key `contents`, value `write`; the read level covers clone/fetch only). The token is entered in place of the password (Username: YOUR-USERNAME, Password: YOUR-PERSONAL-ACCESS-TOKEN) and is limited to resources owned by ONE resource owner (the user or one organization); it cannot access multiple organizations at once. CRITICAL ADDITIONS the original claim omits: (1) a fine-grained PAT "cannot contribute to repositories where the user is an outside or repository collaborator" nor "to public repos where the user is not a member" — so pushing to the OpenSpineConsortium org copy requires the student to be an org MEMBER and a token with resource owner = OpenSpineConsortium; an outside collaborator must use a PAT (classic) with `repo` scope instead. (2) An org-scoped token is subject to the org's maximum-lifetime policy, whose default is 366 days; the "infinite lifetime" option applies in practice only to user-owned-resource tokens (personal default expiration 30 days). (3) If the org requires approval the token is `pending` and can only read public resources until approved; tokens created by org owners need no approval. (4) "Metadata read is implicit/mandatory" is NOT stated in the docs text; it is a UI label only and the REST installation-token API even accepts `metadata: read|write` — treat as unverified. (5) Since 2025-03-18 fine-grained PATs are GA and enabled by default for orgs; an org that blocked them will not appear in the Resource owner list. (6) GitHub deletes PATs unused for a year. (7) For the gh CLI, `--with-token` is documented for classic tokens; GitHub says "Favour setting GH_TOKEN for fine-grained personal access token usage".
verdict.evidence:
VERIFIED VERBATIM from the original source (docs.github.com managing-your-personal-access-tokens, fetched 2026-09-27): "Once you have a personal access token, you can enter it instead of your password when performing Git operations over HTTPS." / example: "$ git clone https://github.com/USERNAME/REPO.git / Username: YOUR-USERNAME / Password: YOUR-PERSONAL-ACCESS-TOKEN" / "Each token is limited to access resources owned by a single user or organization." / "Each token can be further limited to only access specific repositories for that user or organization." / "Under Resource owner, select a resource owner. The token will only be able to access resources owned by the selected resource owner. Organizations that you are a member of will not appear if the organization has blocked the use of fine-grained personal access tokens." / Repository access options "Public repositories", "All repositories", "Only select repositories"; "Tokens always include read-only access to all public repositories on GitHub." / "Under Permissions, select which permissions to grant the token. Depending on which resource owner and which repository access you specified, there are repository, organization, and account permissions. You should choose the minimal permissions necessary for your needs." / default expiration "30 days"; "infinite lifetimes are allowed but may be blocked by a maximum lifetime policy set by your organization or enterprise owner." / "your token will be marked as `pending` until it is reviewed by an organization administrator. Your token will only be able to read public resources until it is approved." / "GitHub automatically removes personal access tokens that haven't been used in a year." / "Personal access tokens (classic) are less secure." / "GitHub recommends that you use fine-grained personal access tokens instead of personal access tokens (classic) whenever possible."

CRITICAL (critical=true) — LIMITATIONS LIST on the same page, verbatim bullets of what only classic tokens can do: "Using fine-grained personal access token to contribute to public repos where the user is not a member." / "Using fine-grained personal access token to contribute to repositories where the user is an outside or repository collaborator." / "Using fine-grained personal access token to access multiple organizations at once." / "...to access Packages." / "...to call the Checks API." / "...to access Projects owned by a user account." Design consequence: the extension must know whether the student is an OpenSpineConsortium org member; if not, a fine-grained PAT cannot push to the osc remote at all, regardless of permissions. Two remotes with two owners (personal fork + org) = two fine-grained tokens, or one classic `repo`-scoped token.

CONTENTS = WRITE FOR PUSH (critical=true; supported by official API mapping, no single official sentence says "push needs Read and write"): GitHub Apps doc "Choosing permissions for a GitHub App" (https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/choosing-permissions-for-a-github-app): "If you want your app to use an installation or user access token to authenticate for HTTP-based Git access, you should request the 'Contents' repository permission." ... "You can then use the access token as the HTTP password." REST description of the `contents` key (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/apps/apps?apiVersion=2022-11-28#create-an-installation-access-token-for-an-app): "The level of permission to grant the access token for repository contents, commits, branches, downloads, releases, and merges. Can be one of: read, write". Fine-grained PAT permission table (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/authentication/permissions-required-for-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens), heading "Repository permissions for 'Contents'": `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits (write)`, `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs (write)`, `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/{ref} (write)`, `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/blobs (write)`, `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees (write)`, `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} (write)`, `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/merges (write)`; reads: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits/{commit_sha} (read)`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/{ref} (read)`. Actions workflow-syntax doc (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax): "`contents: read` permits an action to list the commits, and `contents: write` allows the action to create a release." Same key/level vocabulary (`contents`, `read|write|none`).

METADATA (unverified): No fetched docs page (managing PATs; permissions-required-for-fine-grained-PATs; permissions-required-for-github-apps; choosing-permissions; registering-a-github-app) contains any sentence that Metadata is mandatory or implicit. The permissions page even states "These permissions are required to access private resources. Some endpoints can also be used to access public resources without these permissions." The 'mandatory Read-only' wording is a token-creation UI label only; do not cite docs for it.

ORG POLICY (critical=true) https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-programmatic-access-to-your-organization/setting-a-personal-access-token-policy-for-your-organization: "By default, both Personal access tokens (classic) and fine-grained personal access tokens are enabled." / heading "Enforcing a maximum lifetime policy for personal access tokens": "For fine-grained personal access tokens, the default the maximum lifetime policy for organizations is set to expire within 366 days. Personal access tokens (classic) do not have an expiration requirement." / "When you set a policy, tokens with non-compliant lifetimes will be blocked from accessing your organization if the token belongs to a member of your organization. Setting this policy does not revoke or disable these tokens. Users will learn that their existing token is non-compliant when API calls for your organization are rejected." / "Fine-grained personal access tokens created by organization owners will not need approval." / "Fine-grained personal access tokens will still be able to read public resources within the organization without approval." Options: "Restrict access via personal access tokens" / "Allow access via personal access tokens"; "Require administrator approval" / "Do not require administrator approval".

GA STATUS: GitHub Changelog 2025-03-18 (https://github.blog/changelog/2025-03-18-fine-grained-pats-are-now-generally-available/): "Fine-grained PATs are now enabled by default for all organizations on GitHub, unless that organization or enterprise explicitly disabled them during the preview." Original announcement 2022-10-18 (https://github.blog/2022-10-18-introducing-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens-for-github/): "over 50 granular permissions"; org opt-in was beta-only.

gh CLI (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_login): "The minimum required scopes for the token are: repo, read:org, and gist." (classic); `--with-token` "pass in a personal access token (classic) on standard input"; "Take care when passing a fine-grained personal access token to --with-token as the inherent scoping to certain resources may cause confusing behaviour when interacting with other resources." "Favour setting GH_TOKEN for fine-grained personal access token usage."

HTTPS ERROR STRINGS (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/troubleshooting-cloning-errors): "error: The requested URL returned error: 401 while accessing https://github.com/USER/REPO.git/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack fatal: HTTP request failed" and "Error: The requested URL returned error: 403 while accessing https://github.com/USER/REPO.git/info/refs fatal: HTTP request failed" — "you must authenticate with a personal access token instead of your password". The commonly reported "remote: Write access to repository not granted." string for a token lacking contents:write was NOT confirmable (WebSearch budget exhausted; DuckDuckGo CAPTCHA; Stack Overflow unfetchable; GitHub community search returned no results) — treat as unverified.

Credential storage (https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/git-basics/caching-your-github-credentials-in-git): Linux recommendations are `gh auth login` or Git Credential Manager; no PAT-specific sentence on that page.

findings.claim: Hugging Face tokens come in fine-grained, read and write roles; pushing requires write (or a fine-grained token with write on the target repos); tokens start with hf_ and work as the git password.
findings.detail: 'write: tokens with this role additionally grant write access to the repositories you have write access to. Use this token if you need to create or push content to a repository'. 'We also recommend using only fine-grained tokens for production usage.' Tokens 'used in place of a password to access the Hugging Face Hub with git'. Org policies: read/write tokens 'will be rejected with a 403 error' where only fine-grained are allowed; org-scoped fine-grained tokens may sit 'Pending' until an admin approves. Manage at https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens.

verdict.corrected_claim: Hugging Face User Access Tokens have three roles: `fine-grained`, `read`, `write`. Creating a repo or pushing to it requires a `write` token, or a fine-grained token granting write on the target repo(s). Tokens are "used in place of a password to access the Hugging Face Hub with git or with basic authentication" (HTTPS). The `hf_` prefix is shown in official examples (`access_token = "hf_..."`) but is not stated as a formal rule; tokens obtained via the browser/device-code login are shown as `hf_oauth_...` and expire (auto-refreshed while in use). Org token policies (read/write tokens rejected with 403 where only fine-grained are allowed; org-scoped fine-grained tokens Pending until admin approval) apply only to organizations on Team and Enterprise plans. Manage at https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens.
verdict.evidence:
VERIFIED 2026-09-27 against the live pages (all fetched).

1. ROLES (critical=true) — https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security-tokens, section "What are User Access Tokens?" lists exactly three roles verbatim: "`fine-grained`: tokens with this role can be used to provide fine-grained access to specific resources, such as a specific model or models in a specific organization." / "`read`: tokens with this role can only be used to provide read access to repositories you could read." / "`write`: tokens with this role additionally grant write access to the repositories you have write access to. Use this token if you need to create or push content to a repository (e.g., when training a model or modifying a model card)." Also: "If you are a member of an organization with read/write/admin role, then your User Access Tokens will be able to read/write the resources according to the token permission (read/write) and organization membership (read/write/admin)."

2. WRITE REQUIRED FOR PUSH (critical=true) — https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/quick-start (huggingface_hub v2.0.0 docs): "User Access Tokens can have `read` or `write` permissions. Make sure to have a `write` access token if you want to create or edit a repository." and "To create a repository or to push content to the Hub, you must provide a User Access Token that has the `write` permission." CLI output on login with a write token: "Token is valid (permission: write)." (https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli). The exact fine-grained permission checkbox name for repo write was NOT found on any fetched page; the fine-grained role description ("fine-grained access to specific resources, such as a specific model") is the only official text.

3. GIT PASSWORD (critical=true) — security-tokens page, "How to use User Access Tokens?": tokens can be "used **in place of a password** to access the Hugging Face Hub with git or with basic authentication." https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/repositories-getting-started confirms HTTPS clones prompt "your username and password on every push operation" and recommends "switch to SSH" or "setup a git credential helper". The HTTPS git USERNAME is not specified on any fetched page. CLI: `hf auth login --token $HF_TOKEN --add-to-git-credential` -> "Your token has been saved in your configured git credential helpers (store)." `login(token=..., add_to_git_credential=True)`: "If no git credential helper is configured, a warning will be displayed to the user. Only used when `token` is provided; ignored by the browser-based flow." `logout()`: "Token is deleted from the machine and removed from git credential." (https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/package_reference/authentication). SSH alternative: `git@hf.co`, keys at https://huggingface.co/settings/keys, test `ssh -T git@hf.co`, ED25519 fingerprint SHA256:dVjzGIdV7d6cwKIeZiCoRMa2gMvSKfGZAvHf4gMiMao (https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security-git-ssh).

4. hf_ PREFIX (critical=false) — security-tokens page shows only a code example `access_token = "hf_..."`; no prose states the prefix as a rule. https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/oauth shows OAuth-issued tokens as `"access_token": "hf_oauth_..."`. quick-start: browser-based `hf auth login` (default since huggingface_hub v2.0.0; device flow at https://huggingface.co/oauth/device) saves a token that "expires after a while but is refreshed automatically as long as you keep using it." DESIGN NOTE: for a persistent 30-day Slurm job, have the student paste a long-lived User Access Token (`--token`) rather than rely on the browser/OAuth flow's expiring token. `hf auth login --format agent` exists for non-interactive agent use ("the command never prompts"). `login()` raises `ValueError` "If an organization token is passed. Only personal account tokens are valid to log in."

5. FINE-GRAINED FOR PRODUCTION — verbatim: "We also recommend using only fine-grained tokens for production usage. The impact, if leaked, will be reduced, and they can be shared among your organization without impacting your account."

6. ORG POLICIES (critical=false unless the target org is Team/Enterprise) — security-tokens, "Tokens in organizations with token management policies": "Organizations on Team and Enterprise plans can enforce token policies". "If your organization has set a policy requiring fine-grained tokens, read/write tokens will be rejected with a `403` error when used against that organization's resources." Pending: "When you create a fine-grained token scoped to an organization that requires administrator approval, the token enters a **Pending** state automatically. It cannot access that organization's resources until an administrator approves it." Admin-created tokens auto-approved. Exact 403 strings (https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/enterprise-hub-tokens-management): pending/denied -> "Due to the organization token policy, your token needs to be approved by the organization before you can access this resource."; revoked (Enterprise only) -> "Your token has been revoked by the organization administrator, you can no longer access organization resources. Please contact them for more information." Policy table: "Allow access via User Access Tokens (default)" authorizes both unscoped and fine-grained; "Only access via fine-grained tokens" -> unscoped Unauthorized; "Require administrator approval" -> both Unauthorized without approval (except admin-created). The claim omitted the Team/Enterprise scoping; a free-tier org cannot enforce these policies.

7. ENV/STORAGE (useful for the extension) — https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/package_reference/environment_variables: `HF_TOKEN` "If set, this value will overwrite the token stored on the machine (in either `$HF_TOKEN_PATH` or `"$HF_HOME/token"` if the former is not set)". `HF_HOME` defaults to `~/.cache/huggingface`; `HF_TOKEN_PATH` defaults to `$HF_HOME/token`. `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN` is deprecated in favour of `HF_TOKEN`. Multiple tokens stored at `~/.cache/huggingface/stored_tokens`; `hf auth switch`, `hf auth list`, `hf auth whoami`. quick-start: "Authentication via an environment variable or a secret has priority over the token stored on your machine."

8. LEAK REVOCATION — `POST https://huggingface.co/api/credentials/revoke` with `{"credentials": ["<raw token>"]}`, no auth needed, always returns `202 Accepted`. TruffleHog runs on every push (https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security-secrets).

9. MANAGE URL — confirmed: https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens ("New token" button; "Manage" to delete/refresh).

Method note: WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before this task; all evidence is from direct WebFetch of official huggingface.co docs pages. No page dated the last edit; the huggingface_hub pages self-identify as v2.0.0 and reference Claude Code/`hf skills add`, so they are current 2026 content.

If set, this value will overwrite the token stored on the machine (in either $HF_TOKEN_PATH or "$HF_HOME/token" if the former is not set).' Deprecated table: HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN -> HF_TOKEN; HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE -> HF_HUB_CACHE. HF_HOME defaults to ~/.cache/huggingface -- on the grid point HF_HOME at CephFS, not the Panasas home.

verdict.corrected_claim: huggingface_hub (current release 2.0.0, 2026-09-24, Python >=3.10) reads HF_TOKEN and, if set, it overrides the token stored on disk at $HF_TOKEN_PATH, defaulting to "$HF_HOME/token" (i.e. ~/.cache/huggingface/token). HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN is listed as deprecated in favour of HF_TOKEN, but it is NOT ignored: it "remain[s] functional" and is still read as a fallback when HF_TOKEN is unset (code: os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN")). Three qualifications the original claim omitted: (1) HF_HOME defaults to ~/.cache/huggingface ONLY when XDG_CACHE_HOME is unset; otherwise it is $XDG_CACHE_HOME/huggingface. (2) All huggingface_hub environment variables are read at import time, so HF_HOME / HF_TOKEN must be exported before Python starts (in the Slurm script or Singularity --env), not set from inside a running process. (3) Full token precedence in 2.0.0 is: OIDC exchange when HF_OIDC_RESOURCE is set (CI only) > HF_TOKEN > HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN > token file (auto-refreshed) > Google Colab secret. The deprecated table also includes HUGGINGFACE_ASSETS_CACHE -> HF_ASSETS_CACHE. On the grid, point HF_HOME (which also places HF_HUB_CACHE=$HF_HOME/hub and HF_XET_CACHE=$HF_HOME/xet) at CephFS, not the Panasas home. The login CLI is now `hf auth login` (browser code flow or pasted User Access Token), not `huggingface-cli login`.
verdict.evidence:
Claim HELD; refinements only, no refutation. WebSearch could not be run (session budget exhausted), so all evidence is from directly fetched official docs and source.

1. Official env-var page (huggingface_hub docs, internal links resolve to /v2.0.0/), fetched 2026-09-27, verbatim: "### HF_TOKEN — To configure the User Access Token to authenticate to the Hub. If set, this value will overwrite the token stored on the machine (in either `$HF_TOKEN_PATH` or `"$HF_HOME/token"` if the former is not set)." "### HF_TOKEN_PATH — ... Defaults to `"$HF_HOME/token"` (e.g. `~/.cache/huggingface/token` by default)." "### HF_HOME — ... Defaults to `"~/.cache/huggingface"` unless XDG_CACHE_HOME is set." "### XDG_CACHE_HOME — Used only when `HF_HOME` is not set! ... the default home will be `"$XDG_CACHE_HOME/huggingface"`." Tip at top: "All environment variables are read at import time of `huggingface_hub`. Any modification made afterwards will not be taken into account." Deprecated table verbatim: "Although they remain functional, they no longer take precedence over their replacements." Rows: HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE -> HF_HUB_CACHE; HUGGINGFACE_ASSETS_CACHE -> HF_ASSETS_CACHE; HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN -> HF_TOKEN. Also HF_HUB_CACHE defaults to "$HF_HOME/hub", HF_XET_CACHE to "$HF_HOME/xet", HF_ASSETS_CACHE to "$HF_HOME/assets". HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER is now itself deprecated (Xet backend).

2. Source, src/huggingface_hub/constants.py (main branch, fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/main/...): HF_HOME = os.getenv("HF_HOME", os.path.join(os.getenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", default_home), "huggingface")) with default_home = ~/.cache; HF_TOKEN_PATH = os.getenv("HF_TOKEN_PATH", os.path.join(HF_HOME, "token")); HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE = os.getenv("HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE", default_cache_path); HF_HUB_CACHE = os.getenv("HF_HUB_CACHE", HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE).

3. Source, src/huggingface_hub/utils/_auth.py (main): get_token() returns _get_token_from_oidc() or _get_token_from_environment() or _get_token_from_file_refreshed() or _get_token_from_google_colab(). _get_token_from_environment(): return _clean_token(os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN")) with comment "`HF_TOKEN` has priority (keep `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN` for backward compatibility)". Docstring: "If `HF_OIDC_RESOURCE` is set (Trusted Publishers, typically in CI), a short-lived token obtained via OIDC token exchange takes precedence." _clean_token strips \r \n and whitespace, so a trailing newline in a token file is harmless.

4. Quickstart Authentication section (https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/quick-start): "Authentication via an environment variable or a secret has priority over the token stored on your machine." Login is `hf auth login` (browser short-code flow; "an access token is retrieved and saved in your `HF_HOME` directory (defaults to `~/.cache/huggingface/token`). The token expires after a while but is refreshed automatically as long as you keep using it. ... Alternatively, you can paste a User Access Token"). `hf auth switch` / `hf auth list` manage multiple stored tokens; `HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1` stops the token being sent on public requests.

5. PyPI (https://pypi.org/project/huggingface-hub/): latest 2.0.0 released September 24, 2026; Requires Python >=3.10.0.

Design consequences (critical=true): export HF_HOME=/rs/rs_grp_oschome/go2432/... and HF_TOKEN in the sbatch script / Singularity environment BEFORE any Python import (import-time read); if the extension writes a static token to $HF_HOME/token instead of HF_TOKEN, it works but HF_TOKEN in the environment silently wins over it; do not rely on HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN but do not assume it is inert either (a stale one set by a student's old .bashrc will still authenticate when HF_TOKEN is absent). Non-critical: the whole-home-directory move also relocates the hub, xet and assets caches, which is the intended effect on the Panasas quota.

verdict.corrected_claim: Wayne State's EZproxy prefix is https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login?url= ; login is AccessID + password; on-campus users typically are not prompted.
verdict.evidence:
CLAIM HELD on every point; each was verified against a page actually fetched on 2026-09-27 (WebSearch budget was exhausted, so verification is by direct fetch only).

(1) PREFIX — confirmed verbatim. https://ask.lib.wayne.edu/faq/443149 ("How do I link to resources through EZproxy?", Last Updated Jun 05, 2026): "The EZproxy URL [https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login?url=] should be pasted at the front of your electronic resource URL, including the https://". Note the prefix is NOT stated on the original source page https://library.wayne.edu/services/computing/ezproxy/ (fetched; it names EZproxy and the login behavior but gives no URL string) — the prefix comes from the ask.lib.wayne.edu FAQ, which this time fetched successfully. Independently, https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login is live and serves an EZproxy login page (title "EZProxy Login"), so the host and path are current.

(2) CREDENTIALS = AccessID + password — confirmed on four pages. library.wayne.edu/services/computing/ezproxy/: "enter your AccessID and password (the same credentials used for Canvas and Academica)". ask.lib.wayne.edu/faq/443148 ("How do I use EZproxy?", Jun 05, 2026): "By logging in with your WSU AccessID and password, just like logging into Canvas or your WSU email." Live form at https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login: fields AccessID + Password, text "In order to use this resource you must enter your AccessID and password" and "Do not include "@wayne.edu" in your AccessID" (this is where the @wayne.edu sentence lives — on the login form itself, not in the FAQ), submit button "Send". The fetch tool reported this is the native EZproxy form, not a cross-host redirect to WSU SSO/Shibboleth/Duo (the tool returns cross-host redirects rather than following them, so a redirect would have been visible). No page mentions Duo/2FA for EZproxy.

(3) ON-CAMPUS NOT PROMPTED — confirmed verbatim. library.wayne.edu/services/computing/ezproxy/: "If you're on campus, you typically won't need to sign in." The live login form also carries a lock icon captioned "requires log in if off campus". ask.lib.wayne.edu/faq/443146 (Jun 05, 2026) defines EZproxy as giving "access from outside the Wayne State network to licensed resources that authenticate users by IP address", consistent with on-campus IP passthrough.

(4) VPN ALTERNATIVE — confirmed. The library page describes Wayne State's Virtual Private Network as providing "secure access to Wayne State resources that are normally restricted to on-campus use", listed beside EZproxy as the off-campus route.

(5) ADDITIONAL, relevant to a credential-collecting tool: https://ask.lib.wayne.edu/faq/354612 (Jun 05, 2026) lists exact EZproxy error strings: "We're not recognizing your Access ID and/or password."; "This resource is reserved for current faculty, staff or students of Wayne State University." (eligibility gate — valid AccessID but wrong status still fails); "We're having trouble connecting to the network." (verification directory down). Help route is the C&IT Help Desk.

Caveats: page text was extracted by the fetch tool's summarizer, but the quoted strings were requested verbatim. No dated evidence of a planned migration of EZproxy to WSU SSO/Duo was found, but the search budget prevented a broader sweep for such announcements; the four FAQ pages were all last updated Jun 05, 2026 and the login endpoint is live today, so the claim is current as of 2026-09-27.

verdict.evidence:
VERIFIED VERBATIM (all fetched 2026-09-27, no authentication needed => public):

[critical=true] https://guides.lib.wayne.edu/dmcwsu (page title "Shiffman Library: Previous DMC-Sponsored Residents"; "Last Updated: Jun 30, 2026 3:07 PM"):

[critical=true] FAQ linked from that page, https://guides.lib.wayne.edu/c.php?g=174966&p=11542304 ("FAQs: DMC WSU Library Access", Last Updated Jun 30, 2026 3:07 PM):
- Q1 answer: "As of June 30, 2026, the DMC made the decision to discontinue library services provided by Wayne State University. Kindly reach out to the DMC Graduate Medical Education department for guidance on contacting what medical library to use: DMC Graduate Medical Education, 4201 St. Antoine, UHC 9C, Detroit, Michigan 48201, Main Telephone Number: (313) 745-5146, Hours: 8:30 a.m. - 3:00 p.m."
- "I am a DMC resident; can I still visit the Shiffman Medical Library?" -> "Yes, public guests are welcome to visit Shiffman library, however they cannot access licensed online material via the guest Wi-Fi."
- "As a DMC resident, can I request guest library access through WSU?" -> "Not at this time; the DMC decided to discontinue library services through Wayne State University."

CORROBORATION THAT STUDENTS AND WSU-SPONSORED RESIDENTS ARE UNAFFECTED (inference support):
[critical=true] https://library.wayne.edu/policies/resources (no date on page): "Access to licensed electronic resources is restricted to current Wayne State University students, faculty, staff and other authorized users." and "When current WSU students, faculty and staff are off-campus, access to licensed electronic resources will require confirmation of university status via the Wayne State University AccessID." Also "Most of the electronic resources are available to the WSU Libraries' walk-in users." DMC residents were an "other authorized users" class created by contract; current students are named directly.
[critical=true] https://guides.lib.wayne.edu/residents ("Shiffman - WSU Residents: Get started", "Last Updated: Jul 28, 2026 1:58 PM", i.e. after the cutoff): "To access many library resources, you'll need to enter your WSU AccessID, which consists of 2 letters and 4 numbers (e.g., ab1234)." Audience: "Essential information on library resources and research support for WSU Residents." No June-30 notice on this page.
https://gme.med.wayne.edu/ : under "As a resident at Wayne State, you have all the benefits associated with employment by a well-established research institution:" the bullet "Free access to WSUSOM's Shiffman Medical Library databases such as PubMed, MEDLINE, and UpDate" [sic]. => WSU-sponsored residents are WSU employees and keep access.
[critical=true] https://gme.med.wayne.edu/programs heading "Wayne State University sole-sponsored programs": Anesthesiology; Dermatology; Family Medicine/Family Medicine-Underserved Track; Internal Medicine; Otolaryngology; Preventive Medicine; Transitional Year; Urology. General Surgery and Neurosurgery are NOT on this list, so they are DMC-sponsored. The PI's affiliation is Department of General Surgery, WSU SOM / DMC; if the PI is a DMC-sponsored resident the loss applies to the PI's own AccessID, not merely "a DMC-resident co-author's". Not verifiable from the web; check directly.

PROXY MECHANISM:
https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login (EZproxy): "In order to use this resource you must enter your AccessID and password (the same one as Academica, Canvas, and WSU email)"; "Do not include "@wayne.edu" in your AccessID." No eligibility list on the login page; no DMC notice.
https://services.wayne.edu/TDClient/277/Portal/KB/Article/20331/... (Guest ID KB): "Guest IDs provide temporary access to Wayne State University systems and services for non-WSU personnel"; sponsorable: "employees not paid by the university, employees in the University Physicians Group, short-term contractors, conference attendees, and other select guests"; services: "Wayne State email, Academica, VPN"; library access requires a separate special request form; "Guest IDs are valid for one year from the date of creation"; unrenewed IDs "will be automatically disabled." => library entitlement is separate from holding an AccessID; an AccessID can exist and still fail the proxy. https://services.wayne.edu/TDClient/277/Portal/KB/Article/20082/... lists only three disable reasons: "more than five login attempts using an incorrect password", "A student has not registered for classes for four consecutive terms", "An employee has left the university". verdict.corrected_claim: WSU University Libraries' "Acceptable Use of Electronic Resources" policy (canonical URL https://library.wayne.edu/policies/resources#acceptable; the legacy URL https://library.wayne.edu/info/about/policies/eresources.php serves word-for-word identical text) prohibits, verbatim: "Systematic downloading of materials; downloading should be limited to an individual's research needs"; "Downloading of whole issues of journals or attempts to create large databases"; "Sharing of passwords, access codes or licensed software clients"; "Use of robots, spiders, crawlers or any software designed to automatically browse the Web, record Web browsing activity, or systematically download electronic resources"; systematic redistribution to anyone outside WSU education/research/clinical care; and any commercial use. Violations "may result in suspension or cancellation of continued access rights to a given licensed resource for the entire Wayne State University community" — discretionary ("may"), scoped per resource, community-wide in effect — and "Electronic resource account activity is tracked closely by its vendors or publishers." The policy is undated (footer © 2026) and never names EZproxy, scripting, VPN, APIs or text-and-data mining. WSU's off-campus gateway is OCLC EZproxy at https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login, a plain AccessID+password HTML form (no SSO/Duo redirect observed), with Palo Alto GlobalProtect and a School of Medicine VPN as alternatives. Design consequence (an inference the policy supports but does not state): Ashley must not store the AccessID password for, or drive, EZproxy or VPN logins, and must not fetch licensed library content from the grid job; the only compliant path is the student's own interactive browser session on their laptop. University Policy UP 00-1 "Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resources" (effective 2000-05-12) applies in parallel: users must "prevent others from obtaining access" to their accounts, and "Subverting restrictions associated with computer accounts" is prohibited, with sanctions via the Student Due Process Policy.
verdict.evidence: critical=true. All four quoted phrases confirmed verbatim on the original URL (fetched 2026-09-27) and again on the canonical URL https://library.wayne.edu/policies/resources, which the Libraries' own policy index (https://library.wayne.edu/info/about/policies/) links as "Acceptable Use of Electronic Resources"; the fetcher reported the two pages "word-for-word identical". Full prohibited-use list has six bullets, not three: the claim omitted "Downloading of whole issues of journals or attempts to create large databases", systematic redistribution outside WSU, and commercial use. Consequences sentence exact: "Engaging in following actions, which violate the University's licenses with vendors/publishers or U.S. Copyright Law, may result in suspension or cancellation of continued access rights to a given licensed resource for the entire Wayne State University community" — note "may" and "a given licensed resource"; the claim's "community-wide suspension as the penalty" slightly overstates a discretionary, per-resource sanction. Detection is vendor-side: "Electronic resource account activity is tracked closely by its vendors or publishers." Authorized users: "current Wayne State University students, faculty, staff and other authorized users"; authorized use: "individual educational, research and clinical care purposes" (view on screen, print, store records for later display). No last-updated date; footer "© 2026". Words "EZproxy", "proxy", "pipeline", "scripting" do NOT appear on the policy page, so "must not script EZproxy" is a design inference, not policy text; the operative clauses are "any software designed to automatically browse the Web ... or systematically download electronic resources" and "Sharing of passwords, access codes or licensed software clients". EZproxy confirmed independently: https://proxy.lib.wayne.edu/login renders a page titled "EZProxy Login" with an "About EZProxy" link (https://library.wayne.edu/services/computing/ezproxy/), fields AccessID + Password ("the same one as Academica, Canvas, and WSU email", omit "@wayne.edu"); no SSO redirect, no Duo/2FA observed — a stored password alone authenticates, which is why an extension that holds the AccessID password is a compliance hazard. Remote-access page https://library.wayne.edu/spaces-tech/access-resources: EZproxy is primary; alternatives are Wayne State VPN (Palo Alto GlobalProtect) and School of Medicine VPN; it references both the Libraries' policy and the "Wayne State University Acceptable Use of Information Resources Policy"; EZproxy page also prohibits "Non-licensed resource usage, including but not limited to, general web browsing, game playing, social media and audio/video" through the proxy. University-level policy located via https://policies.wayne.edu/information-technology: UP 00-1 "Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resources" (https://wayne.edu/policies/acceptable-use.php, effective May 12, 2000): §3.1 users "should take appropriate precautions to ensure the security of their passwords and prevent others from obtaining access"; §3.3 prohibits "Subverting restrictions associated with computer accounts" and supplying "false or misleading data"; §4.3 sanctions via Student Due Process Policy; it does not address automated/bot access. Not found: any WSU text-and-data-mining or generative-AI carve-out (https://guides.lib.wayne.edu/tdm returned 404; the Libraries' policy index lists none). WebSearch budget was exhausted this session, so absence of a TDM policy is "not located", not "does not exist". Dead URLs tried: library.wayne.edu/info/services/remote-access.php (404), library.wayne.edu/info/about/policies/remote-access.php (404), policies.wayne.edu/administrative/10-01-acceptable-use-of-information-technology-resources (404), tech.wayne.edu/kb/security/acceptable-use (307 to services.wayne.edu KB portal). Prefer the canonical /policies/resources URL in the design doc; the eresources.php path is a legacy alias that may not persist.

topics_verified.recommendation: Wizard credential model for the literature step: collect ONE contact email (reused as E-utilities `email`, Crossref `mailto`, Unpaywall `email`, and the arXiv/Europe PMC User-Agent), then three required tokens and a set of optional ones. Required: (1) NCBI_API_KEY (free, from NCBI Account settings -> API Key Management; lifts PubMed from 3 to 10 req/s; pipeline should pace at ~8 req/s, back off on the exact body `{"error":"API rate limit exceeded",...}`, and schedule bulk EFetch/ELink runs weekends or 21:00-05:00 Eastern); (2) OPENALEX_API_KEY (free from openalex.org/settings/api; since 2026-02-13 keyless use is a ~$0.10/day trial; $1/day ≈ 1,000 searches or 10,000 list calls; expect 429 on budget or >100 req/s; prefer list+filter endpoints over search and never use content download in bulk); (3) GitHub fine-grained PAT (github_pat_ prefix) with Repository permissions Contents: Read and write on the named repos, exported as GH_TOKEN; if the OpenSpineConsortium org repo is a target, either scope a second token to that org (may be `pending` until approved) or push there via SSH. HF_TOKEN (hf_ prefix, write or fine-grained-with-write) is required only if the review outputs go to the Hub; validate the role before saving. Optional, off by default: S2_API_KEY (free but 1 req/s; keyless shared pool is usually faster for small batches), ELSEVIER_API_KEY (+ ELSEVIER_INSTTOKEN only if the library issues one), WOS_API_KEY (Free Trial tier is 50/day and no times-cited; the 5,000/day tier needs WSU's subscription to be recognised), SERPAPI_API_KEY (Google Scholar spot checks, $25/month per 1,000 searches), ZENODO_TOKEN (deposit:write + deposit:actions, only for archiving). Store all of these on the grid in a mode-600 file under the user's home (never /tmp, which is swept), and inject them into the Slurm job environment for the Singularity container with `--env-file` or an exported env; set HF_HOME on CephFS. Rate-limit per client to the documented ceilings (Europe PMC 10/s and 500/min per IP — remember several students may share one node's IP; Crossref 50/s polite; NIH RePORTER 1/s; arXiv one call per 3 s; ClinicalTrials.gov undocumented, stay under 1/s; Scopus 9/s and 20,000/week). Full text: resolve OA copies via Unpaywall and Europe PMC/PMC first; for paywalled Elsevier content use the Article Retrieval API under the TDM terms only from a WSU IP, and never automate EZproxy with a student's AccessID (WSU policy bars robots and systematic downloading; the sanction is university-wide). Before shipping, run a one-time probe job from a compute node: `curl -sI https://api.elsevier.com/content/search/scopus?query=test -H 'X-ELS-APIKey: ...'` and a publisher page, to learn whether the node egress IP is inside WSU's registered ranges; if not, the Scopus/WoS and full-text steps must run from the laptop on VPN or be dropped. Have the wizard also record, for the PRISMA flow diagram, each database's query string, run date, and hit count, since Scopus/WoS results cannot be stored beyond a temporary cache under Elsevier's policy.
